## 提交分析：[3ba1d9e] meter global packed tokens without changing training inputs (#982)

### 1. 主要更新类型
- **功能新增（观测/日志维度）**，属于数据管道与训练监控的增强，而非核心算法或模型结构变更。
- 从提交标签 `[logging, data] feat:` 可见，改动集中在训练过程的可观测性与数据统计上。

### 2. 关键变更点及与项目方向的关系
- **新增"全局打包 token 数"的计量能力**：在分布式训练中统计所有 rank 上真正参与计算的 packed token 总量，作为吞吐与算力利用率的真实指标。
- **关键设计约束是"不改动训练输入"**：即该统计以旁路（side-effect free）方式实现，不影响数据加载、打包（packing）逻辑与模型前向结果，保证训练语义与数值完全不变。
- 这与 VeOmni 的项目定位高度一致：作为一个"以模型为中心的分布式训练配方库"，其价值不仅在于能跑多模态训练，更在于提供**可度量、可复现、可扩展**的分布式 recipe。全局 token 计量正是衡量多模态（变长、异构、packing 程度不同）训练效率的关键标尺。

### 3. 对项目的影响和潜在意义
- **提升指标可信度**：传统按"样本数"或"本地 batch"统计的吞吐在 packing 场景下会失真，全局 packed token 能反映真实计算量，便于跨模型、跨模态、跨并行策略横向对比。
- **降低接入成本**：不改训练输入意味着用户升级后无需调整数据配置或重跑实验即可获得新指标，符合"recipe zoo"强调的开箱即用与低侵入性。
- **为容量规划与调优提供依据**：可用于识别数据不平衡（各 rank packed token 差异）、packing 效率瓶颈，进而指导 sequence packing 策略与负载均衡优化。

### 4. 值得关注的技术点
- **零侵入的观测实现方式**：如何在不触碰数据通路的前提下拿到全局聚合值（如通过已有通信集合、计数器或钩子），是分布式框架设计中"可观测性与正确性解耦"的典型范例。
- **跨 rank 归约的一致性**：全局统计需保证所有进程计数口径一致、聚合时机同步，避免引入额外同步开销或死锁风险。
- **packing 场景的语义**：需区分 padding、被截断 token 与有效 token，统计口径的定义直接影响指标意义。

### 5. 结合项目背景对发展的影响
VeOmni 的目标是"用模型为中心的分布式配方扩展任意模态模型训练"，其论文与文档强调训练效率与可扩展性。此次提交虽小，却补上了**效率评估闭环**中的一环：只有能准确度量全局计算量，配方（并行策略、packing、调度）的优劣才具备可比性，recipe zoo 的"配方"才有可验证的价值。这体现了项目从"能训"向"能训得好、能说清好在哪"的成熟度演进，也为后续自动化调优、性能回归测试奠定了数据基础。

**总结**：这是一次低风险、高价值的观测能力增强，强化了 VeOmni 作为可度量分布式训练框架的基础设施，对多模态长序列、packing 密集型训练场景的效率分析具有直接意义。

## AI分析总结

# FlashInfer 昨日提交综合分析（共 142 个提交）

## 一、主要更新
昨日提交以**性能优化**为绝对主体（约七至九成），其次是**正确性修复**、少量**功能新增**（SDSA 稀疏注意力索引器、分布式低精度通信、`bwd_reserve_sms` 等）与**硬件平台扩展**（SM107a/Rubin、SM120），辅以 CI/发布链路等工程治理改动，无重大架构变更。改动集中于 `cake_fmha`（注意力）与 `cake_fused_moe`（MoE 融合）两大关键模块，属于对潜在隐患的一次集中清理。

## 二、关键变更
**性能优化**三条主线：一是 "Cake" 内核族（KDA、MoE、GDN、FMHA、RMSNorm-SiLU、FP8 GEMM、causal conv1d、LM head loss 等）微架构级打磨，普遍 1.01x–1.7x，局部达 1.5–4x；二是形状感知的主机端路由持续细化——tinygemm 路由窗口扩至 952 甚至覆盖 20480 特征、175 万+ 形状，按 GB200/GB300/B200/SM107 行规则与 SM 数量分派程序，仅调 host 参数即获 1%–5% 提速；三是系统级融合与开销削减——PDL 预加载铺开至多内核（≤128 token 正收益，需精细控制）、MoE finalize+all-reduce+RMSNorm 融合单内核、FFI launch 缓存、双流 ping-pong、Cluster Launch Control 动态调度等，端到端 host 收益累计达 1.6 倍。MSA indexer 按 CUDA Graph 实际序列长度裁剪 tile，解码最高 9.9x；length-aware stream-K 带来 1.2–2.2x；JIT 运行时化（最高 2x）降低首调用延迟。多数提交保证 bitwise 一致。

**正确性修复**覆盖多类生产级缺陷：BF16 解码路径四项修复——页表对齐非法地址崩溃、retained-KV 网格维数错误致约 50ms 退化、B128 retained-KV 非确定性成员（racecheck 曾报 3.4 万条错误）、correction-warp WAR 竞争（以 `stats_empty` 初始化同步消除）；六个 BF16 解码程序越界读取 V 页槽位致 NaN 污染与 `kv_len=0` 写非零结果，改用哨兵页修复；NVFP4 context JIT 的 `page_empty` mbarrier 补 `__syncwarp()` 消除线程失步竞争。另有 RMSNorm 共享内存阈值不一致致寄存器溢出、GEMM workspace 多流并发损坏、32 位偏移溢出改为按请求拆分 launch、NVFP4 E2M1 `-0` 值致接收端死等、FMHA softmax 统计竞态（引入独立 mbarrier）、`tcgen05.alloc` 与 cluster barrier 顺序竞争、全 NaN 行越界写、FP4 量化在 SM100 以下静默输出改为显式拒绝、SM 缓存改用 `cuStreamGetId` 规避 handle 复用污染，以及 rendezvous、CUTLASS DSL 安装、发布链路等 CI 故障。

**功能与生态**：SDSA 稀疏注意力索引器（阈值采样避免 64 GiB 中间读写，确立 Top-K 稀疏路线）；SageAttention2 低精度 all-to-all、四秩 FP4 全归约；SM107 启用 NVLink Lamport；`--kernel-variant auto`、`use_cp="auto"` 自动路由；`deterministic=False` 复用确定性程序缓存，eager 路径提速 1.2–1.4×。测试新增 Kimi-K3 NVFP4 融合 quant+route 位级一致用例。

## 三、项目影响
项目正从纯推理库演进为**训练-推理全栈、带智能路由的内核平台**：GDN/router 梯度、LM head loss、确定性 KDA 等训练内核密集合入；三代 Blackwell（sm_100a/103a/107a）与 SM120 全覆盖，巩固 vLLM/SGLang 底层供应商地位。上述修复消除了页表崩溃、NaN 传播、错误结果等用户可感知缺陷，提升窄页表、空 KV 等边界场景鲁棒性；严谨基准文化（A/A 噪声带、冷 L2、racecheck 清零）与 racecheck/synccheck/memcheck 全绿、位级对比合入标准提供工程级可信度。CODEOWNERS 精简与 opt-in 参数策略反映团队在激进性能与向后兼容间的审慎平衡。

## 四、值得关注的技术点
- **哨兵页技巧**：用 `2**30` 页 ID 触发 TMA 零填充替代边界分支，零开销解决越界读取，K 槽位因 softmax 掩码无需改动。
- **确定性双路径设计**贯穿多内核，非确定性路径经跳零梯度获额外加速；LPT 调度仅读 host 整数保证 forward/recompute/replay 决策一致。
- **elected ready-count publish**：64 线程经命名 barrier 选举单线程发 fence 批量递增，替代逐线程 fence。
- **warp 级同步陷阱**：mbarrier 等待不保证 warp 内线程收敛，等待后仍需 `__syncwarp()`。
- **持久化 1 维网格约定**：kernel 按 `gridDim.x` 跨步平铺，绑定层误用 3D 网格会导致 CTA 重复执行，暴露隐式耦合风险。
- **CUDA Graph 与动态形状矛盾**：按设备端长度裁剪提供可复用范式；TMA descriptor 编码约束与低数值规范（`-0` 规范化、无符号发布防 NaN 伪装）是量化传输常见陷阱。
- **流间干扰折中**：`cooperative=False` 以 1% 空载代价换负载下 5x–18x 提速。

## 五、整体评估
FlashInfer 已进入**极致调优与严格验证并进的成熟阶段**：性能极限压榨、正确性加固、API 治理三线并进。但路由窗口与程序矩阵快速膨胀（单内核 52 程序/架构、行规则超 366 条）带来的可维护性与自动化测试压力，是后续需重点关注的挑战。

### [dafedad](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/dafedad245ead69d2b5c7400af247a0fc934f5eb)

- **作者**: Jin Jingyuan
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T23:58:50Z
- **提交信息**: fix(norm): align RMSNorm cluster smem budget with the cp.async threshold (#5729)

## 📌 Description

`RMSNormKernel._compute_cluster_n` picks `cluster_n` against the
**full** `shared_memory_per_block_optin`, but `__init__` enables
`cp.async` only when the tile fits in **half** of it:

```python
# __init__, rmsnorm.py:99-104
self.use_async_copy = tile_bytes <= props.shared_memory_per_block_optin // 2

# _compute_cluster_n, rmsnorm.py:107-123
max_smem_bytes = props.shared_memory_per_block_optin   # <- full limit
...
    if smem_needed <= max_smem_bytes:
        return cluster_n
```

When `tile_bytes` lands between the two thresholds, `cluster_n` stays at
1 (the tile "fits") while `cp.async` is disabled — and
`_smem_size_in_bytes` drops the tile entirely in that case, so pass 2
loses the shared-memory reload it uses to keep `x` off the critical
register path:

```python
# Pass 2
if cutlass.const_expr(self.use_async_copy):
    cute.autovec_copy(tXsX, tXrX)   # reload x from smem
    x = tXrX.load().to(Float32)
```

Every thread then has to keep its whole `x` fragment live across the
reduction barrier, on top of the `weight` fragment loaded in pass 1. On
H100 (`optin = 232448`) fp16 `H = 65536` gives 256 elements/thread, ~384
live registers, and ptxas gives up: 32 registers/thread, 1.5 GB of
local-memory traffic per launch, effective bandwidth 142 GB/s instead of
~1.5 TB/s.

This affects **all 16-bit hidden sizes above `optin/4`**, not just
65536/131072, because `cluster_n` keeps returning 1 until the tile
exceeds the full limit:

| H | 65536 | 98304 | 131072 | 262144 | 524288 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fp16 GB/s | 142 | 139 | 156 | 153 | 146 |

fp32 is hit too, at non-power-of-two sizes (`H =
40960/49152/98304/163840`, ~255-286 GB/s) — the benchmark shapes in the
wild happen to be powers of two, which is why this went unnoticed.

## Fix

Target half the opt-in limit in `_compute_cluster_n`, the same threshold
`use_async_copy` uses, so the two decisions stay in sync: any
`cluster_n` that passes the occupancy target also leaves `cp.async`
enabled. This mirrors `FusedAddRMSNormKernel._compute_cluster_n`
(`fused_add_rmsnorm.py:111-139`), which already does exactly this,
including the `best_fit` fallback for hidden sizes too large to satisfy
the occupancy target at any cluster size.

Side benefit: `cluster_n` grows, so `H_per_cta` shrinks and so does
`elems_per_thread` — 256 → 128 for fp16 `H = 65536` — giving headroom
even if `cp.async` is ever disabled again.

## Measurements

H100 PCIe, M=1024, warmup 5 + 20 CUDA-event median, `io_bytes = M × H ×
elem_size × 2`.

| dtype | H | before | after | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fp16 | 65536 | 1894us | **163us** | 11.6x |
| fp16 | 131072 | 3436us | **306us** | 11.2x |
| fp16 | 262144 | 7017us | **599us** | 11.7x |
| bf16 | 58112 | 3094us | **151us** | 20.6x |
| bf16 | 116224 | 5408us | **299us** | 18.1x |
| fp32 | 163840 | 5228us | **745us** | 7.0x |

Below the threshold the generated kernel is unchanged and there is no
regression (all points within ±3%, i.e. run-to-run noise):

| dtype | H | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fp16 | 16384 | 45.2us | 45.9us |
| fp16 | 32768 | 88.5us | 88.5us |
| bf16 | 32768 | 88.4us | 88.5us |
| fp32 | 131072 | 617.2us | 600.8us |
| fp32 | 524288 | 2597.9us | 2575.2us |

Correctness is unchanged — `max_abs_err` against
`torch.nn.functional.rms_norm` is bit-identical before and after (fp16
0.00444 / 0.00671, bf16 0.05217 / 0.06064, fp32 0.0).

Also verified against `flashinfer-python==0.7.0` from PyPI (24 configs,
point-by-point within 0.5% in the degraded region), so this is not a
stale-checkout artifact.

This is the invariant the fix establishes, and it is exactly what the

new test deselected, **1552 passed / 33 deselected** — the delta is

## Reviewer Notes

**Scope.** One method in `rmsnorm.py` plus a regression test. The code
change is intentionally identical in shape to
`FusedAddRMSNormKernel._compute_cluster_n` so the two kernels converge
rather than diverge.

**Two adjacent issues I found while auditing this path but deliberately
left out of scope** (both pre-existing, neither reachable through
`RMSNormKernel` as far as I can tell — flagging so you can decide
whether they deserve their own fix):

1. `RMSNormQuantKernel` reuses this method (`rmsnorm.py:740`) but
overrides `num_threads` to 256 when `H_per_cta > 8192`
(`rmsnorm.py:752-753`), which `_estimate_smem_bytes` does not model — so
its smem estimate is ~2x low for `H_per_cta ∈ (8192, 16384]`. Harmless
in magnitude (the tile is only 32 KB there, far below either budget) and
`FusedAddRMSNormKernel` has the same gap, but the estimator and the
caller disagree in principle.

2. The `best_fit = 1` sentinel shares its value with the legitimate
candidate `cluster_n = 1`. It cannot change the result here: if
`cluster_n = 1` fits the full limit, then `cluster_n = 2` already
satisfies the occupancy target and returns early, so the fallback is
only reached when no small candidate fits. Same shape as the existing
`FusedAddRMSNormKernel` code.

**Not covered.** No hardware other than H100 PCIe was available, so the
numbers above are single-GPU. The trigger depends only on
`shared_memory_per_block_optin` (227 KB on H100/H200/B200/B300) and the
255-register limit, both identical across those parts, and
`RMSNormKernel` has a single architecture branch (`sm_version < 90`), so
the same thresholds are expected elsewhere — but that is reasoning, not
measurement.

## 📌 Description

CUDA LayerNorm accepts last-dimension-contiguous views but drops their
row strides in the C++ binding. A BF16 input with shape `(2, 128)` and
stride `(256, 1)` therefore reads the first row's padding as its second
row. On A100, a deterministic alternating ±1 input returns zeros for
that row; the CuTe backend returns the expected values.

Pass input/output row strides through the CUDA launcher and use separate
64-bit row offsets for every kernel read and write. Use packed loads
only when both strides and the input, output, gamma and beta pointers
meet their alignment requirements; otherwise use the scalar path.
Preserve the existing contiguous C++ overload and the quantized API's
contiguous layout.

The large-row regression also exercises the no-shared-memory fallback.
Clear the handled `cudaErrorInvalidValue` from a rejected shared-memory
opt-in request so it does not leak into a subsequent CUDA call.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Independently reproduced on main
`a101601c82aacea4536ece72eeb507a95109cb13`. Targeted issue/PR searches
did not find an existing row-stride fix. #3607 is a neighboring
contiguous-input LayerNorm performance change.

### [4893498](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/4893498df8079af371257c13deebf3f4ec6ab3c5)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T23:52:16Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): cache the router entry points' calls by their own tensors (#8539)

The `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` family has
BF16-input dense and batched projection GEMMs and an FP32 router GEMM
(256 experts, BF16x3 emulation). `deterministic=True` (the default)
calls `dense_projection_det_gemm`. `deterministic=False` runs this
package's split-K and stream-K programs. Both packages ship on
`sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

This PR changes only the host path of the eager `deterministic=False`
router entry points `router_forward`, `router_dgrad` and `router_wgrad`.
Each entry point keeps its prepared launch in a cache keyed by the
call's own tensors, so a repeated call does not plan again. Programs,
plans, split counts and outputs (bitwise) do not change.

is an earlier run of the same harness on another node, without the
cuBLASLt BF16x9 arm. Control = a run with this PR in both arms on the
run 1 node, which gives the timer noise.

- **Row:** one GPU, shape, op and mode; 45 rows per GPU and mode (9
shapes x 5 ops).
- **Shapes:** FP32 router `[T, H] x [256, H]^T`, H = 4096, 5120 and
6144, T = 64, 256 and 1024 tokens; FP32 outputs.
- **Ops:** fwd = `router_forward`. dgrad = `router_dgrad` (input
gradient). wgrad = `router_wgrad` (weight gradient). bwd = dgrad +
wgrad. 2fwd+bwd = checkpointed step (2 x fwd + bwd).
- **Modes:** eager = a call sequence of the entry points (det Cake,
previous, new) or of the library calls. CUDA graph = the prepared
launches (det Cake, previous, new) or the library calls, captured once
and replayed; the entry points are not captured.
- **Latency:** median us of the CUPTI GPU interval of the op, from the
first kernel begin to the last kernel end. L2 is cold before every
iteration.
- **Runs:** a run has 15 paired groups x 20 timed steps per arm, in
rotated arm order, on the 4 GPUs of 1 node. Each GPU uses one process
layout (one long-lived process, or a new process per shape) and one
cuBLAS version (13.8.0 or 13.1.1). A Cake cell is the median of the 4
per-GPU medians.
- **Baselines:** det Cake = `deterministic=True`. Previous Cake =
`deterministic=False` at FlashInfer main 18d8a034. SOTA = per row the
fastest of cuBLAS FP32 (`cublasSgemm`), cuBLASLt FP32 (top-8 heuristic
algorithms), `torch.mm` FP32 (TF32 off), cuBLAS BF16x9 FP32 emulation
(`cublasSgemm`), cuBLASLt BF16x9 (top-8 heuristic algorithms), and the
per-GEMM fastest sequence (each GEMM uses the call that CUDA-event
timing picks). A call counts only when every GEMM it runs meets the
router accuracy budget against FP64 (relative Frobenius error at most
2e-6, and the same top-8 experts per token in fwd); every call met it on
every row. A library cell is the median of the 2 GPUs with the faster
cuBLAS version (13.8.0 or 13.1.1). The table names the call.
- **Ratio:** baseline us / new us of the cells shown. A value above
1.000 means this PR is faster.
- **Setup:** NVIDIA GB300, `sm_103a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03, 1400
W; NVIDIA GB200, `sm_100a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.126.20, 1200 W; CUDA
13.4 (driver API), nvcc 13.4.92, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. No clock or power
throttle reason was set during the runs.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Performance**
* Repeated dense projection GEMM routing calls can reuse launch
decisions, reducing repeated planning overhead.
* Cached routing decisions refresh when routing tables or applicable
routes change. Calls that cannot use a cached launch continue through
the existing path.
* Cached launches support CUDA graph replay and reuse across calls on
the same stream.
* **Documentation**
* Clarified how cached launches handle caller views, stream context, and
routing updates.

### [7b20619](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7b20619a9c26f017826109e6c7b59bc1ba0c0d27)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T23:34:00Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate): with grad, short forward up to 59 rows per SM on SM107 (#8556)

This PR raises the short forward's bound on sm_107a from 10 to 59 rows
per SM. The change applies to the non-deterministic package of Cake's
SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train` with `deterministic=False`).
On R200 with 212 SMs, forward inputs of up to T x H = 12508 rows now run
the short forward (up to 2120 rows before).

At this bound, the short forward's grid is one wave of at most 4 CTAs
per SM on all SMs but 16. That holds on GPUs with 205 or more SMs (782
<= 784 CTAs at 212 SMs, 797 <= 800 at 216). It does not hold on fewer
SMs, such as small MIG instances.

The change is host routing only: no kernel or build entry changes, and
sm_100a and sm_103a keep their bound of 12 rows per SM. The PR is one
commit on FlashInfer main after PR #8540 (merge commit
fe82a1d5ba6bf3cb13707a33829195c0fa98568b). That route, with the short
forward up to 10 rows per SM on sm_107a, is the "previous Cake" baseline
below.

The 9 shapes this PR newly routes are 303x7 to 1786x7 in the tables
(10.005 to 58.97 rows per SM). At those shapes the forward and the
checkpointed step run new code. The backward runs the same code as
before. In the pre-registered A/B (Table 2), all 36 cells whose code
changes are faster than the previous Cake route.

The table below gives speedup ranges (min-max) over those 9 shapes. A
speedup is baseline us / new us, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster:

| op | det Cake / new (Table 1) | strongest non-Cake / new (Table 1) |
previous Cake / new (Table 1) | previous Cake / new (A/B, Table 2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fwd | 1.207x-1.262x | 0.887x-0.947x | 1.207x-1.275x | 1.217x-1.280x |
| fwdg | 1.156x-1.309x | 0.872x-0.966x | 1.189x-1.324x | 1.185x-1.294x |
| ckptg | 1.117x-1.197x | 0.956x-1.062x | 1.068x-1.127x | 1.071x-1.118x
|
| stepg_f32 | - | - | - | 1.071x-1.111x |

The forward is still slower than the strongest non-Cake kernel at every
row of Table 1 (fwd and fwdg, 12 of 12 rows). The checkpointed step is
slower at 3 of 12 rows. Every cell below 1x is listed under "Cells below
1x".

The kernel's other Cake variants are the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` (the same API with
`deterministic=True`) and the FP32 weight-gradient output of the
non-deterministic package. Both packages ship on sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a, and this PR changes only the non-deterministic package's
forward route on sm_107a.

## Results on R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs)

- GPU: R200 (VR200 node; nvidia-smi name 'NVIDIA Graphics Device'),
sm_107a, compute capability 10.7, 212 SMs, driver 620.43.
- CUDA: toolkit Build cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0; PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0).
- Latency: median over 10 rounds of each round's median CUPTI kernel
time, cold L2. All times are in us.
- Base: FlashInfer main after PR #8540 (merge commit
fe82a1d5ba6bf3cb13707a33829195c0fa98568b). Previous Cake = that route
(short forward up to 10 rows per SM on sm_107a); new = up to 59. The
measured previous tree has the same package files as that commit; the
measured new tree has this PR's package files, apart from one module
docstring.
- Deterministic Cake: the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`, identical in both trees
and in this PR.
- Strongest non-Cake kernel per row: the fastest of FLA 0.6.0
rms_norm_gated, mamba_ssm v2.3.2 rmsnorm_fn, torch.compile (default
mode, best of 5 fresh compiles), torch.compile
(max-autotune-no-cudagraphs mode, best of 5 fresh compiles) and the
inductor-generated Triton kernel of the same formula launched directly
with XBLOCK=1 (Triton 3.8.0), measured in the same process.
- Operations:
  - `fwd` is one eager forward call.
  - `fwdg` is the forward replayed from a CUDA graph.
- `bwdg` is the backward replayed from a CUDA graph, and `bwdg_f32` is
the same with an FP32 dw.
- `ckptg` is the checkpointed step (2 x forward + backward) replayed
from a CUDA graph, and `stepg_f32` is the same with an FP32 dw.
- `rows / SM` is T x H divided by 212 SMs.

newly routed shapes: 1031x7 bwdg 0.993 (shift +0.667%, new slower in 9
of 16 pairs).
  - not judged slower but with new slower in all 16 pairs: none.
- over all 36 same-code cells the shifts range from -1.756% (70x32 bwdg)
to +2.367% (1786x7 bwdg): layout effects (their mean +0.027% and largest
+2.367% are within the six padding placebos' largest, +0.295% and
+7.822%).
- Second R200 board class (212 SMs; 4 process pairs on one node,
interleaved with an A/A twin, no placebo), cells whose code does not
change where new was slower in 4 of 4 pairs (ratio and shift = medians
over the 4 pairs; measured on 4 pairs only): at newly routed shapes
303x7 bwdg 0.966 (shift +3.561%), 1786x7 bwdg_f32 0.973 (shift +2.761%),
70x32 bwdg_f32 0.978 (shift +2.222%), 303x7 bwdg_f32 0.991 (shift
+0.860%); at 261x48, whose route does not change, fwdg 0.994 (shift
+0.561%), ckptg 0.998 (shift +0.153%), stepg_f32 0.998 (shift +0.152%).
Same-code shift range there -3.903% to +3.561%.

The same pre-registered per-cell test also judged slower 4 cells whose
ratio is not below 1x (median shift +0.000%), all at shapes whose route
does not change, where both arms run the same programs: 261x48 fwdg
(ratio 1.000, shift +0.000%, new slower in 6 of 16 pairs), 512x48 fwdg
(ratio 1.000, shift +0.000%, new slower in 2 of 16 pairs), 512x48 bwdg
(ratio 1.000, shift +0.000%, new slower in 3 of 16 pairs), 512x48
bwdg_f32 (ratio 1.000, shift +0.000%, new slower in 0 of 16 pairs); the
test compares new with the A/A twin of previous, not with previous
itself, so a cell can be judged slower with a median shift of 0.

### R200 with 216 SMs: supporting evidence only

- The pre-registered side-kernel test of FlashInfer issue #7548 item 1
(against an A/A twin; 10 rounds of fresh processes per group; batch 3000
us and 0) passed on R200 with 216 SMs (one board): neither the forward's
busy time beside the side kernels nor its ratio to the deterministic
forward's in the same process was worse than on the 10-rows-per-SM route
in any of the 4 groups (one-sided p >= 0.99 in all 8 tests); the placebo
calibration held and the #7548 contract check counted 0 misses for the
new route in every group (84 cells each). At 216 SMs, 303x7 and 45x48
are inside the 10-rows-per-SM band in both arms. No speedup number comes
from this test.

### [91cbe89](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/91cbe896cb98ec68da0a729014a73006e9f43c59)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T23:26:32Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): PDL-free twin of the FP8 H128 persistent program on SM100/SM103 (#8557)

`cake_dsv4` is the Cake DSv4 sparse-MLA decode and prefill backend in
FlashInfer for BF16 and FP8 KV caches. On FlashInfer main, 21 programs
serve the 197-shape list on each architecture. This PR changes how one
program runs with PDL off on SM100 (sm_100a) and SM103 (sm_103a). The
program is `fp8_h128_prefill_source_persistent`, the FP8 128-head
persistent prefill. It gained programmatic dependent launch (PDL) in
#8314. When a call leaves PDL off (`enable_pdl=False`), this PR launches
a PDL-free twin instead: `fp8_h128_prefill_source_persistent_no_pdl`.
The twin is the machine code this program ran before #8314. On SM103,
the twin runs for launches of at least 384 query rows (the total query
tokens of the call). On SM100, it runs for calls whose longest request
has at least 257 query tokens. All other calls run the same code as
main. So does every call with `enable_pdl=True`. The twin serves 3
shapes on B200 and 5 shapes on GB300, so 22 programs serve the list with
this PR. Outputs are bitwise identical to main on all 197 shapes on both
GPUs. The baseline is FlashInfer main, which ships the previous Cake
version of this program. On B200 (SM100) with CUDA 13.4, the 197 shapes
break down as 1 faster (1.001x), 2 tie, 0 slower and 194 same code. On
GB300 (SM103) with CUDA 13.4, they break down as 4 faster (1.002x to
1.006x), 1 tie, 0 slower and 192 same code.

Latencies are in microseconds. Speedup = FlashInfer main latency / this
PR latency. The 197-shape tables below were measured with PDL off
(`enable_pdl=False`). Each twin row is the median of 6 readings from 3
GPUs, in both run orders. Same-code rows carry one measurement.

Verdicts: **faster** = every counted reading shows this PR faster than
main by more than the measured run-to-run noise band, with readings in
both run orders. **tie** = the readings are not all faster (or all
slower) than main beyond the noise band. **same code** = this PR does
not change the machine code that runs this shape, so both columns carry
one measurement of that code and the row reads 1.000x.

tie, 0 slower, 194 same code)

Besides `fp8_h128_prefill_source_persistent_no_pdl`, `cake_dsv4` serves
the 197-shape list with 21 more BF16 and FP8 KV-cache decode and prefill
programs. The family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, and this PR
touches only sm_100a and sm_103a.

Co-authored-by: Avery Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [20a4c1f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/20a4c1feec94bdc84834769fde8330f6bf0fb3d1)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T23:22:34Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_tinygemm2_wgmma): sm_90a multi-wave U4 shapes routed to the two-CTA-per-SM packed programs (#8555)

`tinygemm_bf16` is a small-M bf16 GEMM (out = x @ W^T [+ bias]) with
four variants: with or without bias, each with or without programmatic
dependent launch (PDL). On sm_90a, host routing windows pick a generated
wgmma program (`cake_tinygemm2_wgmma`) for each shape. Other shapes use
the mma.sync reference `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. This PR changes only the
sm_90a host routing, for all four variants. The programs are unchanged.
PACKED_U4 and PACKED_U4_IL request 199,680 bytes of shared memory, so
only one CTA fits per SM. A launch has ceil(batch/8) * ceil(out/16)
CTAs. Above 132 CTAs, it runs in several waves on the 132-SM H100.
PACKED_S8 and PACKED_S8_IL fit two CTAs per SM. Above 132 CTAs, the new
windows send a U4 window, or a band of its output or input features, to
a PACKED_S8 or PACKED_S8_IL program. The program uses the BOX3D load
form or not, to match the shape. The window count goes from 628 to 952,
with 324 windows added. In a dense count, 1,911,859 shapes change
routing. All of them move from a U4 program to an S8 program, and all
are above 132 CTAs. A region moves only if the S8 program meets three
conditions at every shape measured there on two H100s. It is
bit-identical to `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. It is at least 3% faster than
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. It is faster than the U4 tile in every round, by at
least the larger of 0.5% and 40 ns. Regions where S8 lost keep the U4
tile. One example is a launch of exactly 264 CTAs (two full waves) with
2112 output features and large input features. None of the
representative shapes changes program. All 16 shapes, with and without
bias and PDL, keep the #8529 program. On the table GPU, their speedup vs
#8529 is 0.984x to 1.015x with PDL off and 0.984x to 1.007x with PDL on.
This is noise between identical code. No representative row was slower
in every round on any of the four GPUs. The representative rows are
1.027x to 4.287x (PDL off) and 1.018x to 4.295x (PDL on) faster than
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. Each PDL mode has 409 distinct re-routed shapes. A
few thin-margin shapes were timed more than once, and every timing
passed. On the table GPU, the re-routed shapes are 1.012x to 1.451x
faster than #8529 with PDL off and 1.012x to 1.456x with PDL on. Each
one is faster in all 7 rounds by the rule. Against `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`,
they are 1.108x to 2.167x (PDL off) and 1.111x to 2.176x (PDL on)
faster. The largest gain is 63x512x1024 with bias, PDL on. It drops from
5.280 us (`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`) and 4.799 us (#8529, PACKED_U4_IL_BOX3D)
to 3.296 us on PACKED_S8_IL_BOX3D. The smallest gain is 3x2368x20480
with bias, PDL on. It drops from 46.784 us (`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`) and
42.639 us (#8529, PACKED_U4_IL_BOX3D) to 42.128 us on PACKED_S8_BOX3D.
It is faster in all 7 rounds.

*NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (SXM, 132 SMs), sm_90a, CUDA 13.4 toolkit (nvcc
13.4.92, torch 2.14.1+cu130). Median CUPTI kernel time, cold L2, 7
interleaved rounds x 200 iterations. The arm order was rotated and
reversed between rounds. All three arms (`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`, #8529,
this PR) were measured in the same process on the same GPU. Every row on
all four GPUs is bit-identical to `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. The "#8529"
column is FlashInfer main after #8529. The `csrc/tinygemm2.cu` column is
current main. The tables come from one H100. Three more H100s were
measured the same way. On each of them, all re-routed rows (the same 409
shapes per PDL mode) were faster than #8529 in all 7 rounds by the rule.
Their speedups vs #8529 were 1.011x to 1.465x. The representative rows
were 1.018x to 4.299x faster than `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. In the "Program"
column, "(unchanged)" means the same program as #8529. "X -> Y" gives
the #8529 program and then this PR's program. The representative tables
cover PDL off and PDL on. The re-routed table lists PDL off only, in a
collapsed section. The full PDL on list does not fit in the PR body. The
PDL on ranges above cover those rows.*

### [cbb7d40](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/cbb7d4081a1adedb024a2e2d7ee4496e74ff8fbf)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T23:18:07Z
- **提交信息**: tests(cake_kda_det_kcp): rendezvous spawned ranks through a file store; skip uncovered GPUs without raising (#8516)

## 📌 Description

The multi-rank tests for the deterministic KDA KCP package sometimes
fail before any KCP code runs. They pick `MASTER_PORT` with
`_free_port()`, which binds port 0 on `127.0.0.1`, reads the port
number, and closes the socket. The spawned ranks then set `MASTER_PORT`,
and rank 0's `TCPStore` listens on that port. If another process takes
the port after the close and before the listen, the test fails with
`torch.distributed.DistNetworkError` from `TCPStore`: "The server socket
has failed to listen on any local network address ... EADDRINUSE".

This failure happens intermittently on GB300 runs, on both main and
branch trees. For example,
`tests/experimental/test_cake_kda_det_train_kcp_l2n.py::test_l2n_raw_gate_rows_match_single_rank_and_fp64[s3000-h4-w4-ragged]`
failed this way in one run and passed in another run of the same tree.

This PR has the spawned ranks meet through a file store instead of a
picked port:

- A new helper, `_rendezvous(tmp)` in
`tests/experimental/test_cake_kda_det_train_kcp_dist.py`, returns a
`file://` URL for a store path. The path is in a new directory under the
test's temporary directory.
- A new helper, `_init_group(rank, W, device, rdzv)`, joins the NCCL
group with `init_method=rdzv`.
- Every test that spawns its ranks with `torch.multiprocessing` now
passes `_rendezvous(tmp)` instead of a port. The CPU gloo test in the
l2n file that checks refusal messages also uses the file store.
- When a test runs as one process per Slurm task, `rdzv` is `None`. In
that case the group still forms from `MASTER_ADDR` / `MASTER_PORT` in
the environment, as before.
- `_free_port()` is removed from the dist and shared-workspace test
files.

The library code is unchanged. No KCP code uses the default store
directly.

The PR also fixes the skip check that the H100 lane of PR CI runs.
`_skip_unless_runnable` in the dist, l2n and raw_gate test files called
`cake_jit.device_arch()`, which raises `RuntimeError` for a device
outside sm_100a / sm_103a / sm_107a. On an H100 (sm_90) runner, seven
single-GPU nodes of the l2n and raw_gate files failed with that error
instead of skipping. The helpers now map the device capability with
`cake_jit.arch_for_capability()`, which returns `None` for such a
device, and skip. On a covered device the decision is unchanged.

### [2a79e30](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2a79e302817a94c816d3b90cabe6748e08eb8701)

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_attn_res): faster programs for more B200, B300 and GB300 shapes (#8554)

This PR changes routes of the Cake AttnRes operator,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kimi_k3_attn_res`, which is exposed as
`flashinfer.kimi_k3_attn_res.prepare_kimi_k3_attn_res` and
`kimi_k3_attn_res`. One launch does residual add, an optional snapshot
write, K+1 candidate scoring, softmax, mix and output RMSNorm. It takes
BF16 inputs with hidden size 7168 and K in [0, 8]. It has one data type,
one layout and two fused forms: dense and snapshot write. This PR
changes routes on GB300, B300 and B200. All changes apply at both PDL
modes, except two GB300 shapes that change only with PDL on. Among the
measured shapes, 19 change on GB300, 14 on B300 and 8 on B200.

- **New token-queue builds (GB300, B300, B200):** These shapes move to
token-queue (`_clc`) programs that this PR adds. A token-queue build
launches one CTA per token (grid M) and uses cluster launch control.
Each running CTA processes its own token and then the tokens of the CTAs
it cancels, so tokens are spread over the SMs dynamically instead of by
a static stride.
- On GB300 and B300 (sm_103a): primary_m8192_k4, serving_m12288_k4 and
primary_m16384_k4 move to `persistent:k4_nc5_d2_f010001000000000_clc`.

### [3f0bf6d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3f0bf6d57697eeacd374593e86b2aeeee92abb50)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T23:02:52Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_kda): with grad, raw forget-gate mode in the non-deterministic single-rank and context-parallel packages (#8550)

Cake's KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) chunked training kernels come as
deterministic and non-deterministic (ND) packages. Each has a
single-rank package and a KCP context-parallel package. The kernels have
two forget-gate modes: precomputed `g`, and raw, where the gate is
computed in-kernel from `A_log`, `dt_bias` and `lower_bound`. They also
have an in-kernel Q/K L2-norm option. Raw mode was only in the
deterministic packages. This PR adds it to the ND single-rank
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_kda_train`) and ND KCP
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_train_kcp`) packages. In raw mode,
their outputs and gradients are bitwise equal to the deterministic
packages'.

No row is slower than the deterministic packages (FlashInfer main
12943e00) in both build orders. Single-rank det/ND geomeans are 1.0055
(B200) and 1.0315 (GB200) on sm_100a, 1.0124 (B300) and 1.0396 (GB300)
on sm_103a, and 1.0054 (R200) on sm_107a. Most single-rank rows are at
parity. Faster/parity counts per GPU, in that order, are 8/43, 11/40,
8/27, 2/49 and 4/47; the other 16 B300 rows flip sign with build order.
The lowest cell is B200 P14 ckpt 0.9934, judged parity. The largest
single-rank ratios (up to 1.5074 on GB300) are on host-bound shapes
(T16k-H4, P9/P10 ckpt). There, the ND package's lighter host launch path
(cached FFI entry, launch on the current stream) cuts host issue time,
and the GPU kernels are the same. R200's ckpt gains come from this:
1.1200 (T16k-H4-d1), 1.0968 (T16k-H4-d3) and 1.0484 (P9). Without these
rows, single-rank geomeans are 1.0003 to 1.0019. KCP det/ND geomeans are
1.0146, 1.0261, 1.0166, 1.0297 and 1.0177 in the same GPU order. The
lowest KCP cell is 1.0007, and faster/parity counts are 28/8, 36/0,
36/0, 46/2 and 31/5. ND is faster than FLA on every single-rank row.
FLA/ND geomeans are 4.0263, 3.9511, 4.0394, 4.0559 and 4.7188, and the
lowest cell is 1.6090 (GB200 T16k-H4-d3 bwd).

det/ND = deterministic Cake latency / ND latency. FLA/ND = FLA
`chunk_kda` 0.6.0 latency / ND latency, run with
`use_gate_in_kernel=True`, `safe_gate=True` and `lower_bound=-5`. FLA is
the strongest non-Cake KDA implementation with an in-kernel gate. Above
1 means ND is faster. ckpt = activation-checkpointed step (2 x forward +
backward). KCP rows have no FLA baseline because no non-Cake
context-parallel KDA implementation exists.

Cake also ships the precomputed-`g` mode in all four packages and raw
mode in the two deterministic packages, with the in-kernel Q/K L2-norm
option; this family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

Workloads (bf16 q/k/v/g/beta, FP32 A_log/dt_bias, raw forget-gate mode:
the gate is computed in-kernel from A_log, dt_bias and lower_bound):

### [0ade0f4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0ade0f48b3255e81b06ac08aded784bfa4a2d3d3)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T22:55:00Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe_v3): faster TP4 EP1 and TP8 EP8 T4096 rank programs on sm_103a (#8553)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline for the 384-expert, top-6, hidden-5120 model with activation
clamp 10. A single kernel launch covers dispatch, FC1, clamped SwiGLU,
MXFP8 activation quantization, FC2 and weighted combine. The kernel has
four variants on main, and this PR updates one of them: the TP/EP rank
variant. It changes 2 of the variant's 32 programs: TP4 EP1 (384
experts) at 4096 tokens and TP8 EP8 (48 local experts) at 4096 tokens.

In both programs, every CTA now computes the prefix of the per-expert
token counts itself. Its scheduler starts as soon as that local prefix
is ready. Before, it waited for a prefix that one CTA published for all
of them.

The outputs are bitwise identical to the previous version. No host
binding changes. The catalog closure hashes of the 2 changed programs
change. The baseline is the previous Cake version on main, which is the
rank variant as last updated by #8515. For replicates a / b, the
speedups for the changed programs are:

- TP4 EP1 at 4096 tokens: 1.006x / 1.006x, saving 2.68 / 2.39 µs per
call
- TP8 EP8 at 4096 tokens: 1.007x / 1.006x, saving 1.37 / 1.10 µs per
call

Both changes are faster than the A/A noise band in both replicates. The
other 30 programs run 0.999x to 1.002x in replicate a and 0.999x to
1.002x in replicate b.

*NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, driver 580.159.03, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130. Per-call latency comes from CUDA-graph replays (20 calls
per graph), taking the median of 21 in-process rounds. The previous
version and this PR ran in separate processes, alternating over 6
rounds. Each value is the median of the 6 process medians. Speedup =
previous / this PR, computed from the latencies before rounding to two
decimals. Columns a and b are two independent replicates, each run alone
on its own node. Each replicate also timed the previous version against
itself (an A/A control) to measure its noise band. The widest band is
0.22 % in replicate a and 0.09 % in replicate b. The kernels and host
bindings of the other 30 programs are byte-identical to the previous
version, and they compile to the same machine code. Four of them read
slower than their narrow A/A band in both replicates: TP4 EP1 at 16
tokens (+0.015 / +0.012 µs), TP4 EP4 at 16 tokens (+0.063 / +0.023 µs),
TP4 EP4 at 128 tokens (+0.032 / +0.016 µs) and TP8 EP8 at 1024 tokens
(+0.090 / +0.028 µs). Their kernels and bindings are unchanged, so this
is process-level noise, not a regression.*

The other three variants (single-rank routed-FP4, single-rank routed-FP8
and grouped-GEMM routes) ship on sm_100a and sm_103a; the rank variant
ships on sm_103a only.

### [93b865b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/93b865bc12628d22e2c905c2f74386e888f06c54)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T22:33:20Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): per-warp TMA final-state store and lower host launch cost in BF16 KDA prefill (#8544)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has 85 modules: 51 with
BF16 inputs and 34 with TF32 inputs. They come in fused and split forms.
This PR changes only the prepared BF16-input path with FP32 state
(`flashinfer.prepare_bf16_kda_prefill`). It makes three changes. First,
the runtime spends less host time on each launch. It re-points aliased
launch arguments with one view. It hands a moved tensor to the launch
once when that tensor fills adjacent argument positions. A fresh binding
launches with the bound torch tensors. Together these save about 9 to 12
us of host time per serving call. Second, on sm_103a, the two binned
turnover programs of the direct route now store the final FP32 state
with a per-warp TMA store. This covers the form with the bin mix and the
form without it. The runtime binds the final-state tensor map for the
programs that take it. This change targets 12 and 16 heads with no gate
lower bound, at BS64 x T64, BS16 x T128 and BS16 x T256. Third, the
binned program for bounded gates with chunk size 16 and TMA checkpoints
gets the same per-warp TMA final-state store, on both arches. It targets
12 heads with gate lower bound -5, at BS16 x T64 and BS64 x T64. The PR
also re-renders 63 other prefill programs with the current generator.
Their SASS is identical. Outputs are bit-identical. The tables compare
this PR with the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main. They report
median latency per call in microseconds, with a cold L2. Each table has
56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower bound or -5, and 14
sequence-length shapes. TIE means no difference beyond the measurement
band. The first table covers repeated calls on the same buffers, which
use the plan-cache fast path. There, B200 has 2 faster rows and 54 TIE,
from 0.99x to 1.03x. The 0.99x row is a TIE. GB300 has 8 faster rows and
48 TIE, from 1.00x to 1.05x. The second table covers the serving
pattern, where every call rebinds the cached plan to new buffers. There,
B200 has 2 faster rows and 54 TIE, from 0.99x to 1.03x. The 0.99x rows
are TIE. GB300 has 7 faster rows and 48 TIE, from 1.00x to 1.05x, over
55 counted rows. One more GB300 serving row is marked † and not counted:
16 heads, gate lower bound -5, 2x(8128+64). In that row, the timing of
both sides drifted beyond the measurement guard within one run, which
also happens when FlashInfer main is timed against itself. The largest
gains come from the final-state store on GB300 at BS64 x T64 with no
gate lower bound. With 12 heads, latency drops from 54.53 to 51.74 us
(1.05x) on the fast path and from 54.72 to 52.13 us (1.05x) in serving.
With 16 heads, it drops from 65.12 to 62.56 us (1.04x) on the fast path
and from 65.28 to 62.69 us (1.04x) in serving. The other four GB300 rows
of this change gain 1.01x on the fast path. In serving they show 1.01x
to 1.02x, and the 12-head BS16 x T256 row is a TIE. The chunk-16 change
helps most at 12 heads, gate lower bound -5, BS64 x T64. On the fast
path, latency drops from 67.68 to 65.76 us (1.03x) on B200 and from
63.42 to 61.70 us (1.03x) on GB300. In serving, it drops from 68.35 to
66.40 us (1.03x) and from 63.20 to 61.54 us (1.03x). At BS16 x T64 on
the fast path, it drops from 27.62 to 27.20 us (1.02x) on B200 and from
25.79 to 25.34 us (1.02x) on GB300. In serving, it drops from 27.78 to
27.46 us (1.01x) and from 25.73 to 25.44 us (1.01x).

B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. GB300: NVIDIA
GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.167.08. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.

run, also when FI main is timed against itself)

The other Cake variants keep their programs: the TF32-input modules, the
BF16-state forms and the other fused and split launches. The family
ships on sm_100a and sm_103a. The final-state store in the direct-route
turnover programs is built only for sm_103a, so B200 keeps those
programs and their rows are TIE there. The chunk-16 program change and
the host changes apply to both arches.

### [fc0a3c1](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/fc0a3c1f3ca68f123283fa8d709b454eded15359)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T22:27:47Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): sm_103a router weight-gradient head/tail windows at hidden 4096 and 6144 (#8518)

The `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` family has three
kinds of GEMM: BF16-input dense projection GEMMs, BF16-input batched
projection GEMMs, and an FP32 router GEMM (256 experts, BF16x3
emulation). Each kind has forward, input-gradient and weight-gradient
programs. `deterministic=True` (the default) calls
`dense_projection_det_gemm`. `deterministic=False` runs this package's
split-K / stream-K programs. This PR changes one variant: the router
weight gradient (FP32 out) on 152-SM `sm_103a` parts (GB300). It runs
the head/tail program of #8444
(`router_fp32_gemm_ts_r6p6_atomic_nn_t_ht_c2_nreg`) in two more token
windows: hidden 4096 at 20480 to 49152 tokens (`"H1x4p44"`) and hidden
6144 at 16172 to 20480 tokens (`"H1x5p44"`). 148-SM `sm_103a` parts
(B300) keep the deterministic program in every router row, as on main.
On every row of the table below, FlashInfer main runs the deterministic
program, so previous Cake is det Cake.

The weight gradient gives det/new 1.040-1.116 in eager and 1.057-1.122
in graph, and SOTA/new 1.532-1.558 and 1.530-1.624. bwd gives det/new
1.028-1.057 (eager) and 1.028-1.055 (graph), and SOTA/new 1.288-1.316
and 1.310-1.353. 2fwd+bwd gives det/new 1.008-1.026 (eager) and
1.007-1.027 (graph), and SOTA/new 1.481-1.561 and 1.503-1.587. At hidden
6144 and T 20480, the 2fwd+bwd det/new is 1.007-1.008: inside the eager
A/A band (up to 1.008) and just above the graph A/A band (up to 1.005).
That row is counted as parity, not as a gain. An earlier measurement
with another timer (4 runs on 2 GB300 parts) found the hidden 4096, T
49152 graph 2fwd+bwd 0.1-0.7 % slower than det Cake in paired runs; here
its det/new is 1.016.

- **Rows:** FP32 router GEMM, 256 experts, on GB300: hidden 4096 at T
20480, 24576, 32768 and 49152, and hidden 6144 at T 16172, 16231, 16384
and 20480. Ops are wgrad (router weight gradient, the changed op), bwd
(input gradient + weight gradient) and 2fwd+bwd (checkpointed step: 2 x
forward + bwd). Modes are eager (calls of the prepared launches) and
graph (CUDA graph replays).
- **Latency:** median us of the op's GPU span from CUPTI activity
records (`flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time`). The span runs from the
first kernel begin to the last kernel end of every launch of the op,
including the BF16x3 split and memset launches. L2 is flushed before
every iteration. Per row, op and mode, every arm runs 9 paired groups x
20 timed iterations (3 untimed iterations before them), in an arm order
that rotates per group and reverses every other group. A run's cell is
the median of its group medians. The table gives the median of 3 runs,
one per GPU of one GB300 node, run at the same time (the fourth GPU ran
the cuBLAS 13.1.1 check below).
- **Baselines:** det Cake = `deterministic=True`
(`dense_projection_det_gemm`). SOTA = per row, op and mode, the fastest
of four cuBLAS 13.8.0 arms that meets the router's FP32 budget on every
GEMM of the op: a relative Frobenius error <= 2e-6 against FP64 of the
same operands, a finite output, and for the forward the FP64 top-8
experts in every row. The arms are `cublas` (`torch.mm`, FP32, TF32
off), `cublaslt` (the fastest of cuBLASLt's top 8 FP32 algorithms that
meets the budget), `bf16x9` (`cublasSgemm` in
`CUBLAS_FP32_EMULATED_BF16X9_MATH`) and `cublaslt_bf16x9` (the same
top-8 sweep in `CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_EMULATED_16BFX9`): the router SOTA
rule of `benchmarks/bench_cake_dense_projection_gemm.py`. The table
names the arm that won. The two BF16x9 arms are within 1.5 % of each
other (the winner takes x0.986-1.000 of the `bf16x9` time). Where they
meet the budget, the plain FP32 arms take 2.46-2.92x the SOTA time; the
`cublas` weight gradient misses the budget at hidden 4096. At hidden
6144 and T 20480, no library forward meets the top-8 check (`bf16x9`
differs in 1 of 20480 rows), so the 2fwd+bwd rows there have no SOTA.
With torch's bundled cuBLAS 13.1.1 (one run), the SOTA took x0.991-1.022
of these times.
- **Noise:** an A/A arm (det Cake in a second prepared launch, timed in
the same groups) gave per-run median det_aa/det ratios of 0.997-1.005
(eager) and 0.997-1.004 (graph) for wgrad, 0.997-1.003 and 0.997-1.002
for bwd, and 0.996-1.008 and 0.992-1.005 for 2fwd+bwd, over all rows and
runs. Between the 3 runs (3 GPUs), a cell differed from the median of
the runs by up to 2.1 % below and 4.2 % above for the new wgrad, and by
up to 1.5 % for det Cake.
- **Setup:** NVIDIA GB300, `sm_103a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03; CUDA
13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. The median SM clock was 2070
MHz (the maximum) in every run; the software power cap
(`clocks_event_reasons` 0x4) was active in 15-25 of about 400 samples
per run (500 ms apart), at a power of at most 1285 W of 1400 W. A ratio
is the quotient of the two us columns. A ratio above 1.00 means this PR
is faster.
- **Accuracy:** the new partitions' relative Frobenius error against
FP64 is at most 3.2e-7 on every row (3 seeds or more per row and part,
each with 3 input sets x 10 reruns), within the 2e-6 budget.

forward and input gradient, and the router weight gradient on `sm_100a`,

programs, and the family ships on `sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Performance**
* Updated router weight-gradient processing on `sm_103a` GPUs to use
measured plans for hidden sizes 4096 and 6144 within their supported
token ranges. Benchmark results and measurement notes are documented.
* **Tests**
* Added coverage for both routing ranges, their boundary conditions,
out-of-range behavior, and GPU execution. Updated deterministic-path
expectations for cases without a routing verdict.

### [2acdf24](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2acdf249b2b395de0a4bdff5e43a095ba86dba39)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T22:14:32Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_msa_icp_indexer): fused prefill scoring with local Top-16 lists for TP2/TP4 x P128/P256 (#8502)

Part of #8170.

The CAKE MSA ICP indexer
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake_msa_icp_indexer`) scores the
sparse-attention index for MiniMax-M3 (MSA) with indexer context
parallelism. Its prefill path now has two variants, each for four
layouts (page size 128 or 256 at TP2 or TP4): the materialized variant,
which writes the FP32 score matrix and then selects the Top-16 per rank,
and the fused variant added by this PR. The fused variant keeps the
local Top-16 lists in registers and builds the cross-rank exchange
carrier directly, so it does not write the score matrix; windows of at
most 512 query tokens (page 128) or 1024 (page 256; 512 on sm_100a at
TP4 page 256) keep the materialized score and select. Candidate ids and
scores are byte-identical to the materialized variant. The tables
compare against "previous", the materialized prefill variant shipped
before this PR; the full-model table also compares against running with
indexer context parallelism off ("CP off").

Full MiniMax-M3 (NVFP4) step time in vLLM on GB300 (sm_103a), 4 GPUs per
node, CUDA 13.4 build with PyTorch 2.14 (cu130). Prefill = an 8192- or
4096-token prefill chunk; mixed = that chunk plus a 14-request decode
cohort; speedup = baseline ms / this PR ms (>1 is faster).

### [e32cf76](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e32cf76ebb41636f4556d9675949e8a107891da5)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T22:11:53Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mok_bf16): vectorized shared-memory MXFP8 dispatch quantize in the sm_107a backward (#7821) (#8546)

`cake_mok_bf16` is FlashInfer's MoK mixture-of-experts training kernel
family. It covers forward, full-forward checkpoint recompute (replay)
and backward, and has four variants: BF16 or MXFP8 routed experts, each
with plain or clamped SwiGLU. This PR speeds up the MXFP8 backward
kernel on sm_107a (for #7821). The change covers plain and clamped
SwiGLU, each with bf16 or FP32 weight-gradient outputs, which are the
four rendered sm_107a backward MXFP8 kernels. It applies to the backward
kernel the same vectorized shared-memory MXFP8 dispatch quantize that
#8506 applied to the forward. The backward kernel's communication CTAs
quantize each dispatched 128x128 BF16 token tile to MXFP8 twice, once
row-major and once transposed. Two of its four dispatch streams first
scale each token row by its routing weight. All four streams now read
shared memory in 128-bit chunks and write the MXFP8 words with 64-bit
and 128-bit vector stores, in a per-lane order whose accesses hit
distinct shared-memory banks. The weighted streams apply the same
per-token weights with the same arithmetic as before. Outputs are
bitwise identical to before. The forward and full-forward replay code is
unchanged.

**Kernel phases** (ms, before → after, speedup)

| Workload | Forward | Full-forward replay | Backward |
|---|---|---|---|
| T=27116, uniform routing | 3.898 → 3.887 (1.003x) | 3.876 → 3.866
(1.003x) | 6.844 → 6.821 (1.003x) |
| T=32768, uniform routing | 5.174 → 5.169 (1.001x) | 5.158 → 5.153
(1.001x) | 8.748 → 8.702 (1.005x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 1.25x | 6.203 → 6.202 (1.000x) | 6.188 →
6.190 (1.000x) | 10.758 → 10.699 (1.006x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 2x | 11.067 → 11.098 (0.997x) | 10.996 →
11.041 (0.996x) | 22.766 → 22.492 (1.012x) |

**End to end** (ms, before → after, speedup)

| Workload | MoE microbatch | Training update, 5 layers |
|---|---|---|
| T=27116, uniform routing | 15.959 → 15.914 (1.003x) | 157.692 →
157.503 (1.001x) |
| T=32768, uniform routing | 20.420 → 20.367 (1.003x) | 200.403 →
199.991 (1.002x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 1.25x | 24.475 → 24.408 (1.003x) | 239.767
→ 239.544 (1.001x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 2x | 46.161 → 45.983 (1.004x) | 460.762 →
458.502 (1.005x) |

*8 NVIDIA VR NVL72 GPUs (sm_107a, 212 SMs, two 4-GPU trays in one NVLink
domain), driver 620.62, CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. EP8, H=4096,
I=2048, 288 experts, top-8, one shared expert, clamped SwiGLU (limit
10), FP32 weight gradients, MXFP8 routed experts, macrobatch 262144. The
training update runs 5 layers with 2 microbatches each. Before is
FlashInfer main before this PR, which already includes #8506. Times are
in ms and are means of two runs per side, in rotated order on the same
nodes (before, after, after, before). Forward and replay use identical
code on both sides, so their differences (up to 0.4%) are run-to-run
noise. Peak memory is unchanged (19.141 / 19.464 / 19.141 / 19.145 GiB
per rank for the four rows). Outputs, input gradients and weight
gradients are bitwise identical to before.*

The family also ships the BF16 routed-expert variants and the MXFP8
forward and recompute kernels, and every variant runs on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [e50837d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e50837d8fa63647acb638e8604ad941781e529af)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T21:57:03Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn): route sm_107a FP32 T=1 nontranspose decode B 21-31 to the TMA-state body (up to 1.17x) (#8547)

`gated_delta_rule_decode(backend="cake_gdn")` runs the Cake GDN decode.
The family covers FP32 and BF16 state, pretranspose and nontranspose
state layouts, and T=1 decode as well as multi-token verify and update
forms. On sm_107a, its bodies include hqsplit, tile and mid4 bodies.
This PR changes the routing of one variant: sm_107a, FP32 state, T=1,
nontranspose decode, H16/HV32, at scales K^-0.5 and 1.0. It adds no new
kernels. For batch sizes 21 <= B < 32, this variant ran the mid4 body.
It now runs the existing TMA-state hqsplit body, which already serves B
>= 32. One row is an exception: B=28 at scale 1.0 keeps the mid4 body,
because the TMA-state body was not faster for that row. Other head
geometries in this band, such as H4/HV8, keep the mid4 body. Batch sizes
B < 21 do not change. Outputs and updated state are bitwise identical to
the previous routes on every measured row. The baseline is the previous
Cake version on FlashInfer main. Against it, the 24 changed rows show a
geomean speedup of 1.084x, from 1.002x to 1.166x per row. This PR is
also faster than the non-Cake `backend="flashinfer"` kernel on every
changed row, with a geomean of 1.475x and a minimum of 1.352x.

GPU: NVIDIA R200 (216 SMs), sm_107a, driver 615.71.10, CUDA 13.4. The
table has 25 rows: 24 changed rows and 1 unchanged row. Times are CUPTI
kernel times with a cold L2. Each arm reports its median time. Each
value is the geomean of 4 runs on one board, with seeds 17 and 29 and 2
rounds each. Previous Cake and this PR ran interleaved. Previous Cake is
the routes that FlashInfer main ships today. The row marked "unchanged"
keeps the FlashInfer main kernel in this PR. speedup = previous Cake /
this PR, so a value above 1 means this PR is faster. Outputs and state
are bitwise identical on every row.

### [25cdfe1](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/25cdfe1aafa07760dc9c6bbad69b93c40511bca1)

- **作者**: Thien Tran
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T21:52:34Z
- **提交信息**: fix(gemm): give each CUDA stream its own GEMM workspace (#8221)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

GEMM workspaces come from `_get_cache_buf`, one buffer per device, so
GEMMs running concurrently on two streams share it. Kernels that write
it (cuBLASLt/cuDNN split-K plans, CUTLASS stream-K on SM120, BF16×FP4
split-K partials, grouped-GEMM argument arrays) then corrupt each
other's results.

Changes:
- GEMM workspaces use the existing `_get_stream_cache_buf` (keyed by the
current stream, as top-k already does for #3618).
- `_get_stream_cache_buf` allocates from a FlashInfer-private `MemPool`
per device. Otherwise a stream's first buffer can land in a private pool
active at the time, e.g. the one torch.compile cudagraph trees warm up
in, which rejects untracked long-lived allocations.
- `mm_fp8` (`cutedsl_low_latency`) passes a fixed-length workspace slice
so the tuner cache key does not depend on the buffer's growth.
- Drop a per-device workspace dict in the SM120 SVDQuant runner.

Two `bmm_fp8` GEMMs overlapped on main and aux streams in one CUDA graph
(K=8192, N=9216/4608/2304 and 64/32/16, 16 layers, 200 replays), GB300,
outputs differing bitwise from serial (of 6400):

| tactic | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `cublas` | up to 3061 | 0 |
| `cudnn` | up to 262 | 0 |
| `auto` | up to 503 | 0 |

`group_gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise` on two streams: 894/960 outputs wrong on
main, 0/960 with this PR. A FlashInfer GEMM or top-k inside a custom op
under `torch.compile(mode="reduce-overhead")` works (it fails without
the private pool).

## 🔍 Related Issues

Same class as #3618 and #6218.

the same change; left for follow-ups.

## 📌 Description

Removes the four CuTe-DSL quantize kernel entry points from the public
FlashInfer API: `nvfp4_quantize_cute_dsl`,
`nvfp4_quantize_per_token_cute_dsl`, `mxfp4_quantize_cute_dsl` and
`mxfp8_quantize_cute_dsl`. Users should call the general APIs with
`backend="cute-dsl"` (`fp4_quantize`, `nvfp4_quantize`,
`mxfp4_quantize`, `mxfp8_quantize`), which already dispatch to these
kernels.

- The four functions are no longer decorated with `@flashinfer_api`, and
the "CuTe-DSL Quantization Kernels (experimental)" section is removed
from `docs/api/quantization.rst`.
- They stay importable from the same paths and remain supported, with no
runtime warning.
- The general APIs call these functions, so every `backend="cute-dsl"`
call was logged twice under `FLASHINFER_LOGLEVEL` (for example
`mxfp8_quantize` and `mxfp8_quantize_cute_dsl`, with identical call
counts in serving logs). Each call is now logged once, under the API the
caller used.
- The section labelled these functions experimental. Experimental APIs
belong in `flashinfer/experimental/`, and these are backend entry points
of stable APIs.

### [da2d143](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/da2d143ce775d11d8a67d1e63b4c84f6f0c653ca)

- **作者**: Sam Mausberg
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T21:37:10Z
- **提交信息**: perf(sampling): split rows across thread block clusters in rejection samplers on SM90 (#5617)

## Description

`top_p_sampling_from_probs`, `top_k_sampling_from_probs` and
`top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs(..., filter_apply_order="joint")` run
one 1024-thread CTA per row. Each rejection round scans the row in
4096-element tiles until the CDF passes the uniform draw and then reads
the whole row again to sum the mass above the two pivots, so a round
costs up to two row reads by a single SM. At decode batch sizes most of
the GPU sits idle. On GH200 with a 151936-entry vocabulary, batch 1
takes 34.6 us for top-p and 46.3 us for top-k on peaked probabilities,
and 203 us for top-k on a flat distribution, which needs more rounds.

On SM90 this PR adds a split-row variant of these three samplers. Each
row is divided across a thread block cluster of 2 to 8 CTAs with 256
threads each. Every CTA copies its chunk of the row into shared memory
once (with `cp.async` when the vocabulary is a multiple of 4, scalar
loads otherwise), and the row is not read from global memory again. A
rejection round is then one pass over the shared-memory chunk that
computes the mass (and, for top-k, the count) above both pivots, with
per-warp partial sums written into every CTA of the cluster through
distributed shared memory, followed by an inverse-CDF search that only
the CTA holding the u-quantile performs (rank, then warp, then thread,
then element prefix sums, all in index order). Two cluster barriers per
round replace up to two row reads per round.

The algorithm is the one the single-CTA kernels use: the same Philox
subsequence and number of draws, the same pivots and accept/reject
rules, and the same parameter indexing per mode, including `indices` and
per-request `top_k`/`top_p` tensors. Only the floating-point summation
order differs, so a draw can land on the neighboring token when u falls
within rounding distance of a CDF boundary. Comparing this branch with
its base commit over 189,540 draws (vocab 8192 to 262144, batch 1 to
150, logits `randn * 1` and `randn * 5`, all three modes, per-row
thresholds and `indices`), 438 draws (0.23%) differed; all but 3 were on
the flat `randn * 1` rows, where one token's CDF step near the top of
the range is only tens of float32 ulps wide. In a single-round setting
(top-k with k above the vocabulary size, 28,200 draws), each of the 106
differing draws was the adjacent token. For scale, the base kernel's
`deterministic=True` and `deterministic=False` variants, which differ
only in the scan inside a 4096-element tile, disagreed on 9 of the same
189,540 draws.

All reductions in the split-row kernel use a fixed order, so it is
deterministic whether or not `deterministic=True` is passed; for the
shapes it handles, `deterministic=False` no longer selects a different
kernel. That flag did not buy speed on the single-CTA path at the shapes
I checked (vocab 151936: top-k batch 1 45.3 us vs 46.3 us with
`deterministic=True`, joint batch 8 70.9 us vs 72.3 us).

`GetSplitRowSamplingClusterSize` picks the smallest power-of-two cluster
that keeps each chunk at or below 26624 floats, so that two CTAs fit on
an SM (vocabularies above 212992 get 8 CTAs with one resident per SM),
and doubles it (up to 8) while the grid fills less than half of the SMs
and chunks stay at 4096 floats or more. The single-CTA kernels are kept
in these cases:

- Rows shorter than 8192 entries, and rows whose 8-way chunks do not fit
in shared memory (above roughly 460K entries on GH200).
- Large grids that need 8-CTA clusters, where the single-CTA kernels
catch up: vocabularies above 212992 at 24 or more CTAs per SM (batch 396
or more on 132 SMs), and vocabularies above 131072 at 64 or more CTAs
per SM (batch 1056 or more); top-p leaves earlier, at 16 and 32 CTAs per
SM (batch 264 and 528). Measured crossovers at vocab 262144 were between
batch 384 (top-p 1.03x, top-k 1.12x) and 448 (top-p 0.97x), and at vocab
151936 between batch 1024 (top-p 1.02x) and 1536 (top-p 0.98x). Clusters
of 2 and 4 CTAs were at least even at every batch size I measured, up to
8192 (for example top-p at vocab 50257 and batch 8192: 2383 us before,
1220 us after).
- GPUs other than SM90, and builds where the kernel was not compiled for
SM90. SM100 and newer also support clusters, but I could not measure
them, so they keep the existing kernels.

`min_p_sampling_from_probs`, `sampling_from_probs`,
`sampling_from_logits` and the renorm kernels are not changed. The
default `filter_apply_order="top_k_first"` reaches the new kernel
through `top_p_sampling_from_probs` when its top-k fast path does not
apply (per-request `top_k` tensor, `indices`, k above 256, or vocabulary
below 65536), and the logits entry points reach it after their softmax.

### Performance

NVIDIA GH200 480GB (sm_90a, 132 SMs), CUDA 12.8, driver 570, torch
2.11.0+cu128. Each value is the per-call time from a CUDA graph of 20
calls with distinct Philox offsets, replayed 15 times (median replay
divided by 20), with the inputs resident in L2 as they are after the LM
head. Probabilities are `softmax(randn(B, V) * 5)` with
`torch.manual_seed(0)`; in a sample of 24 such rows at vocab 32000 to
262144, the top-1 probability ranged from 0.12 to 0.71 and a top-p 0.9
nucleus held 4 to 205 tokens. `top_k` and `top_p` are per-row tensors of
50 and 0.9, and `deterministic` is left at its default (`True`). Before
is the base commit 8589d49b (the sampling code is the same on current
main) and after is this branch, measured in separate processes in two
interleaved rounds (base first, then branch first); the table shows the
median of the two, and no cell moved by more than 1.4% between rounds.

The gain is largest at batch 1 to 32, where the old kernel leaves most
SMs idle, and shrinks as the grid fills the GPU; the smallest gain on
the new path is 1.02x (top-p, vocab 151936, batch 1024). Vocabulary
50257 gains more than its size suggests because an odd row length forces
the single-CTA kernel onto scalar loads in every pass, while the
split-row kernel pays for scalar loads once.

Flat distributions need more rejection rounds, and the gain grows with
the round count. Same setup with `softmax(randn(B, V))`, where a top-p
0.9 nucleus holds about 61% of the vocabulary:

To reproduce the tables, run this script on each revision, for example
`python bench.py 151936:1:5:top_p 151936:8:5:joint` (arguments
`vocab:batch:logit_std:mode`); on the shapes I rechecked it gives the
table values to within 0.1 us.

<details>
<summary>bench.py</summary>

```python
import statistics
import sys

import torch

import flashinfer

# usage: python bench.py vocab:batch:std:mode ...   (mode = top_p | top_k | joint)
for case in sys.argv[1:]:
    v, b, std, mode = case.split(":")
    v, b, std = int(v), int(b), float(std)
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    probs = torch.softmax(torch.randn(b, v, device="cuda") * std, dim=-1)
    k = torch.full((b,), 50, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    p = torch.full((b,), 0.9, device="cuda")
    fn = {
        "top_p": lambda o: flashinfer.sampling.top_p_sampling_from_probs(
            probs, p, seed=1, offset=o
        ),
        "top_k": lambda o: flashinfer.sampling.top_k_sampling_from_probs(
            probs, k, seed=1, offset=o
        ),
        "joint": lambda o: flashinfer.sampling.top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs(
            probs, k, p, filter_apply_order="joint", seed=1, offset=o
        ),
    }[mode]
    s = torch.cuda.Stream()
    s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
    with torch.cuda.stream(s):
        for i in range(3):
            fn(i)
    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s)
    g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(g):
        for i in range(20):  # 20 calls with distinct Philox offsets
            fn(i * 64)
    g.replay()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    times = []
    for _ in range(15):
        start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        start.record()
        g.replay()
        end.record()
        end.synchronize()
        times.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / 20)
    print(f"{v},{b},{std},{mode},{statistics.median(times):.1f} us")
```

</details>

The existing benchmark routines show the same trend. They use cold L2,
uniform random probabilities (a flat distribution), scalar `top_k=50`
and `top_p=0.9`, and a fixed seed and offset, and they print
milliseconds with three decimals:

```bash
for r in top_p_sampling_from_probs top_k_sampling_from_probs top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs; do
  for vb in "151936 1" "151936 32" "151936 512" "262144 8"; do
    set -- $vb
    python benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine $r --filter_apply_order joint \
      --batch_size $2 --vocab_size $1 --top_k 50 --top_p 0.9
  done
done
```

## Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

On the GH200 (sm_90a), JIT build for 9.0a:

- `pytest tests/utils/test_sampling.py -k "sampling and not softmax and
not blackwell and not renorm and not mask and not chain and not
speculative and not freq"`: 399 passed, 9 skipped.
- `pytest tests/utils/test_sampling.py -k "freq and not softmax and not
logits"`: 87 passed, 3 skipped. This includes the new frequency test and
the existing 5,000,000-draw frequency tests, which at vocab 32000 and
128256 take the new path with clusters of 2 and 8.

Two tests are added. `test_split_row_rejection_sampling` checks every
sample against the top-k/top-p masks for shapes that use clusters of 2,
4 and 8, an odd vocabulary (50257, scalar staging), per-row
`top_k`/`top_p`, `k = 1`, a row whose first half has zero probability,
`indices`, and repeatability for a fixed seed and offset.
`test_split_row_rejection_sampling_freq` puts the probability mass on a
sparse set that covers both sides of every chunk and warp-segment
boundary for clusters of 2, 4 and 8, draws 51,200 samples per case at
decode batch sizes, and requires every token frequency to be within 6
standard deviations of the renormalized probability. To check that the
frequency test detects a subtle error, I removed the warp-level prefix
subtraction from the kernel; all 9 frequency cases failed while the
mask-based test still passed.

`compute-sanitizer` (2025.1) `memcheck`, `racecheck` and `synccheck`
report no errors or hazards on the split-row kernel for vocab 8192,
32000, 50257, 151936 and 262144 in all three modes, including an
all-zero row. Only sm_90a was tested.

## Reviewer Notes

- The split-row kernel ignores `deterministic=False`, because its
reductions are already fixed-order. The Description gives the old path's
timing with that flag.
- `top_k_sampling_from_probs` reads `top_k_arr` by output index and the
joint sampler by row index, as the existing kernels do. Open PRs #5340
and #5324 change that indexing in the single-CTA kernels; whichever
lands second needs the same change in
`SplitRowRejectionSamplingFromProbKernel`. #5352 changes
`DeviceSamplingFromProb` in the single-CTA kernels, which the new kernel
does not use; it still applies to the shapes that keep the single-CTA
path, and the "before" numbers here do not include it.
- The launch path adds three `cudaDeviceGetAttribute` queries and a
`cudaFuncGetAttributes` call per launch, in the style of the existing
launchers. In eager mode at batch 1 (vocab 151936, top-p) a call went
from 29.9 us to 14.4 us of wall time, which is host-bound after this
change.
- The tuning constants (26624-float target chunk, 4096-float minimum
chunk, the two large-grid cutoffs) come from GH200 measurements and are
expressed per SM count; other SM90 parts (H100 PCIe, H20) were not
measured.

### [3346d95](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3346d959557d4761b2821bfcdb5ac8eceb0795cf)

- **作者**: wuyaole

- **提交信息**: fix(quantization): reject unsupported FP4 quantization targets (#7987)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Reject unsupported CUDA targets before FP4 quantization enters its
backend or JIT loader. The CUDA kernels have no useful implementation
below SM100, so the public entry points should fail clearly instead of
leaving output untouched.

This covers `fp4_quantize`, NVFP4 global/per-token quantization and
MXFP4 for the CUDA and CuTe-DSL backends. Each wrapper checks the device
its existing branch actually uses: NVFP4 and CUDA MXFP4 transfer to the
current CUDA device; CuTe-DSL MXFP4 consumes the input device.
Quantization kernels, transfers and dequantization stay unchanged.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Addresses the FP4 Python API portion of #7980 and complements #7986,
which handles CUDA MXFP8. This PR does not change MXFP8 or depend on
that PR. Native binding launch-status checks remain separate.

### [0a3a715](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0a3a715d11596d7e3b10a444ed5a210eec8522c8)

- **作者**: cherry77-cloud
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T21:34:51Z
- **提交信息**: fix(sampling): align indexed top-k and speculative metrics (#8002)

## 📌 Description

This PR fixes two independent sampling inconsistencies.

### Keep `top_k_first` semantics stable when `indices` is provided

The large-vocabulary fast path uses radix top-k and retains exactly `k`
entries. It previously rejected every call with `indices`, so adding
even an identity mapping routed the same probabilities through
`top_k_renorm_probs` instead. That fallback retains every entry equal to
the k-th threshold.

Consequently, a boundary tie could change the sampling distribution
solely because `indices` was present. For example, with `V=65536`,
`k=1`, `top_p=1`, and probabilities `[3/8, 3/8, 1/4, 0, ...]`, the fast
path selects one of the two maximum entries while the indexed fallback
renormalizes both to `[1/2, 1/2]`.

The fix allows valid same-device int32/int64 index vectors to use the
existing fast path. Top-k is still computed once for each unique source
row; `indices` is passed through the compact top-p sampling step, and
sampled compact indices are mapped back through the corresponding source
row. Per-row `top_k`/`top_p` validation and the returned index dtype are
preserved. This keeps exact-k tie behavior independent of an otherwise
identity-preserving row mapping without expanding full-vocabulary or
compact rows.

### Do not count the first speculative rejection twice

`chain_speculative_sampling` first samples the accepted prefix and
records the first rejected position in `pos`. Its independent
acceptance-metric loop then started from `pos` and sampled that already
rejected token again. For one draft token with true acceptance
probability `alpha=0.5`, the reported expectation became `alpha +
(1-alpha)alpha = 0.75` instead of `0.5`.

The metric loop now excludes `pos` from the count. It deliberately still
consumes the same random draw at that position, preserving the RNG state
used by the subsequent correction sample and therefore preserving
fixed-seed generated tokens.

### Compatibility and performance notes

- For indexed calls with vocabulary size ≥ 65536 and `k ≤ 256`, a fixed
seed/offset now yields different tokens than before because the call
takes the exact-k fast path; the sampling distribution is unchanged.
- `output_accepted_token_num` will read lower for callers comparing
acceptance rates across versions because the previous value
double-counted some first rejections. Generated output tokens are
unchanged by this metric fix.
- On SM100 with `V=128256` and `k=50`, using 2-D advanced indexing for
non-indexed calls regressed logits from 0.151 to 0.169 ms through 128
rows and from 0.160 to 0.171 ms at 256 rows; probs regressed from 0.170
to 0.187 ms. The final revision keeps the original single-`gather`
mapping when `indices` is absent and uses 2-D indexing only for indexed
calls, restoring non-indexed timings to within 0.006 ms of the previous
fast path. Indexed calls pass `indices` through the compact sampler
without expanding compact rows. Measurements are from SM100 and have not
been repeated on B200.

### [61bc8b6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/61bc8b6dd7049a44d614b2a0cd4a036cb3c46ad0)

- **作者**: S.J. Lee
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T20:44:51Z
- **提交信息**: perf(qsa): speed up BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 on SM80-SM90 (#8423)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Switch NVFP4 `backend="auto"` to the existing `default` QSA kernel on
compute capabilities 8.x and 9.0, joining FP8 and BF16. Other
architectures keep their current routing, and explicit `backend="cake"`
remains available.

This also reduces host overhead, improves NVFP4 decoding and launch
order, and speeds up split merging. Outside the package, only
`_qsa_auto_backend` and the `backend` docstring in
`flashinfer/sparse.py` change; the signature doesn't. NVFP4 outputs can
differ from main in the last bit, since the merge sums the splits in a
different order.

## Performance

Speedup over Cake (higher is better):

| Architecture | Measurement | Geometric mean | Per-shape range |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| sm_80 | GPU events, memset L2 flush | 1.046x | 1.001–1.176x |
| sm_80 | GPU events, read L2 flush | 1.054x | 1.000–1.230x |
| sm_80 | CUDA graph | 1.041x | 1.013–1.090x |
| sm_90 | CUDA graph, seventh commit | 1.072x | 0.994–1.162x |

The sm_80 event tests use 24 query heads, 2 KV heads, head dimension
256, top-k 2051, page size 16, NHD/HND layouts and 1–128 rows. Results
are medians of 18 rounds across three runs. Graph tests use 12/1 and
24/2 heads, top-k 2048 and page size 3136, with six rotated rounds. The
sm_90 results precede the final merge-parameter change.

On sm_80, NVFP4 eager host calls improve by 1.13–1.17x. FP8/BF16 eager
host time also drops from 78.3/80.6 µs to 59.4/60.0 µs.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Tracking issue: #6803
