### [724920f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/724920fdbaac890b005037e5adc11b6752cb5b66)

- **作者**: Brandon Zhang
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T20:44:08Z
- **提交信息**: fix(gdn): fp32 MTP pool scatter against real serving pools (#7882)

## 📌 Description

`flashinfer.gdn_decode.gated_delta_rule_mtp` advertises FLA-style
per-token
pool scatter (`ssm_state_indices: [B, T]`, the vLLM-compat
speculative-decode
form: initial state gathered per request, h after token t scattered to
`pool[ssm_state_indices[i, t]]`). Integrating it at vLLM's Qwen3.5-class
GDN
MTP decode call site surfaced three independent defects in
`flashinfer/gdn_kernels/gdn_decode_mtp.py` that make the mode unusable
against
the pools serving frameworks actually allocate. All three are fixed
here, in
severity order:

**1. Int32 pool-offset arithmetic → silent data corruption / illegal
memory
access on any production-size pool.** Slot views and scatter
destinations
index the pool with 32-bit math; the element offset (16,384 fp32
elements per
slot row at K=V=128) wraps Int32 at flat index ≥ 131,072 — slot ≥ 10,923
at
HV=12 (figures corrected per review; an earlier revision said 32,768),
while
a serving pool sized from hundreds of GiB of cache has tens of thousands
of
slots. Observed both ways: silently corrupted states/outputs in a
standalone
run (top-of-pool indices on a 16,384-slot pool), and a deterministic
`an illegal memory access was encountered` on the first full-size-pool
decode
step of a real serve. The dense `intermediate_states_buffer` cache tiles
carry the same wrap (flat index `i * cache_steps * HV`; T=8, HV=32 wraps
from
B ≥ 513 — thanks @kahyunnam for the repro). Fix: fold the 64-bit slot
offset
into a per-(slot, head) `(V, K)` view base ONCE (`_slot_view_i64`:
`cute.make_tensor` over the iterator advanced by the Int64 offset, with
the
alignment the offset terms preserve re-asserted), used by the read/write
views, the per-token scatter, and the intermediate-state cache tiles;
tile
offsets inside the views stay 32-bit.

**2. Flat-only scatter addressing → MLIR compile failure on strided
pools.**
The five scatter blocks addressed the pool exclusively through the flat
3D
view (`local_tile(h0_source, (1,1,vec), (fla_idx, v, lane))`). A
page-strided
pool (per-slot stride > HV·V·K, as vLLM carves the SSM state out of a
padded
page allocation) takes the 4D `use_pool_indexing=True` path, where the
3-coordinate tile fails MLIR op construction:
`failed to construct a valid coordinate from #cute.coord<"(?,?,?)">
resulting
in an incorrect profile`. So scatter mode has never worked against the
pools
the "vLLM API compat" comment targets. Fix: the same `_slot_view_i64`
view,
rank-aware (4D or flat per `use_pool_indexing`), tiled in 2D (20 tile
sites
across the warp-specialized and inline kernels).

**3. The 4D-pool JIT cache key misses the pool shape → wrong-kernel
reuse.**
The compile bakes the pool's static layout, but the cache key held only
`tuple(h0_source.stride())`: two pools with identical per-slot strides
and
different slot counts (a small profiling-phase pool, then the full
serving
pool) hit the same cached kernel and fail its signature validation —
`Mismatched h0_source.shape[0] on argument #0` — and without that
validation
would run with the wrong baked shape. Fix: key the compile on
`(h0_source.shape[0], *strides)`.

**Correctness evidence.** The patched kernels match a PyTorch float32
reference of the FLA recurrence (softplus gating, sigmoid beta,
qk-l2norm,
per-token scatter) bitwise on the scattered fp32 states (abs err ≤
7.2e-7)
and within bf16 tolerance on outputs (max rel ≤ 3.2e-3), across
contiguous
and page-strided pools, inline and warp-specialized variants, B ∈
{2…256},
pools 64–16,384 slots including top-of-pool indices beyond the overflow
threshold. Validated on this branch (main @ ac7771a2e + fix) on SM103:
the
new test file passes 8/8 (large-pool relocation invariance at 12,288
slots,
contiguous AND page-strided, inline and warp kernels; same-stride
pool-size
change; strided-vs-contiguous equality; the B=528/T=8/HV=32
intermediate-buffer case), the full reference sweep passes 8/8, and the
existing scatter/pool coverage is regression-free
(`pytest tests/gdn/test_decode_delta_rule.py -k "scatter or pool"`: 101
passed). Red-on-main verified for every new failure mode: at 12,288
slots
stock main fails the relocation checks (it passes at 8,192 — below the
real
threshold), and the B=528 intermediate-buffer case fails on stock main.
End-to-end, a TP4 MTP-3 vLLM serve of a Qwen3.5-class GDN
model routed its speculative decode step through this kernel: dispatch
on
every spec step across six concurrency points (149–2,440 requests each),
zero
request errors, CUDA graph capture/replay clean, coherent model output.

This is a correctness fix, with the measured cost disclosed (per review
the
original per-subscript Int64 views were not free). With the view-base
form:
same-job A/B on SM103, CUPTI median of 100, contiguous fp32 pool, H=16
HV=32
K=V=128 — verify T=2 B=32: 23.47 µs (main) → 23.42 µs (parity restored,
was
27.81 µs with per-subscript Int64 views); update T=2 B=8: 10.50 µs
(main) →
12.14 µs (a residual +1.6 µs on this smallest shape; the Int32
addressing it
would take to remove is exactly the overflow defect).

integration;
this PR carries the full report.

## Reviewer Notes

- The new test (`tests/gdn/test_mtp_fp32_pool_scatter.py`) is designed
so each
of the three defects fails it on the unpatched kernel:
strided-vs-contiguous
pool equivalence on both kernel variants (defect 2 crashes the compile),
same-stride pool-size change in one process (defect 3 fails the
signature
check), relocation invariance with top-of-pool indices on a 12,288-slot
pool, contiguous and page-strided, B=8 and B=16 (defect 1 corrupts; the
  cases skip when the device lacks ~10 GiB free), and the
B=528/T=8/HV=32 buffer-vs-scatter equivalence for the intermediate-state
  tiles (~20 GiB).
- The scatter rewrite deliberately mirrors the
`h_read_view`/`h_write_view`
construction a few lines above it in each kernel, so the two addressing
  paths stay structurally identical.
- Defect 1 also affects the Int32 read/write slot views outside scatter
mode
and the dense intermediate-state cache tiles; both go through the shared
  `_slot_view_i64` base now.
- `ssm_state_indices` destination contract documented: entries must be
valid
  in-range slots; per-token scatter carries no negative-padding promise
  (whole-request padding goes through a negative `initial_state_indices`
  entry, which keeps its skip semantics).
- AI-assisted; developed and validated on SM103 hardware.

### [3ed39c6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3ed39c6620b829f6d4139124de786401bdd1a30f)

- **作者**: Ji Sung Han
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T20:33:44Z
- **提交信息**: fix(autotuner): serve lookups above the largest tuned bucket from it (#7626)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Outside tuning mode, a lookup whose bucket lies above every bucket tuned
for the op now retries at the largest tuned bucket before it falls back
to
`(runners[0], -1)`. Today such a lookup silently runs the untuned
default.

This happens when the tune-time and run-time bucket keys disagree. For
example, a caller tunes inside `autotune(tuning_buckets=hybrid(21504))`,
so
the top profile is stored under 21504, while at run time the op's own
`map_to_tuning_buckets` sends every M in 16385..21504 to 32768. Every
one of
those lookups misses. (The matching vLLM-side fix is
vllm-project/vllm#63159; this PR makes FlashInfer tolerate the mismatch
whatever the caller does.)

- Candidates are the tuned profiles `search_cache` can serve: the active
in-memory partition, user-loaded file configs and the hydrated entries
of
  the active managed store. They must match the lookup's op, runners,
  cache-key extras and non-dynamic dims. For each dynamic dim above all
candidates, the bucket is set to the largest candidate; other dims keep
theirs. Legacy bundled package configs are looked up by key and are not
  scanned for the largest bucket.
- Lookups below or between tuned buckets still miss, and so do lookups
in
  tuning mode or with `require_profiling_policy`, so a miss there still
  triggers profiling.
- A tactic rejected by the runner's `validate_tactic` turns back into a
miss.
- Replay coverage (`replay_report` / `strict_replay`) is unchanged: it
reports such a lookup as a miss instead of hiding it behind the
fallback.
- File configs that `search_cache` itself skips (an isolated context
scope,
or keys excluded from the winner partition) do not count as tuned
buckets.
- The first fallback per `(op, requested profile)` is logged at INFO.


## 🔍 Related Issues

- vllm-project/vllm#63159 (fixes the same key mismatch on the vLLM side)

## Reviewer Notes

- **This changes the fallback for every op outside tuning mode:** a size
above
the tuned range now gets the top bucket's tactic instead of tactic -1.
This
is what the clamping mappers (`make_bucket_mapper`,
`map_to_hybrid_bucket`,
`round_up` overrides) already do. Runners whose tactics depend on M
reject an
unusable tactic through `validate_tactic`, which this path checks and
which
  turns a rejection back into a miss. A runner with neither that nor a
re-check after selection could now receive a tactic tuned for a smaller
M.
  Is that acceptable, or should the fallback be opt-in per op?
- Of the 142 `TunableRunner` subclasses in `flashinfer/`, 15 define
`validate_tactic`; the
rest are trusted as before. `CuteDslFusedMoERunner` does not define it;
its runtime
backstop in `_moe_core_impl` checks the plan's tile and cluster shape
before routing.
  I did not audit which of the other runners' tactics depend on M.
- If no tactic at the top profiled bucket produced a winner (all failed
or
  OOM), lookups there now use the next lower tuned bucket instead of the
  default.
- Each miss outside tuning mode now scans the tuned entries; file-key
parsing
  is `lru_cache`d and hits are unaffected. The scan returns at once when
nothing is tuned. Eager callers above the tuned range pay the scan on
every
  call.
- Managed-store entries count only after they are hydrated.
- AI assistance (Claude, via Claude Code) was used to write parts of
this change and the tests. I reviewed every change and ran all of the
validation above on SM107.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* **New Features**
* Lookups above the largest tuned bucket can retry using that bucket’s
configuration when the operation, runner, and other relevant cache-key
settings match. This applies outside tuning and replay diagnostics,
including runtime sizes beyond the tuned range.
* If no matching configuration is available, the existing fallback
remains. Lookups below or between tuned buckets retain their existing
behavior, and replay diagnostics continue to report above-range lookups
as misses.
* **Documentation**
* Updated autotuning guidance to describe lookups above the tuned range.

### [7f526f9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7f526f9a006776c77efe700eea0cadcb25edfe2b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T20:31:33Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_kcp): chain-aware value widths for the state walks of the non-deterministic KCP package (#8521)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp` is the non-deterministic
KCP GDN training package (BF16; contiguous, zigzag and
zigzag-per-document layouts; optional in-kernel Q/K L2 norm; forward,
backward and checkpointed calls, eager and CUDA graph). This PR changes
only the host rule that picks the per-CTA value width (128, or 64 with
two CTAs per segment and head) for the forward and backward state walks:
the width now follows the plan's chain lengths, except that on sm_100a a
backward walk with a segment of at least 400 chunks keeps the previous
rule when the two-CTA grid would finish later. Kernels are unchanged;
outputs and gradients are bitwise equal to the previous version (eager
and CUDA graph).

**Conventions**

- Ratio = baseline ms / this PR ms. Above 1 means this PR is faster.
Below 1 (marked `*` in the tables) means this PR is slower.
- Workload label = shape letter (shapes are listed in the table legend),
then CPn = context parallel over n GPUs, then the layout: C =
contiguous, Z = zigzag, D = per-document zigzag. Example: `G CP4 Z`.
Pre-norm = q/k L2-normalised before the call; other rows normalise in
the kernel. A cell is one workload x operation (fwd, fwd+bwd, ckpt = 2 x
fwd + bwd).
- Table A = this PR vs previous, with an A/A arm (a second copy of
previous). Table B = det(main), the strongest non-Cake arm and this PR.
A multi-node CP16 sub-table (B200 2 x 8, GB300 4 x 4 GPUs) is separate
from both.
- A single-rank proxy (`proxy <workload> r<rank>`) runs one rank's share
of a CP > 1 workload on one GPU at CP1. It excludes communication and is
not a full step. Its documents are listed in [this
comment](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8521#issuecomment-6612373113).
- Unmarked cells: timed at an earlier commit of this PR with identical
launch forms; `[this PR]`: timed at this head; `[merge]`: timed after
the merge with main.
- Per group, c = this PR ms / previous ms and a = A/A ms / previous ms.
A run is win if every c is below 1 and below every a, REGRESSION if
every c is above 1 and above every a, and parity otherwise.
- A workload regresses if two or more of its published runs are
REGRESSION and its fwd+bwd and ckpt cells point the same way.
- Win counts = win cells / changed workloads with a published cell. A
changed workload is one whose launch forms differ from the previous
version. A win cell has every used run classed win. Used runs are all
published runs of the cell, including earlier runs not shown in the
table, except in the B200 F CP2 D fwd+bwd and ckpt cells, whose launch
forms the last commit changes; there only the runs at this head count.
Medians and ranges are over the used runs of the win cells.

**Baselines**

- Previous = the non-deterministic package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp` of FlashInfer main.
det(main) = the deterministic KCP package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp` of FlashInfer main.
Both come from main bf0605d519ecf585a73372037baedda4a159fb45 for rows
timed at the rules commit, and from main
358c1756342f0fbbb0bb4192bbd0643153d7513f for rows re-timed after the
merge. The deterministic package is code-identical between the two
(docstrings and README only). The non-deterministic package differs only
in code these rows do not reach.
- Non-Cake arms: FLA = flash-linear-attention / fla-core 0.6.0 from PyPI
(upstream tag v0.6.0 = 413ad2c655ece57b94bc9ddc51fdbd43cf09d984). It
runs as FLA-CP (its own context parallelism; layouts C and Z only) or
FLA-HS (head split: all-to-all around FLA's single-GPU kernels). The
cuDNN FROST GDN plan runs in the same head split. FROST-ck0 recomputes
the states in the backward; FROST-ck64 stores them every 64 tokens. The
FROST plan is CuTe DSL code (nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.1) shipped in
nvidia-cudnn-frontend 1.32.1 from PyPI (upstream tag v1.32.1 =
73f69cf0d704bbc384da4ecd1358f36579bf1d80). The environment has
nvidia-cudnn-cu13 9.24.0.43.
- The GDN training implementations with forward and backward that run on
these GPUs in the same process and accept the same packed
variable-length inputs are FLA and cuDNN FROST; FlashQLA needs its own
environment and is covered below.
- Per row, each arm's outputs and input gradients are checked against
this PR on that row's inputs: finite, rel-RMS <= 1e-2, max-abs <= 2e-2 x
max|ref|. Table B shows the fastest arm that passes.

**Setup (all tables)**

B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) and R200 (sm_107a, 208
SMs); CUDA 13.4 development container (CUDA 13.4.2), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130, NCCL 2.30.7. BF16 q/k/v, head dim 128, FP32 g and beta;
every rank draws the same seeded inputs. Every timed arm runs eager;
CUDA graph replay was not timed. The arms of a run share one process and
run palindromically in groups (two blocks per arm per group; block =
warm-up calls + timed calls). Paired runs reverse the arm order. L2 is
cold: a 256 MiB buffer fill, a device synchronize and a barrier run
before every iteration. Timing uses CUDA events on every rank, and an
iteration's time is the slowest rank's. The statistic is the median over
all timed iterations of an arm.

| groups x blocks x timed (warm-up): count | B200 | GB300 | R200 |
|---|---|---|---|
| table A runs | 5x2x8 (5): 409; 5x2x12 (10): 70; sustained: 78 | 5x2x12
(10): 487; 5x2x8 (5): 18; 7x2x24 (10): 11 | 5x2x12 (10): 371 |
| table B rows | 5x2x8 (5): 85; sustained: 2 | 5x2x12 (10): 79; 5x2x8
(5): 59 | 5x2x12 (10): 13 CP1 + 149 proxy rows |
| CP16 runs | 5x2x12 (10) | 5x2x12 (10) | none |

Sustained (B200 only) = 3 groups, block = 5 s idle + 20 warm-up + 300
timed. The other protocols have no idle time.

Not published: runs with a group drift above 2 % (table A also accepts a
run when >= 5 per-group paired ratios lie within 1 % of their median;
table B uses the largest drift over all arms of the run), and short
table A runs with >= 5 % of timed samples under the software power cap
on any compared arm (sustained runs show that share when it is >= 5 %).

A/A noise (a = A/A ms / previous ms per published table A run, p5-p95,
full workloads / proxies): B200 0.997-1.003 / 0.996-1.003, GB300
0.998-1.002 / 0.994-1.004, R200 0.997-1.008 / 0.997-1.003.

**B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs)**

- **vs previous (table A):** fwd 14/65 win cells (median 1.086x, range
1.000-1.114x), fwd+bwd 49/64 (1.013x, 1.000-1.058x), ckpt 44/64 (1.013x,
1.001-1.057x). Single-rank proxies: fwd 0/8, fwd+bwd 2/8 (1.014x,
1.010-1.017x), ckpt 2/8 (1.013x, 1.010-1.015x). Largest: A CP1 C
pre-norm fwd 1.114x in both runs, H CP1 C pre-norm fwd 1.111x/1.109x.
- **Runs below 1 (table A):** 0.980-0.999x (proxies 0.996-0.998x). 7
cells have one REGRESSION run (lowest 0.996x); each also has a parity or
win run. No workload regresses. All other runs below 1 are parity.
- **vs det(main) (table B):** faster on all 87 published rows: fwd
1.105-1.271x, fwd+bwd 1.047-1.269x, ckpt 1.046-1.358x.
- **vs non-Cake (table B):** fwd 0.361-1.952x, fwd+bwd 0.555-1.584x,
ckpt 0.694-1.924x. Below 1 on all 13 CP1 (single GPU) rows: FROST-ck0 in
4 fwd rows, FROST-ck64 in 5 fwd+bwd and 4 ckpt rows. None of the 74 CP2
rows is below 1.

**R200 (sm_107a, 208 SMs)**

- **vs previous (table A):** R200 runs used one GPU. Table A has 6 CP1
workloads and 56 single-rank proxies, so most of the evidence, and all
CP > 1 evidence, comes from proxies, which exclude communication. CP1:
2/3 win cells per op (M CP1 C and M CP1 C pre-norm): fwd median 1.099x
(range 1.090-1.109x), fwd+bwd 1.054x (1.052-1.061x), ckpt 1.051x
(1.049-1.054x). Proxies: 14/56 win cells per op: fwd 1.067x
(1.027-1.105x), fwd+bwd 1.038x (1.019-1.064x), ckpt 1.037x
(1.010-1.060x). Largest: M CP1 C pre-norm fwd 1.105x/1.109x, proxy G CP4
Z r3 pre-norm fwd 1.104x/1.105x.
- **Runs below 1 (table A):** 0.994-0.999x (proxies 0.995-0.999x). 6
cells (1 CP1, 5 proxies) have one REGRESSION run (lowest 0.995x); each
also has a parity or win run. Proxy E CP4 C r3 has one REGRESSION run in
fwd and one in fwd+bwd, but both of its ckpt runs are parity. No
workload regresses. All other runs below 1 are parity.
- **vs det(main) (table B, timed at this head):** faster on all 13
published CP1 rows: fwd 1.162-1.311x, fwd+bwd 1.048-1.115x, ckpt
1.047-1.156x. Faster on all 149 published single-rank proxy rows too:
fwd 1.171-1.354x, fwd+bwd 1.053-1.271x, ckpt 1.050-1.157x.
- **vs non-Cake (table B, timed at this head):** this PR is slower on
all 13 published CP1 rows; cuDNN FROST is faster on every one. fwd
0.321-0.403x (FROST-ck0), fwd+bwd 0.717-0.764x (FROST-ck64), ckpt
0.834-0.925x (FROST-ck0 on 2 rows, FROST-ck64 on 3). Single-rank proxies
(one GPU, no communication; rows in [this
comment](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8521#issuecomment-6614291049)):
below 1 on 140 of 149 published rows: fwd 51 of 51 (0.316-0.797x,
FROST-ck0), fwd+bwd 49 of 49 (0.736-0.852x, FROST-ck64), ckpt 40 of 49
(0.865-1.069x; FROST-ck0 on 7 of the 40, FROST-ck64 on 33).

**cuDNN FROST on B200.** On the inputs of the earlier comparison (#8435,
B200 CP1 shape M), both FROST modes fail the accuracy check (dbeta = 0
at one element where an FP64 reference gives 0.986; max-abs error 0.1349
of max|ref|, limit 0.02). The failure is input-dependent: with two other
seeds of the same recipe and with this benchmark's inputs, FROST's
largest max-abs error vs FP64 is 0.0082-0.0094 of max|ref|, and FROST
passes the per-row check on every B200 row where table B shows it.

**FlashQLA 0.1.3 is not an arm:** it needs its own environment and
cannot share a process with the FROST arm. On CP1 shape M (B200 and
GB300) it was slower than both FROST modes and faster than FLA in all 12
measured cells. On those B200 inputs FROST fails the accuracy check, so
there FlashQLA could be the strongest passing arm; no table B row has
that case. Other shapes and R200 were not measured.

## Performance tables

Previous = the non-deterministic KCP package of FlashInfer main; this PR
= this PR's head; both run in one process with det(main) and an A/A copy
of previous. Unmarked cells: timed at an earlier commit of this PR with
identical launch forms; [this PR]: timed at this head; [merge]: timed
after the merge with main.

Table A cells: previous ms -> this PR ms of run 1 (absolutes are run 1),
then the ratios previous / this PR of run 1 / run 2 and the class per
run (A/A envelope of per-group ratios: win, parity = inside the A/A
spread, REGRESSION). Table B: ratio = baseline ms / this PR ms from the
absolutes in the row. Shown: the latest step's published runs plus any
earlier REGRESSION run at the shipped launch forms (the B200 F CP2 D
backward runs before the last commit measured replaced launch forms and
are not shown); no workload regresses (a workload regresses if two or
more of its published runs are REGRESSION and its fwd+bwd and ckpt cells
point the same way).

Legend: '*' = ratio below 1.000 (this PR slower than that baseline);
'sust.' = sustained protocol, else short; 'cap x %' = timed samples
under the software power cap (>= 5 %); 'n/p cap' / 'n/p unstable' = not
published (power-capped short run / drift above 2 %), listed at the end.

Shapes (head dim 128, BF16 q / k / v; documents in tokens; heads = (q/k
heads, v heads)); layouts C = contiguous, Z = zigzag, D = per-document
zigzag; CPn = context parallel over n GPUs; pre-norm = q and k
L2-normalised before the call (other rows: in the kernel):

### [ff79fd7](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ff79fd709308f3d8f4bd4e85986b584280219302)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T20:21:37Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): route short FP8 64-head decode to fp8_lowhead_h64 with PDL on sm_100a/sm_103a (#8543)

`cake_dsv4` is the Cake DSv4 sparse-MLA decode and prefill backend in
FlashInfer for BF16 and FP8 KV caches. On FlashInfer main, twenty
programs serve the 197-shape list on each architecture. This PR changes
how one group of rows is routed on SM100 (sm_100a) and SM103 (sm_103a).
The group is FP8 64-head decode with at most 12 query tokens and sparse
widths 260 to 380. These rows used to run on
`fp8_h64_prefill_source_persistent_m64_multi_tile`. They now run on the
H64 cluster decode program `fp8_lowhead_h64`. That program also gains
programmatic dependent launch (PDL). Three shapes of the 197-shape list
take the new route, so 21 programs serve the list with this PR. The
baseline is FlashInfer main, which ships the previous Cake version of
these programs. On B200 (SM100), the 197 shapes break down as 3 faster
(1.047x to 1.065x), 0 tie, 0 slower and 194 same code. On GB300 (SM103),
the 197 shapes break down as 3 faster (1.027x to 1.034x), 0 tie, 0
slower and 194 same code.

Latencies are in microseconds. Speedup = FlashInfer main latency / this
PR latency. The 197-shape tables below were measured with PDL off
(`enable_pdl=False`).

**With `enable_pdl=True`**: 64 decode points per GPU in the rerouted
range (1 to 12 query tokens, sparse widths 260 to 380, page sizes 2 and
64). Latency is per call in a CUDA graph of 8 calls, CUDA 13.4.
FlashInfer main runs `fp8_h64_prefill_source_persistent_m64_multi_tile`
and this PR runs `fp8_lowhead_h64`, both with PDL. The speedup range is
taken per point.

| GPU | points | FlashInfer main (us) | this PR (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA B200 (SM100, sm_100a) | 64 | 8.83 to 9.28 | 7.75 to 8.33 |
1.098x to 1.151x |
| NVIDIA GB300 (SM103, sm_103a) | 64 | 8.42 to 8.64 | 7.53 to 7.86 |
1.090x to 1.137x |

Verdicts: **faster** = every counted reading shows this PR faster than
main by more than the measured run-to-run noise band, with readings in
both run orders. **tie** = the readings are not all faster (or all
slower) than main beyond the noise band. **same code** = this PR does
not change the machine code that runs this shape, so both columns carry
one measurement of that code and the row reads 1.000x.

### [c53f429](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c53f4297b1b10a94c461b8fd76f9bee1f098ed96)

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): L2 cache-policy hints for the DCP spec-decode E4M3 hd256 balanced programs on sm_100a / sm_103a (#8504)

`flashinfer.cake_dcp` (`run_dcp_spec_decode`, decode-context-parallel
speculative decode) has three Cake on-device load-balanced families:
`dcp_spec_bf16_balanced` (BF16 KV, page 16, head_dim 128),
`dcp_spec_bf16_fp8_balanced` (BF16 Q over an E4M3 page-64 KV cache,
head_dim 128) and `dcp_spec_bf16_fp8_d256_balanced` (BF16 Q over an E4M3
page-64 KV cache, head_dim 256, 16 query heads per KV head). This PR
regenerates the four programs of `dcp_spec_bf16_fp8_d256_balanced` for
sm_100a and sm_103a. They are the on-device balanced planner and the
static one-wave plan, each as a 32-row and a 64-row packed instance.
Every K/V TMA load now carries a per-work-item L2 cache-policy hint
(evict_first / evict_normal). The baseline P0 is the previous Cake
version (`route="balanced"` on FlashInfer main). On B200, against P0,
the new balanced route (NEW) runs at 0.9889–1.1316× in eager and
0.9995–1.1336× under CUDA-graph replay. NEW is faster on 14 of 18 rows
in eager and 17 of 18 in graph. The rows just below 1.00 are
random-length b128 eager (0.9889), agentx b16 (eager 0.9986, graph
0.9995), agentx b64 eager (0.9984) and b64 / KV 32768 eager (0.9961).
Against the static split-KV program (T, `route="static"`), NEW is
1.0193–4.0756× in eager and 1.0186–4.0865× in graph, with the minimum on
b128 q_len 1. On GB300, NEW runs at 1.0024–1.1476× against P0 in eager
and 1.0024–1.1442× in graph, and is faster than P0 on all 18 rows in
both modes. Against T on GB300, NEW is 0.9880–3.9455× in eager and
0.9920–3.9251× in graph. The minimum is on b128 q_len 1, the only row
below 1.00. Every other row is at least 1.0741× in eager and 1.0766× in
graph. Auto routing is unchanged.

### [fe82a1d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/fe82a1d5ba6bf3cb13707a33829195c0fa98568b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T19:51:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train): short forward up to 10 rows per SM and one-cluster short backward on SM107 (#8540)

This PR adds the short forward and the one-cluster short backward of
Cake's SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel (BF16 inputs, head dim 128) to
sm_107a. The kernel ships as two Cake packages: the deterministic
package `flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` and a
non-deterministic package. `flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train`
runs the deterministic package by default. When called with
`deterministic=False`, it runs the non-deterministic package, which has
a non-deterministic weight gradient.

In the non-deterministic package on sm_107a, forward inputs of up to 10
rows per SM now run the short forward, which uses 16 threads per row. On
R200 (212 SMs) that is T x H <= 2120 rows. Backward inputs of up to 256
rows now run the short backward, which is one thread-block cluster of 16
CTAs. It handles both the BF16 and the FP32 weight-gradient outputs.
Before this PR, both routes existed only on sm_100a and sm_103a. The
short forward's limit is now set per architecture: 12 rows per SM on
sm_100a and sm_103a (unchanged since PR #8505) and 10 on sm_107a. No
kernel, build entry or routing changes on sm_100a or sm_103a. This PR is
one commit on FlashInfer main 18d8a034, which contains PR #8505.

The kernel's other Cake variants are the deterministic package and the
FP32 weight-gradient output of the non-deterministic package. Both
packages ship on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, and this PR changes the
non-deterministic package on sm_107a only.

The table below gives speedup ranges (min-max) over the rows the new
routes serve on R200 board class 1. A speedup is baseline us / new us,
so a value above 1 means this PR is faster. Per-row values with absolute
times follow.

| GPU | op | rows | det/new | non-Cake/new | previous/new | A/B
previous/new | rows faster than strongest non-Cake |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R200 (sm_107a) | fwd | 22 | 1.203x-1.297x | 0.888x-0.959x |
1.203x-1.297x | 1.211x-1.324x | 0 of 22 |
| R200 (sm_107a) | fwd graph | 22 | 1.227x-1.354x | 0.835x-0.970x |
1.229x-1.350x | - | 0 of 22 |
| R200 (sm_107a) | bwd graph | 6 | 1.660x-1.814x | 1.065x-1.593x |
1.525x-1.706x | 1.572x-1.656x | 6 of 6 |
| R200 (sm_107a) | ckpt graph | 22 | 1.093x-1.471x | 0.877x-1.171x |
1.103x-1.476x | 1.085x-1.492x | 4 of 22 |
| R200 (sm_107a) | bwd graph, FP32 dw | 6 | - | - | - | 1.604x-1.640x |
- |
| R200 (sm_107a) | ckpt graph, FP32 dw | 22 | - | - | - | 1.077x-1.468x
| - |

The short backward beats the strongest non-Cake arm at every row it
serves, with speedups of 1.065x (1x48) to 1.593x (8x32). The short
forward is slower than the strongest non-Cake arm at every row it
serves: 0.888x-0.959x eager and 0.835x-0.970x in a graph. The
checkpointed step is slower than the strongest non-Cake arm at 18 of 22
served rows. It is faster at 5x48 (1.122x), 8x32 (1.115x), 33x48
(1.038x) and 36x7 (1.171x). At every cell whose code changed, the new
route is faster than det Cake and previous Cake in the main table and
faster than previous Cake in the A/B; the FP32-dw rows (†) are also
faster than det Cake.

## Per-row results

**Columns.** Times are in us. A speedup is baseline us / new us, so a
value above 1 means this PR is faster.

- `det`: the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` (the same API with
`deterministic=True`). Its files are identical at main 17e24cd1, at main
18d8a034 and in this PR.
- `prev`: this package on FlashInfer main, measured at main 17e24cd1.
Between 17e24cd1 and this PR's base 18d8a034, the package changed only
its short forward on sm_100a and sm_103a. Its sm_107a programs, build
entries and host plan are identical at both commits, so on sm_107a these
values stand for the package at this PR's base.
- `new`: a measured tree whose sm_107a kernels and build entries are
identical to this PR's. Its host plan launches the same programs with
the same grids at every row count on sm_107a. That tree wrote the short
forward's limit as one value, 10 rows per SM, for every architecture.
This PR writes one value per architecture.
- `strongest non-Cake (arm)`: per row and operation, the fastest of
these arms, each timed in the same process as the Cake arms:
  - `FLA`: FLA 0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated`.
- `mamba_ssm`: mamba_ssm v2.3.2 `rmsnorm_fn`. It is never the fastest
arm here.
- `tc-def`: torch.compile of the FP32 formula in mode "default", best of
5 fresh compiles.
- `tc-max`: torch.compile of the FP32 formula in mode
"max-autotune-no-cudagraphs", best of 5 fresh compiles. That mode is
"max-autotune" without torch.compile's own CUDA-graph wrapping. The
graph columns capture and replay one CUDA graph of each arm's call, the
same way for every arm.
- `pin` / `pin-g`: the Triton kernel that torch.compile (inductor)
generates for this formula, launched directly at XBLOCK=1 with
num_warps=2 (inductor's own candidate for XBLOCK=1). It is forward only.
`pin` is the no-grad variant, and `pin-g` is the grad variant, which
also stores rstd.
- On an exact tie, the cell names the earlier arm in this order: FLA,
mamba_ssm, tc-def, tc-max, pin, pin-g.
- `det`, `non-Cake`, `prev`, `new` and their ratios come from the
same-process main table (S). On board class 1 it ran 6 processes on the
4 GPUs of one node. Each process timed a group of 4-9 shapes of one head
count, and every arm of a shape was timed in that process, with the arm
order alternating each round.
- `A/B prev`, `A/B new`, `A/B prev/new` and `A/B new faster/slower` come
from a separate interleaved A/B: 144 valid processes in 16 sequences,
one sequence per GPU. The arms were previous Cake (main 17e24cd1), this
change, an A/A twin of main, and six arms of main that each hold one
unused device allocation of 256 KiB to 64 MiB. Each process ran 10
rounds.
  - An A/B value is the median over the processes of each arm.
- The last column counts the GPU pairs (of 16) where the new value is
below / above the previous-Cake value.
- † marks a det value from the A/B arm A process, and a det/new ratio of
that value to the `A/B new` value. The FP32 weight-gradient operations
were timed only in the A/B, which runs Cake packages only. Non-Cake
values for those rows were not measured; this is a gap in the
measurements, not a missing non-Cake feature.
- `op`:
  - `fwd` is one eager forward call.
- `fwd graph`, `bwd graph` and `ckpt graph` (checkpointed step: 2 x
forward + backward) are replays of a CUDA graph that the harness
captures for every arm.
- `FP32 dw` marks an FP32 weight gradient. The other rows use a BF16
weight gradient.
- `code`: `new` means this PR routes the short forward and / or the
short backward at that row. `same` means previous Cake and this PR run
identical device code.
- Inputs: x and z BF16 [T, H, 128], weight [128], eps 1e-6.

### R200 board class 1 (sm_107a, 212 SMs)

- GPU: R200, sm_107a, 212 SMs, compute capability 10.7 (the driver
reports the device name NVIDIA Graphics Device), driver 620.43, 2424
MHz, power limit 2300.00 W.
- Software: kernels built by FlashInfer JIT with nvcc 13.4 (build
cuda_13.4.r13.4); PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), Triton 3.8.0, Python
3.14.8.
- Timing: CUPTI GPU span with a cold L2 via
`flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time`; 10 rounds; a cell is the median of
the per-round medians.
- Noise, main table: the spread ((max - min) / min) of the 10 round
medians of a cell is 0.0 %-16.2 % for det Cake, 0.0 %-16.2 % for new and
0.0 %-16.4 % for previous Cake.
- Layout effects at the 107 A/B cells whose device code is identical in
this PR and main: the median per-pair change ranges from -6.39 % to
+3.89 % (mean -0.295 %). The six arms of main that hold an unused
allocation reach +6.63 %, and the A/A twin of main shows a mean of
-0.001 % and a largest change of +0.15 %.

**Rows the short routes serve** (T x H <= 10 x 212 = 2120 rows; the
short backward up to 256 rows)

### R200 board class 2 (sm_107a, 212 SMs)

- GPU: R200, sm_107a, 212 SMs, compute capability 10.7 (the driver
reports the device name NVIDIA Graphics Device), driver 620.62, 2424
MHz, power limit 2300.00 W; the same as board class 1 except the driver
(board class 1: 620.43).
- Software, timing, arms, comparator versions and rounds: the same as on
board class 1 (nvcc 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 with CUDA 13.0). `det`,
`prev` and `new` are the same as on board class 1. At each of the 37
shapes, the measured tree and previous Cake launch the same forward and
backward programs on both board classes.
- Run condition, main table: 6 processes on 2 nodes, one GPU each. One
process (48 heads, T = 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 13, 21, 30, 31) ran on GPU 0 of
one node and was the only main-table process on that node. The other 5
ran later on GPUs 1-3 of a second node, at most 3 at a time. The first
process's absolute times therefore come from a different node than the
others'. Every ratio in the main table compares arms timed in the same
process on the same GPU.
- A/B: 144 valid processes in 16 sequences, one sequence per GPU, on 4
nodes of this board class (4 GPUs each), with the same arms as on board
class 1.
- Noise, main table (round spread as on board class 1): 0.0 %-12.1 % for
det Cake, 0.0 %-10.8 % for new and 0.0 %-15.0 % for previous Cake.
- Layout effects at the 107 A/B cells whose device code is identical in
this PR and main: the median per-pair change ranges from -6.05 % to
+7.25 % (mean -0.030 %). The six arms of main that hold an unused
allocation reach +9.25 %, and the A/A twin of main shows a mean of
-0.002 % and a largest change of +0.04 %.
- Columns: those of the board class 1 tables without `code` (the same
per row as there) and without the A/B columns; the A/B values of the
BF16 rows are not shown. In the FP32 weight-gradient rows, † marks an
A/B median (arm A for `det` and `prev`, arm B for `new`) and a ratio of
two such values.

### [f22d616](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f22d61637355ffcdd3413e563355cc832f29d05e)

- **作者**: 0z5a
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T19:40:13Z
- **提交信息**: fix(rope): guard the non-RoPE tail and honor V cache strides in the paged-KV append (#7494)

## 📌 Description

`rope_quantize_fp8_append_paged_kv_cache` writes outside the target
cache slots in two cases. Both were found while writing the RoPE
contract tests for RFC #3605
([report](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3605#issuecomment-6425890722)).

**1. `no_rope_dim` not a multiple of `rope_dim`.**
`RopeQuantizeAppendPagedKVCacheKernel` walks the non-RoPE part of K and
Q in `rope_dim`-sized chunks, but it loads and stores every chunk in
full. With partial rotary (e.g. rope 32 / no-rope 48), the last chunk
does three things wrong:
- it reads past the end of the input head;
- it writes past the end of the K cache head, into the next head or the
next slot;
- it writes past the `q_nope_out` row.

MLA's `ckv` rows go through the same branch and spill into the next slot
in the same way. `RopeQuantizeKernel` already handles this tail with
`scale_store_partial_chunk`, and both non-RoPE branches of the append
kernel now use it:
- full vectors keep the vectorized load/store;
- lanes past the tail do nothing;
- a vector that straddles the tail falls back to per-element accesses.

The `griddepcontrol` placement is unchanged.

**2. A `v_cache` whose strides differ from `k_cache`'s.** The binding
computed `v_strides` but built `paged_kv_t` from `k_strides` alone, so a
V cache with, for example, padded rows was written at K's offsets.
`paged_kv_t` already has a constructor that takes separate K and V
strides, and the kernel reaches V only through `get_v_ptr`, so the
binding now passes `v_strides`. It also checks that `v_cache` matches
`k_cache` in every dimension except the number of pages, because both
are addressed with one page size, head count and head dim.

## 🔍 Related Issues

No separate issue was filed. Found and reported in RFC #3605 (RoPE
slice).

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit`
(or used your preferred method).
- [ ] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files`
and fixed any reported issues. (`pre-commit run --files` on the four
changed files: all hooks pass.)

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

New `tests/attention/test_rope_append_paged_kv_cache_layouts.py` has 14
cases. The cache and the `q_nope_out` padding are poisoned first, and
every case checks two things: no byte outside the target slots changed,
and the slots match an fp32 reference. The cases are:
- GQA with rope/no-rope 64/64, 32/48, 64/96 and 64/32, in NHD and HND;
- MLA with 64/512 and 32/48;
- GQA with V strides equal to K's, and with V rows padded by 32 bytes,
in NHD and HND.

GH200 (SM90), CUDA 13.2, torch 2.14.1+cu130, main `215f83cb`:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_rope_append_paged_kv_cache_layouts.py` | 9 failed, 5 passed | 14
passed |
| `test_rope.py -k append` | 98 passed | 98 passed |

The 9 failures on main are exactly the non-multiple tails (GQA in both
layouts, plus MLA 32/48) and the padded V rows. In all 7 tail cases, the
first check to fail is the `q_nope_out` padding, with 1280 to 2560 bytes
past the head changed. An earlier probe on the same GPU measured how
many bytes outside the target slots changed (BF16 GQA, 2 KV heads, page
size 16):

| Case | NHD | HND |
|---|---|---|
| 32/48 | 64 | 144 |
| 64/96 | 128 | 288 |
| 64/32 | 128 | 288 |
| V rows padded by 32 bytes | 1984 | 2560 |

64/64 and 64/192 were clean, and so was the non-append
`rope_quantize_fp8` with 32/48. The broader RoPE contract file from the
#3605 slice is not part of this PR. On this branch it gives 60 passed
and 3 skipped; the skips are the cuTile cases, because the CUDA 13.2
`tileiras` has no `sm_90` target.

## Reviewer Notes

- The new `v_cache` vs `k_cache` shape check is stricter than before.
Every caller in the repository passes equal shapes, and the number of
pages may still differ.
- I left the V branch unchanged. It already guards per vector, and it
covers `rope_dim + no_rope_dim` exactly whenever that is a multiple of
the vector width.
- I did not time the change. Full chunks keep the vectorized path, and
only a chunk that ends inside the head takes the guarded path.

### [71b94c3](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/71b94c30f1f731e0e84d2c75fde26d22e5a1323a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T19:31:54Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det_kcp): chain-aware walk widths in the deterministic KCP GDN package (#8538)

Cake's deterministic context-parallel GDN training kernel has one
data-type variant: BF16 q/k/v/out/dout with FP32 scalar log-decay g and
beta. The grouped Q/K head counts `(H_qk, HV)` are runtime parameters
with production shape (16, 48). The kernel has three partition layouts:
contiguous (C), whole-buffer zigzag (Z) and per-document zigzag + ragged
(D). This PR delivers the same variant. It changes the host-side rule
that picks the value-head tile width for the cross-rank state-summary
walk launches. A walk runs either 128 value columns per CTA or 64, and
the 64 form runs two CTAs per segment and head. Forward walks still use
the 64 form when the grid fits one wave. They now also use it when an
LPT schedule of the walk's segment chain lengths shows that the two-CTA
grid finishes within its longest chain. Backward offset walks always use
the 64 form. Backward tape walks use it on sm_100a and sm_103a, while
sm_107a keeps the previous two-wave rule. One exception applies on
sm_100a: a backward walk keeps the previous two-wave rule when its
longest chain is at least 400 chunks and its two-CTA schedule would take
longer than the one-CTA schedule. The rule reads only host plan integers
(segment lengths, head count, SM count and device architecture), never
tensor contents. It takes the same decision in the forward, the
checkpoint recompute and the recompute-handle replay. The
non-deterministic KCP package (PR #8521) uses the same thresholds. The
change is host-side Python only and the kernels are unchanged. Only
launch widths differ, so outputs and gradients are bitwise identical to
before on every measured row, and peak memory is unchanged. A is the
previous Cake version of this package, as shipped after PR #8385. B is
this PR on the same base. B/A < 1 means faster. Each GPU was measured on
66 rows: packs P1-P5 x CP 2/4/8 x layouts C/Z/D at B1 and B3. On 33 of
these rows the launch form changes, and the other 33 are unchanged
controls. On GB300 (sm_103a), changed rows range from 0.984 to 1.004 at
B3 (median 0.989) and from 0.976 to 1.001 at B1 (median 0.999), though
only 6 B1 rows change. Unchanged GB300 rows range from 0.994 to 1.013
(median 1.000). On GB200 (sm_100a), changed rows range from 0.987 to
1.016 at B3 (median 0.992) and from 0.978 to 1.002 at B1 (median 1.000).
Unchanged GB200 rows range from 0.992 to 1.003 (median 1.000). Taking
the median over both sessions, changed rows at CP 2 / 4 / 8 come to
0.989 / 0.990 / 0.999 on GB300 and 0.991 / 0.994 / 1.000 on GB200. That
is about a 1 % gain at CP 2 and CP 4 and about parity at CP 8. The
largest gain is CP 8 P3 C B1 on GB300 at 0.977 / 0.976. The slowest
changed row is CP 8 P3 C B3 on GB200, at 1.016 in session 1 and 1.006 in
session 2. R200 (sm_107a) rows were not measured.

ms = slowest-rank median; B1 = module forward with autograd recording;
B3 = forward + non-reentrant checkpoint replay + backward, including all
communication and copies; Walk forms = changed (this PR launches a
different width) or unchanged (same launches as A); s1/s2 = two
sessions.

Packs: P1 241,817 tokens / 6 documents, P2 261,987 / 3, P3 259,174 / 2,
P4 254,976 / 1 (one document spans the whole group), P5 249,856 / 4.
Heads (16, 48); causal conv1d width 4 over 10,240 channels.

Software: CUDA 13.4 toolkit, torch 2.14.1+cu130.

kernel, single-GPU GDN training packages without context parallelism

sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [3385188](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3385188a7090e10963b567bc7ba4c9409cc29593)

- **作者**: Netanel Haber
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T19:27:52Z
- **提交信息**: [SDSA] Add the SDSA (Simplified DSA) indexer for Blackwell, with BF16 scores on other GPUs (#8374)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Adds the SDSA (Simplified DSA) indexer in `flashinfer/sdsa/`. SDSA is
sparse attention: a one-head indexer selects the Top-K keys of each
query token, and an MQA core attends to them. All the APIs run on
Blackwell (SM100, SM103). On other GPUs, such as Hopper, only
`indexer_scores` runs, with BF16 keys.

- `indexer_scores` computes the dot product of each query row with the
paged keys of its request, for decode. The keys are BF16 or NVFP4.
- `quantize_write_index_qk_nvfp4` quantizes keys and query rows to
NVFP4, and writes the keys to the paged cache.
- Top-K fusion is an extra path for many query rows, such as in prefill.
With `indexer_scores`, each query row and key gets an FP32 score, and a
Top-K kernel then reads all of them back: 64 GiB for 16K prefill tokens
over 1M keys. Top-K fusion writes only the keys that score above a
threshold:
1. `gather_key_sample` and `thresholds_from_sample` set a threshold for
each row from a key sample.
2. `indexer_threshold_select` keeps the keys that score above the
threshold. With `arrivals` and `ranges`, the result is exact for any
threshold.
3. `top_k_from_candidates` writes the Top-K keys of each row from the
kept keys.
- Removes `single_head_paged_mqa_logits`. `indexer_scores` replaces it.

Tested on GB200 (SM100): `tests/sdsa/` (90 passed), the trace tests
(1663 passed, 246 skipped) and the token-sparse tests (87 passed). On
H100, before the move into `flashinfer/sdsa/`: the SDSA, token-sparse
and trace tests (1187 passed, 165 skipped). Not tested on SM103.

I used AI assistance.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Replaces #6423, #6424 and #6425. Merge either this PR or those three.

### [3b40353](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3b40353b6418b4c3374df4fd1f52138c7b4bda6e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T19:20:22Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): 212-SM sm_107a router weight-gradient windows run the head/tail program with the A parts in tensor memory (#8517)

The `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` family has three
kinds of GEMM. They are BF16-input dense projection GEMMs, BF16-input
batched projection GEMMs, and an FP32 router GEMM (256 experts, BF16x3
emulation). Each kind has forward, input-gradient and weight-gradient
programs. `deterministic=True` (the default) calls
`dense_projection_det_gemm`. `deterministic=False` runs this package's
split-K / stream-K programs. This PR changes one variant: the router
weight gradient (FP32 out, 256 experts) on `sm_107a` parts with exactly
212 SMs, at 16172 to 16384 tokens.

At hidden 5120, this window already exists on FlashInfer main with plan
`"H0.5x4"` (106 head and 424 tail units). In that window,
`router_fp32_gemm_ts_r6p6_atomic_nn_t_ht_c2_nreg` replaces
`router_fp32_gemm_atomic_nn_t_ht_c3_nreg`. The new program is the
head/tail program that already ships for `sm_103a`. It keeps the three
BF16 parts of `A` in tensor memory. The partition, the products and
their accumulation order are unchanged.

At hidden 6144, this PR adds a new window with plan `"H0.5x4"`. That
window runs only the tensor-memory program. On FlashInfer main, this row
runs the deterministic program at 212 SMs.

`ROUTER_HEAD_TAIL_TEMPLATES_BY_SM` selects the program by SM count.
208-SM and 216-SM `sm_107a` parts keep their programs and plans.
`sm_100a` and `sm_103a` also keep their programs and plans. Hidden 4096
keeps the deterministic plan. The forward and input gradient are
unchanged.

These results are on R200, against FlashInfer main. Each range below
covers all runs. At hidden 5120:

- The router weight gradient gives det/new 1.299-1.360, previous/new
1.048-1.091 and SOTA/new 1.809-1.875.
- bwd gives det/new 1.130-1.191, previous/new 1.025-1.064 and SOTA/new
1.446-1.524.
- 2fwd+bwd gives det/new 1.057-1.084, previous/new 1.010-1.031 and
SOTA/new 1.732-1.807.

At hidden 6144:

- The router weight gradient gives det/new 1.147-1.201 and SOTA/new
1.827-1.915. Previous Cake runs the deterministic program here, so its
weight-gradient column equals det Cake.
- bwd gives det/new 1.042-1.100, previous/new 1.041-1.098 and SOTA/new
1.454-1.521.
- 2fwd+bwd gives det/new 1.015-1.043, previous/new 1.019-1.045 and
SOTA/new 1.706-1.840.

The forward runs the same program in every Cake arm. Its previous/new
ratio is 0.979-1.008 at hidden 5120 and 0.994-1.017 at hidden 6144.

An A/A control runs the new program against a second prepared copy of
itself. It ran in 6 of the runs at each hidden size. On the weight
gradient, it spans 0.994-1.009. On bwd, it spans 1.001-1.030 at hidden
5120 and 1.011-1.037 at hidden 6144. On 2fwd+bwd, it spans 0.994-1.010
at hidden 5120 and 0.941-1.009 at hidden 6144.

The weight-gradient and bwd gains over det Cake are larger than the A/A
spread. At hidden 5120 the previous Cake arm is also a separately
prepared copy, and the A/A control shows that such a copy can be up to 3
% slower on bwd. Against the second copy of the new program,
previous/new bwd is 1.007-1.038 (in the 6 A/A runs). So the hidden-5120
bwd previous/new ratios in the table (1.045-1.051) may be up to about 3
% too high. The hidden-5120 2fwd+bwd gain over det Cake is also larger
than the A/A spread. The hidden-5120 2fwd+bwd previous/new ratio
(1.010-1.031) is about as large as its A/A spread (0.994-1.010). At
hidden 6144, the 2fwd+bwd gain over both Cake baselines (1.015-1.045) is
smaller than its A/A spread (0.941-1.009). That row is parity with no
regression, not a measured gain.

- **Rows:** FP32 router GEMM, hidden 5120 and 6144, 256 experts, T
16172, 16231 and 16384 tokens (the windows this PR changes) on a 212-SM
`sm_107a` part. Ops are wgrad (router weight gradient, the changed op),
bwd (input gradient + weight gradient) and 2fwd+bwd (checkpointed step:
2 x forward + bwd). Modes are eager (calls of the prepared launches) and
graph (CUDA graph replays).
- **Latency:** The table reports median us of the op's GPU span from
CUPTI activity records.
- The span runs from the first kernel begin to the last kernel end of
every launch of the op. It includes the BF16x3 split and memset
launches.
- L2 is flushed before every iteration. Programmatic dependent launch is
at the package default.
- Hidden 5120 has 12 runs on four GPUs. Hidden 6144 has 10 runs on four
GPUs.
- Half of the runs use one long-lived process for all rows. The other
half use a fresh process per row in reverse row order.
- In each run, each arm runs 15 paired groups x 20 timed steps in
rotated arm order. The per-run cell is the median of the per-group
medians. A table cell is the median of the per-run cells.
- **Baselines:** det Cake = `deterministic=True`
(`dense_projection_det_gemm`).
- Previous Cake = `deterministic=False` on FlashInfer main. At hidden
5120, it runs `router_fp32_gemm_atomic_nn_t_ht_c3_nreg` at the same
plan. At hidden 6144, it runs the deterministic program, which is main's
plan for that row.
- SOTA (every GEMM of the op) = cuBLAS 13.8.0 `cublasSgemm` with
`CUBLAS_FP32_EMULATED_BF16X9_MATH`.
- Plain FP32 cuBLAS takes 1.80-2.71x the SOTA time on the hidden-5120
rows. TF32 and BF16 miss the router's FP32 accuracy budget. This makes
SOTA the strongest applicable library baseline.
- **Setup:** NVIDIA R200, `sm_107a`, 212 SMs, driver 620.43, CUDA 13.4
(nvcc 13.4.92), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, cuBLAS 13.8.0.
- The GPUs ran at their software power cap part of the time.
`nvidia-smi` was sampled every 200 ms only in 6 of the 12 hidden-5120
runs and 6 of the 10 hidden-6144 runs (the runs on two of the four
GPUs). It reported clock event reason 0x4 in 17-47 % of the non-idle
samples.
- In those samples, the median SM clock was 2388-2400 MHz (2424 MHz
maximum).
- A ratio is the quotient of the two us columns. A ratio above 1.00
means this PR is faster.
- **Accuracy:** The new program's relative Frobenius error against FP64
is within the 2e-6 budget. This holds in every run at both hidden sizes.

### [782a5fe](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/782a5fe5468cc62bd553499b7c758e3822705efa)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T18:52:41Z
- **提交信息**: cake batch DeepGEMM FP8: 256-byte L2 promotion on the A and B tensor maps of two masked programs (#8528)

FlashInfer ships 38 Cake programs for the masked batched FP8 GEMM (cake
batch DeepGEMM FP8). They take FP8 inputs with FP32 or packed UE8M0
block scales and come in six forms: masked BLOCK_N, swap-AB BLOCK_M,
static-K N=512, swap-AB M224, M32 serving, and two-CTA large N/K.

This PR updates two masked BLOCK_N programs. Each one now adds 256-byte
L2 promotion (`CU_TENSOR_MAP_L2_PROMOTION_L2_256B`) to its A and B TMA
tensor maps. The kernels themselves are unchanged. The new program names
are:

- `cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8_1f648c51c814b0a20548` ->
`cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8_44b779bf274c07ad013b` (sm_100a and sm_103a;
BLOCK_N 32, K tile 256)
- `cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8_967f03d4b4e131c6805e` ->
`cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8_8f1c2d0e26ca3d1d5b61` (sm_103a only; BLOCK_N
112)

Latencies are medians in microseconds. The baseline is the previous Cake

### [a44e732](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a44e7323fe21797184b6a711d6530314708215e7)

- **作者**: Zhihao Jia
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T18:45:40Z
- **提交信息**: Guard redundant same-value stores in norm, decode, and cascade kernels (#5740)

## Summary

Several kernels let every lane of a warp (or every thread of a thread
group) store the *same* reduced value to the *same* shared or global
location. The stores are benign in practice because the values are
identical, but they are unordered same-address writes from different
threads, they show up as data-race candidates under a race verifier, and
they issue up to 31 redundant stores per warp. This PR lets a single
thread perform each such store; there is no numerical change.

Sites changed:

- `include/flashinfer/norm.cuh`: `smem[ty] = sum_sq` after the
intra-warp `shfl_xor_sync` reduction and `smem[0] = sum_sq` after the
cross-warp reduction in `RMSNormKernel`, `RMSNormQuantKernel`,
`FusedAddRMSNormKernel`, `FusedAddRMSNormQuantKernel` and
`FusedAddRMSNormFP8BlockQuantKernel` (guarded by `tx == 0`).
- `include/flashinfer/attention/decode.cuh`: `sync_state` stores `st.m`
/ `st.d` to `smem_md` from every lane of the `(ty, tz)` group (guarded
by `tx == 0`); `SingleDecodeWithKVCacheKernel` stores the merged output
and `lse` from every `tz` group after `sync_state` (guarded by `tz ==
0`, matching what `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheKernel` and the MLA decode
kernel already do).
- `include/flashinfer/attention/cascade.cuh`: `threadblock_sync_state` /
`warp_sync_state` store `s_smem[ty]` from every lane (guarded by `tx ==
0`); `MergeStateKernel`, `MergeStateInPlaceKernel` and
`MergeStatesKernel` store the merged logsumexp from every `tx` thread of
a head slice (guarded by `tx == 0`);
`MergeStatesLargeNumIndexSetsKernel` and
`PersistentVariableLengthMergeStatesKernel` store it from every thread
of the block after `threadblock_sync_state` (guarded by `tx == 0 && ty
== 0`).

## Motivation

These were found by a PTX data-race verifier run on FlashInfer kernels
compiled for `sm_100a`: `FusedAddRMSNormKernel<8, bf16>`,
`SingleDecodeWithKVCacheKernel` (8 heads, kv_len 64) and
`MergeStateKernel<8, bf16, bf16>` each reported a `race_candidate` whose
witness was two lanes storing the same value to the same address with no
ordering between them (tracking issues: wmdi/wasp_verification#49, #50,
#52). With this patch all three kernels verify `race_free` with a
complete memory search on the same inputs; the decode kernel
additionally needed the `tz == 0` guard on the output store, which is
the only remaining difference from the batch decode kernel.

## Validation

- Compiled to PTX for `sm_100a` with nvcc 13.0 (explicit instantiations
of `RMSNorm`, `RMSNormQuant`, `QKRMSNorm`, `FusedAddRMSNorm`,
`FusedAddRMSNormQuant`, `FusedAddRMSNormFP8BlockQuant`, `MergeState`,
`MergeStateInPlace`, `MergeStates`, `VariableLengthMergeStates`, and the
JIT-rendered `single_decode` kernel).
- Re-verified the three kernels above with the race verifier:
`race_free`, zero warnings, memory search complete.
- I could not run the GPU unit tests on this machine (no
FlashInfer/torch install); `tests/utils/test_norm.py`,
`tests/attention/test_batch_decode_kernels.py` (single and batch decode)
and `tests/attention/test_shared_prefix_kernels.py` /
`tests/trace/test_merge_states_reference_correctness.py` (merge-state
kernels) cover the touched kernels and should pass unchanged since the
stored values are identical to before.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### [e5909c6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e5909c6e06179d3c73a31bcdb4e1b4701bf4a6e4)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T18:32:49Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_tinygemm2_wgmma): sm_90a routing extended to input features above 14336 (#8529)

`tinygemm_bf16` is a small-M bf16 GEMM (out = x @ W^T [+ bias]) with
four variants: with or without bias, each with or without programmatic
dependent launch (PDL). On sm_90a, host routing windows pick a generated
wgmma program (`cake_tinygemm2_wgmma`) for each shape. Other shapes use
the mma.sync reference `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. This PR changes only the
sm_90a host routing, for all four variants. The programs are unchanged.
Before this PR, the routing grid stopped at 14336 input features. Every
shape with more input features ran `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. The grid now
also covers 16384, 18432 and 20480 input features. Larger inputs keep
the reference. New windows send these shapes to existing programs. Most
go to PACKED_U4_IL_BOX3D. The others go to PACKED_S8_IL_BOX3D,
PACKED_S8_BOX3D, PACKED_U4_BOX3D, ACCUMULATORS_CN16,
ACCUMULATORS_CN32_BOX3D and CLUSTER_S8U8_C4. Some small-batch shapes
with up to 14336 input features (batches 3, 7, 14 and 15) also move to
CLUSTER_S8U8_C4, from the reference or from a packed tile. The window
count goes from 423 to 628. In a dense count, 1,753,402 shapes with bias
change routing: 1,751,162 above 14336 input features and 2,240 at or
below. Without bias, 1,754,053 shapes change: 1,751,799 above and 2,254
at or below. A window is added only if the new program meets three
conditions at every shape re-measured inside it. It is bit-identical to
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. It is at least 3% faster than `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`.
It is faster than the previous routing in every round, by at least the
larger of 0.5% and 40 ns. Above 14336 input features, the first
measurements also had to show at least 5% over the reference. Every
window that showed less than 5% on any H100 was re-measured at its
corners and midpoint on two more H100s, with and without bias and PDL.
It was kept only if it met the rule on both. Batches 13-16 with 256-383
output features and 18432 input features keep the reference, because
their margin over it differed most between H100s. The previous Cake
routing (#8417) also runs `csrc/tinygemm2.cu` above 14336 input
features, so the two speedups are nearly equal there. None of the
representative shapes changes program. All 16 shapes, with and without
bias and PDL, keep the #8417 program. On the table GPU, their speedup vs
#8417 is 0.997x to 1.016x with PDL off and 0.994x to 1.001x with PDL on.
This is noise between identical code. No representative row was slower
in every round on any of the three GPUs. The representative rows are
1.027x to 4.284x (PDL off) and 1.018x to 4.295x (PDL on) faster than
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. Each PDL mode has 179 re-routed rows. On the table
GPU, they are 1.040x to 6.492x faster than #8417 with PDL off and 1.041x
to 6.494x with PDL on. Each one is faster in all 7 rounds by the rule.
Against `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`, they are 1.045x to 6.492x (PDL off) and
1.042x to 6.494x (PDL on) faster. The largest gain is 64x4096x16384
without bias, PDL off. It drops from 358.013 us (`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`)
and 357.982 us (#8417) to 55.168 us on ACCUMULATORS_CN32_BOX3D. The
smallest margin is 4x400x20480 with bias, PDL on. It drops from 12.736
us on both baselines to 12.224 us on PACKED_U4_IL_BOX3D.

*NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (SXM, 132 SMs), sm_90a, CUDA 13.4 toolkit (nvcc
13.4.92, torch 2.14.1+cu130). Median CUPTI kernel time, cold L2, 7
interleaved rounds x 200 iterations. The arm order was rotated and
reversed between rounds. All three arms (`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`, #8417,
this PR) were measured in the same process on the same GPU. Every row on
all three GPUs is bit-identical to `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. The "#8417"
column is FlashInfer main after #8417. The `csrc/tinygemm2.cu` column is
current main. The tables come from one H100. Two more H100s were
measured the same way. On each of them, all 358 re-routed rows were
faster than #8417 in all 7 rounds by the rule. Their speedups vs #8417
were 1.033x to 6.500x with PDL off and 1.040x to 6.503x with PDL on. The
representative rows were 1.017x to 4.287x faster than
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. In the "Program" column, "(unchanged)" means the
same program as #8417. "X -> Y" gives the #8417 program and then this
PR's program. X is "csrc/tinygemm2.cu" when #8417 used the reference.
The re-routed rows for each PDL mode are in a collapsed section.*

The Cake tinygemm2 family also ships tcgen05 programs for sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a (Blackwell), and this PR touches only the sm_90a
wgmma routing.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [3986928](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/39869289b6cdf6b64a517fa572851f217e41899c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T18:11:54Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_cp): int32 cu_seqlens Stage-1 program for FP16 CP prefill on sm_107a (up to 1.05x) (#8523)

Cake's Gated DeltaNet (GDN) context-parallel (CP) prefill kernel in
FlashInfer has six variants: BF16 and FP16 I/O on each of sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR changes the sm_107a FP16 variant, only for
calls with int32 `cu_seqlens`. Before, the host cast the int32 prefix
sums to int64. Then the int64 Stage-1 (T-precompute) program ran. Now, a
dedicated Stage-1 program reads the int32 prefix sums directly. This
program also writes the int64 copy that later stages use. It is built
with 6 CTAs per SM, the same bound as the sm_107a int64 program. Outputs
and final state are bitwise identical to main on every measured shape.
Calls with int64 `cu_seqlens` are unchanged. The baseline is the
previous Cake version on FlashInfer main. On 47 FP16 shapes, this PR is
faster than that baseline on every shape. The eager geomean speedup is
1.020x, and the per-shape range is 1.002x to 1.046x. The CUDA graph
geomean speedup is 1.012x, and the per-shape range is 1.001x to 1.027x.
Versus `backend="flashinfer"` (eager), this PR is faster on every shape.
That geomean speedup is 1.239x, and the lowest is 1.138x.

GPU: NVIDIA R200 (216 SMs), sm_107a, driver 615.71.10. Kernels
JIT-compiled with CUDA 13.4; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. FP16 inputs and
outputs, FP32 initial and final state, int32 `cu_seqlens`, head size
128. Time = median CUPTI span of one CP prefill call (first kernel start
to last kernel end) with a cold L2, mean of seeds 17 and 29. Previous
Cake, this PR and an A/A control run interleaved on the same GPU. new =
this PR. eager = synchronized single calls; CUDA graph = back-to-back
graph replays. speedup = previous Cake / this PR (above 1 = this PR
faster). backend="flashinfer" =
`chunk_gated_delta_rule(backend="flashinfer")`, eager.

### [a1b4ed3](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a1b4ed390c56ea5df8770710b29f16649acdd905)

- **作者**: yonglai24
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T17:28:14Z
- **提交信息**: fix(sampling): remove CUDA 11.8 FlagHeads fallback (#5124)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re
needed. -->

The FlagHeads branch in DeviceSamplingFromProb was added in #265 to
support CUDA 11.8, whose bundled CUB predates SubtractLeft. FlashInfer's
minimum supported CUDA is now 12.9 and CI covers cu129/cu130 only, so
the condition the fallback was written for can no longer occur.

The guard selecting it is also keyed on the wrong thing:
__CUDACC_VER_MAJOR__/MINOR describes the compiler, but the availability
of SubtractLeft vs FlagHeads is a property of the CUB headers on the
include path. FlashInfer bundles its own CCCL and adds it with -I while
the CUDA toolkit's own headers go in with -isystem
(jit/cpp_ext.py:build_common_cflags), so the vendored copy deliberately
takes precedence over the CTK-bundled one — and the compiler version
therefore tells you nothing about which CUB you are compiling against.
On nvcc < 12.1 the macro goes undefined and FlagHeads is emitted against
bundled CCCL, where the public overloads were removed in CCCL 3.0,
producing a compile failure that names neither the real cause nor the
unsupported toolkit.

SubtractLeft is present in every CUB tested here, down to 2.0.1 -- well
below the CCCL version shipped with CUDA 12.9, the minimum supported
toolkit. Removing the fallback deletes code unreachable on every
supported configuration and additionally lets nvcc 12.0 compile rather
than fail.

### Verification

One source file (`probe.cu`, below), API branch selected explicitly via
`-D`, only the CUB headers on the include path varied:

| nvcc | CUB / CCCL headers | Source | `FlagHeads` | `SubtractLeft` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12.0.140 | CUB 2.0.1 | Ubuntu `libcub-dev`, `/usr/include` | pass
(deprecated) | pass |
| 12.0.140 | CCCL 3.0.0 | `NVIDIA/cccl` tag `v3.0.0` | **fail** | pass |
| 12.0.140 | CCCL 3.0.3 | `NVIDIA/cccl` tag `v3.0.3` | **fail** | pass |
| 12.0.140 | CCCL 3.3.2 | wheel, `flashinfer-python` 0.6.18.post1 |
**fail** | pass |
| 13.3.73 | CCCL 3.3.2 | wheel, `flashinfer-python` 0.6.18.post1 |
**fail** | pass |
| 12.0.140 | CCCL 3.6.0 | `3rdparty/cccl` submodule at `main` | **fail**
| pass |

`FlagHeads` is deprecated in CUB 2.0.1 and absent from CCCL 3.0.0
onward; `SubtractLeft` compiles across the entire range, including CUB
2.0.1 — older than anything reachable under the CUDA 12.9 floor. In CCCL
3.6.0 a `FlagHeads` symbol survives at
`block_adjacent_difference.cuh:155`, but it is a private helper taking
`int linear_tid` and is not the public overload this code calls, so the
fallback cannot be repaired — only removed.

Error signature (nvcc 12.0.140, bundled CCCL 3.6.0, before this change):

```
include/flashinfer/sampling.cuh(623): error:
class "cub::_V_300600_SM_860::BlockAdjacentDifference<__nv_bool, 128, 1, 1>"
has no member "FlagHeads"
    detected during instantiation of
    "void flashinfer::sampling::DeviceSamplingFromProb<...>"
```

After this change, `sampling.cuh` compiles under both nvcc 12.0.140 and
13.3.73 against bundled CCCL 3.6.0.

<details>
<summary><code>probe.cu</code> — minimal reproduction</summary>

```cuda
#include <cub/cub.cuh>

struct BoolDiffOp {
  __device__ __forceinline__ bool operator()(const bool &a, const bool &b) const {
    return a != b;
  }
};

constexpr int BLOCK_THREADS = 128;
constexpr int VEC_SIZE = 4;

__global__ void probe(bool *out) {
  using BAD = cub::BlockAdjacentDifference<bool, BLOCK_THREADS>;
  __shared__ typename BAD::TempStorage tmp;
  bool in[VEC_SIZE] = {true, false, true, false};
  bool diff[VEC_SIZE];
#ifdef USE_SUBTRACTLEFT
  BAD(tmp).SubtractLeft<VEC_SIZE>(in, diff, BoolDiffOp());
#else
  BAD(tmp).template FlagHeads<VEC_SIZE>(diff, in, BoolDiffOp(), 0);
#endif
  out[threadIdx.x] = diff[0];
}
```

Compile with and without `-DUSE_SUBTRACTLEFT`, varying `-I` to select
the header set:

```bash
nvcc -ccbin g++-12 -arch=sm_86 $INC -c probe.cu -o /dev/null
nvcc -ccbin g++-12 -arch=sm_86 $INC -c probe.cu -o /dev/null -DUSE_SUBTRACTLEFT
```

</details>

## 🔍 Related Issues

<!-- Link any related issues here -->

- #265 introduced the `FlagHeads` fallback in May 2024 to support CUDA
11.8, closing #261 (the same `has no member` compile failure, in the
opposite direction: `SubtractLeft` missing on CUB 1.x). #410 was a
follow-up cu118 CUB fix.
- #4763 reports the same failure and fixes it by preferring system
CUB/Thrust over the bundled CCCL in `env.py`. This PR fixes the version
predicate instead, so the two are alternatives rather than complements —
deferring to maintainers on which is preferable. I raised the root cause
there before opening this.

One clarification for anyone comparing the two reports: #4763's
description says "bundled CCCL 3.0.3", but the pasted error names
`cub::_V_300302_SM_890`. Per the `MMMmmmpp` encoding documented in
`cub/version.cuh`, `300302` decodes as 3.3.2 — the same version reported
here, not 3.0.3. (For contrast, `_V_300003` in the table above really is
3.0.3.)

### [bd0c0d3](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/bd0c0d3d80767958528b2e3f44b799cb779e0ede)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T17:27:34Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): run the half-tail TMA-store program on the sm_103a 5120 x 17408 weight gradients at T 16231 / 16384 (#8522)

This PR adds and updates row rules in the Cake
`dense_projection_det_gemm` package in `flashinfer.experimental`, the
deterministic dense projection GEMM. The package has 127 programs built
from 124 templates, and this PR leaves both counts unchanged. Most
programs are BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and wgrad), and one is
an FP32 router GEMM. The PR changes 3 row rules, all for `sm_103a`, and
each applies at a single token count T. It adds one rule for the
5120→17408 weight gradient at T 16231. The other two are the empty
`sm_103a` keys for the 17408→5120 weight gradient at T 16231 and 16384.
The previous PR added those keys to keep that row's plan unchanged, and
this PR gives them a real rule. All three rules route BF16-output
weight-gradient rows to a program that already ships: the half-tail
program with a TMA-store epilogue and 12-row raster groups. No program
or template is added or removed, the rule count goes from 366 to 367,
and `sm_100a` and `sm_107a` are unchanged.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of the package on main.
Against it, the changed rows have a speedup of 1.013 on GB300 for all
three rows and 1.042–1.045 on B300. No changed row is slower on either
GPU, and outputs on those rows are bitwise identical to main. All other
rows of the 294-row shape list plan the same programs as main.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB300
(`sm_103a`, 152 SMs), B300 (`sm_103a`, 148 SMs); CUDA 13.4, cold L2,
BF16 output. Speedup = previous time / this PR time, and values above 1
mean this PR is faster.

### [670912f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/670912f6d27644d9b783d2f7bd9c42a2d956ab7b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T17:22:34Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_causal_conv1d): opt-in SM reserve for the non-deterministic KCP autograd backward (#8501)

Related issue: #8065. Tracker: #6595.

`cake_causal_conv1d` has three training backwards: single-rank `bwd`,
single-rank `bwd_fp32g`, and the context-parallel (KCP) backward. Each
has a deterministic and a non-deterministic variant. This PR adds an
opt-in keyword, `bwd_reserve_sms`, to the non-deterministic KCP autograd
backward on sm_100a and sm_103a. With `bwd_reserve_sms=1` (R1 in the
tables), the main backward launches one SM's CTAs fewer. It therefore
stays in one wave when a small kernel on another stream holds an SM (the
#8365 case). Without the keyword (the default), it runs the same kernels
and grids as main. On sm_107a the keyword raises `ValueError`, because
its unloaded cost there reached 1.055x (C1024 / T62585).

The PR also adds `cooperative: Optional[bool] = None` to the
selectable-mode KCP facade. The facade again takes the deterministic KCP
facade's keywords (#8459), and
`test_facade_signatures_mirror_the_packages` passes again.

Backward kernel time with a side kernel (CUPTI):

- **vs ND main:** with a side kernel, ND main falls into a second wave
and R1 does not. ND main / new R1 = 1.316-1.387 on the side-load rows of
C1024, C4096 and C8192, on all three GPUs. Example: B200, C8192 /
T16384, 2 ms side kernel: ND main 257.0 us, new R1 185.4 us (1.386).
C10240 already fits on main (0.995-1.001 across GPUs).
- **vs deterministic Cake:** under side load, det / new R1 = 1.010-1.035
(B200), 0.992-1.124 (GB200), 1.002-1.135 (GB300). Over all rows, det
coopF / new R1 = 1.007-1.061 (B200), 1.007-1.083 (GB200), 0.996-1.070
(GB300).
- **vs SOTA (fla_cp_triton):** SOTA / new R1 = 4.348-5.685 (B200),
4.278-5.636 (GB200), 4.488-5.761 (GB300).

**How to read the tables.**

- **Workload:** KCP backward, one rank, contiguous layout, 4 shapes (C /
T / docs). Conditions are unloaded and side load. Side load is one
1-thread spin kernel on a second stream, launched just before the
backward, that runs for 2 ms or 4 ms ("side 1x2 ms" / "side 1x4 ms").
- **CUPTI tables:** for each iteration, the sum of the backward's kernel
durations, excluding the spin kernel. Median of 30, in us.
- **CUDA-event tables:** event time around the backward. Each iteration
runs a fresh forward, which is not timed. Median of 30 after 5 warm-up
iterations, in ms.
- Eager mode, warm caches. Ratios are baseline / new, so a ratio above 1
means the new arm is faster.
- **Arms:**
  - `det`: deterministic Cake KCP at its default (cooperative launch).
  - `det coopF`: deterministic Cake with `cooperative=False` (#8459).
- `fla_cp_triton`: fla 0.6.0 `causal_conv1d(..., cp_context=...,
backend='triton')` (deterministic FP32 per-chunk partials). It is the
strongest eligible non-Cake arm on every row ("SOTA").
  - `ND main`: non-deterministic FlashInfer main.
  - `new default`: this PR without the keyword.
  - `new R1`: this PR with `bwd_reserve_sms=1`.
- **Software:** PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0 runtime), nvcc 13.4,
triton 3.8.0.

**Default-path cost (keyword absent).** ND main / new default =
0.977-1.003 on all CUPTI rows. The kernels and grids are the same as
main, so this range is run-to-run spread. Host cost per call vs main, at
C128, 4100 tokens, one rank ("step" = forward + backward, "ckpt" =
checkpointed):

- B200: step +0.5 us [95 % CI -1.0, +2.8], ckpt +2.3 us [+1.0, +3.8].
Main's host time per call in the same runs: 601 us (step), 1023 us
(ckpt).
- GB200: step +0.9 us [+0.5, +1.1], ckpt +0.9 us [+0.0, +1.7]. Main's
host time per call in the same runs: 367 us (step), 797 us (ckpt).

Per call, the default path executes 14 (step) / 22 (ckpt) more Python
bytecode instructions and makes no extra Python or C calls.

**Cost of R1 without a side kernel.** On the unloaded rows, ND main /
new R1 = 0.992-1.005 (B200), 0.974-1.046 (GB200), 0.977-1.057 (GB300).
The worst rows are at C8192 / T16384. On GB200, ND main takes 174.0 us
and new R1 takes 178.7 us (0.974). On GB300, ND main takes 166.0 us and
new R1 takes 170.0 us (0.977). A wider unloaded sweep of KCP shapes
(median of 11 rounds) found a largest R1 cost of 1.016x (B200), 1.027x
(GB200) and 1.030x (GB300), each at C8192 / T250340. That is why the
keyword is opt-in.

**CUDA-event tables.** In these runs the eager backward is
host-launch-bound. On B200 the Cake arms' event times are 0.37-0.75 ms,
while their kernels take 57-400 us. The exceptions are det under side
load (below) and two 0.15-0.17 ms values of the new tree at C1024
unloaded. So the event ratios mostly show host-time spread. We repeated
the default-vs-main comparison on another GPU with the arm order
reversed; the repeat table shows the results:

- B200: 0.930-0.960, except C1024: 0.540 / 1.301 / 1.041 (unloaded / 2
ms / 4 ms)
- GB200: 0.979-1.022
- GB300: 0.984-1.012

The B200 C1024 / T31292 unloaded event row is not a speedup. It reads ND
main 0.5426 ms and new default 0.1523 ms (shown as 3.563). The kernel
times on that row are 57.8 us (ND main) and 57.9 us (new default), and
the repeat reads 0.540.

Under side load, det (cooperative) reads 2.0-4.3 ms on B200 because a
cooperative launch waits for the side kernel. det coopF and the
non-deterministic arms do not wait.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Added optional `cooperative` and `bwd_reserve_sms` settings to single-
and multi-tensor KCP convolution APIs.
* `bwd_reserve_sms` lets non-deterministic backward operations reserve
GPU streaming multiprocessors. The default is zero; positive values can
reduce the available backward work and are subject to device and
workload limits.

* Added validation for unsupported option values and combinations, with
clear errors for invalid settings. Deterministic-algorithm mode
continues to use the deterministic backend.
