### [728a748](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/728a74876dd25afd0fc68886e3ccd742f4afd512)

- **作者**: Sam
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T17:05:28Z
- **提交信息**: fix(quantization): make the FP8 NVFP4 TMA quantize path encode and cover whole column chunks (#6276)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`nvfp4_quantize(x, global_sf, backend="cuda")` with `float8_e4m3fn`
input, `m >= 1024` and `n % 512 == 0` is routed to the TMA quantize
kernel. Every such call fails:

RuntimeError: [TensorRT-LLM][ERROR] Assertion failed: Failed to encode
TMA tensor map
    (csrc/nv_internal/cpp/kernels/quantization.cu:344)

There are two bugs on this path. Both date from the original TMA change
(#2343).

**1. Invalid OOB fill for FP8.** `make_3d_tma_copy_desc` encodes FP8 as
`CU_TENSOR_MAP_DATA_TYPE_UINT8`, but it requests
`CU_TENSOR_MAP_FLOAT_OOB_FILL_NAN_REQUEST_ZERO_FMA`. `cuda.h` says this
fill "can only be used when tensorDataType represents a floating-point
data type". The CUDA 12.0 header already has the same note. Calling
`cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` directly with the kernel's arguments returns
`CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` with this fill and `CUDA_SUCCESS` with
`OOB_FILL_NONE`. The kernel never uses out-of-bound elements, because
consumer warps skip rows `>= numRows` and columns `>= numCols`. The
descriptor now uses `OOB_FILL_NONE` for every input type.

**2. Wrong column chunk in the FP8 dispatch.** Dispatch hardcoded
`TMA_COL_CHUNK = 8 * 64 = 512`, which is the half/bf16 value. FP8 uses
`TMA_COL_TILE = 128`, so the kernel walks `n` in 1024-column chunks.
When `n` is 512 or 1536, warps 4–7 of the last chunk have `colIdx >= n`.
They write zero scale-factor "padding" at out-of-range offsets, which
overwrites other rows' scale factors and writes past the end of the
buffer. Bug 1 has hidden this until now.

`TMA_COL_CHUNK = NUM_CONSUMER_WARPS * TMA_COL_TILE` now lives in
`TmaKernelTraits`, and both dispatch branches read it. A branch can
therefore take the TMA path only for whole chunks. Half/bf16 keep their
512-column threshold, so their behavior does not change. FP8 shapes
where `n` is an odd multiple of 512 now use the non-TMA kernel.

No FP8 test reached this path before: every shape in `NVFP4_FP8_SHAPES`
has `m <= 512`.

## 🔍 Related Issues

I found no related upstream issue. #3831 changes the `alignas` on the
tensor map in the same function. The lines are adjacent, but the changes
do not overlap in meaning.

New test: `test_nvfp4_quantize_fp8_tma_matches_non_tma` in
`tests/utils/test_fp4_quantize.py`. It compares the CUDA-backend result
bitwise against the same input run in 512-row blocks, which stay on the
non-TMA kernel. It covers m ∈ {1024, 4096} × n ∈ {512, 1024, 1536,
2048}, for all three SF layouts.

Results:

| GPU (SM) | Driver / CUDA toolkit | `main` | OOB fill fix only | This
PR | `test_fp4_quantize.py` (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B200 (SM100) | 580.95.05 / 12.9 | 18 failed (TMA encode error) | not
run | 18 passed | 10583 passed |
| Thor (SM110) | 580.00 (Tegra) / 13.0 | 18 failed (TMA encode error) |
not run | 18 passed | 10583 passed |
| RTX 5080 (SM120) | 580.173.02 / 13.3 | 18 failed (TMA encode error) |
12 failed (n = 512, 1536: scale-factor mismatch), 6 passed | 18 passed |
10583 passed |

On all three GPUs, calling `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` directly with the
kernel's FP8 arguments returns `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` with
`NAN_REQUEST_ZERO_FMA` and `CUDA_SUCCESS` with `OOB_FILL_NONE`, for n =
512, 1024 and 2048.

Outside the test suite, I also compared the fixed TMA path against
`backend="cute-dsl"`. Scale factors match bitwise. About 1.4% of FP4
bytes differ, and the non-TMA CUDA kernel differs from cute-dsl at the
same rate. This is the existing difference between the two backends, and
the existing FP8 parity test allows it with a >95% match threshold.

- **Not verified:** SM103 and SM121 hardware, and drivers older than the

### [9277542](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/927754255ec1061308c7eab20a07b0ba8c076992)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T17:04:10Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_alpha_moe): keep all-NaN rows in range in the generic fused router (#8519)

The generic fused-router kernels in AlphaMoE (`csrc/alphamoe_router`
tiny, small, medium, large and their `_routed` variants) take the
per-route maximum with `fmaxf`, which drops NaN. When every logit in a
row is NaN, no expert matches. Every route lane then keeps an
out-of-range expert index equal to the maximum expert count. The plan
step counts that index and writes expert counts and local offsets past
the end of their buffers. On the previous code, compute-sanitizer
memcheck reports invalid 4-byte global writes on these inputs (30 on
B200 and 38 on GB300 over the NaN test set). The sorted token ids can
also differ from run to run. Rows without NaN never take this path.

The route loop is unchanged. After it runs, a route lane that still
holds an out-of-range expert takes the expert equal to its route index
and a +inf logit. An all-NaN row therefore selects experts 0..top_k-1
with NaN weights, and the plan stays in bounds. The new
`test_alphamoe_fused_router_nan_rows` checks this, and memcheck reports
no invalid writes. Rows without NaN produce bitwise identical top-k ids,
weights and routing plans. All finite test cases were checked bitwise
against the previous code on B200 and GB300. One limitation remains: a
row that is only partly NaN, with fewer finite logits than top_k, can
repeat an in-range expert, and NaN logits are not ranked in such rows.
Full NaN ranking for the generic kernels is not part of this PR.

This is a correctness fix, not a speedup. The tables give kernel time
per router call in microseconds, which is the sum of the router's
kernels in one call measured with CUPTI. Runs were on NVIDIA B200
(sm_100a) and GB300 (sm_103a) with CUDA 13.3 (NVRTC), driver 580.159.03
on GB300. "Previous" is FlashInfer main before this PR, and "this PR" is
the same tree with the fix. Both come from paired, interleaved runs on
the same GPU. Each shape is timed with two L2 flush modes: "memset"
makes L2 cold with a memset of a large buffer, and "read" flushes L2 by
reading a large buffer. The previous and this PR columns are medians
over runs on one node (B200: 4 runs, GB300: 8 runs). The ratio column is
the median over runs of this PR / previous, so values above 1 mean
slower. The last column is the same ratio on a second node of the same

means one shared expert inside top_k. There are 88 comparisons (11

within the same-node noise band, measured by running the previous code

1.003x to 1.007x in all 8 cells.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
* Improved mixture-of-experts routing for inputs containing NaN values.
When routing cannot select a valid expert, the affected route now falls
back to an in-range expert, helping prevent invalid routing results for
all-NaN rows and other rows with no eligible selection.
* Valid expert selections continue to use the existing routing and
weighting behavior.

### [18d8a03](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/18d8a0341668866b2ae32c002ee0ddafb6543c2b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T16:40:20Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_softmax): low-latency shared-tile kernels at every wave count on sm_100 (#8513)

The Cake Blackwell FP32 softmax behind `flashinfer.sampling.softmax`
sends each shape to one of several kernels. #8449 added low-latency
forms of the shared-tile kernels, `c8_t4_s4_lat` and `c16_t4_s4_lat`,
with PDL twins. It used them only when the batch fits in at most two
waves of resident shared-tile clusters, because on GB300 larger grids
run faster with the existing shared-tile kernels. On B200 the
low-latency kernels are also faster past two waves. This PR makes sm_100
take the low-latency form at every batch size. sm_103 (GB300) and sm_107
keep the two-wave limit, so their kernel choice is unchanged. Only host
dispatch changes. The kernels are unchanged, and the outputs are bitwise
identical to main. On B200, the changed shapes run 1.015x to 1.050x
faster than main. The 32 x 151936 row already used the low-latency
kernel on main. The 32 x 128000 row takes a different kernel. Both rows
use unchanged paths and show parity.

**B200 (sm_100a)**, FP32 logits, temperature 1.0, CUDA 13.4, median of
16 runs (µs).

| batch x vocab | main | this PR | speedup vs main |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 x 151936 | 11.200 | 11.176 | 1.002x |
| 64 x 151936 | 18.528 | 17.672 | 1.048x |
| 96 x 151936 | 24.768 | 23.584 | 1.050x |
| 128 x 151936 | 30.616 | 29.328 | 1.044x |
| 180 x 151936 | 40.039 | 38.608 | 1.037x |
| 256 x 151936 | 53.344 | 51.736 | 1.031x |
| 512 x 151936 | 99.568 | 97.696 | 1.019x |
| 1024 x 151936 | 190.904 | 188.063 | 1.015x |
| 32 x 128000 | 9.040 | 9.048 | 0.999x |
| 96 x 128000 | 17.520 | 17.448 | 1.004x |

The other kernels in the family are unchanged: the warp kernel, the
row-wise kernel, the cached-cluster row kernels (1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 12 or
16 CTAs per row) and the persistent cached-cluster kernel. The family
covers sm_100a (B200), sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Performance**
* Updated GPU execution-path selection for Blackwell hardware. On GB300,
workloads spanning more than two waves now favor the shared-tile path,
while smaller workloads favor the low-latency path. On B200, the
low-latency path is selected at every wave count. Other architectures
retain the existing two-wave threshold.

### [14e9e7b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/14e9e7b771373ceb92bd1d0b297edf556c9fd0b2)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T16:30:13Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_lm_head_loss): zero-gradient row skip for the log-probability backward with a temperature (#8514)

Cake's chunked LM-head + loss training backend has a deterministic form
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake_lm_head_det_loss`, the default) and a
non-deterministic (ND) form
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_loss`,
`deterministic=False`). The ND log-probability backward skips rows whose
log-probability gradient (dlogp) is zero (#8268; sm_107a in #8492), but
the temperature entry (scalar or per-token FP32 `[T]`, #8436) ran
without the skip. This PR runs the skip with a temperature too, on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a: the counted dX / dW programs skip the zero
rows, and the temperature dz recompute still covers all rows; no kernel
program changes. At z = 0.5 (half the valid rows have zero dlogp) and T
>= 4097, the new ND backward is 1.113x-1.419x (B200), 1.287x-1.420x
(GB300) and 1.264x-1.518x (R200) faster than skip-off ND, and
1.116x-1.420x, 1.290x-1.422x and 1.268x-1.531x vs deterministic Cake. At
z = 0, new ND is at parity or inconclusive vs both, and 1.045x-1.155x,
1.045x-1.197x and 1.061x-1.370x vs non-Cake SOTA, the fastest
exact-semantics PyTorch temperature implementation.

- **B200.** Skip-off ND (T >= 4097, z = 0.166 / 0.5): bwd 1.046x-1.099x
/ 1.113x-1.419x, ckpt 1.026x-1.063x / 1.056x-1.223x, all ND faster.
Deterministic Cake (same): bwd 1.051x-1.097x / 1.116x-1.420x, ckpt
1.027x-1.062x / 1.058x-1.222x, all ND faster. Non-Cake SOTA (same): bwd
1.121x-1.166x / 1.185x-1.499x, ckpt 1.110x-1.157x / 1.145x-1.330x. At z
= 0: skip-off ND 0.988x-1.006x (22 parity, 10 inconclusive),
deterministic Cake 0.982x-1.007x (22 parity, 10 inconclusive), non-Cake
SOTA 1.045x-1.155x (32/32 ND faster).
- **GB300.** Skip-off ND (T >= 4097, z = 0.166 / 0.5): bwd 1.054x-1.103x
/ 1.287x-1.420x, ckpt 1.034x-1.062x / 1.147x-1.211x, all ND faster.
Deterministic Cake (same): bwd 1.057x-1.106x / 1.290x-1.422x, ckpt
1.034x-1.063x / 1.149x-1.214x. Non-Cake SOTA (z = 0.166 / 0.5): bwd
1.146x-1.187x / 1.404x-1.520x, ckpt 1.149x-1.182x / 1.268x-1.357x. At z
= 0: skip-off ND 0.992x-1.002x (29 parity, 3 inconclusive),
deterministic Cake 0.995x-1.006x (30 parity, 2 inconclusive), non-Cake
SOTA 1.045x-1.197x (31 ND faster, 1 inconclusive).
- **R200.** Skip-off ND (T >= 4097, z = 0.166 / 0.5): bwd 1.012x-1.122x
/ 1.264x-1.518x, ckpt 1.013x-1.064x / 1.142x-1.259x; z = 0.5 all ND
faster; z = 0.166 bwd 3 ND faster, 2 inconclusive, 2 parity, ckpt 3 ND
faster, 4 inconclusive. Deterministic Cake (same): bwd 1.011x-1.126x /
1.268x-1.531x, ckpt 1.016x-1.065x / 1.139x-1.263x. Non-Cake SOTA (z =
0.166 / 0.5): bwd 1.122x-1.218x / 1.398x-1.633x, ckpt 1.169x-1.230x /
1.332x-1.441x. At z = 0: skip-off ND 0.977x-1.064x (22 parity, 10
inconclusive), deterministic Cake 0.985x-1.018x (21 parity, 11
inconclusive), non-Cake SOTA 1.061x-1.370x (29 ND faster, 1 parity, 2
inconclusive).
- No cell on any GPU is 'ND slower' vs any baseline.

**Method (all GPUs).** Log-probability with a temperature, H = 6144, V =
154880, BF16, chunk 4096, 5 % ignored rows. Per-token temperature at T =
2048, 4096, 8117, 16172, 16231, 32463, 65031; scalar temperature 0.7 at
T = 16231. z = fraction of valid rows with zero dlogp: 0, 0.166 and 0.5
(random rows), plus whole groups of 512 rows at T = 16231. The skip
applies from 4097 valid rows, so T = 2048 and 4096 run the skip-off path
by design. Ops: fwd, bwd, fwd+bwd, ckpt (2xfwd+bwd). Arms, timed in the
same steps: new ND (skip on), skip-off ND (same head, skip off),
deterministic Cake (same build), and non-Cake SOTA, per cell the fastest
of (c) chunked + torch.compile, (e) chunked eager and (u) unchunked
autograd; (e) and (u) were timed at z = 0 only because their work does
not depend on z. Cut Cross-Entropy has no temperature argument. Kernels
built with CUDA 13.4; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0 runtime); state
cooled. Latency = median over steps of the per-step median CUPTI GPU
span. Speedup = baseline latency / new ND latency (> 1 = new ND faster);
CI95 = hierarchical bootstrap. Verdict 'ND faster' / 'ND slower' only
when the CI95 lies wholly outside 1 ± band (band = max(1 %, A/A floor);
A/A = the new ND arm timed twice) and every step agrees; 'parity' when
wholly inside; else 'inconclusive'. Only the 'vs skip-off ND' column
shows the CI95; the other two columns show the ratio and the verdict.

**B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), driver 580.82.07, CUDA 13.4 (PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130).** One node, 2 steps; the 4 per-token cells at T = 32463,
z = 0 use a third step after one step lost them. Measured on a build
whose package and Python files are identical to the PR head. Example,
per-token T = 16231, z = 0.5, bwd: new ND 40.463 ms, skip-off ND 55.386
ms, deterministic Cake 55.283 ms, non-Cake SOTA 59.246 ms (c).

and ragged candidate-support log-probabilities / KL. Both ship on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Performance**
* Temperature-enabled log-probability calculations can now skip rows
with zero gradients in selected backward computations, potentially
reducing unnecessary work.
* **Behavior**
* Temperature values remain aligned with rows when processing order
changes. Weight-gradient results may vary slightly when zero-gradient
rows are skipped, while remaining within the documented accuracy
budgets.
* **Documentation**
* Clarified which computations skip zero-gradient rows and how
temperature-enabled calls handle row ordering and numerical results.

### [1c4d65b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1c4d65b7c8ef758e5b483c1e7056f888b57a86a8)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T16:21:02Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe_v3): faster TP4 / TP8 EP1 T128, T512, T1024, TP8 EP1 T4096 and TP4 EP4 T4096 rank programs on sm_103a (#8515)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline for the 384-expert, top-6, hidden-5120 model with activation
clamp 10. A single kernel launch covers dispatch, FC1, clamped SwiGLU,
MXFP8 activation quantization, FC2 and weighted combine. The kernel has
four variants on main, and this PR updates one of them: the TP/EP rank
variant. It changes 8 of the variant's 32 programs: TP4 EP1 and TP8 EP1
(384 experts) at 128, 512 and 1024 tokens, TP8 EP1 at 4096 tokens, and
TP4 EP4 (96 local experts) at 4096 tokens.

In each of these programs, every CTA now computes the prefix of the
per-expert token counts itself. Its scheduler starts as soon as that
local prefix is ready. Before, it waited for a prefix that one CTA
published for all of them.

The outputs are bitwise identical to the previous version. No host
binding changes. The catalog closure hashes of the 32 rank programs
change. The baseline is the previous Cake version on main, which is the
rank variant as last updated by #8458. For replicates a / b, the
speedups for the changed programs are:

- TP4 EP1 at 128 tokens: 1.010x / 1.009x, saving 2.89 / 2.64 µs per call
- TP4 EP1 at 512 tokens: 1.009x / 1.009x, saving 2.82 / 2.82 µs per call
- TP4 EP1 at 1024 tokens: 1.008x / 1.007x, saving 2.53 / 2.30 µs per
call
- TP8 EP1 at 128 tokens: 1.016x / 1.015x, saving 2.81 / 2.60 µs per call
- TP8 EP1 at 512 tokens: 1.016x / 1.016x, saving 2.96 / 2.94 µs per call
- TP8 EP1 at 1024 tokens: 1.012x / 1.013x, saving 2.44 / 2.66 µs per
call
- TP8 EP1 at 4096 tokens: 1.008x / 1.008x, saving 2.41 / 2.44 µs per
call
- TP4 EP4 at 4096 tokens: 1.003x / 1.003x, saving 1.07 / 1.16 µs per
call

All eight changes are faster than the A/A noise band in both replicates.
The other 24 programs run 0.999x to 1.001x in replicate a and 0.997x to
1.003x in replicate b.

*NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, driver 580.159.03, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130. Per-call latency comes from CUDA-graph replays (20 calls
per graph), taking the median of 21 in-process rounds. The previous
version and this PR ran in separate processes, alternating over 6
rounds. Each value is the median of the 6 process medians. Speedup =
previous / this PR, computed from the latencies before rounding to two
decimals. Columns a and b are two independent replicates, each run alone
on its own node. Each replicate also timed the previous version against
itself (an A/A control) to measure its noise band. The widest band is
0.21 % in replicate a and 0.22 % in replicate b. The other 24 programs
are re-rendered from the current generator. Their kernel text changes
only in comment lines and in `unsigned int` tensor-memory address
locals. Their host bindings are unchanged, and they compile to the same
machine code on sm_103a as the previous version. Seven of them read
slower than their band in one replicate. In replicate a, these are TP4
EP1 at 4096 tokens (+0.10 µs), TP4 EP4 at 1024 tokens (+0.01 µs) and TP8
EP8 at 16 tokens (+0.03 µs). In replicate b, they are TP4 EP4 at 512
tokens (+0.03 µs), TP8 EP8 at 1 token (+0.03 µs), TP8 EP8 at 4 tokens
(+0.05 µs) and TP8 EP8 at 512 tokens (+0.10 µs). In the other replicate,
each of them is within its band or faster, and none is slower than its
band in both replicates. Their machine code and bindings are unchanged,
so this is process-level noise, not a regression.*

The other three variants (single-rank routed-FP4, single-rank routed-FP8
and grouped-GEMM routes) ship on sm_100a and sm_103a; the rank variant
ships on sm_103a only.

### [5b2180c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5b2180ccc4534a97151f3b3149eb6d54baf5f9a1)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T16:05:10Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mok_bf16): vectorized shared-memory MXFP8 dispatch quantize in the sm_107a forward (#7821) (#8506)

`cake_mok_bf16` is FlashInfer's MoK mixture-of-experts training kernel
family. It covers forward, full-forward checkpoint recompute (replay)
and backward, and has four variants: BF16 or MXFP8 routed experts, each
with plain or clamped SwiGLU. This PR speeds up the MXFP8 forward kernel
on sm_107a for both plain and clamped SwiGLU (for #7821). The kernel's
communication CTAs quantize each dispatched 128x128 BF16 token tile to
MXFP8 twice, once row-major and once transposed. They now read shared
memory in 128-bit chunks and write the MXFP8 words with 64-bit and
128-bit vector stores, in a per-lane order whose accesses hit distinct
shared-memory banks. Outputs are bitwise identical to before. The
full-forward checkpoint replay runs the same forward kernel, so it
speeds up as well.

**Kernel phases** (ms, before → after, speedup)

| Workload | Forward | Full-forward replay | Backward |
|---|---|---|---|
| T=27116, uniform routing | 4.106 → 3.917 (1.048x) | 4.090 → 3.906
(1.047x) | 6.798 → 6.846 (0.993x) |
| T=32768, uniform routing | 5.323 → 5.227 (1.018x) | 5.310 → 5.217
(1.018x) | 8.861 → 8.806 (1.006x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 1.25x | 6.326 → 6.219 (1.017x) | 6.310 →
6.202 (1.018x) | 10.839 → 10.826 (1.001x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 2x | 11.501 → 11.165 (1.030x) | 11.445 →
11.105 (1.031x) | 22.979 → 22.979 (1.000x) |

**End to end** (ms, before → after, speedup)

| Workload | MoE microbatch | Training update, 5 layers |
|---|---|---|
| T=27116, uniform routing | 16.325 → 16.010 (1.020x) | 161.604 →
157.536 (1.026x) |
| T=32768, uniform routing | 20.838 → 20.598 (1.012x) | 203.706 →
200.986 (1.014x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 1.25x | 24.799 → 24.566 (1.009x) | 243.390
→ 241.266 (1.009x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 2x | 47.248 → 46.558 (1.015x) | 468.283 →
463.001 (1.011x) |

*8 NVIDIA VR NVL72 GPUs (sm_107a, 212 SMs, two 4-GPU trays in one NVLink
domain), driver 620.69, CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. EP8, H=4096,
I=2048, 288 experts, top-8, one shared expert, clamped SwiGLU (limit
10), MXFP8 routed experts, macrobatch 262144. The training update runs 5
layers with 2 microbatches each. Before is FlashInfer main before this
PR. Times are in ms and are means of two runs per side, in rotated order
on the same nodes (before, after, after, before). Peak memory is
unchanged (19.141 / 19.464 / 19.141 / 19.145 GiB per rank for the four
rows). Outputs, input gradients and weight gradients are bitwise
identical to before.*

The family also ships the BF16 routed-expert variants and the MXFP8
recompute and backward kernels, and every variant runs on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [f0140aa](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f0140aa3c67c7c3e18eaffaff5bbf9de65dc0be2)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T15:37:30Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_causal_conv1d): sm_107a C=1024 channel-band programs for the non-deterministic backward (#8510)

Related issue: #8065. Tracker: #6595.

The Cake causal conv1d training kernel (packed width-4 depthwise causal
conv1d + SiLU) has two packages. The non-deterministic one is
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_causal_conv1d_train_backend`, and the
deterministic one is `flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_det_train`. The
non-deterministic package has five single-rank routes and three
context-parallel (KCP) forms. This PR changes only the single-rank
non-deterministic backward on sm_107a (R200), and only at exactly C =
1024 channels. It adds three sm_107a backward programs that are used
only at C = 1024:

- the default `bwd`
- the bias backward
- the FP32 SiLU-gradient backward (`bwd_fp32g`)

They are the C = 1024 twins of the existing sm_107a programs, with a
narrower channel band. C >= 1032 keeps the existing programs. The
sm_100a and sm_103a programs, the forward programs and the KCP forms are
unchanged.

On R200 at C = 1024, these are the backward geomeans against FlashInfer
main over the 5 shapes per route: 1.017x for `sr_fp32g_bf16w`, 1.016x
for `sr_bias_f32`, 1.015x for `sr_dt_bias_bf16`, 1.012x for `sr_fp32g`
and 1.005x for `sr_default`. The per-route backward geomeans for det/new
are 1.031 (`sr_bias_f32`), 1.029 (`sr_dt_bias_bf16`), 1.000
(`sr_default`), 0.958 (`sr_fp32g`) and 0.959 (`sr_fp32g_bf16w`). The
rows below det are listed below.

1.007 [0.997, 1.030], fwd 1.000 [0.999, 1.002]
- det/new: bwd 0.995 [0.902, 1.054], step 1.000 [0.926, 1.062], ckpt
0.995 [0.929, 1.030], fwd 1.001 [0.997, 1.004]
- SOTA/new: bwd 2.967 [1.426, 5.724], step 2.745 [1.934, 4.691], ckpt
2.214 [1.187, 4.212], fwd 1.687 [0.947, 3.180]

**Geomean per route and phase, NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), CUDA 13.0
runtime, with [min, max] over shapes.** There are 25 shapes per phase.

- `sr_default` at S = 31292 (bwd, step and ckpt)
- `sr_default` at S = 62585 (ckpt)

FlashInfer main is also below det on every one of these 34 rows. On
them, main/new is 0.997 to 1.045.

- The worst row is `sr_fp32g` at S = 31292, bwd: det 39.33 us, main
44.62 us, new 43.68 us (det/new 0.902, main/new 1.022).
- Next is `sr_fp32g_bf16w` at S = 31292, bwd: det 39.23 us, main 44.82
us, new 43.34 us (det/new 0.904).
- The FP32 SiLU-gradient gap narrows as S grows. At S = 500680,
`sr_fp32g` bwd is det 304.35 us, new 309.04 us (0.985).
- For `sr_default` at S = 31292, bwd is det 36.42 us, main 38.06 us, new
37.86 us (0.961). Its ckpt is det 77.66 us, main 83.22 us, new 83.16 us
(0.934).

**Rows below SOTA.** The forward programs are unchanged (main/new
1.000). SOTA is faster on two forward rows, both at S = 31292:

- `sr_bias_f32`: `fla_gluon` 21.09 us, new 22.08 us (SOTA/new 0.956)
- `sr_dt_bias_bf16`: `fla_gluon` 20.74 us, new 21.95 us (SOTA/new 0.947)

No bwd, step or ckpt row has SOTA/new < 1.

This PR leaves the family's deterministic package and three KCP forms
unchanged, and the family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

`cake_grouped_fp8_gemm` is Cake's contiguous grouped FP8 (E4M3) GEMM for
MoE layouts on Blackwell. It produces BF16 output. It supports two
block-scale formats: FP32 per-128-block scales (16 routes) and packed
power-of-two UE8M0 int32 block scales (15 routes). This PR changes one
UE8M0 program, the sm_103a 64-row-block swap-AB program behind the
`bs_ue8m0_swap_bm64` route. Its prologue two-CTA cluster synchronization
now arrives with relaxed ordering instead of release, and the wait keeps
acquire. The program is renamed
`cake_grouped_fp8_gemm_9bfa8c96c5191f51e2b8` ->
`cake_grouped_fp8_gemm_ad951349d53d895b5975`. Routes and all other
programs are unchanged. The baseline is the previous Cake version of
this kernel: FlashInfer main's shipped program 9bfa8c96 on the same
route. Against that baseline, the new program's new/shipped latency
ratio is 0.9693 to 0.9784 on the two measured shapes that route to it.
All other measured shapes run the same program before and after this PR.

NVIDIA GB300 (Blackwell, sm_103a), CUDA 13.4 toolkit, PyTorch 2.14.1
(CUDA 13.0 runtime), driver 580.167.08. Some GB300 GPUs run 2-CTA
cluster kernels slower, so the table shows one fast and one slow GB300.
Latencies are medians in microseconds with a cold L2. "shipped" is
main's program 9bfa8c96 and "new" is this PR's program ad951349.
new/shipped is the paired, position-cancelled ratio (the geometric mean
of the median paired ratios in both timing orders), so it can differ
slightly from the quotient of the two medians. A ratio below 1 means the
new program is faster. M is the row count of the padded contiguous
layout, groups is the number of experts, align is the per-group row
alignment, and valid rows lists the valid rows in each group.

GB300 fast new us | GB300 fast new/shipped | GB300 slow shipped us |

### [dfe69cc](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/dfe69ccf348c0b4ca24eb064fc7bdd74e5961484)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T15:33:13Z
- **提交信息**: benchmark(cake_dense_projection_gemm): router SOTA = the fastest library arm that meets the router budget (#8508)

## Summary

For the FP32 router rows, the script's non-Cake SOTA was always one
call: `cublasSgemm` in `CUBLAS_FP32_EMULATED_BF16X9_MATH` with the
default cuBLAS heuristic (the `bf16x9` arm). The script already timed
plain FP32 `torch.mm` with TF32 off (the `cublas` arm), but that arm was
never a SOTA candidate. The cuBLASLt sweep (the `cublaslt` arm) ran only
on the BF16-input projection rows. Plain FP32 meets the router's FP32
accuracy budget at small token counts and is faster than BF16x9 there.
At large token counts, plain FP32 is slower, and its weight gradient can
miss the budget (hidden 4096, T >= 16172). A cuBLASLt sweep in the
BF16x9 compute type can be faster than the single `cublasSgemm` BF16x9
call. This change picks the router SOTA from four library arms and
applies the router budget to each one.

- The router SOTA is now the fastest of `cublas`, `cublaslt`, `bf16x9`
and `cublaslt_bf16x9` that meets the router budget on that row. The
budget has three parts: relative Frobenius error <= 2e-6 against FP64 of
the same operands, a finite output, and, for the forward, the same top-8
experts as FP64 in every row. The JSON / CSV field `sota_arm` names the
arm that won. The new JSON field `sota_budget` records each candidate's
error and pass flag. The markdown table names the arm in each SOTA cell,
and its caption states the rule.
- `CublasLt` now also takes FP32 inputs with `CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F`, so
TF32 stays off. Router rows get the `cublaslt` sweep over the
heuristic's top `--lt-algos` (default 8) algorithms. The script checks
each algorithm against the router budget. The fastest passing algorithm
is the arm.
- The new `cublaslt_bf16x9` arm runs the same sweep with FP32 inputs in
`CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_EMULATED_16BFX9`. It uses the eager emulation
strategy, which is the strategy of the `bf16x9` arm. The script sets
this strategy through the cuBLASLt emulation descriptor when the library
has it. The script checks each algorithm against the router budget. The
new CSV column `cublaslt_bf16x9_ms` holds its time. The new JSON field
`cublaslt_bf16x9_sweep` records the sweep and the strategy used.
- For the router, `--composite` (2 x forward + input gradient + weight
gradient) times each of the four library arms that meets the budget on
all three operations. The new JSON field `composite_sota_budget` records
the per-operation errors.
- Projection (K1) rows, every default and every command-line option are
unchanged.

Benchmark-only change; no package code changes.

## Checked on GB300

The script ran at the PR head on an NVIDIA GB300 (`sm_103a`, 152 SMs)
with torch 2.14.1+cu130. The command was `python
benchmarks/bench_cake_dense_projection_gemm.py --families router --T
128,16231 --composite --groups 5 --steps 20`. It ran once with cuBLAS
13.8.0 and once with cuBLAS 13.1.1 (the version bundled with the torch
wheel), and each run measured 18 router rows (hidden 4096, 5120 and 6144
x T 128 and 16231 x forward, input gradient and weight gradient) and the
composite of each hidden size and T, in eager and graph mode, with 0
errors.

| hidden | T | operation | Cake `deterministic=False` | `cublas` |
`cublaslt` | `bf16x9` | `cublaslt_bf16x9` | SOTA arm |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 128 | forward | 28.1 | 17.0 | 16.5 | 36.4 | 36.0 | `cublaslt` |
| 4096 | 128 | input gradient | 13.5 | 9.6 | 9.6 | 19.2 | 19.2 |
`cublas` |
| 4096 | 128 | weight gradient | 19.5 | 9.1 | 9.1 | 17.2 | 17.6 |

*Graph mode (replayed CUDA graph), cuBLAS 13.8.0 run. Latency in us:
median of 5 paired groups x 20 iterations of CUPTI GPU time, cold L2.
"misses budget": the script excludes that arm from the SOTA choice.
Composite: 2 x forward + input gradient + weight gradient.*

- At T 128, a plain FP32 arm (`cublas` or `cublaslt`) is the SOTA on
every row, in both modes and with both cuBLAS versions. Both BF16x9 arms
are slower there.
- At T 16231, a BF16x9 arm is the SOTA on every row, in both modes and
with both cuBLAS versions. With cuBLAS 13.8.0, `cublaslt_bf16x9` wins 19
of the 24 cells and `bf16x9` wins 5. With cuBLAS 13.1.1,
`cublaslt_bf16x9` wins 15 and `bf16x9` wins 9. With the faster cuBLAS
version for each arm, `cublaslt_bf16x9` takes 0.966-1.004x the `bf16x9`
time at T 16231.
- At hidden 4096, T 16231, the `cublas` weight gradient misses the
budget. Its relative Frobenius error is 2.28e-06 with both cuBLAS
versions; the limit is 2e-6. The script excludes `cublas` from the SOTA
choice for that row and does not time the `cublas` composite. The
`cublaslt` weight gradient meets the budget there (8.62e-07 with cuBLAS
13.8.0, 3.92e-07 with cuBLAS 13.1.1). Every `cublaslt_bf16x9` and
`bf16x9` result meets the budget.
- On every row, the JSON / CSV field `sota_arm` and the markdown SOTA
cells name the winning arm.
- A second GB300 run used the same command with `--T 1024,32768`. It
measured 18 router rows per cuBLAS version with 0 errors. A BF16x9 arm
(`bf16x9` or `cublaslt_bf16x9`) is the SOTA on every cell, with one
exception. At hidden 4096, T 1024, with cuBLAS 13.1.1, `cublaslt` wins
the weight gradient (41.6 us eager, 41.7 us graph). At T 32768, the
budget also excludes the `cublas` hidden 5120 forward, because its top-8
experts differ from FP64. It also excludes both plain FP32 composites at
hidden 5120.
- In eager mode, the `cublaslt_bf16x9` composite is faster than the
`bf16x9` composite at T 128 and 1024 (0.804-0.808x at T 1024, with each
arm at its faster cuBLAS version). The cause is host-side gaps between
the eager `cublasSgemm` BF16x9 calls. In graph mode, the two composites
are within 0.977-1.013x at T 1024, 16231 and 32768.

### [12943e0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/12943e0079531caec45789fb7aa4e9e4cecb1351)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T15:18:34Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_deepgemm_mega_mhc): weight-staging tail routes for 3- and 4-wave sm_107a launches on R200 (#8507)

`flashinfer.mega_mhc` (`prepare_mega_mhc`) runs the fused
manifold-constrained hyper-connection (mHC) inference step. FlashInfer
main ships 45 per-arch programs for it:

- 14 hidden-5120 FP8-E4M3-output programs on sm_100a and sm_103a.
- For hidden 4096, five programs on each of sm_107a, sm_100a and
sm_103a: BF16 output, its tailpipe twin, its weight-staging tailpipe
twin, FP8 group-128 output and NVFP4 output.
- Four sm_107a-only tailpipe and weight-staging tailpipe forms of the
FP8 group-128 and NVFP4 variants.
- Three sm_107a-only FP8 group-128 UE8M0-scale-mode programs (plain,
tailpipe and weight-staging tailpipe).
- One sm_107a-only fast-division form of the plain FP8 group-128
program.
- Six sm_107a-only fast-chain forms: one each of the BF16-output
tailpipe program, the plain FP8 group-128 program (raw scale mode), the
plain FP8 group-128 program (UE8M0 scale mode), the FP8 group-128
weight-staging tailpipe program (raw scale mode), the FP8 group-128
UE8M0 tailpipe program and the NVFP4 tailpipe program.
- Two sm_107a-only chain-packing forms: one of the FP8 group-128
tailpipe program (raw scale mode) and one of the plain FP8 group-128
UE8M0 program.

Routes on main can already carry an optional SM-count key.

This PR adds no program and changes no program. It adds routes, and each
route is keyed to one SM count (208 or 216). Each route moves launches
in the 3-wave and 4-wave 16-split bands to the existing weight-staging
tailpipe program with the same output layout and scale mode. Main
switches to that program only from 5 waves: T = 3329 on 208-SM devices
and T = 3457 on 216-SM devices. These routes use it earlier, on the
bands listed below. The weight-staging tailpipe program keeps the 16
splits and the grid of the program it replaces. It also stages the
RMSNorm weight in shared memory. Outputs are bitwise identical, and the
deterministic launches stay batch invariant. Every other SM count, and a
call with no SM count, dispatch exactly as on main. No sm_100a or
sm_103a launch changes.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of the kernel, which is what
FlashInfer main dispatches today. A is the program main dispatches, and
B is the program this PR dispatches. Speedup = A / B. Both sides run
through FlashInfer's loader on the same GPU, with the same inputs, in
one process. Both use programmatic dependent launch, as main already
does. The tables show medians. Each table lists the owner shapes first,
then the changed rows. The GPU is an NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a), with 208-SM
and 216-SM devices. All launches below use 16 splits.

- **NVFP4 output, deterministic** (plain NVFP4 program → NVFP4
weight-staging tailpipe program). 208 SMs: T = 2112–2496 (1.020–1.034×)
and 2944–3328 (1.017–1.026×). T = 2048 already takes the weight-staging
program on main. 216 SMs: T = 3008–3456 (1.017–1.028×).
- **NVFP4 output, non-deterministic** (NVFP4 tailpipe program → NVFP4
weight-staging tailpipe program). 208 SMs: T = 2497–3328 (1.008–1.019×).
216 SMs: T = 2561–3456 (1.008–1.025×).
- **FP8 group-128 output, UE8M0 scales, deterministic** (UE8M0 tailpipe
program → UE8M0 weight-staging tailpipe program). 208 SMs: T = 2048–2496
(1.016–1.031×) and 2944–3328 (1.018–1.025×). 216 SMs: T = 2048–2560
(1.009–1.038×) and 3008–3456 (1.024–1.036×). On 216 SMs, this route
replaces main's existing route that sends T = 3329–3456 to the UE8M0
tailpipe program.
- **FP8 group-128 output, UE8M0 scales, non-deterministic** (UE8M0
tailpipe program → UE8M0 weight-staging tailpipe program). 208 SMs: T =
2944–3328 (1.019–1.026×). 216 SMs: T = 3008–3456 (1.022–1.032×).
- **FP8 group-128 output, raw scales, deterministic** (fast-division
form of the plain FP8 group-128 program → FP8 group-128 weight-staging
tailpipe program). 208 SMs: T = 1984–3328 (1.010–1.033×). 216 SMs: T =
1984–2560 (1.014–1.035×) and 2880–3456 (1.018–1.030×).
- **FP8 group-128 output, raw scales, non-deterministic** (FP8 group-128
tailpipe program → FP8 group-128 weight-staging tailpipe program). 208
SMs: T = 2816–3328 (1.019–1.027×). 216 SMs: T = 2880–3456
(1.017–1.033×).
- **Owner shapes.** T = 2048 is a changed row in four tables: UE8M0
deterministic on 208 SMs (1.024×) and 216 SMs (1.009×), and raw
deterministic on 208 SMs (1.032×) and 216 SMs (1.035×). The owner-shape
rows that keep their program measure 0.996–1.003× on the 208-SM GPU and
0.994–1.003× on the 216-SM GPU; those rows are all within noise.

### [1798b52](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1798b527fa18607ebf59fbba279154650b1ff526)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T14:19:46Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train): short forward up to 12 rows per SM on SM100/SM103 (#8505)

This PR extends the short forward of Cake's SiLU-gated RMSNorm training
kernel (BF16 inputs, head dim 128) to inputs of up to 12 rows per SM.
The kernel ships as two Cake packages: the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` and a non-deterministic
package. `flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train` runs the
deterministic package by default. When called with
`deterministic=False`, it runs the non-deterministic package, which has
a non-deterministic weight gradient.

In the non-deterministic package on sm_100a and sm_103a, forward inputs
of more than 10 and up to 12 rows per SM now run the short forward. The
short forward uses 16 threads per row and one 16-row block per
256-thread CTA, and it already serves inputs of up to 10 rows per SM.
Before this PR those inputs ran the deterministic package's forward
kernel. On B200 (148 SMs) the newly routed inputs are 1480 < T x H <=
1776 rows, and at 12 rows per SM the short forward launches 111 CTAs. On
GB300 (152 SMs) they are 1520 < T x H <= 1824 rows, with 114 CTAs at 12
rows per SM. No kernel source, program or build entry changes. Every
backward and all of sm_107a are unchanged.

The kernel's other Cake variants are the deterministic package and the
FP32 weight-gradient output of the non-deterministic package; the family
ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, the short forward exists only on
sm_100a and sm_103a, and this change is on sm_100a and sm_103a only
(sm_107a is unchanged).

The table below gives speedup ranges (min-max) over the rows the new
route serves, per GPU and operation. A speedup is baseline us / new us,
so a value above 1 means this PR is faster. Per-row values with absolute
times follow in the next section.

The bwd graph rows run the same code in this PR and main.

On B200 the new forward does not beat the strongest non-Cake forward: it
wins 0 of 6 rows for fwd and 0 of 6 for fwd graph. At every one of those
rows the strongest arm is torch.compile max-autotune-no-cudagraphs. On
GB300 the new forward is faster at 5 of 7 rows for fwd and 5 of 7 for
fwd graph. GB300 37x48 fwd is a tie (1.000x). GB300 33x48 fwd (0.973x),
33x48 fwd graph (0.942x) and 37x48 fwd graph (0.975x) are slower.

**The GB300 checkpointed results against non-Cake are not robust wins.**

- torch.compile picks the forward kernel's launch configuration when it
compiles. At the GB300 rows it picked XBLOCK=1 (the pinned kernel's
configuration) in only 3 of 70 compiles (3 of 35 default, 0 of 35
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs). At the B200 rows it picked XBLOCK=1 in 20
of 60 (14 of 30 default, 6 of 30 max-autotune-no-cudagraphs).
- The table shows each GB300 ckpt graph row and compares the eager
forward of the pinned XBLOCK=1 kernel with the best torch.compile
forward at that shape (us):

| T x H | strongest non-Cake ckpt graph (arm; XBLOCK its forward ran) |
new | non-Cake/new | pinned XBLOCK=1 fwd | best torch.compile fwd |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 253x7 | 11.696 (torch.compile max-autotune-no-cudagraphs; XBLOCK=32) |
8.224 | 1.422x | 2.528 | 2.496 |
| 260x7 | 13.552 (FLA) | 8.216 | 1.649x | 2.528 | 2.528 |
| 55x32 | 11.696 (torch.compile max-autotune-no-cudagraphs; XBLOCK=16) |
8.176 | 1.431x | 2.528 | 2.912 (pinned faster) |
| 57x32 | 11.760 (torch.compile max-autotune-no-cudagraphs; XBLOCK=16) |
8.208 | 1.433x | 2.592 | 2.944 (pinned faster) |
| 33x48 | 10.528 (torch.compile max-autotune-no-cudagraphs; XBLOCK=8) |
8.176 | 1.288x | 2.400 | 2.304 |
| 37x48 | 10.128 (torch.compile max-autotune-no-cudagraphs; XBLOCK=4) |
8.240 | 1.229x | 2.528 | 2.432 |

8.225 | 1.436x | 2.560 | 2.880 (pinned faster) |

- At 55x32, 57x32 and 38x48 the pinned XBLOCK=1 forward is faster than
the best torch.compile forward. At those shapes the strongest non-Cake
checkpointed step comes from a compile whose forward did not run
XBLOCK=1. A compile that picks XBLOCK=1 could narrow or reverse the
checkpointed wins at these shapes. This was not measured.
- At 260x7 the 1.649x is against FLA (13.552 us). The best torch.compile
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs compile took 13.824 us and the best
torch.compile default compile took 14.896 us.
- So the GB300 checkpointed results against non-Cake (1.229x-1.649x) are
not robust wins. They are reported as measured, with this caveat.
- On B200, at none of the 6 shapes is the pinned XBLOCK=1 forward faster
than the best torch.compile forward.

## Per-row results

**Columns.** Times are in us. A speedup is baseline us / new us, so a
value above 1 means this PR is faster.
- `det Cake`: the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` (the same API with
`deterministic=True`).
- `previous Cake`: this package as on FlashInfer main before this PR. In
the main tables it is loaded beside the PR's package in the same
process. On the rows the new route serves, its forward runs the
deterministic package's forward kernel.
- `strongest non-Cake (arm)`: per row and operation, the fastest of
these arms, each timed in the same process as the Cake arms:
  - `FLA`: FLA 0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated`;
  - `mamba_ssm`: mamba_ssm v2.3.2 `rmsnorm_fn`;
- `torch.compile default`: torch.compile of the FP32 formula in mode
'default', best of 5 fresh compiles;
- `torch.compile max-autotune-no-cudagraphs`: torch.compile of the FP32
formula in mode 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', best of 5 fresh compiles.
That mode is 'max-autotune' without inductor's own CUDA graphs. The
harness applies CUDA-graph replay to every arm itself;
- `pinned Triton XBLOCK=1`: a copy of the Triton kernel that
torch.compile (inductor) generates for this formula. It is launched
directly at XBLOCK=1 with inductor's own num_warps for that
configuration. It is forward only, in a no-grad variant and a grad
variant that also stores rstd.
- A torch.compile cell is the best of 5 fresh compiles, because
torch.compile picks the forward kernel's launch configuration when it
compiles and the pick differs between compiles.
- The `det Cake`, `strongest non-Cake`, `previous Cake` and `new`
columns and their ratios come from the main tables. There is one Python
process per GPU, and each process times its shapes (listed per GPU
below). Every arm of a shape is timed in that process, and the arm order
alternates each round.
- `A/B previous`, `A/B new`, `A/B previous/new`, `GPUs new faster` and
`GPUs new slower` come from the A/B, which ran separately on 16 GPUs
with one sequence per GPU. On each GPU, previous Cake (FlashInfer main)
and this PR ran in separate fresh processes, one after the other in a
permuted order, next to an A/A process (main again). Each process ran 10
rounds. An A/B value is the median over the 16 GPUs of each process's
cell. `GPUs new faster` counts the GPUs whose new cell is below their
previous-Cake cell, and `GPUs new slower` counts those whose new cell is
above it.
- `op`:
  - `fwd` is one eager forward call.
- `fwd graph`, `bwd graph` and `ckpt graph` (checkpointed step: 2 x
forward + backward) are replays of a CUDA graph that the harness
captures for every arm.
- `, FP32 dw` marks an FP32 weight gradient; the other rows use a BF16
weight gradient.
- `(same code)` marks an operation that runs the same code in this PR
and main at that row.
- Inputs: x and z BF16 [T, H, 128], weight [128], eps 1e-6.

### NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs)

- GPU: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, compute capability 10.0, driver
580.82.07.
- Software: kernels built by FlashInfer JIT with nvcc 13.4 (build
cuda_13.4.r13.4); PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), Triton 3.8.0, Python
3.12.15.
- Timing: CUPTI GPU time with a cold L2 via
`flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time`; 10 rounds; a cell is the median of
the 10 per-round medians.
- Main tables: 4 processes on the 4 GPUs of one node, shapes per
process: 31x48,33x48; 217x7,253x7; 55x32; 37x48.
- A/B: 16 GPUs on 3 nodes.
- Noise, main tables: the spread ((max - min) / min) of the 10 round
medians of a cell is 0.0 %-14.3 % for the Cake arms (det Cake, previous
Cake, new) and 0.0 %-21.8 % for the strongest non-Cake arm.
- Noise, A/B, changed cells: the new route is faster than previous Cake
on 16 of 16 GPUs at 24 of 24 cells whose code changed (every newly
routed shape x fwd, fwd graph, ckpt graph, ckpt graph FP32 dw).
- Noise, A/B, unchanged cells: at the 42 cells whose code did not change
(bwd, the FP32-dw bwd and every shape outside the new band), the median
per-GPU change is -0.163 % to +0.041 %.
- Noise, A/A: the A/A process differs from main by 0.000 % to +0.003 %
over all 66 cells.

### NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs)

- GPU: NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, compute capability 10.3, driver
580.159.03.
- Software: kernels built by FlashInfer JIT with nvcc 13.4 (build
cuda_13.4.r13.4); PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), Triton 3.8.0, Python
3.14.8.
- Timing: CUPTI GPU time with a cold L2 via
`flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time`; 10 rounds; a cell is the median of
the 10 per-round medians.
- Main tables: 4 processes on the 4 GPUs of one node, shapes per
process: 33x48,37x48; 253x7,260x7; 55x32,57x32; 38x48.
- A/B: 16 GPUs on 4 nodes.
- Noise, main tables: the spread ((max - min) / min) of the 10 round
medians of a cell is 0.0 %-14.9 % for the Cake arms (det Cake, previous
Cake, new) and 0.0 %-17.6 % for the strongest non-Cake arm.
- Noise, A/B, changed cells: the new route is faster than previous Cake
on 16 of 16 GPUs at 28 of 28 cells whose code changed (every newly
routed shape x fwd, fwd graph, ckpt graph, ckpt graph FP32 dw).
- Noise, A/B, unchanged cells: at the 38 cells whose code did not change
(bwd, the FP32-dw bwd and every shape outside the new band), the median
per-GPU change is 0.000 % to 0.000 %.
- Noise, A/A: the A/A process differs from main by 0.000 % to 0.000 %
over all 66 cells.

## Cells below 1x

B200 has 27 speedup cells below 1 and GB300 has 12. None is against det
Cake. A cell is listed once for each comparison below 1 (non-Cake/new,
previous/new, A/B previous/new), so a row can appear twice against
previous Cake (main tables and A/B). The absolute times are in the
tables above. Values with four decimals (0.9999x, 1.0000x) are below 1
before rounding and appear as 1.000x in the tables. Every previous/new
or A/B previous/new value below 1 is at a same-code cell. At every cell
whose code changed, previous/new and A/B previous/new are above 1 on
both GPUs. GB300 37x48 fwd is exactly 1.000x against the strongest
non-Cake (a tie) and is not counted.

### [283300b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/283300b79da41aeaad237a1c53c2db68c29a4e6c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T14:09:01Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion): quad-route programs for batches of up to 142 tokens at world size 2 (#8503)

This PR adds 4 quad-route programs to
`cake_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion` at world size 2 (2 data types x 2
epilogues). A quad-route program uses the same protocol, workspace and
summation order as the persistent program. It gives the same outputs. It
gathers four routes per round instead of two, as the world size 4
persistent program does. It loads the shared-expert row at the start of
each token. It holds four resident CTAs per SM, so up to 142 clusters
run in one wave. At world size 2, a batch of at most 142 tokens that
would otherwise run the persistent program now runs the quad-route
program. The small-token and large-token choices come first. With the
default `small_token_max` of 64, this covers 65 to 142 tokens for top-k
4 without a shared expert. For the other combinations, it covers 72 to
142 tokens. With a smaller `small_token_max`, top-k 4 without a shared
expert runs the quad-route program from `small_token_max + 1` tokens.
World sizes 4 and 8 do not change.

The kernel fuses MoE finalize, the all-reduce across the ranks of one
NVLink node, the residual add and RMSNorm at hidden size 7168. MoE
finalize uses the top-k expert rows with their routing scale, plus an
optional shared-expert row. The entry point is
`flashinfer.comm.allreduce_fusion(..., moe_finalize_backend="cake")`.
The kernel has no other Cake variants: it ships only in this fused form
and covers sm_100a and sm_103a. With this PR, it has 52 programs per
architecture (48 before): 2 data types (fp16, bf16) x 2 epilogues
(BF16/FP16 output, packed NVFP4 output) x 13 program kinds. World size 2
has small-token, persistent, quad-route and large-token programs. World
size 4 has small-token, persistent, two-shot, two-shot early and
deferred two-shot programs. World size 8 has small-token, two-shot,
two-shot early and deferred two-shot programs.

The baseline is the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main (PR #8321).
In the table, this PR changes the program of the 32 shapes with 128
tokens at world size 2. Their geomean speedup is 1.041x on B300 (min
1.010x, max 1.070x) and 1.043x on B200 (min 1.001x, max 1.069x). The
other 688 shapes run the same program on both sides. Their geomean is
1.000x on B300 (min 0.974x, max 1.025x) and 0.999x on B200 (min 0.984x,
max 1.018x). Over all 720 shapes in the table, the geomean is 1.002x on
B300 and 1.001x on B200.

The measurement also covers all 176 shapes at world size 2 whose program
this PR changes with the default `small_token_max`. They are 65 and 71
tokens with top-k 4 and no shared expert, 8 combinations each of dtype,
PDL and NVFP4 output; and 72, 96, 128, 141 and 142 tokens, 32
combinations each of dtype, top-k, PDL, NVFP4 output and shared expert.
The 32 changed shapes in the table are among them. On those 176 shapes,
the geomean speedup is 1.038x on B300 (min 0.996x) and 1.041x on B200
(min 0.985x). Of them, 1 on B300 and 2 on B200 measure below 1.000. Per
token count, the geomean speedup on B300 / B200 is 1.013x / 1.020x at
65, 1.013x / 1.017x at 71, 1.043x / 1.041x at 72, 1.039x / 1.044x at 96,
1.041x / 1.043x at 128, 1.040x / 1.045x at 141 and 1.041x / 1.045x at
142 tokens. With `small_token_max` 16, the 8 shapes with 64 tokens,
top-k 4 and no shared expert also change program. Their geomean is
1.013x on B300 and 1.019x on B200.

The tables below give one row per shape of the owner shape list. The
measurements ran on NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103a) and NVIDIA B200
(sm_100a) with CUDA 13.4 and the default `small_token_max` of 64. The
previous and this-PR columns are the median CUPTI kernel time in
microseconds, taking the minimum over ranks. Speedup is the median of
paired previous/this-PR ratios from interleaved runs, with its 95%
bootstrap confidence interval. For this reason, the speedup of some rows
differs slightly from the ratio of the two median times. Values above 1
mean this PR is faster. In the flag columns (PDL, NVFP4 out, shared
expert), 1 means yes and 0 means no.

### [27b38c1](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/27b38c15c3a7e6c1ecee6f6153e2c6ef6674e517)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T13:54:51Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): launch the K1 programs through bound argument lists (#8456)

The `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` family has
BF16-input dense and batched projection GEMMs. It also has an FP32
router GEMM (256 experts, BF16x3 emulation). `deterministic=True` (the
default) calls `dense_projection_det_gemm`. `deterministic=False` runs
the split-K / stream-K programs of #8190, #8238, #8261 and #8275. #8309,
#8373 and #8430 cut their host (CPU) cost. Both packages ship on
`sm_100a`, `sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

This PR extends the router change of #8430 to the projection GEMM (K1)
calls. On the eager convenience path, some `deterministic=False`
projection calls run the deterministic program. These calls now launch
it through this package's own cached launch binding. This covers the
projection forward and the input gradient. It also covers layouts that
route to the deterministic program, and weight-gradient rows without a
measured split-K plan. The binding uses the deterministic package's plan
and program, so the results are bitwise the same as
`deterministic=True`. The binding orders the argument list once per
cache key. It converts the workspace once per arena growth. Each call
converts only the entry point's own tensors as launch views. This
package's split-K weight-gradient program binds its arguments the same
way. With #8389, each binding also binds the call's programmatic
dependent launch (PDL) flag and keys on it. Some batched forward calls
run on the deterministic package's swapped small-token program. These
calls keep that package's call. Plans, split counts, numeric results and
prepared launches do not change.

Three rows are host-bound: 4096 -> 32 and 4096 -> 128 at T 1024, and
4096 -> 512 at T 4096. On these rows, 2fwd+bwd previous/new is
1.602-1.684 on GB300 and 1.593-1.673 on GB200. bwd is 1.518-1.687
(GB300) and 1.449-1.636 (GB200). fwd is one kernel, and its GPU interval
does not include host time, so fwd is 1.000-1.008. The 5120 -> 1024 row
at T 16231 is GPU-bound. On this row, previous/new is 0.997-1.021
(GB300) and 1.019-1.034 (GB200). A control run with the same code in
both arms gives 0.971-1.037 (GB300) and 0.971-1.025 (GB200) in eager
mode. The control covers 16 cells and 4 runs per GPU. CUDA graph replays
of prepared launches do not change. Over 16 cells per GPU, graph
previous/new is 0.996-1.014 (GB300) and 0.969-1.014 (GB200). The graph
control gives 0.996-1.022 (GB300) and 0.941-1.018 (GB200). Host time per
eager forward or weight-gradient call drops from 36.0-38.8 us (det Cake)
to 19.1-23.8 us. `torch.mm` takes 17.6-21.7 us.

Before this PR, eager 2fwd+bwd was slower than det Cake on two
host-bound rows. At 4096 -> 128, det/previous was 0.945 (GB300) and
0.949 (GB200). At 4096 -> 512, det/previous was 0.947 (GB300) and 0.958
(GB200). With this PR, det/new 2fwd+bwd is 1.566-1.720 (GB300) and
1.532-1.721 (GB200) on the three host-bound rows. bwd is 1.429-1.772
(GB300) and 1.451-1.741 (GB200). At T 16231, det/new is 0.998-1.002
(GB300) and 1.018-1.035 (GB200).

SOTA stays faster on the host-bound rows. For 2fwd+bwd, SOTA/new is
0.681-0.773 (GB300) and 0.666-0.758 (GB200). For bwd, SOTA/new is
0.431-0.624 (GB300) and 0.410-0.667 (GB200). For fwd, SOTA/new is
0.546-0.645 (GB300) and 0.535-0.643 (GB200). At these shapes, the
deterministic kernels are slower than cuBLAS: fwd takes 14.4-25.6 us
(GB300) against 7.9-16.5 us. At T 16231, SOTA/new is 0.997-1.039 (GB300)
and 0.977-1.025 (GB200). R200 (`sm_107a`) runs the same host code but
was not timed.

- **Row:** one GPU, shape and op, measured as an eager call sequence of
the entry points (no prepared launch, no CUDA graph). There are 12 rows
per GPU and 24 in all.
- **Shapes:** BF16 dense projection `[T, K] x [N, K]^T`, K -> N = 4096
-> 32, 4096 -> 128, 4096 -> 512 and 5120 -> 1024, T 1024, 4096 or 16231
tokens; BF16 forward and input-gradient output, FP32 weight-gradient
output.
- **Ops:** fwd = forward GEMM. bwd = input gradient + weight gradient.
2fwd+bwd = checkpointed step (2 x fwd + bwd).
- **Latency:** median us of the CUPTI GPU interval of the op, from first
kernel begin to last kernel end. L2 is cold before every iteration.
- **Runs:** each run has 15 paired groups x 20 timed steps per arm, in
rotated arm order. A cell is the median of the per-run medians. Each GPU
has 4 runs on 1 node, one per GPU. Two runs use one long-lived process,
and two runs use a new process per row.
- **Baselines:** det Cake = `deterministic=True`. Previous Cake =
`deterministic=False` at FlashInfer main 5ca7f52c (with #8389 and
#8430). SOTA (every GEMM of the op) = `torch.mm` (cuBLAS heuristic),
FP32 weight-gradient output.
- **Ratio:** baseline us / new us of the cells shown. A value above 1.00
means this PR is faster.
- **Setup:** NVIDIA GB300, `sm_103a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03; NVIDIA
GB200, `sm_100a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.126.20; CUDA 13.4 (driver API);
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

### [dc4bf34](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/dc4bf3420d014e519d2be33b379b0ae28b81f410)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T12:46:36Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc_det): with grad, dual-layout fn split for the activation-checkpoint recompute on sm_107a (#8488)

FlashInfer's `cake_mhc_det_train` backend holds the deterministic
four-stream mHC kernels with grad. These are forward prepare / recompute
and gradient routes at hidden sizes 4096, 5120 and 7168, plus group-row
token owner and reduction forms above 14927 tokens, which are already in
main. #8312 added a dual-layout form of the fn split kernel on the
activation-checkpoint route at hidden size 4096 (4 streams). It writes
both fn layouts in one launch: the forward layout and the transposed
layout. The checkpoint recompute launches it. The gradient pass then
reuses the transposed layout instead of splitting fn a second time. That
form runs for T ≤ 4096 on sm_100a and T ≤ 2048 on sm_103a. This PR
extends it to sm_107a for T ≤ 4096. On sm_107a it uses the same
256-thread dual-layout form. This removes one launch per checkpointed
step on sm_107a. sm_100a and sm_103a are unchanged, and their compiled
machine code is identical to main. Outside T ≤ 4096 on sm_107a, the
route is unchanged. Outputs are bitwise identical, and the public API is
unchanged.

The baseline, "previous", is the current Cake version of the same
kernels in FlashInfer main. On sm_107a it uses two fn split launches on
the checkpoint route. Times are the median GPU active time (CUPTI) of
the checkpoint route in microseconds, with cold L2. The route covers
forward statistics recompute, gradient prepare and gradient finish.
Every shape uses 4 streams, hidden 4096 and T tokens. Each value is the
mean over 2 independent sessions with separate allocations, run on two
different boards. Each session interleaves both versions in 6 paired A/B
groups. Speedup = previous / this PR, where a value above 1 means
faster.

**NVIDIA R200, sm_107a, 216 SMs; CUDA 13.4 toolkit, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130**

| T | previous (us) | this PR (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 44.14 | 42.97 | 1.027 |
| 64 | 40.60 | 39.47 | 1.029 |
| 256 | 44.01 | 42.62 | 1.033 |
| 512 | 49.80 | 48.36 | 1.030 |
| 1024 | 62.56 | 60.94 | 1.027 |
| 2048 | 99.51 | 96.59 | 1.030 |
| 4096 | 161.28 | 158.58 | 1.017 |

The other Cake variants in this family are unchanged: the forward route,
the saved-activation gradient route, hidden sizes 5120 and 7168, and the
group-row forms above 14927 tokens. The family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a
and sm_107a, and with this PR the dual-layout form ships on all three:
sm_100a for T ≤ 4096, sm_103a for T ≤ 2048 and sm_107a for T ≤ 4096.

### [791a9a8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/791a9a8b092925481f1cbeeea6b581a4ce64e046)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T12:36:00Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_rmsnorm): deterministic=False forward parity and dw accuracy (#8253)

Follow-up to #8208 for the opt-in non-deterministic weight gradient
(deterministic=False) of flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_train.

Forward: on every architecture, route and token count the package now
runs the program the deterministic package selects (its programs and
windows rendered into this package), so y, rstd and the residual output
are bitwise equal to deterministic=True.  In #8208 the H = 256 routes
and, on SM100 and SM103, the H = 5120 routes ran forward windows and
programs that differ from the deterministic package's.

Why the backward windows move: in #8208 dw elements of five routed
deterministic pairs besides the SM107 H = 5120 pair (below) exceed the
per-element budget (atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 against FP64 at the kernel's
FP32 rstd) at sampled token counts up to 65536: on GB300 (SM103)
H = 4096 at T 50688 (1.032 of the budget) and the FP32-weight H = 6144
route at T 56320 (1.010; 1.085 at T 54273 against FP64 at torch's FP32
rstd), and on a 212-SM R200 (SM107) both H = 6144 routes at T 31040
(1.057) and the FP32-weight H = 1536 route at T 61952 (1.020).  Up to
T 65536, six more routed pair windows reach more than 0.85 of the budget
with inputs of their own weight dtype: on B200 (SM100) H = 2048 (0.883
at T 59392), H = 4096 (0.923 at T 52737) and its FP32-weight route
(0.909 at T 44544 and 0.916 at T 65024; 0.983 at T 63488 against FP64 at
torch's FP32 rstd), on GB300 the FP32-weight H = 2048 (0.904 at T 62464)
and H = 5120 (0.888 at T 62464) routes, and on a 212-SM R200 H = 1536
(0.980 at T 62976).  On a 212-SM R200 the BF16-weight form of the
FP32-weight H = 2048 pair, the same dw computation, reaches 0.900 of the
budget at T 51200 (0.873 at T 55296 on a 216-SM R200), and on GB300 the
FP32-weight form of the BF16-weight H = 1536 pair, the same dw
computation, reaches 0.890 at T 47104.  The worst dw error of seven
FP32-weight pairs exceeds the FP32 eager reduction's: on a 212-SM R200
H = 512 at T 1088, 1664, 1920 and 2368, H = 4096 at T 24576 (0.7328
against 0.7241), H = 6144 at T 30784 (0.8671 against 0.8066) and H = 256
at 2048 rows (512 tokens of 4 heads; 0.1435 against 0.1158), on B200
H = 1536 at T 33280 (0.6840 against 0.6219), and on GB300 H = 1536 at
T 38400 (0.7399 against 0.7092) and H = 4096 at T 9728 (0.3383 against
0.3332).  On a 216-SM R200 the worst dw error of the SM107 FP32-weight
H = 6144 pair exceeds the eager reduction's at T 29184 (0.8224 against
0.8121), and that of the SM107 FP32-weight H = 4096 pair that ran from
T 1 to 256 at T 64 (0.0256 against 0.0233).  On a 212-SM R200 the median
dw error of that H = 4096 pair also exceeds the eager reduction's at T 4
(0.0024 against 0.0022), and its worst at T 8 and 16 (0.0079 against
0.0078 and 0.0109 against 0.0106) and, on the input family for which the
BF16-weight H = 4096 pair computes the same dw (measured with that
pair), at T 5, 6, 9 and 20 (0.0043 against 0.0037, 0.0063 against
0.0049, 0.0071 against 0.0070 and 0.0119 against 0.0108).

Backward windows: the single kernel (FP64 dw column sums; twosum
per-thread sums on SM103 and on SM107 FP32-weight H = 2048) now runs
above
- SM100: T 58880 on H = 2048, T 44032 on H = 4096 and T 32768 on
  FP32-weight H = 1536;
- SM103: T 49152 on H = 6144, T 61952 on H = 5120 and H = 2048, T 46592
  on BF16-weight and T 37888 on FP32-weight H = 1536, and T 50176 on
  BF16-weight and T 9216 on FP32-weight H = 4096;
- SM107: T 30720 on BF16-weight and T 28672 on FP32-weight H = 6144,
  T 53248 on H = 1536, T 24064 on FP32-weight H = 4096, T 50176 on
  FP32-weight H = 2048 (where the BF16-weight route already ends) and
  1536 rows on FP32-weight H = 256; FP32-weight H = 512 runs it above
  T 1024 up to T 4096, and FP32-weight H = 4096 also from T 1 to 256
  (the single kernel of that route's top window).
Each move covers both weight dtypes unless a weight is named: the
BF16- and FP32-weight deterministic pairs compute the same dw for equal
inputs, so a failing input of one is a failing input of the other.  A
worst error above the FP32 eager reduction's (read on the FP32-weight,
H = 5120 and H = 256 routes) moves only the route on which it
occurs.  SM103 H = 2048 (its twosum form) and SM107 H = 1536 get new
single kernel programs, builds of the same kernel sources; SM107

  (H = 5120), 212.128 to 212.353 us (H = 6144, session medians),
  209.503 us (FP32-weight H = 6144) and 207.376 us (FP32-weight residual
  H = 6144) against 5.872, 6.048 to 6.336, 6.464 and 6.144 us for the
  pairs; the median time of every timed single kernel is at most
  0.22 ms.
- R200: not timed.

Backward, SM107 H = 5120 (both weight dtypes): the compensated
deterministic pair that #8208 runs from T 19968 now runs up to T 49152
and the FP64-accumulating single kernel above it.  In #8208 the pair ran
up to T 65536 (BF16 weight) and T 57344 (FP32 weight).  On a 212-SM R200
one BF16-weight dw element of that pair exceeds the budget at T 61440
(1.110 of it); on a 216-SM R200 its worst element reaches 0.867 of the
budget at T 53248 and 0.891 at T 61440 with BF16 weight, and 0.905 at
T 57344 with FP32 weight (worst of 200 inputs of each of three
families).  Above T 49152 the single kernels stay within 0.703 (BF16
weight) and 0.646 (FP32 weight) of the budget at the sampled token
counts up to 65537.  Their median backward time is 1.80-1.87x the pair's
on a 212-SM R200 (T 53248 to 65536).  Since #8251 the deterministic
package runs other programs on SM107 H = 5120 from T 19968, so from
T 19968 to 49152 deterministic=True and deterministic=False run
different deterministic pairs.

Backward, SM103 H = 256 (both weight dtypes): above 5120 rows each row
count runs a deterministic pair instead of this package's single
kernels, except from 93184 to 139264 rows, where the twosum single
kernel of #8208 keeps running.  The pair's main kernel is the one the
deterministic package runs for that row count on a device with 152 or
more SMs; its dw reduce is that package's up to 40960 rows and above
1572864 rows, and from 40960 to 93184 and from 139264 to 1572864 rows
the one that package ran there before #8319 (the measured
pairs).  From #8293 to #8319 the deterministic package ran the pair of
40960 to 93184 rows up to 99840 rows; that pair reaches 0.9807 of the
budget at 93696 rows (3904 tokens of 24 heads, FP32 weight, worst of 60
inputs of each of three families).  In that time it ran another pair
from 99840 rows, whose worst dw element stays within 0.353 (BF16
weight) and 0.373 (FP32 weight) of the budget at the sampled row counts
up to 139264 rows (worst of 200 inputs of each of three families); this
package keeps the twosum single kernel up to 139264 rows.  From 139264
to 1572864 rows, where this package now runs that pair in place of the
twosum single kernel, the twosum single kernel's median backward time
on GB300 is 1.058-1.095x (1.060-1.093x pooled) that pair's at every
timed row count; below 139264 rows the two are not timed against each
other.  Where the pairs run, their worst dw element stays within 0.837
of the budget at every sampled row count, and on GB300 their median
backward time is 0.820-0.989x (0.829-0.972x pooled) that of the single
kernels they replace.  From 93184 to 139264 rows the twosum single
kernel's median backward time is 1.130-1.188x that of the pair of 40960
to 93184 rows on GB300.  Up to 1080 rows the single kernel runs (small
token counts, above); from 1081 to 5120 rows nothing changes.

Accuracy of dw with deterministic=False at this head, against FP64 at
the kernel's FP32 rstd and at torch's FP32 rstd with the per-element
budget atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4, worst over 60 or more inputs of each of
three input families, BF16 and FP32 weight, at every sampled token count
up to 65536, the top of the qualified range (every sampled row count of
the H = 256 views): the routed deterministic pairs stay within 0.850 of
the budget (B200 0.842; GB300 0.850; R200 0.832 with 212 SMs and 0.844
with 216 SMs) and the single kernels within 0.751 (B200 0.713; GB300
0.572, the twosum forms 0.0006; R200 0.727 with 212 SMs and 0.751 with
216 SMs).  Over the same samples the median dw error over the inputs is
no worse than the FP32 eager reduction's at every sampled token count
where both were recorded; above T 256 the median over the inputs of each
family is no worse either, except one family of the SM103 FP32-weight
H = 512 route at T 1088 (0.0395 against 0.0376).  On the H = 5120,
H = 256 and FP32-weight routes the worst dw error over those inputs is
also no worse than the FP32 eager reduction's at every sampled token
count on B200, GB300 and R200 (212 and 216 SMs).

The window tables record the measured outcome at each of the 74 new
backward edges (10 on SM100, 37 on SM103 and 27 on SM107; dx is bitwise
identical across every one) and, for each of the 130 new backward
windows (19, 64 and 47), the smallest side allocation (100 or 132 KB per
CTA) beside which it waits for a kernel resident on every SM, or that it
waits beside neither, measured on B200, GB300 and a 212-SM R200.  Beside
100 KB per CTA the SM103 H = 6144 single kernels above T 49152 wait,
where the pairs they replace waited from 132 KB.  Other new windows that
wait beside a smaller allocation than the program that ran their token
counts in #8208: SM100 bwd_w32_h5120 (0, 22]; SM103 none; SM107 none.

The registry's window-reason comments state measured values, except the
two SM100 H = 5120 comments above T 65536, which name the top of the
qualified range; the H = 5120 test comment states measured values.  The
window notes name the small-T windows and the twosum windows from
T 1.  The docstrings say that deterministic=True reproduces dw bitwise
for a given token count on devices with the same SM count.  The
mixed-form workspace test in test_cake_rmsnorm_train_pairs.py takes the
first BF16-weight route without residual of SM100, SM103 or SM107 whose
window at 257 tokens runs the deterministic pair, and discounts the
route's own single-kernel records up to 256 tokens: no route runs the
deterministic pair at 1 token now.

### [936cd32](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/936cd32a539aeacd15f461370f2bf99b6af292d6)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T12:21:19Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_softmax): low-latency shared-tile kernels for grids of at most two waves (#8449)

The Cake Blackwell FP32 softmax behind `flashinfer.sampling.softmax`
sends each shape to one of several kernels. #8236 made the exponent and
reduction numerics more accurate. It also slowed the shared-tile kernels
`c8_t4_s4` and `c16_t4_s4` on small batches. This PR adds the
low-latency variants `c8_t4_s4_lat` and `c16_t4_s4_lat`, with PDL twins.
They keep the #8236 numerics, and their outputs are bitwise identical to
main. They run only when the batch fits in at most two waves of resident
clusters. Larger batches keep the existing kernels.

The other kernels in the family are unchanged: the warp kernel, the
row-wise kernel, the cached-cluster row kernels (1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 12 or

covers sm_100a (B200), sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a.

### [2880964](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2880964658235c984278cbf157325e23fa096308)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T12:13:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_lm_head_loss): zero-gradient row skip and short-chunk TMA dW cast on sm_107a (#8492)

Cake's chunked LM-head + loss training backend has two numerical forms.
The deterministic form (`flashinfer.experimental.cake_lm_head_det_loss`)
is the default. The non-deterministic (ND) form
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_loss`) is selected with
`deterministic=False`. The ND log-probability backward can skip rows
whose log-probability gradient (dlogp) is zero. This zero-gradient row
skip shipped in #8268 for sm_100a and sm_103a. On those architectures,
#8426 added a counted TMA-epilogue bf16 dW cast for a short last chunk.
On sm_107a (R200), the skip was off. This PR enables the skip and the
counted TMA-epilogue bf16 dW cast on sm_107a. Below, z is the fraction
of valid rows whose dlogp is zero. On R200 at z = 0.5, the new ND
backward speedup is 1.5683x-2.0651x vs skip-off ND. Against
deterministic Cake, it is 1.5662x-2.0697x. Against Cut Cross-Entropy
25.1.1, the new ND backward is slower at z = 0 and z = 0.166. A
re-measurement of 8 rows on a second R200 node finds no row where new ND
is slower than skip-off ND. At z = 0, kernel time is equal, but new ND
shows more GPU idle time per call: about 40-60 µs at T = 4600 (forward +
backward and checkpointed) and 25-110 µs on the T = 9000 backward. The
kernel trace places this idle time at the skip's host-side setup.

- On sm_107a, the row partition and the counted dz / dX / dW-accumulate
/ dW-cast programs now ship. Counted programs process only rows with
dlogp != 0. This adds 11 sm_107a kernel programs.
- On sm_107a, a short last chunk (up to 1792 rows) uses the counted
TMA-epilogue bf16 dW cast.
- sm_100a and sm_103a kernels are unchanged, and their SASS is identical
to FlashInfer main. B200 and GB300 performance does not change.
- **vs skip-off ND (the effect of this PR on sm_107a):**
- z = 0 (24 rows): 0.9561x-1.0048x. 17 parity, 7 inconclusive, 0 ND
slower.
- z = 0.166 (48 rows): backward 1.1273x-1.2069x, forward + backward
1.0826x-1.1498x, checkpointed 1.0598x-1.1126x, forward 0.9960x-1.0023x.
34 ND faster, 9 parity, 5 inconclusive.
- z = 0.5 (48 rows): backward 1.5683x-2.0651x, forward + backward
1.3432x-1.6206x, checkpointed 1.2370x-1.4570x, forward 0.9956x-1.0008x.
36 ND faster, 11 parity, 1 inconclusive.
- **vs deterministic Cake:**
- z = 0 (24 rows): 0.9889x-1.0217x. 12 parity, 11 inconclusive, 1 ND
faster, 0 ND slower.
- z = 0.166 (48 rows): backward 1.1519x-1.2264x, forward + backward
1.0845x-1.1841x, checkpointed 1.0715x-1.1238x, forward 0.9978x-1.0041x.
36 ND faster, 9 parity, 3 inconclusive.
- z = 0.5 (48 rows): backward 1.5662x-2.0697x, forward + backward
1.3356x-1.6244x, checkpointed 1.2538x-1.4721x, forward 0.9972x-1.0045x.
36 ND faster, 11 parity, 1 inconclusive.
- **vs Cut Cross-Entropy 25.1.1:**
  - Forward: 1.2336x-1.4255x. ND faster in all 30 forward rows.
- Backward: 0.6869x-0.7692x at z = 0 and 0.7996x-0.8925x at z = 0.166.
ND slower in all 18 of these rows. At z = 0.5, 1.1342x-1.4552x, with ND
faster in all 12 rows.
- Forward + backward: 0.8417x-0.9292x at z = 0, with ND slower in all 6

- Example (T = 4600, z = 0, backward): new ND 9.078 ms, skip-off ND
8.679 ms, deterministic Cake 9.009 ms, Cut Cross-Entropy 6.236 ms.

**R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), driver 620.43, CUDA 13.4 (PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130).** The board is VR200. Kernels are built with CUDA 13.4,
and PyTorch uses the CUDA 13.0 runtime. The measured build is a
pre-rebase build of this PR. For every entry, its kernels have SASS
identical to the PR head, including the 11 new sm_107a programs.
Workload: log-probability entry, H = 6144, V = 154880, BF16, chunk 4096,
5 % ignored rows. T = 4600, 8117, 9000, 13500, 32463, 65031. z = 0, or z
= 0.166 / 0.5 with zero-dlogp rows chosen at random or as whole groups
of 512 rows. Operations: forward, backward, forward + backward, and
checkpointed 2x forward + backward. Arms: new ND (this PR, skip on),
skip-off ND (this PR, skip off), deterministic Cake (same build), Cut
Cross-Entropy 25.1.1 (`impl="torch_compile"`). Cut Cross-Entropy is the
strongest applicable non-Cake implementation, as in #8268 and #8426. All
arms are timed in the same steps, in paired rounds. There are 2 timing
steps on different GPUs of 1 node. The state is cooled: cold L2, and an
idle gap sized to the back-to-back median. Latency is the median over
steps of the per-step median CUPTI GPU span. Speedup = baseline latency
/ new ND latency, so > 1 means new ND is faster. CI95 is a hierarchical
bootstrap over steps, then over paired rounds. A row is "ND faster" or
"ND slower" only if two conditions hold. First, the CI95 lies wholly
outside 1 ± max(1 %, A/A floor). Second, every step agrees. A row is
"parity" when the CI95 lies wholly inside that band. Otherwise, it is
"inconclusive".

**Re-measurement of 8 rows (R200, sm_107a).** The 8 rows are the 7 rows
of the main table, outside the forward operation, that are inconclusive
vs skip-off ND, plus T = 9000, z = 0, forward + backward. The forward
pass does not use the skip. They are measured at the PR head on a second
R200 node. That node uses the same driver 620.43, CUDA 13.4 and PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130. 4 timing steps run one after another on the node's 4 GPUs.
The arms, workload and method are the same as in the main table. The
first table below uses these 4 steps alone. The second table pools them
with the 2 steps of the main table (6 steps, 2 nodes).

Speedup vs skip-off ND, with verdicts:

- 4 steps alone:
- T = 4600, z = 0: backward 0.9827x, forward + backward 0.9952x,
checkpointed 0.9969x. All parity.
- T = 4600, z = 0.166: group512 checkpointed 1.0763x and random backward
1.1649x. Both ND faster.
- T = 9000, z = 0: backward 0.9921x and forward + backward 0.9957x. Both
inconclusive.
  - T = 65031, z = 0, forward + backward: 1.0013x, parity.
- Pooled, 6 steps:
  - T = 4600, z = 0: 0.9827x / 0.9952x / 0.9969x. All inconclusive.
- T = 4600, z = 0.166: group512 checkpointed 1.0758x, inconclusive.
Random backward 1.1649x, ND faster.
- T = 9000, z = 0: backward 0.9885x and forward + backward 0.9942x. Both
inconclusive.
  - T = 65031, z = 0, forward + backward: 1.0037x, parity.
- No row is ND slower in either table.

A kernel trace at T = 4600, z = 0 (50 calls) shows equal GPU kernel time
per backward: new ND 7.876 ms, skip-off ND 7.880 ms. New ND launches the
counted TMA-epilogue bf16 dW cast once per call (0.561 ms). In every
arm, GPU idle time after a host synchronization in the timing harness
alternates between about 0.25 ms and 0.75 ms per call. In the first step
of the main table, new ND took the higher level in every round. This
explains the main table's 0.9561x (9.078 ms) backward row at T = 4600, z
= 0.
