### [358c175](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/358c1756342f0fbbb0bb4192bbd0643153d7513f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T11:25:54Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dsv4): stage misaligned caller out on every route with wide O stores (#8493)

## Problem

For `backend="cake"` DSv4 sparse MLA, each of the 20 routes that
`_route` can return writes O with one of three store types: 16-byte
(int4) vector stores, 32-byte (`st.global.v8.b32`) vector stores, or a
TMA store. Only `fp8_lowhead_one_partition` (32 B) was listed in
`_OUT_ALIGN_BY_ROUTE`.

As a result, some valid caller-provided `out` tensors failed:

- A contiguous `out` that starts 2 bytes past a 16-byte boundary (for
example, a view at element offset 1 of a bf16 buffer) faulted with
`misaligned address`. One example is `bf16_h128_topk4x_v52` on sm_103a.
- On the v8 routes, an `out` that starts 16 bytes past a 32-byte
boundary faulted the same way.
- The three TMA routes (`bf16_h64_guard_q_tma_batch_r25`,
`fp8_h128_prefill_source_persistent`,
`fp8_h128_prefill_source_persistent_uniform`) rejected these tensors
with a `ValueError` saying the output "must be 16-byte aligned".

## Fix

`_OUT_ALIGN_BY_ROUTE` now lists all 20 routes. Each entry is the widest
O store used by that route's kernels on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a,
which is 16 or 32 bytes. When the caller's `out` is misaligned, the
kernels write to an aligned staging buffer and the result is copied back
to `out`. The kernels are the same, so the output is bitwise identical.
An aligned `out` skips staging and allocates nothing.

The staging mechanism already existed for `fp8_lowhead_one_partition`.
This PR changes only the table and its comment, and kernel code is
unchanged. `fp8_lowhead_h64` is in the dispatch table but `_route` never
returns it, so it is not listed.

## Tests


`tests/mla/test_cake_dsv4_hardening.py::test_misaligned_caller_out_matches_aligned`
now builds 24 calls that cover every route, including
`bf16_h128_topk128x` in its split4, vsplit and row_first forms. Each
call runs with the caller's `out` offset by +2 B and by +16 B, for 48
cases. Each case checks that:

- the expected route was dispatched
- an aligned `out` allocates nothing and gives bitwise-stable output
- the misaligned view matches the aligned result bitwise
- the NaN guard bytes outside the view are untouched

GB300 (sm_103a):

- With the fix, 48/48 pass.
- On current `main` with only the new test, 29/48 fail, as predicted
from the kernels' store widths:
- At +2 B, 18 routes fail with `misaligned address` and the 3 TMA routes
raise `ValueError`.
  - At +16 B, 8 v8 cases fail with `misaligned address`.
  - All 6 `fp8_lowhead_one_partition` cases pass.
- The full run of `tests/mla/test_cake_dsv4_hardening.py` and
`tests/cpu/mla/test_cake_dsv4.py` has the same failures with and without
the fix: 6 that were already failing, all `test_trtllm_gen_*`. They
belong to the trtllm-gen backend, not this code path.

B200 (sm_100a):

- With the fix, 48/48 pass.
- On current `main` with only the new test, 29/48 fail: 26 with
`misaligned address` (8 of them at +16 B) and the 3 TMA cases with
`ValueError`.
- The full run has the same 6 pre-existing `test_trtllm_gen_*` failures
with and without the fix.

pre-commit passes.

### [c7fc681](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c7fc6814f50ee7559d2cb65a5aafee6c181ad43e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T11:14:28Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): add GB200 / GB300 T-exact row rules for the q_b input gradient and the 17408 x 5120 weight gradients (#8491)

This PR adds row rules to the Cake `dense_projection_det_gemm` package
in `flashinfer.experimental`, the deterministic dense projection GEMM.
The package has 127 programs built from 124 templates. Most are
BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and wgrad), and one is an FP32 router
GEMM. The PR adds 9 rules: 4 for `sm_100a` and 5 for `sm_103a`. Each
rule applies at a single token count T and routes BF16-output dgrad and
wgrad rows to programs that already ship. On both architectures, the q_b
input gradient (2048→16384) at T 16172 and 16231 goes to the row's
existing program with a column-grouped raster. The 17408→5120 weight
gradient at T 16231 and 16384 on `sm_100a`, and the 5120→17408 weight
gradient at T 16384 on `sm_103a`, go to the half-tail program with a
TMA-store epilogue and 12-row raster groups. Two of the `sm_103a` rules
are empty keys for the 17408→5120 weight gradient at T 16231 and 16384.
They keep that row's current plan on `sm_103a`, which would otherwise
inherit the new `sm_100a` rule, so those rows do not change. No program
or template is added or removed, the rule count goes from 357 to 366,
and `sm_107a` is unchanged.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of the package on main.
Against it, the changed rows have speedups of 1.012–1.025 on GB200,
1.015–1.018 on GB300, 1.021–1.045 on B200 and 1.027–1.042 on B300. No
changed row is slower on any of the four GPUs, and outputs on those rows
are bitwise identical to main. All other rows of the 294-row shape list
plan the same programs as main.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB200
(`sm_100a`, 152 SMs), GB300 (`sm_103a`, 152 SMs), B200 (`sm_100a`, 148
SMs), B300 (`sm_103a`, 148 SMs); CUDA 13.4, cold L2, BF16 output.
Speedup = previous time / this PR time, and values above 1 mean this PR
is faster. "—" means the PR does not change that row on that GPU.

B200 previous µs | B200 this PR µs | B200 speedup | B300 previous µs |
B300 this PR µs | B300 speedup |

### [60459a4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/60459a46f914195d7669d54f08e95b717f81d77b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T11:10:47Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): sm_103a router weight-gradient head/tail program with the A parts in tensor memory (#8444)

The `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` family has three
kinds of GEMM. They are BF16-input dense projection GEMMs, BF16-input
batched projection GEMMs, and an FP32 router GEMM (256 experts, BF16x3
emulation). Each kind has forward, input-gradient and weight-gradient
programs. `deterministic=True` (the default) calls
`dense_projection_det_gemm`. `deterministic=False` runs this package's
split-K / stream-K programs. This PR changes one variant: the router
weight gradient (FP32 out) on `sm_103a` in the hidden-5120 head/tail
window. That window is exactly 152 SMs and 16172 to 32768 tokens. In
that window, a new head/tail program,
`router_fp32_gemm_ts_r6p6_atomic_nn_t_ht_c2_nreg`, replaces
`router_fp32_gemm_atomic_nn_t_ht_c3_nreg`. The new program keeps the
three BF16 parts of `A` in tensor memory and feeds the MMA from there.
The partition, the six products and their accumulation order are
unchanged. Plans and every other row are unchanged.

These results are on GB300, against FlashInfer main. In the table's run,
the router weight gradient gives det/new 1.169-1.245, previous/new
1.030-1.041 and SOTA/new 1.590-1.668. Over three runs, each in two
launch orders, the same ratios are 1.169-1.274, 1.027-1.056 and
1.585-1.680. Over all runs, bwd gives det/new 1.058-1.149, previous/new
1.019-1.077 and SOTA/new 1.312-1.404. Over all runs, 2fwd+bwd gives
det/new 1.004-1.088, previous/new 0.999-1.042 and SOTA/new 1.508-1.577.
The forward runs the same program in every Cake arm (previous/new
0.979-1.004). An A/A control runs the new program against a second
prepared copy of itself. It spans 0.999-1.031 on bwd and 0.995-1.029 on
2fwd+bwd. The 2fwd+bwd differences against previous Cake are about as
large as that spread.

- **Rows:** FP32 router GEMM, hidden 5120, 256 experts, T 16172, 16231,
16384 and 32768 tokens (the window this PR changes). Ops are wgrad
(router weight gradient, the changed op), bwd (input gradient + weight
gradient) and 2fwd+bwd (checkpointed step: 2 x forward + bwd). Modes are
eager (calls of the prepared launches) and graph (CUDA graph replays).
- **Latency:** median us of the op's GPU span from CUPTI activity
records. The span runs from the first kernel begin to the last kernel
end of every launch of the op. It includes the BF16x3 split and memset
launches. L2 is flushed before every iteration. Programmatic dependent
launch is at the package default. Each arm runs 15 paired groups x 20
timed steps in rotated arm order. A cell is the median of the per-group
medians. The table is one long-lived process for all rows.
- **Baselines:** det Cake = `deterministic=True`
(`dense_projection_det_gemm`). Previous Cake = `deterministic=False`
with FlashInfer main's head/tail program
`router_fp32_gemm_atomic_nn_t_ht_c3_nreg` at the same plan. SOTA (every
GEMM of the op) = cuBLAS 13.8.0 `cublasSgemm` with
`CUBLAS_FP32_EMULATED_BF16X9_MATH`. It is the cuBLAS path that meets the
router's FP32 accuracy budget on Blackwell tensor cores (TF32 and BF16
miss it).
- **Setup:** NVIDIA GB300, `sm_103a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03, CUDA
13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. A ratio is the quotient of
the two us columns. A ratio above 1.00 means this PR is faster.
- **Accuracy:** the reference is FP64 at the four token counts (40
random inputs each, 8 independent runs). The new program's pooled worst
element error is 0.985-0.996x the previous program's. Its relative
Frobenius error is within the 2e-6 budget in every run.

### [70c8e15](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/70c8e15309ce063e55ba152c1a2dc32a7d6eedfe)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T11:09:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): runtime-size FP8 paged context programs for GQA packs 5, 6, 7, 12, 16 (#8486)

The Cake FP8 paged context family already ships runtime-size programs
for GQA packs 1, 2, 4 and 8. Until now, FP8 calls whose pack is 5, 6, 7,
12 or 16 ran a JIT-compiled module. This PR adds runtime-size programs
for those 5 packs and routes these calls to them. On sm_100a there are
page 16 and page 64 variants; on sm_103a there are PX variants. Outputs
are bitwise equal to the JIT module. On sm_100a, calls with more than
8192 keys and more than 64 (batch x KV heads) streams keep the JIT
module. The baseline is the previous Cake path for these calls, the JIT
module. trtllm-gen is shown as a second column.

B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4: 63 rows whose route this PR changes.
Each µs value is a CUPTI measurement with cold L2: the median of 3
rotating rounds on one seeded memory layout. A ratio above 1 means this
PR is faster.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Expanded FP8 context-attention runtime coverage with additional pack

* Runtime pack selection can now choose a matching JIT pack when that
avoids extra tile work.
* **Improvements**

constraints before GPU execution.

### [6b2bdf6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6b2bdf668f470a665f88bce293d2e962787cb56b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T11:02:19Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_attn_res): token-queue programs for more B200, B300 and GB300 shapes (#8489)

This PR changes routes of the Cake AttnRes operator,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kimi_k3_attn_res`, which is exposed as
`flashinfer.kimi_k3_attn_res.prepare_kimi_k3_attn_res` and
`kimi_k3_attn_res`. One launch does residual add, an optional snapshot
write, K+1 candidate scoring, softmax, mix and output RMSNorm. It takes
BF16 inputs with hidden size 7168 and K in [0, 8]. It has one data type,
one layout and two fused forms: dense and snapshot write. This PR
changes routes on GB300, B300 and B200. All changes apply at both PDL
modes, except two GB300 shapes that change only with PDL off. Among the
measured shapes, 20 change on GB300, 16 on B300 and 12 on B200.

- **Token-queue builds of the current programs (GB300, B300, B200):**
These shapes move from their static persistent program to that program's
token-queue (`_clc`) build, which already ships. A token-queue build
launches one CTA per token (grid M) and uses cluster launch control.
Each running CTA processes its own token and then the tokens of the CTAs
it cancels, so tokens are spread over the SMs dynamically instead of by
a static stride.
- On GB300: serving_m3072_k1 to serving_m3072_k5, serving_m2048_k3,
primary_m2048_k4 and write_m1024_k1_write1. primary_m1024_k1 and
primary_m2048_k1 also move, with PDL off only. With PDL on they keep
`persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f110000000100000_fm`.
- On B300: serving_m3072_k1 to serving_m3072_k5, serving_m6144_k5,
serving_m2048_k3, primary_m2048_k4, serving_m2048_k5 and
serving_m1536_k4.
- On B200: all 12 changed shapes. These are serving_m768_k6,
serving_m768_k7, serving_m1536_k6, serving_m1536_k7,
write_m1024_k4_write4, primary_m2048_k1, primary_m2048_k4 and
serving_m3072_k1 to serving_m3072_k5.
- **Other shipped token-queue programs (GB300):** 10 shapes move to a
different token-queue program that already ships:
- serving_m768_k7 and serving_m2048_k7 move to
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_clc`.
- serving_m1536_k6 and serving_m2048_k6 move to
`persistent:k6_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_clc`.
- serving_m768_k8, serving_m1536_k8, serving_m3072_k8 and
primary_m2048_k8 move to `persistent:k8_nc5_d2_f110000000000000_clc`.
- serving_m2048_k5 moves to `persistent:k5_nc3_d3_f010000000000000_clc`.
- serving_m6144_k5 moves to `persistent:k5_nc4_d3_f010000000000000_clc`.
- **New token-queue builds (B300):**
- serving_m1536_k7 and serving_m2048_k7 move from
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_fm` to
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_fm_clc`.
- serving_m1024_k6 and serving_m2048_k6 move from
`persistent:k6_nc4_d2_f111000000000000_fm` to
`persistent:k6_nc4_d2_f111000000000000_fm_clc`.
- primary_m1024_k1 and primary_m2048_k1 move from their per-PDL `_fm`
programs to `persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f110000000000010_fm_clc` (PDL off) and
`persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f110000000100000_fm_clc` (PDL on).

The program set goes from 207 to 197 programs and from 239 to 229
libraries. sm_100a goes from 116 to 112 libraries and sm_103a goes from
123 to 117. This PR adds 3 sm_103a libraries:
`persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f110000000100000_fm_clc`,
`persistent:k6_nc4_d2_f111000000000000_fm_clc` and
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_fm_clc`. It removes 13 libraries
(4 sm_100a, 9 sm_103a) whose only use was the previous route of a
changed shape. All other libraries have SASS identical to the previous
version.

All changed shapes are faster: 20 on GB300 (1.014x to 1.040x), 16 on
B300 (1.011x to 1.046x) and 12 on B200 (1.018x to 1.046x). The only
exceptions are the PDL-on rows of GB300 primary_m1024_k1 and
primary_m2048_k1, which keep their program and measure 1.001x and
1.000x. For shapes not in the tables below, see the timings in PRs
#6980, #7014, #7338, #7374, #7411, #7453, #7540, #7737, #8120, #8143,
#8155, #8171, #8207, #8291, #8351 and #8428.

Cake ships no other data types or layouts for this operator, since the
dense and snapshot-write forms are the whole family, and 197 programs
(229 libraries: 112 sm_100a, 117 sm_103a) cover B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs),
B300 (sm_103a, 148 SMs) and GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs).

### [2351249](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2351249676c6289f229d5fd2eabb005a76c2ccec)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T10:46:05Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_causal_conv1d): faster single-rank non-deterministic backward on sm_107a (#8450)

Related issue: #8065. Tracker: #6595.

The Cake causal conv1d training kernel (packed width-4 depthwise causal
conv1d + SiLU) has two packages. The non-deterministic one is
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_causal_conv1d_train_backend`, and the
deterministic one is `flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_det_train`. The
non-deterministic package has five single-rank routes and three
context-parallel (KCP) forms. This PR changes only the single-rank
non-deterministic backward on sm_107a (R200). It changes three programs:

- exact pair products for the default backward at C 2048-8192
- exact pair products for the default backward at C 256-480 for S >=
262144
- an FP64 word finish for the FP32 SiLU-gradient backward at C 128-768

It also ships the 19 narrower channel-tile rows (`TILE_OVERRIDES`) for
sm_107a, which shipped none before. sm_100a, sm_103a and the forward
programs are unchanged.

Backward on R200, compared with FlashInfer main:

- 1.010-1.020x for the default route at C 256-480 with S >= 262144
- 1.002-1.009x for the default route at C 2048-8192
- 1.005-1.007x for the FP32-gradient route at C 128-768
- within noise of main on the other rows, except the slower rows listed
below

Per route, the backward geomean is det/new 1.000 (`sr_st4`) to 1.023
(`sr_bias_fp32g`) and SOTA/new 1.855x (`sr_st4`) to 4.995x (`sr_fp32g`).

**Geomean per route and phase, NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), CUDA 13.0
runtime, with [min, max] over shapes.** There are 96 shapes per phase:
18 for each of the five routes, plus 6 `sr_st4` shapes at S 262144 and
500680. Ratios are baseline time / this PR's time, so above 1 means this
PR is faster. Baselines:

- **det:** deterministic Cake
(`flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_det_train`) at the same FlashInfer main.
- **SOTA:** per shape, the fastest of fla 0.6.0 (`fla`, `fla_gluon`),
causal-conv1d 1.7.0 (`dao`, `dao_det`) and cuDNN frontend 1.32.1 that
runs every pass.
- **main:** FlashInfer main before this PR.

Forward, backward and step are timed with CUPTI with a cold L2. The
checkpointed step (2x forward + backward) is timed with CUDA events.
Each value is the median of 8 passes per arm. The tables give median
[min, max] in us. Software: nvcc 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. The GPUs
reported a memory clock of 3186 MHz (maximum 4752 MHz) before and after
every run.

Route labels: `sr_default` is default `bwd`, `sr_fp32g` is FP32
SiLU-gradient, `sr_bias_f32` is FP32 bias, `sr_dt_bias_bf16` is BF16
dt-bias, `sr_bias_fp32g` is fused bias + FP32 gradient, and `sr_st4` is
the default route at C 256-480 with S >= 262144.

**Rows slower than main.** 5 of the 288 bwd, step and ckpt rows have
main/new < 0.997. Three of them are the FP32-gradient route at S =
250,340, C = 1536. This is a `TILE_OVERRIDES` row that this PR ships.
Its bwd is 0.987 (main 250.23 us, new 253.64 us; slower in all 8
passes), its step is 0.990 and its ckpt is 0.994. An earlier measurement
on another R200 system found this row 1.0-1.9 % faster with the override
than without it; the two systems disagree, the cause is not known, and
this PR keeps the override. The other two are the FP32-gradient route at
S = 250,340, C = 128: step 0.994 (main 56.42 us, new 56.75 us) and ckpt
0.990 (main 78.42 us, new 79.22 us). Its bwd is 1.005x faster.

**Rows below deterministic Cake.** 59 of the 288 bwd, step and ckpt rows
are below det Cake. FlashInfer main is also below det on 55 of them. The
worst is the FP32-gradient route at S = 250,340, C = 1024, bwd: det
167.39 us, new 171.28 us (0.977), main 171.30 us.

The step, checkpointed step and forward tables per shape are posted as
PR comments, with [min, max] for every shape.

The KCP contiguous, zigzag and zigzag-per-document forms and the
deterministic package are unchanged, and the family ships on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [8ee5c58](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8ee5c5877836ce8588040e700036630e6199ca24)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T10:29:36Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_causal_conv1d): keep the non-deterministic backward one wave beside a concurrent kernel (#8429)

`cake_causal_conv1d` has three training backwards: a single-rank
backward with SiLU' at the BF16 preactivation (`bwd`), the same with
SiLU' at the FP32 preactivation (`bwd_fp32g`), and a context-parallel
(KCP) backward. This PR changes the non-deterministic KCP backward and
the non-deterministic single-rank `bwd` / `bwd_fp32g` at `bwd_grid_mult`
1. At C10240 with a concurrent 1-thread kernel (the #8365 repro), these
backwards no longer pay the second-wave penalty. The CUPTI kernel-time
ratio ND main / new under side load is 1.400 to 1.431 for KCP, 1.357 to
1.386 for `bwd` and 1.392 to 1.436 for `bwd_fp32g`, across GB200, B200
and GB300, and 1.359 to 1.360 for KCP, 1.397 to 1.398 for `bwd` and
1.330 to 1.332 for `bwd_fp32g` on R200. There are two baselines. The
first is the deterministic Cake backward on FlashInfer main (det Cake).
The second is the strongest eligible non-Cake implementation for each
row: fla_cp_triton (FLA 0.6.0 context-parallel conv1d, Triton backend)
for KCP, fla_gluon (FLA 0.6.0) for `bwd`, and dao (Dao-AILab
causal-conv1d 1.7.0) for `bwd_fp32g`.

GPUs: GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs), B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), GB300 (sm_103a,
152 SMs), R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs). On R200, CUPTI comes from the CUDA
13.4 toolkit, because the CUPTI bundled with torch does not record
kernels on this GPU. Toolchain: CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4, torch
2.14.1+cu130). Inputs: BF16 x / dy, FP32 taps [C, 4], no bias. Runs use
eager mode and warm caches. Events: CUDA-event median of 30 iterations
after 5 warm-up. CUPTI: the sum of the backward's kernel durations in
each iteration, side kernel excluded, median of 30. Side load: one
1-thread kernel on a second stream, launched just before the backward.
Ratios are X / new; above 1 means this PR is faster. ND means
non-deterministic. SOTA: the fastest eligible non-Cake arm for each row
and condition. Eligible means SiLU' and taps exact or more precise than
the Cake route, with y / dx / dweight within 1e-2 rel-L2 of the Cake
result. B200 event times are bimodal in host launch gaps, so its CUPTI
table is the stable comparison.

- det Cake KCP's loaded event time includes waiting for the side kernel.
Its CUPTI time stays at the unloaded value, so the large loaded det /
new ratios on KCP rows are waiting time.
- C8192 rows launch the same grid as main, so this PR does not change
them.
- R45 ref new/main is the paired unloaded A/B: the new / main CUPTI
span, median of 11 rounds x 10 blocks. A row fails when 9 or more of the
11 rounds are above 1.003. These values come from a separate run and
were not re-timed with the tables.
- The paired A/B also ran trimmed rows outside these tables (S = 31292,
62585 and 250340 tokens at C10240 and at the second trimmed width,
C6144). On GB200 and B200, six trimmed rows fail it, by at most +0.83 %;
GB300 passes all 21:

| GPU | route | row | new / main (rounds above 1.003) |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 sm_100a | `bwd` | C10240 / T32768 (#8365) | 1.0049 (10/11) |
| B200 sm_100a | KCP | C10240 / S31292 | 1.0075 (11/11) |
| B200 sm_100a | KCP | C10240 / S62585 | 1.0049 (10/11) |
| B200 sm_100a | KCP | C6144 / S250340 | 1.0083 (11/11) |
| B200 sm_100a | `bwd` | C6144 / S31292 | 1.0059 (11/11) |
| B200 sm_100a | `bwd` | C6144 / S62585 | 1.0042 (10/11) |

- On R200 the paired A/B ran three times; a row fails when it fails in
at least two of the three runs. 18 of the 21 trimmed rows pass and three
C6144 rows fail. These slowdowns are accepted as the cost of keeping the
backward in one wave beside a concurrent kernel; they apply to unloaded
R200 C6144 runs only. The KCP row's A/A control was out of range in the
first three runs, so that row was re-measured once with a
counterbalanced A/A control (21 rounds x 10 blocks; A/A 1.0001, valid):

| GPU | route | row | new / main in runs 1, 2, 3 (rounds above 1.003) |
|---|---|---|---|
| R200 sm_107a | `bwd_fp32g` | C6144 / S62585 | 1.0153, 1.0139, 1.0144
(11/11 each) |
| R200 sm_107a | `bwd` | C6144 / S31292 | 1.0086, 1.0097, 1.0077 (11/11
each) |
| R200 sm_107a | KCP | C6144 / S31292 | 1.0083, 1.0089, 1.0096 (11/11
each); controlled re-run 1.0083 (21/21) |

The other Cake variants of this kernel, the deterministic training
conv1d and the non-deterministic variants (single-rank routes including
the bias and dt-bias forms, plus KCP), ship on sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a.

### [be78c80](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/be78c804cc3c236e213d77315759290134e1d7d2)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T10:22:10Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_det): with grad, H=256 column-split dw reduce on SM100/SM103, SM103 lean compensated ring for large T (#8439)

This PR changes the H 256 non-residual backward pass of the
deterministic Cake RMSNorm training package (`cake_rmsnorm_det_train`).
The package covers BF16 and FP32 weights, residual and non-residual
inputs, row widths H 256 (per-head view) / 512 / 1536 / 2048 / 4096 /
5120 / 6144, and both forward and backward passes. This PR changes only
the H 256 non-residual backward (contiguous rows [rows, 256], key view
[T, 4, 256], query view [T, 24, 256], BF16 and FP32 weight), on two row
ranges. The first range is above 2048 rows, up to 80896 rows on sm_100a
and up to 40960 rows on sm_103a. For those rows, the dw column reduction
kernel now splits the columns over more thread blocks. The second range
is above 99840 rows, up to 720896 rows, on sm_103a. For those rows, the
main backward kernel now uses the lighter load pipeline that the package
already uses on sm_100a and sm_107a. Rows above 720896 on sm_103a keep
the previous kernel. Every row is faster than both the previous Cake
package and torch.compile (listed in that order):
- B200 (sm_100a), H 256: 1.017x-1.056x and 1.159x-1.997x (34 rows, BF16
and FP32 weight).
- GB300 (sm_103a), H 256: 1.013x-1.070x and 1.085x-2.016x (36 rows, BF16
and FP32 weight).

**NVIDIA B200 (148 SMs), sm_100a**; CUDA 13.4 (kernels built with nvcc
13.4), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Backward pass. Latency =
CUPTI kernel-active time per call, cold L2, median of 4 x 20 calls per
process. Previous Cake = the previously shipped Cake package; Cake =
this package; both through the package's public backward entry point in
the same processes (counterbalanced). Each Cake value = fastest measured
process over the row's formal sessions (4 sessions; each session a fresh
process set with fresh caches, one GPU per session). torch.compile =
fastest measured per-shape static compile (FP32 formula, dynamic=False;
minimum over every process of the formal sessions and a tc-only sweep,
each with a fresh inductor / Triton cache). Speedup = baseline / Cake.

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Prevent a winner tuned at one live-token count from skipping the knob
search at another. Enabled tuning now requires matching capacity and
EP-wide live-token counts for both fixed and automatic variants. Replay
keeps its fallback lookup. The overall selection record is versioned to
invalidate earlier results that may have skipped that search.

Also fix the offline schedule-sweep findings from #8427: share rank
zero's grid and construction errors across EP ranks, reject a base that
leaves an eligible variant without valid schedule candidates, and check
the routing staged by measured forwards in the skew test.

Follow-up to #8427 and #7911.

### [46924b9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/46924b97bebebfed31571c4cf6bf2a16d23e033d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T09:41:20Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_causal_conv1d_det): opt-in non-cooperative KCP backward (cooperative=False) that does not wait for kernels on other streams (#8459)

For #8365.

The Cake causal depthwise conv1d + SiLU training kernel (BF16
activations, FP32 weight gradient) has four variants: a deterministic
family and a non-deterministic family, each in a single-rank form and a
context-parallel (KCP) form. This PR delivers an opt-in launch of the
deterministic KCP backward, `cooperative=False`. It uses an ordinary
launch on one SM fewer than the cooperative grid, followed by the
existing fixed-order FP32 reduce, so it no longer waits for kernels
resident on other streams. Output and input-gradient are bitwise
identical to the default, the weight gradient stays run-to-run bitwise
deterministic, and the default (`cooperative=None`, i.e. True) is
unchanged. Against the shipped Cake cooperative KCP backward, it is
5x–18x faster when a kernel is resident on another stream; with nothing
else running, it is up to about 1.1% slower on GB200 and within about
±0.2% on B200 and GB300.

*Time of the deterministic KCP backward (µs). Shipped = default
cooperative launch; new = `cooperative=False`. Unloaded: CUPTI span
median, mean of two 300-round sessions. Loaded: a 1-thread side kernel
of 1×2 ms or 1×4 ms already resident on another stream; loaded time =

(sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07); GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver

### [33e71a5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/33e71a5420b1b462cd2a8ec2320a6c1b7fd69f9d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T09:41:04Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): measured 216-SM sm_107a K1 routes: 192-wide 4096 -> 1024 FP32 and six more deterministic token counts (#8438)

## Summary

The Cake dense projection GEMM family covers BF16-input dense and
batched projection GEMMs, with BF16 or FP32 weight-gradient output, and
an FP32 router GEMM. In `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`,
the keyword-only `deterministic` flag selects the variant:
`deterministic=True` (the default) calls
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm`, and
`deterministic=False` runs the split-K / stream-K programs (#8190,
#8238). The family ships on `sm_100a` (GB200), `sm_103a` (GB300) and
`sm_107a` (R200).

This PR changes only the planner of `deterministic=False`. The change
applies to the projection weight gradient (K1) on `sm_107a` parts with
216 or more SMs. There are no kernel changes. #8363 shipped the 216-SM
entries of the deterministic token counts without a 216-SM measurement.
These entries are now measured on two 216-SM parts at 16172, 16231 and
16384 tokens.

This PR uses the rule of #8363. A point keeps the split-K program only
if all three conditions hold:

- (a) At the op level, the split-K program was faster than the
deterministic program in every run. This requires a one-sided paired
sign test p < 0.05 and a median time ratio below 0.99, in eager launches
and in CUDA graph replays.
- (b) Next to a kernel holding 8, 16 or 32 SMs on another stream, it was
no more than 3 % slower than the deterministic program, in both launch
orders.
- (c) It left the backward pass and the checkpointed step at most 1.3 %
slower than the deterministic program. This is the ratio of the medians
over the runs, eager and graph.

Otherwise, the point runs the deterministic program.

Changes:

- `4096 -> 1024` FP32 on exactly 216 SMs, 16172 to 16384 tokens: the
192-wide row-major program at one split (176 CTAs, as on 212 SMs since
#8275) replaces 256-wide tiles at one split (128 CTAs). 16231 tokens
keep the deterministic program.
- The deterministic program at 6 more points, from 216 SMs up: FP32
`4096 -> 32` at 16231 tokens; `4096 -> 64` at 16231 and 16384; `5120 ->
48` and `5120 -> 64` at 16384; BF16 `5120 -> 1024` at 16231.
- The 7 existing 216-SM points are confirmed. Other points, SM counts
and architectures are unchanged.

**Accuracy:** At `4096 -> 1024` FP32 (16172 and 16384 tokens), the
output of the 192-wide program is bitwise equal to the output of the
previous plan (256-wide tiles, one split) on the same inputs. The 6 new
deterministic points return the output of the deterministic program.

**Speedups** (ratio = baseline us / new us; above 1 means this PR is
faster):

- `4096 -> 1024` FP32 at 16172 / 16384 tokens, graph mode:
- previous/new: wgrad 1.160 / 1.164, bwd 1.106 / 1.122, 2fwd+bwd 1.064 /
1.070.
- det/new: wgrad 1.680 / 1.418, bwd 1.420 / 1.270, 2fwd+bwd 1.185 /
1.071.
- SOTA/new: wgrad 0.919 / 0.923, bwd 0.892 / 0.893, 2fwd+bwd 0.972 /
0.960.
- Eager mode previous/new: wgrad 1.177 / 1.179, bwd 1.106 / 1.108,
2fwd+bwd 1.052 / 1.016.
- The 6 new deterministic points against the previous plan
(previous/new; below 1 means the deterministic program is slower):
- Graph: wgrad 0.980 to 1.010 (geomean 0.996), bwd 0.988 to 1.009
(geomean 0.995), 2fwd+bwd 0.999 to 1.007 (geomean 1.003).
- Eager: wgrad 0.973 to 1.007 (geomean 0.990), bwd 0.991 to 1.015
(geomean 0.999), 2fwd+bwd 0.994 to 1.001 (geomean 0.998).
- The lowest value is `4096 -> 32` at 16231 tokens, eager wgrad 0.973.
There, the deterministic program is 2.7 % slower at the op.
- At the five FP32 points, the split-K program missed part (a) or (b) of
the rule in at least one of the 8 run-and-mode cells. It missed 1 of 8
at `4096 -> 32` and 5 to 8 of 8 at the other four.
- At BF16 `5120 -> 1024`, 16231 tokens, the split-K program passed (a)
and (b) in all 8 cells. The deterministic program is 2.0 % slower at the
op there (wgrad previous/new 0.980). However, the eager backward pass
with the split-K program was 1.5 % slower than with the deterministic
program (ratio of the medians over the runs; eager bwd previous/new
1.015). This is above the 1.3 % limit of (c), so that point runs the
deterministic program.

Definitions:

- **Rows:** 48 = 8 points x 3 ops x 2 modes, graph rows first; all on
216 SMs.
- **Ops:** wgrad = weight gradient `[d_out, d_in]` (output dtype as in
the `out` column) from BF16 activations `[T, d_in]` and BF16 output
gradients `[T, d_out]`. bwd = input gradient (BF16) + wgrad. 2fwd+bwd =
checkpointed step (2 x forward + bwd).
- **Modes:** g = CUDA graph replay, e = eager.
- **Latency:** Median us over 4 runs per row. The runs use two 216-SM
GPUs. Each GPU has one long-lived process over all rows and a fresh
process per row, with one arm order per GPU. In a run, all arms of a row
are interleaved in paired groups: 15 groups of 20 steps for wgrad, 9
groups for bwd and 2fwd+bwd. L2 is cold before every iteration. The time
is the CUPTI GPU time of the operation (first kernel begin to last
kernel end, all launches).
- **Baselines:**
- det Cake = `deterministic=True` at FlashInfer main eabf03fe (the
deterministic package with the #8303 plans; the measured deterministic
package is the same tree).
- previous Cake = `deterministic=False` at FlashInfer main eabf03fe,
without this PR. It uses the same kernel programs as this PR. Its
forward and input gradient are the deterministic programs.
- new = `deterministic=False` with this PR. At the 6 new deterministic
points, it runs the deterministic program, so new us is the det Cake
measurement. The `deterministic=False` call that dispatches to it was
not timed separately.
- SOTA = cuBLAS / cuBLASLt, the vendor GEMM library for `sm_107a` and
the strongest non-Cake GEMM available there. For wgrad, it is the
fastest correct launch among `torch.mm` and the cuBLASLt heuristic's
top-8 algorithms. For bwd and 2fwd+bwd, it is the fastest correct
library launch per op.
- Ratio = baseline us / new us, computed from the medians in the table;
above 1.000 = this PR is faster.
- **Setup:** R200 (`sm_107a`), 216 SMs, driver 615.71.10; CUDA 13.4
(nvcc 13.4.92), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, cuBLAS 13.8.0.4.
- **Noise:**
- Per-run paired previous/new: `4096 -> 1024` wgrad 1.156 to 1.196, bwd
1.086 to 1.124, 2fwd+bwd 1.044 to 1.061; the 6 deterministic points
wgrad 0.934 to 1.018, bwd 0.966 to 1.004, 2fwd+bwd 0.985 to 1.029.
- The two GPUs differ in speed by a few percent. Thus, a median over 4
runs (2 per GPU) can differ from the per-run paired ratios. At BF16
`5120 -> 1024`, every per-run paired bwd previous/new is 0.981 to 0.995,
while the ratio of the medians is 1.015 in eager mode.
- Some samples show the software power-cap throttle flag. All arms of a
row run interleaved in one process, so the ratios hold, but absolute
times can be a few percent high.

### [8196950](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8196950eec9a4ef883323de703f3033030565593)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T09:38:40Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_kda_det_kcp): with grad, in-kernel Q/K L2 norm on the KCP route (#7817) [stacked on #8255] (#8259)

This PR adds `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel` to the deterministic KCP package
`flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train_kcp`. With
`use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True`, callers pass raw q/k rows. Each rank
normalizes its own tokens in the first q/k reader. Normalized q/k are
never saved. With the flag off, nothing changes.

#8277, which adds the fused single-rank kernels for this mode, is merged
in `main` as 7dd8b5446b. This branch already contains its final head
1aab68baae through merge commit 4ce0b1040f. `main` merges with this
branch without conflicts, and the files #8277 changed have the same
content on both sides, so no further sync with `main` is needed. The CPU
check passed on 4ce0b1040f. The GPU rows in Status were measured on the
evidence tree cb6026e8aa (#8277 at b015c8cd5b merged with d687a8465d).
That tree has the same KCP and deterministic single-rank kernel code as
this head: #8277's three later commits only rename one sm_103a record
and change the non-deterministic single-rank package, which the KCP
package does not use. The last commit, 9460ddf498, changes only one
memory check in the l2n test file (see Status). The R200 (sm_107a)
correctness runs pass (see Status). The PR merges when CI passes on this
head.

### Stacking
- Head: 9460ddf498. History is kept. The branch is not rebased. It is
synced with merge commits.
- #8255 (KCP raw gate) is merged in `main` as c31ecb5321. This branch
had its commits with the same content, so the diff against `main` no
longer shows them.

7dd8b5446b. It was merged into this branch through merge commits
cf478a3961, dea54db583, 66e75c9fc0 and ce5d2eb44e (#8277 head 20a67232e8
at that time), and its final head 1aab68baae through merge commit
4ce0b1040f.
- `main`: merged in through merge commits 4f21de1b63 (`main` at
bcd12b47e2), 535c37e582 (`main` at e39b0c7178) and 9b31f3499b (`main` at
f9738265cd). The last merge keeps `use_gate_in_kernel`,
`use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel` and `main`'s new `checkpoint_handoff` in
`kda_saved_bytes_kcp`.
- This PR's own commits:
  - c31e189648: KCP host plumbing.
  - e8fbcf6465: CPU rows and gated GPU rows.
  - 8b957a0394: facade byte queries forward the keyword.
  - 1bcb2daca6: flag-off golden values of the base.
- 3fc647400d: selection-based capability check, refusal order,
byte-query device.
- fec4d9a800: the facade saved-set byte query forwards
`use_gate_in_kernel`.
- ffc240078a: CPU rows follow a single-rank plan that takes `l2n` before
its records land.
- 6e033e007f: the test file imports on the base for the flag-off golden
capture.
- 3fa429d30c: the raw local-stage values row binds the `param_finalize`
scratch.
- 921afed8a4, 5efb470c2c: benchmark arms for the in-kernel norm against
separate norms.
- 28ec4d16fa: a passed capability check is kept per (mode, gate mode,
architecture) while the objects it read are unchanged. A refusal is
never kept. Before this, every flag-on call with `workspace=None` re-ran
the full record selection (about 2 ms of host time per call).
- 78525a670b: the flag-on backward keeps the rebuilt normalized q/k in
its local arena instead of a per-call buffer.
- 53572c6439: that placement decision is kept per plan, so the
backward's host prologue does not walk the records again.
- 7554d9544f: formatting and a type annotation for the two commits
above.
- 8b15ec19b0: the shared-workspace four-pack test measures its peak in
requested bytes, so allocator block rounding cannot fail it.
- e5c86d3599: every flag-on refusal reachable through the forward,
backward and autograd entries is pinned to its error type and exact
message, with no collective before it.
  - f623917562: formatting of that test.
- 40e3974151: the host module copies the arena's views with
`types.SimpleNamespace` instead of importing `copy`. The refusal test
reads a CUDA device as an architecture the backend does not serve yet,
instead of sm_100a.
- d687a8465d: the capability check and the backward's reader order
identify the records that normalize q/k by their registry `l2n` key
(fused mode only), not by a name ending in `_l2n`. Before this, the
sm_103a forward record `fwd_intra_l2n_v37` was refused. #8277's final
head names that record `fwd_intra_v37_l2n`; the check does not depend on
the name.
- 9460ddf498: the l2n test counts the bytes a saving forward keeps in
requested bytes, and requires flag on minus flag off to be exactly the
rstd's `8*T*H` bytes. Before, it counted the caching allocator's blocks.
On R200 one row failed that form: in the first flag-on forward, the
saved carry (11796480 bytes requested) took a 12582912-byte cached block
that was not split. A second flag-on/flag-off pair kept exactly the rstd
on every rank.

### What changes
- `chunk_kda_det_kcp`, `chunk_kda_det_fwd_kcp`, `chunk_kda_det_bwd_kcp`,
`WorkspaceDetKcp`, `kda_det_workspace_bytes_kcp` and
`kda_det_saved_bytes_kcp` take a keyword-only
`use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=False`. It is not an `OptionsDetKcp` field.
`flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train_kcp` forwards it explicitly.
- The facade byte queries in `flashinfer.cake_kda_train_kcp` forward the
keyword. The facade saved-set byte query also forwards
`use_gate_in_kernel`, so its flag-on refusal checks the call's gate
mode.
- The norm is per token, so halos, the plan and the all-to-all do not
change.
- Strided q/k views, such as the packed `[T, (2H+HV)*128]` output of a
fused projection/conv, are accepted without a copy under the single-rank
rule. The rule is: innermost stride 1, head stride 128, token stride a
multiple of 8 elements and at least one row, and a 16-byte aligned base.
A length-1 axis is re-strided. Other layouts raise.
- Saved state still keeps the raw q/k. It adds the FP32 inverse norms
`qk_rstd [2, T_r, H]` (plane 0 = q, 1 = k) as its last tensor, plus a
`qk_l2norm` meta key. A rank with no tokens saves an empty `[2, 0, H]`.
The saved-state version stays 2, and older saved sets still load.
`kda_det_saved_bytes_kcp` adds `8*T_r*H` bytes.
- The forward writes normalized q/k only into transient slots of the
local arena. The backward recomputes them in its first q/k reader from
the raw rows and the saved `qk_rstd`, so forward and backward see the
same bits.
- The backward keeps the rebuilt normalized q/k in its local arena. `kn`
uses the bytes of the internal `dv2` rows, and `qn` uses the bytes of
the internal `v_new` rows. Those two buffers move into the bytes of the
call's own outputs: `dv2` into dq/dk (allocated as two halves of one
tensor) and `v_new` into dg. They stay there until the GLM intra program
writes those outputs, after the last read of `dv2`/`v_new`. So the
flag-on backward needs no memory beyond the flag-off backward's. The
move is checked from the selected records, the arena slot table and the
row counts. Where an output is too small (more than `2 * T_r` internal
rows; in raw gate mode, the BF16 gate gradient covers only `T_r`), that
row set takes a per-call `[T_r, H, 128]` BF16 buffer instead.
- A workspace pins the mode. The graph key, the backward key tensors and
the recompute handle's fingerprint include the mode only when the flag
is on. With the flag off, every key, fingerprint, saved tensor, meta
entry, launch and byte count is unchanged.
- The local stages run the single-rank programs with the norm fused into
the first q/k reader. The default route has no separate norm pass. A
private, unfused fallback is kept for testing only.
- Capability check: the KCP route enables the flag only when the
single-rank registry selects a record for every stage that the KCP local
paths launch in this mode. Each record must be delivered and available
for the architecture. The check runs over a fixed, rank-independent grid
of problems. A passed check is kept per (mode, gate mode, architecture)
while the objects it read are unchanged. A refusal is never kept.
- Fused form: `fwd_intra` (forward and replay), `bwd_prep`, `glm_intra`.
- Fallback form (a correctness vehicle only, not the deliverable): also
`qk_l2norm`, `qk_apply` and `qk_pullback`.
- Refusal: the flag-on refusal is decided before any launch or
collective, so no rank waits in a collective. The entries, the workspace
and both byte queries raise the same error on every rank, with or
without tokens. Flag-off byte queries make no CUDA call. The flag-on
byte queries check the call's device and gate mode.
- The flag works on the default ("replay") local arena.
`local_arena="lean"` with the flag raises for now.
- README: a new section on the in-kernel Q/K L2 norm for the KCP
package. It covers usage, the view rule, saved bytes, mode pinning and
the backward's memory.
- `benchmarks/bench_cake_kda_det_train_kcp.py` gets `--l2n-arms`: N (the
in-kernel norm) against S_T (a torch FP32 norm, then the flag-off step)
and S_F (flash-linear-attention's norm, then the flag-off step), with
the checkpoint modes, peak/kept memory, kernel times and allocations.
`--l2n-packed` takes q/k as the column halves of one packed tensor.
- Tests: new `tests/experimental/test_cake_kda_det_train_kcp_l2n.py`.
  - CPU rows cover:
    - keyword validation
- flag-off identity (omitted == explicit `False` for keys, fingerprints,
saved tensors, bytes and plan calls)
    - saved-state round trip, including the empty rank
    - the strided-view rule and the byte queries
    - per-launch argument values and stage order
    - the refusal while the kernels are absent
- `test_l2n_backward_rows_ride_in_the_arena`: records the launches of a
real backward on a CPU arena. It checks that kn/qn sit on the
`dv2`/`v_new` bytes and that `dv2`/`v_new` sit on the output bytes. It
checks that every reader of `dv2`/`v_new` runs before the first writer
of those outputs. It also checks that the backward uses no bytes beyond
the flag-off backward's, except the replay rstd.
- GPU rows skip until the kernels exist. They cover W = 1/2/4/8 with
ragged documents, zero-token ranks, cross-document resets, 4 and 64
heads, and raw rows that are scaled, zero or subnormal. They check
bitwise repeatability, rank 0 against the single-rank flag-on path, and
FP64 error (KCP/single-rank error ratio <= 1.10). They also cover the
raw-gate mode with the flag on.
- `test_cake_kda_det_train_kcp_api.py` checks that the public module
forwards the keyword.

### Status
- [x] KCP host plumbing, keys, saved state, byte queries, and refusal
before any collective.
- [x] CPU rows: on this head 4ce0b1040f, the 10 KCP test files have 0

in both gate modes, on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a (all 12 combinations
served). The CPU check also passed on d687a8465d merged with #8277 at
b015c8cd5b. Flag-off golden values are equal on the base cf478a3961.

- [x] KCP GPU rows on GB200, B200 and GB300: accuracy against the FP64

| GB300 (sm_103a) | fwd+bwd | 8.582 | 8.599 | 0.9981 [0.9977, 0.9986] |
1.0009 | faster | 10232 -> 10232 |
| GB300 (sm_103a) | checkpointed fwd+bwd | 10.909 | 11.023 | 0.9897
[0.9894, 0.9903] | 1.0010 | faster | 10176 -> 10176 |

After and Before are the medians over all timed iterations. The 95% CI
is a percentile bootstrap over whole timing blocks (2000 replicates).
A/A is the ratio of two identical Before arms in the same run. A row is
faster when After/Before < 1, its CI upper bound is < 1, and |1 -
After/Before| is larger than |1 - A/A|. A row is slower under the
mirrored rule. Otherwise it is parity. Peak memory is per rank and
counts only the arm's own workspace.

Slower rows: the backward on all three GPUs (+2.3% on GB200 and B200,
+4.1% on GB300), and fwd+bwd on B200 (+0.2%). No row is parity. All
other rows are faster. Timing is a report, not a merge condition.

Accuracy against the FP64 reference passes the agreed relative-L2 rule
over the 12 seeds on all 12 gradient/output tensors, on all three GPUs.
Checkpoint recompute, determinism, the strided layout and the saved rstd
are bitwise equal (Before and After). Peak memory per rank is After <=
Before in every mode: 512 MiB lower in forward, and equal in the other
modes.

### [a5f3dfe](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a5f3dfe1cbc7d400e8fd5f8eef6de218f4b960d7)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T09:28:56Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_msa_icp_indexer): sm_107a rows-32 list scorer triggers the list publisher after the epilogue (#8481)

The MiniMax-M3 index-context-parallel (ICP) sparse-attention indexer in
`flashinfer.msa_ops` (`msa_icp_*`) has two decode chains. The default
chain is score plane + select publish. The fused chain is list scorer +
list publisher (`msa_icp_decode_score_publish`). Both chains end with a
candidate merge. The list scorer has builds for 128, 64 and 32 rows per
architecture. This PR changes only the sm_107a rows-32 list scorer,
which the fused chain uses at P128 TP4. The scorer now triggers its
dependent launch after the epilogue, not after the load warp's last
load. The scorer grid is about one CTA per SM. With the early trigger,
the list publisher launched while nearly every SM still held a scorer
CTA, so its CTAs crowded onto the few free SMs. With the trigger after
the epilogue, most of the scorer grid has exited, and the publisher's
CTAs spread over the SMs. The baseline is the previous version in
FlashInfer main.

| World | Page | Cohort | Previous (ms) | New (ms) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 | P128 | steady | 10.320 | 10.251 | 1.007x |
| TP4 | P128 | mixed | 10.538 | 10.491 | 1.004x |

*Decode on NVIDIA VR200 (sm_107a), 4 GPUs per node, CUDA 13.4. Workload:
MiniMax-M3 serving, 163840 input tokens, 8192 output tokens, 14
concurrent requests. Steady: the 14 requests decode together. Mixed: the
same 14 requests plus one extra request whose chunked prefill runs in
mixed batches with the 14 decodes. Values are the median GPU time of a
decode step over n = 4 rounds. Each round runs previous and new back to
back on one node. Speedup = previous / new of the medians. All 8
per-round new/previous ratios are below 1 (steady
0.9971/0.9895/0.9982/0.9893, mixed 0.9931/0.9979/0.9950/0.9937).*

The indexer also ships the prefill path, the tagged and legacy receive
rows, and the P128/P256 x TP2/TP4 decode layouts on sm_100a (B200),
sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a (VR200), and all of these, including TP2
P128 and both P256 layouts, run unchanged code because this PR changes
only the sm_107a rows-32 list scorer.

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): add BF16 runtime-size causal paged context programs (#8478)

The Cake BF16 paged context family ships exact programs for some shapes
(Q8192, B128, Q511, Q257). Every other causal BF16 call without LSE or
sinks goes to a JIT-compiled module. This PR adds 9 runtime-size
programs for packs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and 16, covering page sizes
16..1024. They take those calls when the call's pack is one of the 9;
other packs stay on the JIT module. Outputs are bitwise equal to the JIT
module. The baseline is the previous Cake path for these calls, the JIT
module. trtllm-gen is shown as a second comparison column.

### [08d74a4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/08d74a47163138273af02f034a500449b9a2a6d0)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T08:54:09Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_deepgemm_dense_mqa): source consumer release on the sm_103a fp8:qle2048:short program and its stage bucket (#8475)

This PR speeds up the dense FP8, 32-head variant on sm_103a (GB300)
only, by 1.0132× to 1.0614× over the previous Cake version (FlashInfer
`364b53a4bf1f`). The Cake DeepGEMM-form MQA logits family behind
`flashinfer.dense_mqa` and `flashinfer.paged_mqa` has four variants:
dense FP8 with 32 heads, dense FP8 with 64 heads, dense FP4 with 32
heads (including fused metadata + logits sequences), and paged FP8. The
change applies to the `fp8:qle2048:short` route (the fused single-launch
Q ≤ 2048 class) and its short-K stage bucket (Q ≤ 136, K ≤ 8448), which
now launch programs whose math warps return each KV stage (and the Q
stage at the block end) to the TMA producer without a proxy fence, as in
the DeepGEMM / CUTLASS consumer-release form.

*Measurement setup:*
- NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, driver 580.167.08.

over 9 sessions.
- Speedup is baseline / this PR, so values above 1 mean faster. Every
row is faster in all 9 sessions.
- † In the baseline, these rows run two kernels per call (a metadata
kernel plus a logits kernel). In this PR they run one. Their µs is the
sum of kernel times.
- `Q q, K k` means q queries over k keys.

over p cached keys plus themselves (K = p + q).

The other Cake variants in this family (dense FP8 with 64 heads, dense
FP4 with 32 heads including the fused metadata + logits sequences, and
paged FP8) are unchanged; the dense family ships on sm_100a (B200) and

### [2473a88](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2473a88e6437b958e293eb31af12f96dfebe7aa8)

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): 256-bit O stores in fp8_lowhead_one_partition on sm_103a (#8476)

`cake_dsv4` is the Cake DSv4 sparse-MLA decode and prefill backend in
FlashInfer for BF16 and FP8 KV caches. Twenty programs serve the
197-shape list on each architecture. This PR changes one of them,
`fp8_lowhead_one_partition`, on SM103 (sm_103a), where it now stores O
with 256-bit stores. The code for the other architectures is unchanged.
The baseline is FlashInfer main, which ships the previous Cake version
of this program from #8452. On GB300 (SM103), the 197 shapes break down
as 6 faster (1.007x to 1.013x), 2 tie, 0 slower and 189 same code. On
B200 (SM100), all 197 shapes are same code.

Latencies are in microseconds. Speedup = FlashInfer main latency / this
PR latency.

Verdicts: **faster** = every counted reading shows this PR faster than
main by more than the measured run-to-run noise band, with readings in
both run orders. **tie** = the readings are not all faster (or all
slower) than main beyond the noise band. **same code** = this PR does
not change the machine code that runs this shape, so both columns carry
one measurement of that code and the row reads 1.000x.

and FP8 KV-cache decode and prefill programs, and the family ships on

Co-authored-by: Avery Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [e75dbc0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e75dbc03c9ba859532dc67dfe40dff02649aecef)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T08:52:26Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_deepgemm): faster SM120 paged FP8 MQA logits routes for 20 RTX 5090 and 24 RTX PRO 6000 shapes (#8473)

The SM120 paged FP8 MQA logits kernel picks its program from a route
catalog. Each heads/page/next_n configuration has a default route.
Device routes choose a static, `_par` or dynamic-scheduler (`dynv28`)
variant per shape. This PR moves 20 RTX 5090 shapes and 24 RTX PRO 6000
shapes to faster variants. It adds 8 routes, including three static
siblings of the new `_par` routes that no shape selects. It also deletes
the 34 routes, and their 34 programs, that no shape on either device
selects anymore. Every other shape keeps its current route.

RTX 5090:
- h64/p64/next_n 5 moves to the new `atom5_mx_mpf_bta_ha_k2q_ef` par
route for three shapes: batch 32 at context 16384, batch 64 at context
4096, and batch 8 at context 65536. h64/p64/next_n 6 moves to the new
`atom6_mx_mpf_bta_ha_ef` par route at batch 32, context 16384.
- Five h64/p64/next_n 3 shapes move from the default route to the new
`bta_ha_wr_ef` par route.
- h32/p128/next_n 6 at batch 256, context 16384 moves from
`bta_ha_wr_kmax_ef` to its new par twin.
- Ten batch 8 and batch 32 shapes move from a static route to the
existing par twin of the same variant.

RTX PRO 6000:
- 15 shapes at batch 8, context 65536 (h32/p64 next_n 1-5, h32/p128
next_n 1-6, h64/p64 next_n 1-4) move from dynamic-scheduler routes to
the par route of the same variant. That is `mpf_bta_ha_k2q_ef` par, or
`mpf_bta_ha_sp_kf2q_ef` par for h32/p128/next_n 6 and h64/p64/next_n 3.
The h64/p64/next_n 4 par route is new. Seven dynamic-scheduler routes
remain.
- Nine shapes move from a static route to the par twin of the same
variant. Seven of them use `atom2_mpf_bta_ha_k2q` at batch 8, context
4096. Two use `mpf_bta_ha_sp_kf2q_ef` at batch 32, context 65536.

### RTX 5090

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (170 SMs, sm_120a), driver 620.62, CUDA 13.0
runtime (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130), JIT toolchain CUDA 13.4.92. Baseline:
FlashInfer main (e8143622). Latency: median µs of the paged FP8 MQA
logits call (CUPTI, L2 flushed before each launch, 5 interleaved
baseline/new groups). Each seed (760, 52021) runs on its own GPU.
Speedup = baseline µs / new µs. The table covers all 216 shapes. The 20
changed shapes have a geomean speedup of 1.140× (seed 760) and 1.127×
(seed 52021), with a range of 1.007× to 1.357×. On unchanged shapes both
sides run the same program. ² = clock-gate miss (CE): the SM clock gate
(min ≥ 2500 MHz, spread ≤ 250 MHz) failed after one re-time. These
numbers are shown as recorded and are not judged. One row-seed has this
mark: h64/p64/next_n 5, batch 8, context 65536 at seed 52021 (min 2610
MHz, spread 277 MHz).

### RTX PRO 6000

NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (188 SMs, sm_120a), driver
595.84.01, CUDA 13.0 runtime (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130), JIT toolchain CUDA
13.4.92. Baseline, latency method and speedup are the same as for RTX
5090. The table covers all 216 shapes. The 24 changed shapes have a
geomean speedup of 1.085× (seed 760) and 1.084× (seed 52021), with a
range of 1.012× to 1.279×. On unchanged shapes both sides run the same
program. ² = clock-gate miss (CE): the SM clock gate (min ≥ 2335 MHz,
spread ≤ 250 MHz) failed after one re-time. These numbers are shown as
recorded and are not judged. 22 row-seeds have this mark, all on
unchanged shapes.

### [b1b1d1d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b1b1d1d925bd5a858caca1ae5d2f8aed6969706d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T08:46:51Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): BF16 KDA prefill helper-pool bin-mix, mixed-length M64 split and FP32-state ping-pong chain corrections (#8460)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has 85 modules: 51 with
BF16 inputs and 34 with TF32 inputs. They come in fused and split forms.
This PR changes only the prepared BF16-input path with FP32 state
(`flashinfer.prepare_bf16_kda_prefill`). It makes three changes. First,
the bin-mix build on the direct route with no gate bound gets a
helper-pool form. This adds one cooperative program. It targets 12
heads, no gate lower bound, 8x(1024+64). Second, some packed varlen
launches are planned as the M64 value split and mix sequences of 1024
tokens or more with shorter ones. The runtime now splits each such
launch into two launches. The owner/helper program runs the long
sequences, and the M64 program runs the short ones. No kernel changes
for this part. It targets gate lower bound -5, 2x(8128+64), with 12 and
16 heads. Third, the four chain-correction merge programs now move the
FP32 state back and forth between two tensor-memory regions (ping-pong).
They target gate lower bound -5 at 8192 and 32768 tokens, with 12 and 16
heads. The PR also re-renders the other prefill programs from the
current generator. Their SASS is identical. Outputs are bit-identical.
The tables compare this PR with the previous Cake version on FlashInfer
main. They report median latency per call in microseconds, with a cold
L2. Each table has 56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower bound or -5,
and 14 sequence-length shapes. TIE means no difference beyond the
measurement band. The first table covers repeated calls on the same
buffers, which use the plan-cache fast path. There, B200 has 11 faster
rows and 45 TIE, from 1.00x to 1.24x. GB300 has 12 faster rows and 44
TIE, from 1.00x to 1.20x. The second table covers the serving pattern,
where every call rebinds the cached plan to new buffers. There, B200 has
11 faster rows and 45 TIE, from 1.00x to 1.24x. GB300 has 11 faster rows
and 45 TIE, from 1.00x to 1.16x. The mixed-length split gives the
largest gains, at gate lower bound -5 and 2x(8128+64). With 12 heads on
B200, latency drops from 362.81 to 291.57 us (1.24x) on the fast path
and from 364.06 to 292.57 us (1.24x) in serving. With 16 heads on the
fast path, it drops from 358.72 to 298.66 us (1.20x) on B200 and from
341.41 to 285.41 us (1.20x) on GB300. In serving, it drops from 358.27
to 301.47 us (1.19x) and from 341.44 to 294.88 us (1.16x). The
helper-pool row is 12 heads, no gate lower bound, 8x(1024+64). On the
fast path it drops from 106.85 to 97.12 us (1.10x) on B200 and from
99.84 to 92.72 us (1.08x) on GB300. In serving, it drops from 110.59 to
100.64 us (1.10x) and from 103.15 to 92.98 us (1.11x). All other faster
rows have gate lower bound -5 and gain 1.01x to 1.02x. They include the
chain-correction targets at 8192 and 32768 tokens.

B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. GB300: NVIDIA
GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.

### [eefbfa0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/eefbfa0e6ff21aeaee5aa834ad506842e56100bd)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T08:15:41Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det): run serial adjoint scan beside tail_g3 on two streams on B200/GB300 (#8471)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train` is FlashInfer's
deterministic Gated DeltaNet chunked training kernel. Its outputs and
gradients are bitwise reproducible. With a host-built table, the
backward can run a serial adjoint scan as two contiguous sequence groups
on two streams: the caller's stream and a high-priority side stream. The
full-round group runs on the caller's stream and is followed by its
backward tail. Meanwhile, the side stream scans the group that would
otherwise leave the scan's last round partly idle. The kernel already
used this two-stream form beside the fused tail_g2 backward tail. This
PR also uses it on sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300) when the serial
adjoint scan feeds the fused tail_g3 backward tail. Only the host-side
launch plan changes, and the kernels are not modified. Every CTA
computes exactly what it computes in the one-launch scan, so outputs and
gradients are bitwise identical to the previous version. sm_107a (R200)
keeps the one-launch scan. The baseline is the previous version of this
kernel on current FlashInfer main (speedup = main / this PR, so >1 is
faster; median over 56 interleaved cells). Of the measured shapes, only
64 x 4096 with H / HV 2 / 6 changes its launches. For that shape,
forward + backward drops from 3.2564 to 3.2251 ms on B200 (1.010x) and
from 2.9403 to 2.9092 ms on GB300 (1.011x). Every other row runs the
same launches as before, so the spread in their f+b ratios is
measurement noise. On B200 these rows range from 0.998x to 1.028x (for
example, 1 x 16384 8 / 16 shows 1.028x with unchanged launches). On
GB300 every row except the changed one is 1.000x. The forward pass is
unchanged.

### [589d6ac](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/589d6aca7e13423a6e05b1ac19e8e2eac9978a97)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T08:11:50Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_kcp): plain split views of packed Q/K/V get contiguous dq / dk / dv in the non-deterministic KCP backward (#8435)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp` is the non-deterministic
KCP GDN training package. It supports BF16, the contiguous, zigzag and
zigzag-per-document KCP layouts, and runs with or without in-kernel Q/K
L2 norm. It covers forward, backward and checkpointed calls, in eager
and CUDA graph modes. This PR changes only the host side. When q / k / v
are plain split views of one packed QKV tensor (`row.split` + `view`),
the backward now gives three contiguous dq / dk / dv to torch's split
backward. The split-view backward then costs one contiguous
concatenation instead of the slower path on main. Only q / k / v that
come from one `packed_qkv_views_kcp` (or `packed_qkv_views_det_kcp`)
split node keep the single packed dQKV row. There are no device code
changes, and outputs and gradients are bitwise unchanged. Addresses
#8367.

All rows use the PR head after it merged main, so the forward runs the
fused forward output walk.

Compared with the same package on FlashInfer main (CP1, norm off), the
plain-split-view backward gets faster:

- **B200:** eager ckpt goes from 5.930 ms to 4.992 ms (1.188x).
- **GB300:** eager bwd goes from 4.019 ms to 3.142 ms (1.279x).
- **R200 (208 SMs):** eager bwd goes from 3.037 ms to 2.264 ms (1.341x).

Packed and contiguous forms are at parity (0.998-1.006x across all
rows).

Against the deterministic Cake package in the same process (speedup =
baseline ms / this PR ms), this PR is faster with plain split views:

- eager bwd: 1.255-1.277x on B200, 1.255-1.280x on GB300 and
1.313-1.338x on R200.
- eager ckpt: 1.222-1.245x on B200, 1.228-1.254x on GB300 and
1.261-1.286x on R200.
- eager fwd: 1.170-1.192x on B200, 1.192-1.219x on GB300 and
1.172-1.198x on R200.

With packed views, bwd is at parity (1.000-1.003x), ckpt is 1.051-1.065x
and fwd is 1.167-1.219x. Against the previous version, this PR's fwd and
packed-view times are at parity. So the fwd and packed-view ckpt gains
over deterministic Cake do not come from this PR.

Against the strongest qualified non-Cake implementation (both Q/K/V
forms, norm off and on), this PR is slower on every claimed row:

- **GB300:** versus cuDNN FROST, the speedup is 0.378-0.387x (eager
fwd), 0.663-0.739x (eager bwd) and 0.764-0.821x (eager ckpt).
- **R200:** versus cuDNN FROST, the speedup is 0.434-0.438x (eager fwd),
0.889-0.995x (eager bwd) and 0.928-0.993x (eager ckpt). FlashQLA does
not support sm_107a.
- **B200:** cuDNN FROST is faster than this PR in all 24 rows but fails
the accuracy check (dbeta max-abs 0.135 of max|ref|, limit 0.02). The
strongest qualified arm is FlashQLA 0.1.3. It runs in a separate
process, so every B200 non-Cake ratio is shown but not claimed.

### B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs)

NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs. PyTorch 2.14.1 (cu130, CUDA 13.0
runtime), CUDA 13.4 toolkit, BF16. Workload: (H_qk, HV) = (16, 48), D =
128. CP1 = one rank, 32,768 tokens in five documents [12000, 9000, 6000,
3768, 2000], contiguous layout. CP4 zigzag = 4 ranks, documents [49152,
32768, 28672, 20480], 32,768 tokens per rank; each sample takes the
slowest rank. Q/K/V forms: split = `row.split` + `view` (plain views),
packed = `packed_qkv_views_kcp`, contig = contiguous copies. Modes: fwd
= forward only; bwd = autograd backward after an eager forward. ckpt =
`torch.utils.checkpoint(use_reentrant=False)`, 2 forwards + 1 backward.
graph = the package's `graph="replay"` mode with a caller-held
workspace. Timing: 2 runs x 8 palindromic groups; each group has 2
blocks of 5 warm-up + 20 timed calls. Run 2 reverses the arm order. The
shown value is the median of group medians. The previous version is a
byte copy of the package from FlashInfer main before this PR. It runs in
the same process as this PR, with the same build and libraries. Speedup
= previous ms / this PR ms. Power-capped = GPU software power-cap share
>= 5 % of an arm's timed-block samples, for any arm of a mode and norm
setting. When the short runs hit the cap, the rows of that mode come
from a sustained protocol instead. The sustained protocol uses 3
palindromic block pairs (block = 5 s idle + 20 warm-up calls + 300 timed
calls). On B200, this applies to the CP1 norm-off eager fwd and bwd
rows, all CP1 graph rows and the CP4 graph bwd norm-on rows. In the
sustained runs, the CP1 norm-off eager fwd, eager bwd and graph bwd rows
still hit the cap. They are marked "power-capped, not claimed". The CP1
norm-off eager fwd rows also fail the stability check (drift = last /
first group - 1; every arm of the mode and norm setting must stay within
2 %; the previous version's split arm drifted 2.26 %). They are also
marked "timing unstable". All other B200 rows are claimed.

**Two-baseline comparison (CP1)**

These are separate runs from the previous-version tables above, so this
PR's absolute times differ slightly between the two sets. Each run uses
one process for deterministic Cake, this PR, FLA and cuDNN FROST. Run 2
reverses the arm order of run 1. Each run has 8 palindromic groups; each
group has 2 blocks of 5 warm-up + 20 timed calls per arm. The shown
value is the median of group medians. The norm-off eager fwd and bwd
rows come from two sustained runs (3 block pairs; block = 5 s idle + 20
warm-up calls + 300 timed calls). No deterministic Cake, this PR or FLA
cell is power-capped (every in-process arm < 5 %); the separate FlashQLA
process has no power-cap record. Deterministic Cake is
`cake_gdn_det_train_kcp` (`chunk_gdn_det_kcp`) on the same FlashInfer
tree, unchanged by this PR. Its packed views use its own helper,
`packed_qkv_views_det_kcp`. Its outputs and gradients are bitwise equal
to this PR's. Strongest non-Cake is the fastest arm per row that passes
the accuracy check. The check needs rel-RMS <= 1e-2 and max-abs <= 2e-2
of max|ref| on every tensor, with finite values. Candidates are FLA
0.6.0 Triton `chunk_gated_delta_rule`, cuDNN frontend 1.32.1
`gated_delta_net` and FlashQLA 0.1.3. The cuDNN plan is gdn_frost (cuDNN
FROST): ck0 = the backward recomputes the states; ck64 = the forward
stores BF16 states every 64 tokens. In "FlashQLA + FLA l2norm outside",
FLA's Triton l2norm normalizes q / k outside the kernel (timed), and the
in-kernel flag is off. On B200, cuDNN FROST fails the check on dbeta
(max-abs 0.135 of max|ref|), although it is faster than this PR in all
24 rows. FlashQLA is therefore the strongest qualified arm. FlashQLA
cannot share a process with the Cake package, because its TileLang
0.1.15 needs apache-tvm-ffi < 0.1.13. Its values come from a separate
process that used the short protocol. Every B200 non-Cake ratio is
therefore marked "cross-run, not claimed".

### GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs)

NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs. PyTorch 2.14.1 (cu130, CUDA 13.0
runtime), CUDA 13.4 toolkit, BF16. Workload: (H_qk, HV) = (16, 48), D =
128. CP1 = one rank, 32,768 tokens in five documents [12000, 9000, 6000,
3768, 2000], contiguous layout. CP4 zigzag = 4 ranks, documents [49152,
32768, 28672, 20480], 32,768 tokens per rank; each sample takes the
slowest rank. Q/K/V forms: split = `row.split` + `view` (plain views),
packed = `packed_qkv_views_kcp`, contig = contiguous copies. Modes: fwd
= forward only; bwd = autograd backward after an eager forward. ckpt =
`torch.utils.checkpoint(use_reentrant=False)`, 2 forwards + 1 backward.
graph = the package's `graph="replay"` mode with a caller-held
workspace. Timing: 2 runs x 8 palindromic groups; each group has 2
blocks of 5 warm-up + 20 timed calls. Run 2 reverses the arm order. The
shown value is the median of group medians. The previous version is a
byte copy of the package from FlashInfer main before this PR. It runs in
the same process as this PR, with the same build and libraries. Speedup
= previous ms / this PR ms. No GB300 row is power-capped (GPU software
power-cap share >= 5 %). In the CP4 eager ckpt norm-on rows, the time
level shifted within run 2: the drift (last / first group - 1) was
2.2-8.5 % there, and run 1 stayed within 0.3 %. These rows pass the
paired check instead: every paired group ratio stays within ±1 % of its
median. They are claimed and marked "level shift in run 2" with the
paired ratio. The CP4 eager fwd norm-off rows come from a re-measure
with two further runs.

**Two-baseline comparison (CP1)**

These are separate runs from the previous-version tables above, so this
PR's absolute times differ slightly between the two sets. Each run uses
one process for deterministic Cake, this PR, FLA and cuDNN FROST. Run 2
reverses the arm order of run 1. Each run has 8 palindromic groups; each
group has 2 blocks of 5 warm-up + 20 timed calls per arm. The shown
value is the median of group medians. No cell is power-capped or
unstable. Deterministic Cake is `cake_gdn_det_train_kcp`
(`chunk_gdn_det_kcp`) on the same FlashInfer tree, unchanged by this PR.
Its packed views use its own helper, `packed_qkv_views_det_kcp`. Its
outputs and gradients are bitwise equal to this PR's. Strongest non-Cake
is the fastest arm per row that passes the accuracy check. The check
needs rel-RMS <= 1e-2 and max-abs <= 2e-2 of max|ref| on every tensor,
with finite values. Candidates are FLA 0.6.0 Triton
`chunk_gated_delta_rule`, cuDNN frontend 1.32.1 `gated_delta_net` and
FlashQLA 0.1.3. The cuDNN plan is gdn_frost (cuDNN FROST): ck0 = the
backward recomputes the states; ck64 = the forward stores BF16 states
every 64 tokens. On GB300, cuDNN FROST passes the check and is the
strongest arm on every row: ck0 for fwd, ck64 for bwd and ckpt. FlashQLA
ran in a separate process and was not faster than the shown arm in any
row.

### R200 (sm_107a, 208 SMs)

NVIDIA R200 board, sm_107a, 208 SMs; these results cover the 208-SM
board only. PyTorch 2.14.1 (cu130, CUDA 13.0 runtime), CUDA 13.4
toolkit, BF16. Workload: (H_qk, HV) = (16, 48), D = 128. CP1 = one rank,
32,768 tokens in five documents [12000, 9000, 6000, 3768, 2000],
contiguous layout. Only one GPU was visible, so the 4-rank CP4 zigzag
rows were not run on this board. Q/K/V forms: split = `row.split` +
`view` (plain views), packed = `packed_qkv_views_kcp`, contig =
contiguous copies. Modes: fwd = forward only; bwd = autograd backward
after an eager forward. ckpt =
`torch.utils.checkpoint(use_reentrant=False)`, 2 forwards + 1 backward.
graph = the package's `graph="replay"` mode with a caller-held
workspace. Timing: 2 runs x 8 palindromic groups; each group has 2
blocks of 5 warm-up + 20 timed calls. Run 2 reverses the arm order. The
shown value is the median of group medians. The previous version is a
byte copy of the package from FlashInfer main before this PR. It runs in
the same process as this PR, with the same build and libraries. Speedup
= previous ms / this PR ms. No R200 row is power-capped (GPU software
power-cap share >= 5 %).

**Two-baseline comparison (CP1)**

These are separate runs on a different R200 machine from the
previous-version tables, so this PR's absolute times differ slightly
between the two sets. Each run uses one process for deterministic Cake,
this PR, FLA and cuDNN FROST. Run 2 reverses the arm order of run 1.
Each run has 8 palindromic groups; each group has 2 blocks of 5 warm-up
+ 20 timed calls per arm. The shown value is the median of group
medians. The norm-on rows come from a re-measure: two further runs with
the same design. No cell is power-capped or unstable. Deterministic Cake
is `cake_gdn_det_train_kcp` (`chunk_gdn_det_kcp`) on the same FlashInfer
tree, unchanged by this PR. Its packed views use its own helper,
`packed_qkv_views_det_kcp`. Its outputs and gradients are bitwise equal
to this PR's. Strongest non-Cake is the fastest arm per row that passes
the accuracy check. The check needs rel-RMS <= 1e-2 and max-abs <= 2e-2
of max|ref| on every tensor, with finite values. Candidates are FLA
0.6.0 Triton `chunk_gated_delta_rule`, cuDNN frontend 1.32.1
`gated_delta_net` and FlashQLA 0.1.3. The cuDNN plan is gdn_frost (cuDNN
FROST): ck0 = the backward recomputes the states; ck64 = the forward
stores BF16 states every 64 tokens. On R200, cuDNN FROST passes the
check and is the strongest arm on every row: ck0 for fwd, ck64 for bwd
and ckpt. FlashQLA does not support sm_107a; it accepts only sm90,
sm100, sm103, sm120 and sm121. So R200 has no FlashQLA value.

### [db9571f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/db9571f6c1b48db5c22de198c2e74873addff4cd)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T08:09:55Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): with grad, cached FFI launch and per-form fence in the non-deterministic single-rank package (#8455)

The Cake KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) chunked training kernels have four
packages: deterministic and non-deterministic (ND) single-rank packages,
each with a KCP context-parallel package. The ND single-rank package is
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_kda_train`. This PR changes only the
ND package, which the tables call ND v5. It brings the deterministic
package's per-form fence placement to the dqkg_v24 forms that read no
saved rows. It also makes the launcher lighter: `run_module` caches the
FFI entry per (record, device) and launches on the raw current CUDA
stream. The stream and device are the same as before, and the outputs
are bitwise unchanged.

The gain is in host issue time, so it shows on small or host-bound
steps. Summed kernel time is about flat compared with FlashInfer main
before this PR (M; C is this PR). The prev/v5 kernel-sum geomeans are
0.9986 to 1.0000 on B200 and GB300. On B200, the median host issue time
per call drops by 52.2 us for fwd and 75.1 us for bwd. The ckpt issue
times are noisy. P9 ckpt gains the most step span: prev/v5 is 1.0467 on
B200, 1.1341 on GB300 and 1.0399 on R200. Only two prev/v5 span cells
are below 0.99, both on B200:
- P10 ckpt is 0.9737. Its det control was 0.9618, and the rerun gave
1.0068.
- P14 ckpt is 0.9857.

Against the deterministic package, fwd and bwd are at parity. Their
det/ND geomeans are 1.0002 to 1.0051. 25 cells are below 1 in run 1 or
the rerun, and the lowest is 0.9944. ckpt is faster on every row, with
geomeans of 1.0425 to 1.0522 and a lowest cell of 1.0131. FLA chunk_kda
0.6.0 is slower on every row, with FLA/ND geomeans of 4.4775 to 6.0661
and a lowest cell of 2.455.

Speedups: det/ND = deterministic Cake latency / ND v5 latency; FLA/ND =
FLA chunk_kda 0.6.0 latency / ND v5 latency; prev/v5 = previous ND (FI
main) latency / ND v5 latency. Above 1 means ND v5 is faster; values
below 1 are measured slowdowns. ckpt = activation-checkpointed step (2 x
forward + backward).

### B200 (sm_100a)

NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA toolkit 13.4 (V13.4.92), driver
580.82.07, torch 2.14.1 (CUDA 13.0 runtime), FLA 0.6.0. Latency = CUPTI
step span: first kernel start to last kernel end of each timed call, so
host gaps between kernels count (cupti-python 13.4.0). Cold L2. Each
value is the median of 5 round medians; each round median is the median
of the timed calls. The det and ND arms are interleaved and swap order
every other round; FLA is timed after the Cake arms are released; P14
(H=64) times det, ND and FLA each alone. Noise = spread of the round
medians, (max - min) / median: det and ND arms median 0.40 %, max 5.9 %
(P14 ckpt ND); FLA max 24.5 % (P14 ckpt).

### GB300 (sm_103a)

NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA toolkit 13.4 (V13.4.92), driver
580.159.03, torch 2.14.1 (CUDA 13.0 runtime), FLA 0.6.0. Latency = CUPTI
step span: first kernel start to last kernel end of each timed call, so
host gaps between kernels count (cupti-python 13.4.0). Cold L2. Each
value is the median of 5 round medians; each round median is the median
of the timed calls. The det and ND arms are interleaved and swap order
every other round; FLA is timed after the Cake arms are released; P14
(H=64) times det, ND and FLA each alone. Noise = spread of the round
medians, (max - min) / median: det and ND arms median 0.15 %, max 16.5 %
(P12 ckpt ND); FLA max 10.1 % (P13 fwd).
