Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [2940d0a](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2940d0aeb8fd110c4777dd0efe575c8c0eb48c01)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T08:06:54Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train): non-deterministic short forward computes the SiLU gate before the sum of squares on SM100/SM103 (#8465)

This PR changes one program in Cake's SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel
(BF16, head dim 128). The kernel ships as two Cake packages: the
deterministic package `flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` and
a non-deterministic package. `flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_train`
runs the deterministic package by default and the non-deterministic one,
with a non-deterministic weight gradient, when called with
`deterministic=False`. In the non-deterministic package on SM100 and
SM103, the short forward now computes the packed SiLU gate before the
row's sum of squares. The short forward handles inputs of up to 10 rows
per SM and uses 16 threads per row. No other program changes: every
backward and all of SM107 are the same as before.

The kernel's other Cake variants are the deterministic package and the
FP32 weight-gradient output of this package; the family ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, and the short forward exists only on
sm_100a and sm_103a.

The table below gives speedup ranges over the rows the short forward
handles (T x H up to 1480 on B200 and up to 1520 on GB300). Each range
is min..max per GPU and operation; per-row values follow in the next
section.

| GPU | op | rows | vs previous Cake (S) | vs previous Cake (A/B) | vs
det Cake (S) | vs strongest non-Cake (S) | rows faster than strongest
non-Cake |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B200 | fwd | 15 | 1.030x..1.045x | 1.029..1.043 | 1.241x..1.320x |
0.892x..0.943x | 0 of 15 |
| B200 | fwd graph | 15 | 1.026x..1.057x | - | 1.280x..1.352x |
0.849x..0.915x | 0 of 15 |
| B200 | bwd | 15 | 0.923x..1.074x | 0.998..1.003 | 1.141x..1.570x |
1.187x..1.580x | 15 of 15 |
| B200 | ckpt | 15 | 1.004x..1.041x | 1.014..1.028 | 1.153x..1.372x |
0.934x..1.235x | 12 of 15 |
| GB300 | fwd | 17 | 1.027x..1.045x | 1.022..1.043 | 1.213x..1.306x |
0.813x..1.000x | 0 of 17 |
| GB300 | fwd graph | 17 | 1.027x..1.056x | - | 1.273x..1.391x |
0.853x..1.007x | 1 of 17 |
| GB300 | bwd | 17 | 0.961x..1.014x | 0.993..1.000 | 1.268x..1.577x |
1.064x..1.430x | 17 of 17 |

The bwd rows run the same code in this PR and in main. On every forward
row in this range, the strongest non-Cake forward is faster than the new
forward, with one exception: GB300 217x7, where the eager cell is 1.000x
and the graph cell is 1.007x. That is a near-tie, so this PR claims no
forward win over non-Cake on either GPU.

The GB300 checkpointed wins over torch.compile are not robust:
- torch.compile picks the forward kernel's launch configuration when it
compiles. On GB300 it picked XBLOCK=1, the pinned kernel's
configuration, in only 3 of 160 default and 4 of 160
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs compiles.
- On 22 GB300 checkpointed rows, counting rows inside and outside this
range, a torch.compile arm is the strongest non-Cake arm and the new
step beats it. In 19 of them, the torch.compile value comes from a
compile whose forward did not run XBLOCK=1.
- At 10 of those shapes, the pinned XBLOCK=1 forward kernel is faster
than the best torch.compile forward: 7x48, 13x48, 21x48, 30x48, 8x32,
9x32, 13x7, 129x7, 211x7 and 217x7. A compile that picks XBLOCK=1 could
narrow or reverse the checkpointed wins at these shapes.
- Example: 13x7 checkpointed is 1.103x, and its torch.compile value
comes from a compile whose forward ran XBLOCK=16. The eager forward at
13x7 takes 2.064 us with the pinned XBLOCK=1 kernel and 2.656 us with
the best torch.compile.

On B200, torch.compile picked XBLOCK=1 in 73 of 160 default and 42 of
160 max-autotune-no-cudagraphs compiles. On 21 B200 checkpointed rows, a
torch.compile arm is the strongest non-Cake arm and the new step beats
it; 19 of them take their torch.compile value from a compile whose
forward did not run XBLOCK=1. At none of those 19 shapes is the pinned
XBLOCK=1 forward faster than the best torch.compile forward.

## Per-row results

**Columns.** Times are in us. A speedup is baseline us / new us, so a
value above 1 means this PR is faster.
- `det Cake`: the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`.
- `previous Cake`: this package on FlashInfer main, loaded next to the
PR's package in the same process.
- `strongest non-Cake`: the fastest of these arms on each row:
  - FLA 0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated` (`FLA`)
  - mamba_ssm v2.3.2 `rmsnorm_fn`
  - torch.compile of the FP32 formula in mode 'default' (`tc-def`)
- torch.compile of the FP32 formula in mode 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs'
(`tc-max`)
- a copy of the Triton kernel that torch.compile (inductor) generates
for this formula, launched directly at XBLOCK=1 with num_warps 2. It is
forward only: `pin` is the no-grad variant and `pin-g` is the grad
variant that stores rstd.
- Each torch.compile cell is the best of 5 fresh compiles in the same
process, because torch.compile picks the kernel's launch configuration
when it compiles and the pick differs between compiles.
- 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' is 'max-autotune' without inductor's own
CUDA graphs. The harness applies CUDA-graph replay to every arm itself.
- S columns (`det Cake` through `previous/new`): there is one Python
process per shape table, and every arm of a shape is timed in that
process, alternating the order each round.
- A/B columns: a separate two-node test runs previous Cake (arm A,
FlashInfer main) against this PR (arm B), in separate processes
interleaved per GPU. Each value is the median over processes. `A/B
previous/new` is arm A us / arm B us.
- Noise: the round spread of a det Cake, previous Cake or new S cell
(the spread of its 10 round medians) is 0.0-17.3 % on B200 and 0.0-16.9
% on GB300. In the A/B, an A/A run (main against main) reads "overlap"
in 160 of 160 cells on each GPU, and every row whose code is unchanged
reads "overlap" (115 rows on B200, 109 on GB300).
- `op`: `fwd` is an eager forward call. `fwd graph`, `bwd` and `ckpt`
(checkpointed 2 x fwd + bwd) are CUDA graph replays. `stepg_f32` and
`bwdg_f32` are CUDA graph replays with an FP32 weight gradient, measured
only in the A/B. The S tables did not measure these two operations, so
their S cells are empty. This is a gap in the measurements, not a
missing non-Cake feature.

### NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs)

- GPU: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, compute capability 10.0, driver
580.82.07.
- Software: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), Triton 3.8.0, nvcc 13.4.
- Inputs: BF16 [T, H, 128] with H = 48, 32 or 7, eps 1e-6, BF16 weight
gradient.
- Timing: CUPTI GPU span with cold L2 via
`flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time`, 10 rounds.
- Statistic: median of the per-round medians (S); median over processes
(A/B; 16 A/B pairs on 2 nodes x 4 GPUs).

### NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs)

- GPU: NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, compute capability 10.3, driver
580.159.03.
- Software: PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), Triton 3.8.0, nvcc 13.4.
- Inputs: BF16 [T, H, 128] with H = 48, 32 or 7, eps 1e-6, BF16 weight
gradient.
- Timing: CUPTI GPU span with cold L2 via
`flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time`, 10 rounds.
- Statistic: median of the per-round medians (S); median over processes
(A/B; 16 A/B pairs on 2 nodes x 4 GPUs).

**Rows the short forward handles** (T x H <= 10 x SMs = 1520): fwd, fwd
graph, ckpt and stepg_f32 run the new program; bwd and bwdg_f32 run the
same code in this PR and main.

## Rows below 1x

In total, 230 speedup cells are below 1: 94 are on rows the short
forward handles and 136 are on rows it does not handle. A row is listed
once for each baseline it is slower than. Cells shown as 1.000x are
below 1 before rounding. The absolute times are in the tables above.

- **Previous Cake:** every entry runs the same code in this PR and main.
Each one is either a bwd or bwdg_f32 row of a shape the short forward
handles, or a row of a shape it does not handle. Every A/B entry has the
per-pair verdict "overlap".
- **det Cake:** every entry is on a shape the short forward does not
handle.
- **Strongest non-Cake, shapes the short forward handles:** every fwd
and fwd graph row except GB300 217x7, plus ckpt at B200 1x48, 2x48 and
13x7 and at GB300 1x48 and 2x48.

### [7dd8b54](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7dd8b5446becc0e2949997a7e37d99471edb5533)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T08:02:43Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_kda_det): with grad, in-kernel Q/K L2 norm, use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel, single-rank (#7817) [stacked] (#8277)

The deterministic Cake KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) chunked training
package, `flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train`, has four variants. Q/K L2 norm
is either done by the caller or fused in-kernel, and each of those runs
with either the g gate or the raw gate (`use_gate_in_kernel`). Every
variant has forward, backward and checkpoint entries. This PR adds the
fused in-kernel Q/K L2 norm variant through
`use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True` (default False). Callers pass raw BF16
q/k, which removes the separate normalization kernels and the normalized
Q/K copy. Against the same package with the flag off and Q/K normalized
beforehand by the flash-linear-attention `l2norm` kernel and its
backward, it speeds up forward by 1.027x to 1.081x, fwd+bwd by 1.007x to
1.032x and ckpt by 1.014x to 1.031x. Backward alone ranges from 0.969x
to 1.003x, so it is slightly slower on GB200, on GB300 and on the
4-sequence B200 row.

non-deterministic `cake_kda_train` package, which accepts only the flag
off, and a context-parallel (KCP) form of the deterministic package. The

(R200), and this table has no R200 timings.

### [5e8e2b6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5e8e2b6b4ef44003eec2283af8dd568fdf10c1d9)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T08:02:35Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): cheaper setup for the length-aware BF16 decode programs (#8469)

The Cake BF16 decode family has opt-in length-aware stream-K programs,
DEC_B128_LA and DEC_B128_LA_DS. On the cake backend, callers select them
with `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache(...,
length_aware_schedule=True)`. This PR makes their setup cheaper. Outputs
are unchanged bit for bit, and the default programs
(`length_aware_schedule=False`) are untouched.

The baseline is the previous Cake version: the currently shipped
length-aware programs on the same launch.
- **vs the previous version:** across 7 ragged shapes, this PR is 1.091x
to 1.649x faster on B200 and 1.085x to 1.638x faster on GB300.
- **vs trtllm-gen:** on the same ragged shapes, this PR is 1.008x to
1.284x faster on B200 and 1.019x to 1.256x faster on GB300.
- **Uniform lengths:** the opt-in cost is gone. The length-aware
programs now run as fast as the default program.

B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4:

| shape | previous LA µs | this PR µs | trtllm-gen µs | previous/this |
trtllm-gen/this |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rag1375 | 109.54 | 91.71 | 105.73 | 1.194 | 1.153 |
| rag1375, log2 override (device scales) | 109.97 | 91.65 | 105.89 |
1.200 | 1.155 |
| c4096 @ max_seq_len 8192 | 184.75 | 169.33 | 170.66 | 1.091 | 1.008 |
| bim50s1 | 113.20 | 95.89 | 111.78 | 1.181 | 1.166 |
| sq1 | 85.42 | 66.38 | 85.22 | 1.287 | 1.284 |
| seg4096x16 | 55.46 | 33.63 | 38.69 | 1.649 | 1.150 |
| asc | 109.31 | 91.71 | 101.20 | 1.192 | 1.103 |
| *Uniform lengths* | | | | | |
| uniform 4096 | 184.64 | 169.36 | 170.18 | 1.090 | 1.005 |
| uniform 4096, log2 override (device scales) | 185.15 | 169.60 | 171.28
| 1.092 | 1.010 |

GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4:

| shape | previous LA µs | this PR µs | trtllm-gen µs | previous/this |
trtllm-gen/this |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rag1375 | 108.91 | 92.02 | 104.30 | 1.184 | 1.133 |
| rag1375, log2 override (device scales) | 108.75 | 91.34 | 104.69 |
1.191 | 1.146 |
| c4096 @ max_seq_len 8192 | 181.84 | 167.52 | 170.75 | 1.085 | 1.019 |
| bim50s1 | 112.24 | 95.84 | 111.62 | 1.171 | 1.165 |
| sq1 | 84.21 | 66.40 | 83.41 | 1.268 | 1.256 |
| seg4096x16 | 54.61 | 33.34 | 38.08 | 1.638 | 1.142 |
| asc | 107.54 | 91.30 | 100.75 | 1.178 | 1.104 |
| *Uniform lengths* | | | | | |
| uniform 4096 | 181.55 | 167.23 | 171.06 | 1.086 | 1.023 |

| 1.087 | 1.021 |

Shapes:
- All shapes: B=128, q_len 1, 32 query heads, 4 KV heads, head dim 128,
page size 16, BF16, max_seq_len 4096 (8192 for c4096).
- Timing: CUPTI with cold L2. Each µs value is the median over 5 seeded
memory layouts. A ratio above 1 means this PR is faster.
- rag1375: lengths uniform in [1, max_seq_len] (mean 2082).
- bim50s1: half max_seq_len, half <= max_seq_len/8 (mean 2188).
- sq1: max_seq_len*u^2 (mean 1426).
- seg4096x16: 16 requests of 4096, the rest 1 (mean 513).
- asc: a ramp from max_seq_len/128 to max_seq_len (mean 2064).
- c4096: every request 4096 under max_seq_len 8192.
- Device-scale rows run DEC_B128_LA_DS.
- Uniform rows have every request at 4096. With this PR, the
length-aware programs run them as fast as the default program.

The other Cake variants of this decode family (the DEC_B4C4 / _DS
cluster, the DEC_SINK / _DS sinks, and the default DEC_B128 / _DS) are
unchanged, and all programs cover sm_100a and sm_103a.

### [f2b7c8f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f2b7c8f1b6cbe89578391c16a10a61ffea40c574)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T07:57:40Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_grouped_fp8_gemm): route six UE8M0 sm_103a layouts to faster swap-AB programs (#8467)

The Cake contiguous grouped FP8 GEMM (`cake_grouped_fp8_gemm`) is used
through `flashinfer.gemm.prepare_group_gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise_contiguous`
and its launch. It takes FP8 E4M3 inputs and produces BF16 output, with
rows grouped by `m_indices`. It supports two scale formats: FP32 per-128
block scales and packed UE8M0 block scales. This PR changes only
packed-UE8M0-scale launches on sm_103a. It changes the program for six
compact layouts, each given as M x N x K at an alignment. The host's
admission tables in `bs_swap_small_route` make this choice.
`BS_SWAP_SM103_SMALL_ADMIT` now sends four layouts to the one-CTA
swap-AB program `bs_ue8m0_swap_c1`. The first is 1664 x 384 x 128 at
alignment 128, which previously took the non-swapped 128-column store16
program `bs_ue8m0_n128_s16`. The other three previously took
`bs_ue8m0_swap_rp32`: 1024 x 1024 x 512 at alignment 32, 896 x 1024 x
512 at alignment 64 and 1152 x 256 x 1536 at alignment 32. The new
`BS_SWAP_SM103_BM64_ADMIT` table sends 1024 x 1024 x 1024 and 1536 x
1024 x 1024, both at alignment 64, from `bs_ue8m0_swap_rp32` to a new
program, `bs_ue8m0_swap_bm64`. This program is swap-AB with 64-row M
blocks on two-CTA clusters and 64 x 256 tiles. The PR adds it with its
sm_103a module. Every route accumulates each output in the same K order,
so the choice of route never changes the output bits. All other sm_103a
layouts keep their programs. sm_100a ignores both tables, so every
sm_100a launch keeps its program and there is no B200 table. The
baseline is FlashInfer main, which includes the previous Cake version of
this kernel. In the tables below, rows 1-6 change program and run 1.024x
to 1.276x faster than FlashInfer main. Rows 7-90 keep the same program
on both sides. Row 7 (896 x 1024 x 3072 at alignment 64) was evaluated
and is not admitted, so it keeps `bs_ue8m0_swap_rp32`.

Latency per call is in microseconds. Kernel time is measured with CUPTI
with a cold L2. The two sides are interleaved in paired ABBA/BAAB order.
Each measurement uses 8 warmup and 64 timed iterations. Each table comes
from 3 runs with different seeds. The latency is the median over all
measurements of the 3 runs. speedup = FI main latency / this PR latency.
For the six rows that change program, q is the position-cancelled ratio
this PR / FI main. Noise is the largest deviation from 1 among six
same-program A/A comparisons on that row. Both values are shown in
brackets. The reading is FASTER when q < 1 - noise. All six rows read
FASTER on both board classes. Rows 7-90 read "same program", and their
speedups show measured noise around 1.000. GB300 boards fall into two
performance classes, and each table comes from one board of its class.

580.167.08, torch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0 runtime); 90 rows (the owner

Cake also ships the FP32-scale programs of this kernel and three sibling
kernels: the masked batched FP8 GEMM
(`flashinfer.gemm.batch_deepgemm_fp8_nt_groupwise(...,
backend="cake")`), the fused grouped FP8 GEMM + SwiGLU + FP8
quantization (`cake_grouped_fp8_fused_silu_quant`) and the grouped MXFP8
quantizer (`cake_grouped_mxfp8_quantize`); the whole family ships for
sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300).

### [5ca7f52](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5ca7f52c4980cc156a8d93a407cbd937d8a3ed9d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T07:46:02Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): aligned hd256 decode cluster-of-8 program for sm_100a / sm_103a (#8418)

This PR follows up #8337. It adds a fourth program to the Cake FMHA
(`flashinfer.cake_fmha`) paged decode component
`decode_aligned_bf16_hd256`, which provides BF16 programs for
single-query (q_len 1) grouped paged decode at head dim 256 on sm_100a
and sm_103a, with eight query heads per KV head, page size 16 and HND
layout. The new program is a cluster program that splits each (request,
KV head) over a cluster of 8 CTAs. The component now has four programs:
a persistent program, plus cluster programs of 2, 4 and 8 CTAs. The 2-
and 4-CTA cluster programs are regenerated from the same kernel source,
which now computes each rank's push destination once before the merges.
This does not change their results. The persistent program's code is
unchanged. On both B200 and GB300, the decode selector now sends the row
"batch 1, 8 KV heads, 4096 tokens" to the 8-CTA cluster program instead
of `decode_balanced_bf16_hd256`. All other routing is unchanged. The
baseline is main before this PR, which runs the routes #8337 shipped. On
the rerouted row, the new program measures 1.71× on B200 (22.08 → 12.90
µs) and 1.68× on GB300 (21.55 → 12.80 µs). The regenerated 4-CTA program
measures 1.00× on its row.

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_tp_moe_finalize_rmsnorm): route B200 TP8 tokens 640-1008 to the cluster-pair token-owner program (#8463)

The Cake tensor-parallel MoE finalize RMSNorm package (FlashInfer API
backend `"cake"`) ships TP2, TP4 and TP8 routes. #8413 added a
cluster-pair token-owner program, which covers B200 TP8 for T = 145-288
and GB300 TP4 for T = 153-224. This PR adds no new program. It extends
the range where B200 TP8 uses the cluster-pair program.

On B200 (`sm_100a`), TP8 moves T = 640-1008 from the existing
token-owner program to the cluster-pair token-owner program. T = 577-639
and T = 1009-4096 keep the token-owner program. All other ranges, TP
sizes and architectures are unchanged. Compared with the previous Cake
package on FlashInfer main, the window edges measure 1.076 (T = 640) and
1.036 (T = 1008) in Table 1. Every other row runs the same kernel on
both sides. Across T = 640-1008 in steps of 16, the per-session ratios
on two B200 nodes over 3 sessions range from 1.0056 to 1.0847.

### [628c2b9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/628c2b9e6ca0a72a24ce42996c1a9727434c0868)

- **提交信息**: feat(moe_ep): add Rubin offline variant selection (#8427)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Add `--kernel-variant auto` to the Rubin offline tuner. It uses the
existing layer selector to search inference and GenPhase for each
requested capacity, with the same full-forward timing and eligibility
checks.

Offline runs search afresh even when cached winners exist. The CLI
retains its workload, schedule-sweep and iteration options, writes the
per-variant winners and overall selection to v2, and keeps the
per-variant MegaMoE file output. It skips final winner installation.
`--max-candidates` applies to each variant; the default remains
inference.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up to #7911.

Host tests: 192 passed, four CUDA-only skips. Coverage includes

disagreement. All-file pre-commit hooks, CUDA configuration validation

The earlier GPU qualification passed all 15 two-rank variant-selection
cases per rank. GPU tests were not repeated for the typing and host-side
lookup fixes.

CLI tuning and fresh-process replay passed for NVFP4, MXFP8 E4M3/E5M2,
MXFP4/MXFP8 and MXFP4. Checks also covered fresh searches over existing
records, schedule/skew options, multiple capacities, inference-only

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Offline tuning can use `--kernel-variant auto` to compare eligible
SM107 variants with the same workload and select an overall winner.
Results include each variant’s winner and the overall selection.
* You can specify a variant to limit the search. Candidate limits apply
separately to each variant, and workload, warmup, and measurement
settings apply to both searches.
* **Documentation**
* Clarified that automatic selection does not apply or prepare the final
winner. Output-copy timing depends on whether the selected path requires
copies; input generation, weight preparation, compilation, and
correctness checks remain outside measurement.

### [dc067fd](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/dc067fd9274153a73af567f28e8854d212f4b052)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T06:38:54Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn): TMA-staged state for sm_107a nontranspose GDN decode, B>=32 (up to 1.11x) (#8462)

`gated_delta_rule_decode(backend="cake_gdn")` runs the Cake GDN decode.
FlashInfer ships 110 Cake GDN decode records today, and this PR adds 2.
The family covers FP32 and BF16 state, pretranspose and nontranspose
state layouts, and T=1 decode as well as multi-token verify and update
forms. Each shape class has its own bodies; on sm_107a these include
hqsplit, tile and mid4 bodies. This PR delivers one variant: the sm_107a
FP32-state, T=1, nontranspose decode with H16/HV32. It adds one kernel
unit with 2 records, one for scale K^-0.5 and one for scale 1.0. Its
hqsplit body moves the state through TMA, and the state is passed as a
`__grid_constant__` CUDA tensor map. On sm_107a this body now serves the
whole B >= 32 band. Before, B 32 to 36 ran a tile body and B >= 37 ran
the plain hqsplit body. B < 32 is unchanged. Results are bitwise
identical to the previous records on every measured row. The baseline is
the previous Cake version of these routes, which FlashInfer main ships
today. The table has 76 rows: 51 representative decode shapes and 25
shapes across the changed band (B 32 to 1024, including scale 1.0 and
pool slices). Of these, 31 rows move to the new kernel (6 of the 51 and
all 25 band rows), and 45 rows keep their kernel. The geomean speedup is
1.079x over the 31 changed rows and 1.032x over all 76 rows. Per changed
row the speedup is 1.053x to 1.112x, and 1.098x to 1.112x for B 32 to
36. The unchanged rows read 0.996x to 1.005x, which is within the A/A
noise of up to 1.18%. This PR is also faster than FlashInfer's non-Cake
`backend="flashinfer"` kernel on every row in every run. The geomean
against it is 1.293x. The lowest per-run ratio is 1.035x over all rows
(on an unchanged row) and 1.187x over the changed rows.

This PR leaves the other Cake GDN decode variants unchanged: BF16 state,
FP32 pretranspose, FP32 multi-token verify and update, and the other
sm_107a nontranspose bodies. The family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a, and this PR changes only sm_107a.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Added an optimized non-transpose FP32 decode path for supported
hardware when batch sizes are 32 or greater.
* Decode operations can use TMA-backed state access, including during
graph capture and replay.

* **Bug Fixes**
* Improved handling of misaligned state tensors, with invalid inputs
rejected before launch.
* Expanded coverage across additional batch sizes and state-tensor
scenarios.

### [7f1dd09](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7f1dd09f6db04cda1895a7d7823f9e4de12c9dfb)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T06:38:09Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn): sector-complete FP32 state I/O in SM107 full-DV prefill (up to 1.17x) (#8461)

`chunk_gated_delta_rule(backend="cake_gdn")` runs the Cake GDN prefill.
FlashInfer ships 254 Cake GDN prefill records: 115 on sm_100a, 107 on
sm_103a and 111 on sm_107a. One record can serve several architectures.
The records cover BF16 or FP16 I/O with FP32, BF16, FP16 or FP8 state.
Each record runs on either a full-DV body or a DV-split body. This PR
changes one variant: the sm_107a full-DV prefill with BF16 I/O and FP32
initial and final state. This variant has two bodies, plain and
gate-streaming, which serve 15 records. Those records cover Hq/Hv 2/4,
2/8, 4/8, 4/16, 8/16, 8/32, 16/32 and 16/64. Both bodies now move the
FP32 state in full 32-byte sectors. On the global side, each lane moves
two floats. On the TMEM side, the bodies use 16x256b. Outputs and final
states are bitwise identical to main. The baseline is the previous Cake
version of these bodies on FlashInfer main. Across the 74 shapes and
both runs, the geomean speedup is 1.0462x. The largest speedup is
1.1691x (`397b_tp2_hq8_hv32_64x256`, 135.810 -> 116.162 µs).

*NVIDIA VR200 (R200), sm_107a, 212 SMs, driver 620.62, CUDA 13.4
toolchain (torch 2.14.1+cu130). main = the units FlashInfer main ships
today; this PR = the new units. Both sides run on the same GPU,
interleaved per iteration, with a cold L2. Each value is the median
CUPTI GPU time of 1000 calls. s17 and s29 are two runs, with input seeds
17 and 29. Speedup = main / this PR, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster. In a shape label, `hqX_hvY` gives the head counts and `NxL`
means N sequences of L tokens. The batch column gives the sequence count
and lengths. Row 28 is a control row: it runs a DV-split record that
this PR does not change.*

### [e162ed5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e162ed56808c9559bff4455d8c080eff31cefc0e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T06:16:47Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe_v3): faster TP4 EP1 T4096, TP4 EP4 and TP8 EP8 T128 rank programs on sm_103a (#8458)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline for the 384-expert, top-6, hidden-5120 model with activation
clamp 10. A single kernel launch covers dispatch, FC1, clamped SwiGLU,
MXFP8 activation quantization, FC2 and weighted combine. The kernel has
four variants on main, and this PR updates one of them: the TP/EP rank
variant. It changes 3 of the variant's 32 programs: TP4 EP1 (384
experts) at 4096 tokens, and TP4 EP4 (96 local experts) and TP8 EP8 (48
local experts) at 128 tokens.

In the TP4 EP1 4096-token program, each A load now reads its expert row
offset from a shared-memory copy instead of from global memory. In the
two 128-token programs, each thread of the expert histogram loads all of
its routes before it counts them.

The routes are unchanged. Only one host binding changes: the dynamic
shared-memory size of the TP4 EP1 4096-token program. The baseline is
the previous Cake version on main, which is the rank variant as last
updated by #8388. For replicates a / b, the speedups for the changed
programs are:

- TP4 EP1 at 4096 tokens: 1.006x / 1.006x
- TP4 EP4 at 128 tokens: 1.007x / 1.007x
- TP8 EP8 at 128 tokens: 1.007x / 1.007x

In the same order, that saves 2.41 / 2.35 µs, 1.92 / 1.81 µs and 0.97 /
1.00 µs per call. All three changes are faster than the A/A noise band
in both replicates. The other 29 programs run 0.999x to 1.001x in
replicate a and 0.998x to 1.001x in replicate b.

*NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, driver 580.159.03, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130. Per-call latency comes from CUDA-graph replays (20 calls
per graph), taking the median of 21 in-process rounds. The previous
version and this PR ran in separate processes, alternating over 6
rounds. Each value is the median of the 6 process medians. Speedup =
previous / this PR, computed from the latencies before rounding to two
decimals. Columns a and b are two independent replicates, each run alone
on its own node. Each replicate also timed the previous version against
itself (an A/A control) to measure its noise band. The widest band is
0.10 % in replicate a and 0.11 % in replicate b. The other 29 programs
are re-rendered from the current generator. Their kernel text drops
unused macro definitions, their host bindings are byte-identical, and
they compile to the same machine code on sm_103a as the previous
version. Two of them read slower than their band in both replicates: TP4
EP1 at 512 tokens (+0.04 / +0.04 µs) and TP8 EP1 at 512 tokens (+0.02 /
+0.05 µs). Their machine code and bindings are unchanged, so this is
process-level noise, not a regression.*

The other three variants (single-rank routed-FP4, single-rank routed-FP8
and grouped-GEMM routes) ship on sm_100a and sm_103a; the rank variant
ships on sm_103a only.

### [c0cf074](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c0cf0746567209ec0d820584191f30a9d128b2ae)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T06:14:09Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_lm_head_loss): scalar and per-token temperature for chunked_lm_head_logprob(deterministic=False) (#8436)

FlashInfer's Cake chunked LM-head + loss training kernels have a
deterministic form (`flashinfer.experimental.cake_lm_head_det_loss`, the
default) and a non-deterministic (ND) form
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_loss`,
`deterministic=False`). Before this PR, the ND log-probability entry
raised `ValueError` for any temperature other than `None` or `1.0`. This
PR adds the deterministic entry's scalar or per-token FP32 `[T]`
temperature (#8254) to `chunked_lm_head_logprob(...,
deterministic=False, temperature=..., check_temperature=...)` and
`chunked_lm_head_preload(deterministic=False, temperature=True)`, with
kernels for sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. Across B200, GB300 and R200,
ND matches deterministic Cake (0.993x-1.018x, no cell slower) and has a
1.027x-2.421x speedup vs non-Cake SOTA, the fastest PyTorch
implementation.

- **B200, per-token temperature (36 cells):** 0.995x-1.008x vs
deterministic Cake (28 parity, 8 inconclusive, 0 slower); 1.052x-2.421x
vs non-Cake SOTA (36 ND faster).
- **B200, scalar 0.7 (4 cells):** 1.000x-1.007x vs deterministic Cake (2
parity, 2 inconclusive); 1.062x-1.136x vs non-Cake SOTA (4 ND faster).
- **GB300, per-token temperature (36 cells):** 0.997x-1.006x vs
deterministic Cake (31 parity, 5 inconclusive, 0 slower); 1.027x-1.200x
vs non-Cake SOTA (35 ND faster, 1 inconclusive).
- **GB300, scalar 0.7 (4 cells):** 0.999x-1.007x vs deterministic Cake
(4 parity); 1.090x-1.199x vs non-Cake SOTA (4 ND faster).
- **R200, per-token temperature (12 cells):** 0.993x-1.018x vs
deterministic Cake (9 parity, 3 inconclusive, 0 slower); 1.076x-1.335x
vs non-Cake SOTA (12 ND faster).
- **Why PyTorch is the SOTA baseline:** Cut Cross-Entropy 25.1.1 has no
temperature argument (softcap only). It cannot compute this entry. We
timed Liger Kernel 0.8.5's temperature paths on the scalar-temperature
rows. ND is 2.212x-20.361x faster than them on B200 and 2.391x-33.875x
faster on GB300.

**B200.** This table shows B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs) results with driver
580.82.07 and CUDA 13.0 (torch 2.14.1+cu130), 2 steps / 2 nodes per row.
All rows use H = 6144, V = 154880, BF16 and 5 % ignored rows. Per-token
rows use a random FP32 temperature for each token. Scalar rows use
temperature 0.7. Operations are fwd, bwd, fwd+bwd and checkpointed 2x
fwd + bwd (`ckpt 2xfwd+bwd`). Deterministic Cake is the deterministic
package's temperature entry from the same build. Non-Cake SOTA is, per
row, the fastest exact-semantics PyTorch implementation of the same
temperature log-probability. Its tag names the implementation: (c)
PyTorch chunked + torch.compile, (e) PyTorch chunked eager, (u) PyTorch
unchunked autograd. Most rows use (c). In 8 B200 rows, (e) or (u) was
faster, so those rows use it. All runs are cooled, with an idle gap
sized to the back-to-back median and L2 flushed. Latency is the median
over steps of the per-step median CUPTI GPU span. Speedup is baseline
latency / new ND latency, so > 1 means ND is faster. CI95 comes from a
hierarchical bootstrap. The verdict is "ND faster" or "ND slower" only
when the CI95 lies wholly outside 1 ± max(1 %, A/A floor) and every step
agrees. It is "parity" when the CI95 lies wholly inside that band, else
"inconclusive".

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Non-deterministic language-model log-probability calculations now
support temperature scaling, including opt-in memory modes.
* Preloading now supports temperature-specific kernels in
non-deterministic mode.
* Temperature-scaled language-model-head operations are available on
additional supported GPU architectures.
* **Bug Fixes**
* Boolean temperatures are rejected with a clear validation error;
non-unit temperature support is limited to the supported
non-deterministic routes.
* **Documentation**
* Added guidance on temperature inputs, supported operations,
architecture coverage, and preload behavior.

### [9f837cc](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9f837ccef4b9ca63c5d10249a308521a0d91c634)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T06:13:54Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_cp): native BF16 GDN CP prefill on sm_107a (up to 1.35x) (#8457)

Cake's Gated DeltaNet (GDN) context-parallel (CP) prefill kernel in
FlashInfer has six variants: BF16 and FP16 I/O on each of sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR replaces the sm_107a BF16 variant with
native BF16 programs. With it, `backend="cake_gdn"` with `use_cp="auto"`
runs Cake CP for single-sequence calls that have BF16 inputs and
outputs, int32 `cu_seqlens`, FP32 initial and final state, gate and beta
tensors, Q/K already normalized by the caller, and no state checkpoints
or state indices; on `main` these calls fail closed. The call must also
have (Hq, Hv) in {(2, 4), (4, 8), (2, 8), (8, 16), (4, 16), (8, 32)}
with Hk = Hq, and a length that is a multiple of 128 up to 65536 tokens:
at least 4096 tokens for Hv ≤ 8 and at least 8192 tokens for Hv of 16 or
32. Other calls, including int64 `cu_seqlens`, keep their current route,
and the default backend is unchanged. On these shapes the new route is
1.093x to 1.351x faster than FlashInfer's default backend
(`backend="auto"`, `use_cp="auto"`).

GPU: NVIDIA R200 (216 SMs), sm_107a, driver 615.71.10. Kernels
JIT-compiled with CUDA 13.4.92; PyTorch CUDA runtime 13.0. Times are the
median CUPTI kernel span of 4 runs with a cold L2, for one sequence.

### [9f12b61](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9f12b61393441cc0f7a916a5a51b9ad4748e25ab)

- **作者**: Mingyang Wang
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T06:11:49Z
- **提交信息**: fix: update FMHA cubins for grouped NVFP4 decode (#8422)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Multi-token NVFP4 decode can select grouped FMHA kernels that are absent
from the pinned cubin drop, causing a missing-kernel error. Update the
FMHA artifact path and manifest checksum to the published
`f50085594b9adcf9cbde7b8ea108c8587fa99b4c` drop, which supplies those
kernels. Keep the existing dispatcher and add 20 numerical regression
cases spanning head dimensions 128/256, PDL off/on, and
single-token/grouped GQA configurations.

## 🔍 Related Issues

https://nvidia.atlassian.net/browse/IKL-607

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull
request, please make sure the following items are complete.

(or used your preferred method).

pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

Targeted validation on B200 / CUDA 13.4 using the checked-in pin,
default public repository, and a fresh JIT cache with no artifact
overrides or AOT provider:

- Both original `case-1296-False-128/256` failures, 20 new NVFP4
regressions, and two BF16 controls: **24 passed** in 136.29 seconds.
- Additional H256 / KV1024 numerical smoke: passed, with a confirmed
grouped Q8 CGA launch.
- Manifest, metadata and all 30 downloaded cubin checksums verified.
- `pre-commit run --files flashinfer/artifacts.py
tests/attention/test_trtllm_gen_attention_decode.py` and diff checks
passed. The all-files hook run and full test suite were not run.

### [c8e6bca](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c8e6bca2abba80e85607a0c79311dc8a21e7a611)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T06:05:25Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): 256-bit O stores in fp8_lowhead_one_partition and a column-split O drain in bf16_swa128_single_cta on sm_100a (#8452)

`cake_dsv4` is the Cake DSv4 sparse-MLA decode and prefill backend in
FlashInfer for BF16 and FP8 KV caches. Twenty programs serve the
197-shape list on each architecture. This PR changes two of them on
SM100 (sm_100a). `fp8_lowhead_one_partition` now stores O with 256-bit
stores, and `bf16_swa128_single_cta` now splits its O drain by columns.
On SM103 (sm_103a), it renames one unit (`fp8_lowhead_one_partition`)
without changing any instructions. The baseline is FlashInfer main,
which ships the previous Cake version of these programs from #8381. On
B200 (SM100), the 197 shapes break down as 16 faster (1.012x to 1.025x
for `bf16_swa128_single_cta`, 1.007x to 1.015x for
`fp8_lowhead_one_partition`), 0 tie, 0 slower and 181 same code. On
GB300 (SM103), all 197 shapes are same code.

Latencies are in microseconds. Speedup = FlashInfer main latency / this
PR latency.

Verdicts: **faster** = every counted reading shows this PR faster than
main by more than the measured run-to-run noise band, with readings in
both run orders. **tie** = the readings are not all faster (or all
slower) than main beyond the noise band. **same code** = this PR does
not change the machine code that runs this shape, so both columns carry
one measurement of that code and the row reads 1.000x.

**NVIDIA B200 (SM100, sm_100a), CUDA 13.4, 197 shapes** (16 faster, 0
tie, 0 slower, 181 same code)

### [9d78002](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9d780024489c87d87b4114240ae9da47713d35e4)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T05:54:56Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det): elected ready-count publish for split-scan overlap; enable on GB300 (#8448)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train` is FlashInfer's
deterministic Gated DeltaNet chunked training kernel. It runs packed
variable-length training (forward + backward), and its outputs and
gradients are bitwise reproducible. The previous PR extended the overlap
of the backward tail with the adjoint scan to split adjoint scan plans
on sm_100a. That overlap applies when total tokens x value heads >=
393216 (3 x 2^17), and it used the same scan as single-round plans. This
PR makes two changes to that split-plan path. First, the second scan
pass that runs beside the overlapped tail now uses a new scan variant
that publishes the per-chunk ready counts in an elected form. Once every
four chunks, and at a segment's last chunk, the 64 store threads meet at
a named barrier. One thread then issues a single GPU-scope fence and
adds 64 to each chunk's ready count. Before, each of the 64 threads
fenced every second chunk and added 1. This shortens the scan's publish
cost on the overlapped split pass. Second, the split-plan overlap is now
enabled on sm_103a (GB300) with the same rule as on sm_100a: a split
plan whose second pass has more CTAs than SMs, a fused BF16-dbeta HV =
2H tail, no head groups, and tokens x HV >= 393216. The new scan variant
is a separate kernel built only for sm_100a and sm_103a. Single-round
(serial-scan) overlapped plans keep the previous scan kernel and the
same launches as before. Calls under CUDA graph capture also keep plain
launches, and sm_107a is unchanged. Outputs and gradients are bitwise
identical to the previous version on every measured row. The baseline is
the previous version of this kernel on current FlashInfer main (speedup
= main / this PR, so >1 is faster; median over 56 interleaved cells). On
B200, forward + backward on the 7 x ~4.3k real pack with H / HV 8 / 16
drops from 1.0680 to 1.0598 ms (1.008x). On GB300, the same real pack
drops from 0.9889 to 0.9784 ms (1.011x), and 1 x 16384 with H / HV 16 /
32 drops from 1.0575 to 1.0371 ms (1.020x). Rows marked "no" run the
same launches as FlashInfer main, so the spread in their f+b ratios is
measurement noise: B200 ranges from 0.997x to 1.020x (for example, 1 x
16384 8 / 16 shows 1.020x and 131071 + 87531 + 43385 shows 0.997x, both
with unchanged launches), and GB300 is 1.000x. The forward pass is
unchanged.

### [743425c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/743425c5616953b76bd1f51f0deb79a23998dddc)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T05:36:13Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): opt-in length-aware BF16 decode schedule (#8447)

This PR adds length-aware twins of the Cake BF16 decode stream-K
programs DEC_B128 and DEC_B128_DS. On the cake backend, callers select
them with `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache(...,
length_aware_schedule=True)`. The twins size each request's work by its
actual `seq_lens` entry instead of `max_seq_len`. The default
`length_aware_schedule=False` keeps today's programs and routes. The
baseline is the current default Cake program on the same launch. Across
7 ragged shapes, the length-aware programs are 1.184x to 1.946x faster
than it on B200 and 1.227x to 2.209x faster on GB300.

Setup: B=128, q_len 1, 32 query heads, 4 KV heads, head dim 128, page
size 16, BF16, max_seq_len 4096 (8192 for c4096). Timing is paired CUPTI
with cold L2 over 5 seeded layouts. A ratio above 1 means the
length-aware (LA) program is faster. A trtllm-gen/LA ratio below 1 means
trtllm-gen is faster.

B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4:

| shape | default µs | LA µs | trtllm-gen µs | default/LA |
trtllm-gen/LA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rag1375 | 132.0 | 109.8 | 105.6 | 1.201 | 0.961 |
| rag1375, log2 override (device scales) | 132.8 | 110.4 | 105.8 | 1.215
| 0.961 |
| c4096 @ max_seq_len 8192 | 256.1 | 184.5 | 171.5 | 1.387 | 0.930 |
| bim50s1 | 134.2 | 113.3 | 112.3 | 1.184 | 0.989 |
| sq1 | 121.9 | 85.5 | 85.5 | 1.428 | 1.001 |
| seg4096x16 | 107.5 | 55.3 | 38.7 | 1.946 | 0.700 |
| asc | 132.3 | 109.9 | 101.1 | 1.202 | 0.921 |
| *Uniform lengths (opt-in cost)* | | | | | |
| uniform 4096 | 169.5 | 184.6 | 170.1 | 0.917 | 0.920 |
| uniform 4096, log2 override (device scales) | 169.1 | 184.5 | 170.9 |
0.916 | 0.925 |

GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4:

| shape | default µs | LA µs | trtllm-gen µs | default/LA |
trtllm-gen/LA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rag1375 | 133.1 | 108.4 | 104.6 | 1.228 | 0.962 |
| rag1375, log2 override (device scales) | 133.4 | 108.8 | 104.0 | 1.227
| 0.957 |
| c4096 @ max_seq_len 8192 | 251.3 | 182.2 | 170.9 | 1.388 | 0.937 |
| bim50s1 | 137.3 | 111.9 | 111.8 | 1.227 | 0.994 |
| sq1 | 122.8 | 84.3 | 83.3 | 1.459 | 0.987 |
| seg4096x16 | 119.3 | 54.7 | 38.0 | 2.209 | 0.693 |
| asc | 132.4 | 107.8 | 100.3 | 1.230 | 0.927 |
| *Uniform lengths (opt-in cost)* | | | | | |
| uniform 4096 | 167.2 | 181.6 | 170.9 | 0.921 | 0.942 |
| uniform 4096, log2 override (device scales) | 167.2 | 182.0 | 170.5 |
0.919 | 0.938 |

Shapes:
- rag1375: lengths uniform in [1, max_seq_len] (mean 2082).
- bim50s1: half max_seq_len, half <= max_seq_len/8 (mean 2188).
- sq1: max_seq_len*u^2 (mean 1426).
- seg4096x16: 16 requests of 4096, the rest 1 (mean 513).
- asc: a ramp from max_seq_len/128 to max_seq_len (mean 2064).
- c4096: every request 4096 under max_seq_len 8192.
- Device-scale rows run DEC_B128_DS and DEC_B128_LA_DS.
- Uniform rows have every request at 4096. They show the cost only when
`length_aware_schedule=True`. The default path is unchanged.

The other Cake variants of this decode family (DEC_B4C4 / _DS cluster
and DEC_SINK / _DS sinks) are unchanged, and all programs cover sm_100a
and sm_103a.

### [b9e7c21](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b9e7c2128ab7105f17974d591bde8a511a3cc1d0)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T05:31:52Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc): with grad, slab-order column slab on 212-SM R200 boards in the non-deterministic route (#8410)

Cake's mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections) kernel with grad has
a deterministic mode (det) and an opt-in non-deterministic mode, nd
(`deterministic=False` of
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train`). The workload is X BF16
[T, 4, H] (4 streams) with an FP32 mapping and H = 4096, 5120 or 7168.
It is a local (non-KCP) operator and also runs on a context-parallel
rank's local shard. The nd backward finish is an atomic column slab.
Host rules pick its unit order and its two-size LPT
(longest-processing-time) geometry for each token count T. This PR
retunes both for one board: sm_107a with 212 SMs (R200) at hidden 4096.

- nd gets per-board override cells keyed by (architecture, SM count,
hidden size). The route reads the device SM count. Only sm_107a / 212
SMs / hidden 4096 has cells:
- unit order: "chunk" up to 1876 tokens (as before) and "slab"
(slab-fastest) from 1877 tokens;
- LPT keep-fraction pairs: (0.5, 0.97) up to 1876 tokens (as before),
(0.5, 0.985) for 1877..33600, (0.5, 0.98) for 33601..34368 and (0.5,
0.97) above 34368.
- The PR adds sm_107a builds of the slab-order column-slab programs. On
main they were built for sm_100a and sm_103a only.
- Unchanged: every other GPU (including sm_107a boards with 208 or 216
SMs) and every call below 1877 tokens or at hidden 5120/7168 launch
exactly as before. The forward and the backward prepare are unchanged on
every board.
- Outputs: only the order of nd's atomic dfn additions changes. At all
19 token counts below, nd's forward outputs, dX, the other backward
outputs except dfn, and dscale/dbase are bitwise equal to det. nd's dfn
relative L2 vs det is at most 1.02e-07.
- Docstring fix: with grad, nd dscale/dbase are bitwise the
deterministic package's per-CTA reduction. That equals det except at
hidden 4096 above 14927 tokens on sm_100a and sm_103a, where det sums
over 8-token group rows and low-order bits can differ.

212-SM cells removed, which is exactly how nd launched on this board
before this PR. new = this PR. Speedup = previous / new. The backward
runs from saved statistics. The forward launches identically and is not
listed. T = 1024 and 1536 (below 1877) also launch identically and serve
as a noise reference: 0.999..1.000 (evd) and 0.998..1.006 (graph).
Timing: 4 processes, one per GPU of one 4-GPU node, run concurrently.
Each process times every token count with all arms on the same inputs,
and the arms are rotated and mirrored inside each group. evd = eager
calls timed with CUDA events after a 512 MiB L2 flush and a GPU spin
that lets the host enqueue the whole call first (16 groups x 16 calls).
graph = CUDA-graph replays, each after a 512 MiB L2 flush (16 groups x
30 replays). Each process takes the median over groups; the table shows
the median over the 4 processes.
Setup: NVIDIA R200 (VR200 board), sm_107a, 212 SMs, driver 620.43.
Memory clock steady at 3186 MHz during the runs (this board's maximum is
4752 MHz), SM clock 2412 MHz under load, power limit 2300 W. Cake
kernels built with CUDA 13.4. X BF16 [T, 4, 4096], FP32 mapping, 4
streams, non-KCP, random inputs.

## Speedup vs det and B0

- **det** ("deterministic Cake"): `deterministic=True` from the same
build (this PR's head). This is the original deterministic Cake
implementation, and this PR does not change it.
- **B0** ("non-Cake SOTA"): for each row, the faster of IEEE-FP32 eager
PyTorch and `torch.compile` (inductor default, fullgraph=False,
dynamic=False, TF32 off) running the same mHC function with grad.
torch.compile won all 57 rows, and the B0 cell names the winner. PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. B0's dfn relative L2 vs det is at most
2.02e-06, with 0 dX mismatches at 1e-2.
- **Why B0 is the strongest applicable baseline:** it is the only
non-Cake implementation of this exact function at these sizes.
TransformerEngine's mHC (TF32 mapping math, log-domain Sinkhorn without
eps) and Megatron-LM's fused mHC (TF32 projection) compute a different
function. FlashInfer's `flashinfer.mhc` kernels and DeepGEMM's mega_mhc
are inference only.
- **new** ("new non-deterministic Cake"): nd from this PR.
- **Operations:** forward = forward prepare + forward finish. backward =
backward prepare + backward finish from saved statistics. checkpointed
step = forward + statistics recompute + backward on the checkpoint path.
For B0 the checkpointed step is a no-grad forward + a with-grad forward
+ the backward.

| R200 / sm_107a (212 SMs) | T=32768, X BF16 [T, 4, 4096], FP32 mapping,
4 streams, non-KCP | checkpointed step | 1437.4 us | 18705.1 us
(compile) | 1429.1 us | 1.006 | 13.089 | 1305.7 / 1279.5 = 1.020 |
1299.5 / 1274.5 = 1.020 |
| R200 / sm_107a (212 SMs) | T=65536, X BF16 [T, 4, 4096], FP32 mapping,
4 streams, non-KCP | forward | 902.0 us | 15103.5 us (compile) | 902.0
us | 1.000 | 16.744 | 895.7 / 895.7 = 1.000 | 893.4 / 893.3 = 1.000 |
| R200 / sm_107a (212 SMs) | T=65536, X BF16 [T, 4, 4096], FP32 mapping,
4 streams, non-KCP | backward | 1614.5 us | 12282.1 us (compile) |
1669.8 us | 0.967 | 7.356 | 1419.2 / 1408.4 = 1.008 | 1419.1 / 1408.6 =
1.007 |
| R200 / sm_107a (212 SMs) | T=65536, X BF16 [T, 4, 4096], FP32 mapping,
4 streams, non-KCP | checkpointed step | 2801.1 us | 42149.7 us
(compile) | 2804.2 us | 0.999 | 15.031 | 2538.4 / 2527.3 = 1.004 |
2530.5 / 2522.7 = 1.003 |

**Table 2.** Main columns: CUPTI kernel-sum latency (`bench_gpu_time`,
the sum of the operation's kernel durations). Each value is the median
over 4 ABBA-ordered groups of the per-group median of 64 iterations
(warmup 8, cold L2). All three arms run in one process on the same
random inputs. 4 processes (one per GPU) run concurrently, each on a
share of the token counts. Speedup = det / new and B0 / new; above 1
means new is faster. Check columns: det / new nd latency and ratio in
Table 1's evd and graph timings (same 4-process runs; the forward comes
from a separate run of the same method). Setup as in Table 1: R200
(VR200 board), sm_107a, 212 SMs, driver 620.43, memory clock 3186 MHz
(board maximum 4752 MHz), SM clock 2412 MHz under load, power limit 2300
W, CUDA 13.4.

Why the check columns: kernel-sum adds up kernel durations, so time in
which two kernels run at the same time (for example through programmatic
dependent launch, PDL) is counted twice. det overlaps more at small T
and nd overlaps more at large T. So kernel-sum overstates the backward
and checkpointed-step speedups vs det at small T and understates them at
large T. For example, the backward reads 1.271 in kernel-sum at T =
1024, but evd reads 1.060. B0 is only CUPTI-timed, so the main columns
stay on kernel-sum.

Results over the 57 rows:

- **Forward:** parity with det, because nd runs copies of the
deterministic forward programs: 0.997..1.003 (kernel-sum), 0.998..1.004
(evd), 0.999..1.005 (graph). vs B0: 8.055..16.744.
- **Backward:** vs det, 0.967..1.357 in kernel-sum. Kernel-sum is below
1.000 at T = 14928, 15288, 15590, 16114, 16132, 16164 and 65536 (worst
0.967 at 65536). In the evd and graph checks every row is faster:
1.008..1.062 (evd) and 1.007..1.066 (graph). CUPTI active time (the
union of kernel intervals, which does not double-count overlap) is also
faster on those 7 rows except T = 65536. There it reads 0.995, while evd
reads 1.008 and graph 1.007; this row has the smallest margin. vs B0:
7.356..9.001.
- **Checkpointed step:** vs det, 0.988..1.247 in kernel-sum, below 1.000
at the same 7 token counts (worst 0.988 at 15288). evd reads
1.004..1.110 and graph 1.003..1.105, with no row below 1.000. vs B0:
9.853..15.031.

The kernel's other Cake variants are the deterministic mode and hidden
5120 and 7168, and the family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a;
this PR changes only the nd backward column slab on 212-SM sm_107a
boards at hidden 4096.

### [f583862](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f58386284053ea3bbbcaddcd216841b283ba80a8)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T05:29:41Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_fmha): keep the FP8 decode programs' page-32 table slots in the stage (#8445)

## Problem

This affects two FP8 paged decode programs, B4_S8X16_SM100A and
B4_S8X16_SM103A (`cake_fmha_decode_fp8_4a15e1e5d592f3ec8833`,
`cake_fmha_decode_fp8_56920e5612bc123d66c9`).

The page-offset warp stores each page id at slot `g * 8 + page` of its
256-byte stage. Here `g` is the lane's group block. In a page-32 build,
a block spans 4 pages. So the lanes of group blocks 4-7 name slots past
the stage.

Those copies are predicated off. No write leaves the stage, but the
address does.

## Fix

Lanes of blocks 4-7 now take the upper half of the slots of blocks 0-3:

```
pg_id_slot = g % 4 * 8 + g / 4 * pages_per_block + page
```

The load warp does not read that half.

- Every lane's slot is now inside the stage.
- No two lanes share a slot.
- Page-16 builds keep their slots, so those programs do not change.
- One line changes in each of the two programs.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/attention/test_cake_fmha_decode_programs.py -k fp8`: 42
passed, 267 deselected, on both B200 and GB300.
- pre-commit passes on the changed files, including clang-format.
- Outputs are bitwise equal to main on all 10 timed row-layouts below.
- compute-sanitizer memcheck reports 0 device errors on both B200 and
GB300.

## Timing

Setup: B200 (sm_100a), CUDA 13.4.
- old = main
- new = this PR
- ctl = a second copy of main

The timed new kernel files are byte-identical to this PR's files, and
the timed old files to main's files. Each value is GPU-busy time per
call, over batches of 100 back-to-back calls, with cold L2 per sample.

### [d67a1b9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d67a1b9817e4b12687571dd052e251b3842257ae)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T05:29:04Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_fmha): cache the small-M partition SM count per CUDA stream ID (#8420)

## Problem

#8387 (merged) cached the stream context's SM count under (device, raw
stream handle, current context handle). After the merge, CodeRabbit
flagged on #8387 that a stream handle can be reused.

A destroyed stream's handle can come back for a stream of a new green
context of another size. That stream then read the old partition's SM
count. It planned more splits than its partition holds, and it hung.

With merged main's `cake_fmha.py`, the new `torch_recreated` GPU test
hangs until its 120 s watchdog fires. This happens on both B200 and
GB300.

## Fix

The SM count is now cached under the stream's unique ID
(`cuStreamGetId`). The driver never reuses this ID. Measured on B200:

- A reused handle got a new ID (16 -> 19).
- The legacy default stream has its own ID in each context: 7 in the
primary context, and 15 and 18 in two green contexts.

A launch reads the key with one driver call, as before. The cache keeps
the `CUstream` object of each raw handle, so the call builds none. The
stream's context (`cuStreamGetCtx`, else the current context) and its SM
count are read only for a new stream.

The per-thread default stream takes a fallback path. So does a
cuda-python without `cuStreamGetId`. On that path the context is
resolved on every launch, and the cache key is `cuCtxGetId`.

A process with no green context still reads one module flag and queries
nothing.

## Tests

- Host tests for a reused stream handle under the stream-ID key:
  - a known stream reads no context;
  - a reused handle with a new ID reads its own context;
  - the per-thread stream takes the context path.
- The same host tests under the context-ID fallback.
- GPU test variant `torch_recreated` of
`test_cake_decode_smallm_in_an_sm_partition_completes`. It plans on a
64-SM torch green context and destroys it. Then it runs kv8200, kv60008
and kv1032 on a new 32-SM green context whose stream reuses the handle.

Results on B200 and GB300 (CUDA 13.4):

- 8/8 partition tests pass.
- The full-device route audit matches main in 10110/10110 cases in each
of 5 processes.
- All 90 timed outputs are bitwise equal to main.
- pre-commit passes.

SM-count helper alone, per call, main -> this PR:

- B200: 0.35 -> 0.27 µs
- GB300: 0.43 -> 0.34 µs

## Timing

Each value is a host time median in µs, over 5 fresh processes x 24
rounds x 50 calls. Each row shows main / main again / this PR.

- **Partition path:** partition support is enabled and the stream runs
on the whole device.
- **Default path:** the process has no green context. This path runs the
same code as main.

### B200 (sm_100a)

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Partition | kv8200 | 38.38 | 38.37 | 38.13 |
| Partition | kv60008 | 38.88 | 38.97 | 38.52 |
| Partition | kv1032 | 38.71 | 38.80 | 38.59 |
| Default | kv8200 | 36.17 | 36.05 | 35.97 |
| Default | kv60008 | 36.33 | 36.29 | 36.21 |

Over all 9 measured rows:

- Partition path: PR/main is 0.990-0.997 (main/main 0.997-1.002).
- Default path: PR/main is 0.990-1.005 (main/main 0.997-1.002).

This PR changes which program the FP8 paged-context route picks on
sm_100a (B200), using two rules:

- **R1:** pack-1 calls with ≥ 640 tiles now use the one-stage runtime
program (`_Q1`) instead of the runtime program.
- **R2:** the q-term now applies only for kv < 1024 (the kv bound drops
from 2048 to 1024). Long query rows from 1024 keys now take the runtime
program instead of the JIT module.

The route now sends 43 of the 99 screened shapes to a different program.
The baseline is current main's route on the same launch. All 43 moved
shapes are faster than main on both B200 nodes, with median ratios of
1.010–1.402:

- R1 covers 16 shapes, at 1.26–1.40x.
- R2 covers 27 shapes, at 1.01–1.05x. Four of these are moved only by
the new kv bound (128-256-1024, 256-128-1024 at page 16 and 64, and
256-128-1536).

### [da5367e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/da5367e4ddaea15bc0301a22ab5a8f6923d116c0)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T05:03:10Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): add GB200 / GB300 T-exact row rules for the thin input gradient, the N 512 forwards and the 6144 x 2048 rows (#8441)

This PR adds row rules to the Cake `dense_projection_det_gemm` package
in `flashinfer.experimental`, the deterministic dense projection GEMM.
The package has 127 programs built from 124 templates. Most are
BF16-operand GEMMs (forward, dgrad and wgrad), and one is an FP32 router
GEMM. The PR adds 16 rules, 8 for `sm_100a` and 8 for `sm_103a`. Each
rule applies at a single token count T and routes BF16-output forward
and dgrad rows to programs that already ship. No program or template is
added or removed, the rule count goes from 341 to 357, and `sm_107a` is
unchanged.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of the package on main.
Against it, the changed rows have speedups of 1.011–1.030 on GB200,
1.011–1.034 on GB300, 1.004–1.034 on B200 and 1.010–1.016 on B300. No
changed row is slower on any of the four GPUs. All other rows of the
294-row shape list plan the same programs as main.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** GB200
(`sm_100a`, 152 SMs), GB300 (`sm_103a`, 152 SMs), B200 (`sm_100a`, 148
SMs), B300 (`sm_103a`, 148 SMs); CUDA 13.4, cold L2, BF16 output.
Speedup = previous time / this PR time, and values above 1 mean this PR
is faster. "—" means the PR does not change that row on that GPU.

### [8ec7bee](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8ec7beebfac7bb1654cb7d8cf8fca2902e5892ea)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T04:28:30Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): launch the deterministic router program through this package's binding (#8430)

The `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` family has
BF16-input dense and batched projection GEMMs. It also has an FP32
router GEMM (256 experts, BF16x3 emulation). `deterministic=True` (the
default) calls `dense_projection_det_gemm`. `deterministic=False` runs
the split-K / stream-K programs of #8190, #8238, #8261 and #8275. #8309
and #8373 cut their host (CPU) cost. Both packages ship on `sm_100a`,
`sm_103a` and `sm_107a`.

This PR changes the eager convenience path for some
`deterministic=False` router calls. When such a call runs the
deterministic program, it now launches that program through this
package's own cached launch binding. This applies to the router forward
and the input gradient. It also applies to weight-gradient rows that
have no measured stream-K plan. The binding uses the deterministic
package's plan, programs and fixed-order reduction. The results are
therefore bitwise the same as `deterministic=True`. Each call needs
fewer host operations. The workspace views are converted once, and entry
points pass their own tensors as launch views. Plans, split counts,
numeric results, prepared launches and the projection GEMMs do not
change.

Against previous Cake (FlashInfer main 14102c74, which includes #8373),
router 2fwd+bwd is 1.216-1.291 on GB300 and 1.228-1.297 on GB200. This
holds on all 15 router rows per GPU. Router bwd is 1.255-1.398 (GB300)
and 1.285-1.425 (GB200). Router fwd is 1.117-1.211 (GB300) and
1.144-1.224 (GB200). CUDA graph replays of prepared launches do not
change. Previous/new is 0.982-1.015 (GB300) and 0.986-1.013 (GB200) over
60 cells per GPU. A control run with FlashInfer main in both arms spans
0.981-1.012 in CUDA graphs on GB300 (60 cells, 4 runs). These graph
values are therefore run-to-run noise.

Against det Cake (`deterministic=True`), eager router 2fwd+bwd was
slower before this PR. In the control run, det/previous was 0.955-0.992
on GB300. With this PR, it is faster on every router row: 1.173-1.260
(GB300) and 1.184-1.277 (GB200). Router bwd is 1.259-1.425 (GB300) and
1.268-1.481 (GB200). Router fwd is 1.137-1.214 (GB300) and 1.146-1.235
(GB200). The smallest 2fwd+bwd gains are hidden 5120 at T 192 and 128 on
GB300 (1.173 and 1.183). There, the measured stream-K weight-gradient
kernel (about 16-17 us) ends the step after the host has issued it.

Router 2fwd+bwd beats SOTA on every row except two. At T 64, SOTA/new is
1.984-2.726 (GB300) and 1.889-2.578 (GB200). The reason is that the
BF16x9 router forward takes 131.6-189.6 us there on GB300. At T
128-1024, SOTA/new is 0.966-1.250 (GB300) and 1.105-1.381 (GB200). SOTA
is faster on GB300 at T 128 for hidden 4096 (0.990) and hidden 5120
(0.966). We did not measure plain FP32 `cublasSgemm`, which also meets
the router's accuracy budget. Router SOTA/new values above 1 can
therefore overstate the gap. R200 (`sm_107a`) runs the same host code
but was not timed.

- **Row:** one GPU, shape and op, measured as an eager call sequence of
the entry points (no prepared launch, no CUDA graph). There are 45 rows
per GPU and 90 in all.
- **Shapes:** FP32 router GEMM, hidden 4096, 5120 or 6144, 256 experts,
T 64, 128, 192, 224 or 1024 tokens.
- **Ops:** fwd = forward GEMM. bwd = input gradient + weight gradient.
2fwd+bwd = checkpointed step (2 x fwd + bwd).
- **Latency:** median us of the CUPTI GPU interval of the op, from first
kernel begin to last kernel end. L2 is cold before every iteration.
- **Runs:** each run has 15 paired groups x 20 timed steps per arm, in
rotated arm order. A cell is the median of the per-run medians. Each GPU
has 4 runs on 1 node, one per GPU. Two runs use one long-lived process,
and two runs use a new process per row.
- **Baselines:** det Cake = `deterministic=True`. Previous Cake =
`deterministic=False` at FlashInfer main 14102c74 (includes #8373). SOTA
(every GEMM of the op) = cuBLAS 13.1.1 `cublasSgemm` with
`CUBLAS_FP32_EMULATED_BF16X9_MATH`.
- **Ratio:** baseline us / new us of the cells shown. A value above 1.00
means this PR is faster.
- **Setup:** NVIDIA GB300, `sm_103a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03; NVIDIA
GB200, `sm_100a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.126.20; CUDA 13.4 (driver API);
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

Counted TMA-epilogue bf16 dW cast for a short last chunk under the zero-dlogp row skip of the non-deterministic LM-head log-prob backward, and a shorter host path for the skip. Package re-rendered from the merged generator revision (kernel SASS unchanged).

### [98dfbd5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/98dfbd5990b9c24031c716ea3e6842d95ee41ed7)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T03:34:03Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_kcp): fold the output program into the forward walks of the non-deterministic KCP package (#8421)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp` is the non-deterministic
KCP GDN training package. It covers:

- BF16
- the contiguous (C), zigzag (Z) and zigzag-per-document (D) KCP layouts
- with or without in-kernel Q/K L2 norm
- forward, forward+backward, and checkpointed 2 x forward + backward
with or without a recompute handle
- eager and CUDA graph

This PR adds a fused forward output path. The output program now runs
inside the forward walks, through fused output kernels from a new kernel
set (`kcp_fwdh_out`, 6 kernel libraries). The PR also regenerates 21
existing kernel units. The regeneration changes only text: SASS is
identical on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, and the bindings are
unchanged. Outputs and gradients are bitwise equal to the previous
version.

## Speedup vs the previous version (FlashInfer main at #8364)

- **B200:** this PR is faster on all 21 claimed cells. Forward is 1.048
to 1.130. fwd+bwd, ckpt and ckpt + recompute handle are 1.012 to 1.036.
Seven layout C cells reached the power-cap threshold. They are shown but
not claimed.
- **GB300:** this PR is faster on all 24 cells. Forward is 1.050 to
1.110. fwd+bwd, ckpt and ckpt + recompute handle are 1.016 to 1.041.
- **R200 (1 GPU, CP1):** this PR is faster on all 8 cells. Forward is
1.152 to 1.177. fwd+bwd, ckpt and ckpt + recompute handle are 1.042 to
1.051.

**How to read the tables.**
- Speedup = baseline ms / this PR ms, computed from the 3-decimal
absolutes in the same row. Above 1.000 means this PR is faster. Values
below 1.000 are marked "this PR slower" or "REGRESSION: non-Cake
faster".
- Previous version = `cake_gdn_train_kcp` on FlashInfer main at #8364,
without this PR. Deterministic Cake = `cake_gdn_det_train_kcp` on the
same main. This PR does not change it.
- Timed step: the KCP causal conv1d (10240 channels) plus one GDN layer,
head dim 128. Latency is the slowest rank per iteration, and each cell
is the median over samples. bwd = fwd+bwd - fwd, computed from those
medians.
- ckpt = `torch.utils.checkpoint(use_reentrant=False)`, 2 x forward +
backward. ckpt + recompute handle is the same with one recompute handle
per step. The recompute handle exists only in Cake.
- Run 1 and run 2 ran in the same window with the arm order rotated. Run
2 reverses the order of run 1.
- "unstable": an arm drifted more than the 2 % limit, so that ratio is
not claimed. The cell was measured once more in the same window with the
same protocol, shown as a "re-measure" row.
- "power-capped": the GPU software power-cap share reached 5 % or more
(NVML, 50 ms sampling). The cell is shown but not claimed.
- "superseded by the sustained row": this marks a B200 layout C cell
where a short run reached the power-cap threshold. The
sustained-protocol row for that cell replaces the short-run rows.
- "unpaired": on B200 and GB300, the non-Cake values come from a
separate, earlier run. On R200, the run-2 non-Cake cells reuse the run-1
value from the same job.

## Speedup vs deterministic Cake and the strongest non-Cake
implementation (CP8 on B200 and GB300, CP1 on R200)

- **vs deterministic Cake:**
- Forward: 1.047 to 1.128 on B200, 1.068 to 1.130 on GB300 and 1.179 /
1.178 on R200 (runs 1 / 2).
- fwd+bwd, ckpt and ckpt + recompute handle: 1.019 to 1.040 on B200,
1.021 to 1.184 on GB300 and 1.049 to 1.054 on R200 (fwd+bwd 1.054 /
1.051, ckpt 1.051 / 1.049, ckpt + recompute handle 1.051 / 1.049).
- The derived backward stays at parity: 0.999 to 1.006 on B200, 0.994 to
1.000 on GB300 and 1.004 / 1.001 on R200. Rows below 1.000 are marked
"this PR slower".
- **vs the strongest non-Cake implementation on B200 and GB300 (FlashQLA
0.1.3 dual-CP, separate run):**
- Forward: FlashQLA is faster on every row except B200 layout C, where
this PR is ahead (1.012 to 1.014). The rows where FlashQLA is faster are
marked REGRESSION:
    - B200: D 0.991 / 0.992, Z 0.902 / 0.903
    - GB300: C 0.957 to 0.975, D 0.935 / 0.946, Z 0.869 / 0.883
- bwd, fwd+bwd and ckpt: this PR is faster, 1.332 to 1.590 on B200 and
1.323 to 1.622 on GB300.
- **vs the strongest non-Cake implementation on R200 (head-parallel
cuDNN `gdn_frost`):**
- Forward: head-parallel cuDNN `gdn_frost` is faster. It takes 2.104 ms,
compared with 3.776 / 3.780 ms for this PR, which gives 0.557. This row
is marked REGRESSION.
- bwd, fwd+bwd and ckpt: this PR is faster. bwd is 1.446, fwd+bwd is
1.226 and ckpt is 1.337.

Deterministic Cake and this PR ran in the same process, so those ratios
are paired. The non-Cake candidates were:
- FLA 0.6.0 KCP
- head-parallel all-to-all around FLA / cuDNN frontend 1.32.1
`gdn_frost`
- FlashQLA 0.1.3 dual-CP (inter + intra CP on a contiguous partition)

The strongest non-Cake arm is the fastest qualified one, and on every
B200 and GB300 row that is FlashQLA dual-CP on the contiguous layout.
Its contiguous-layout times are therefore also the reference for the D
and Z rows. FlashQLA was timed in a separate earlier run, so its ratios
are unpaired. FlashQLA 0.1.3 dual-CP does not support sm_107a. On R200
the strongest non-Cake candidate for each operation therefore comes from
the other listed candidates (FLA 0.6.0 KCP, head-parallel FLA / cuDNN
`gdn_frost`). On every R200 row it is head-parallel `gdn_frost`, with
the ck64 variant for bwd and fwd+bwd.

**NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a).** 8 GPUs on one node. CUDA 13.4 toolkit,
PyTorch 2.14.1 (cu130), BF16, eager.
- Workload K3E at CP8: documents 98304/65536/57344/40960, T/rank 32768,
heads (16, 48), causal conv on, `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True` on every
arm.
- Short protocol: two runs in one window with the arm order rotated (run
1: deterministic Cake first; run 2: reversed). Each run used 5 groups x
2 palindromic blocks x 12 samples per arm, warmup 10.
- Sustained protocol, layout C only (deterministic Cake and this PR
only): 3 groups x 300 samples per arm, warmup 20, 5 s idle before every
timed call.
- Some short-run layout C cells reached the power-cap threshold: bwd and
fwd+bwd at 6.2 % in run 2, and ckpt + recompute handle at 15.7 % / 10.1
% in runs 1 / 2. For these cells the sustained row supersedes both
short-run rows.
- The sustained bwd and fwd+bwd rows reached 7.0 % themselves, so they
are power-capped and not claimed. This covers their non-Cake cells too.
  - The sustained ckpt + recompute handle row (0.6 %) is claimed.
- All other rows stayed below 5 %.
- The run-2 layout Z ckpt row exceeded the 2 % drift limit. That cell
was measured once more in the same window with the same protocol (this
PR and deterministic Cake only).
- Non-Cake was timed in a separate run. The recompute handle exists only
in Cake.

* Added an optional fused forward path that computes outputs without
allocating intermediate tapes for eligible saved-boundary forwards.
* Added the `fused_o` test control and workspace reporting for fused and
split forward paths.

* The fused path produces bitwise-identical outputs to the split path,
with matching saved tensors.
  * Added support for the fused path across supported GPU architectures.
* **Tests**
* Expanded coverage for output and gradient equivalence, workspace
behavior, and execution modes.

### [c5a5afd](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c5a5afd3bb11e24d5b9e5e78c10024af128ce925)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T03:10:23Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_deepgemm_mega_mhc): SM-count-keyed sm_107a routes to existing tailpipe programs on R200 (#8425)

`flashinfer.mega_mhc` (`prepare_mega_mhc`) runs the fused
manifold-constrained hyper-connection (mHC) inference step. FlashInfer
main ships 45 per-arch programs for it:

- 14 hidden-5120 FP8-E4M3-output programs on sm_100a and sm_103a.
- For hidden 4096, five programs on each of sm_107a, sm_100a and
sm_103a: BF16 output, its tailpipe twin, its weight-staging tailpipe
twin, FP8 group-128 output and NVFP4 output.
- Four sm_107a-only tailpipe and weight-staging tailpipe forms of the
FP8 group-128 and NVFP4 variants.
- Three sm_107a-only FP8 group-128 UE8M0-scale-mode programs (plain,
tailpipe and weight-staging tailpipe).
- One sm_107a-only fast-division form of the plain FP8 group-128
program.
- Six sm_107a-only fast-chain forms: one each of the BF16-output
tailpipe program, the plain FP8 group-128 program (raw scale mode), the
plain FP8 group-128 program (UE8M0 scale mode), the FP8 group-128
weight-staging tailpipe program (raw scale mode), the FP8 group-128
UE8M0 tailpipe program and the NVFP4 tailpipe program.
- Two sm_107a-only chain-packing forms: one of the FP8 group-128
tailpipe program (raw scale mode) and one of the plain FP8 group-128
UE8M0 program.

Routes on main can already carry an optional SM-count key.

This PR adds no program and changes no program. It adds three routes.
Each route is keyed to one SM count, so it changes dispatch only on that
R200 SM class. Every other SM count, and a call with no SM count,
dispatch exactly as on main. No sm_100a or sm_103a launch changes.

- **NVFP4 output, deterministic, 208-SM devices, T = 2048.** This launch
moves from the plain NVFP4 program to the existing NVFP4 weight-staging
tailpipe program. On 208-SM devices, main already uses that program for
deterministic launches from T = 3329. It keeps 16 splits and the same
deterministic launch. Outputs are bitwise identical, and batch
invariance holds. On the 216-SM GPU, T = 2048 keeps the plain program.
- **FP8 group-128 output, UE8M0 scales, deterministic, 216-SM devices, T
= 3329–3456.** These launches move from the plain FP8 group-128 UE8M0
program to the existing UE8M0 tailpipe program. Main already uses that
program for these deterministic launches at T = 1024–3328. They keep 16
splits. Outputs are bitwise identical. On 208-SM devices, main already
dispatches the weight-staging tailpipe program at these token counts,
and that does not change.
- **FP8 group-128 output, raw scales, non-deterministic, 216-SM devices,
T = 1057–1104.** These launches move from the plain FP8 group-128
program (fast-division form) to the existing chain-packing form of the
FP8 group-128 tailpipe program. They keep 11 splits. Outputs are bitwise
identical. On 208-SM devices, these token counts keep their program.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of the kernel, which is what
FlashInfer main dispatches today. A is the program main dispatches, and
B is the program this PR dispatches. Speedup = A / B. Both sides run
through FlashInfer's loader on the same GPU, with the same inputs, in
one process. Both use programmatic dependent launch, as main already
does. The tables show medians. Each table lists the owner shapes first,
then the changed rows. The GPU is an NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a), with 208-SM
and 216-SM devices.

- NVFP4 weight-staging tailpipe program, deterministic, T = 2048 (16
splits): 1.010× on the 208-SM GPU (29.664 → 29.376 µs).
- FP8 group-128 UE8M0 tailpipe program, deterministic, T = 3329–3456 (16
splits): 1.013–1.018× on the 216-SM GPU.
- Chain-packing form of the FP8 group-128 tailpipe program, raw scales,
non-deterministic, T = 1057–1104 (11 splits): 1.025–1.034× on the 216-SM
GPU.
- Owner-shape rows that keep their program: 0.996–1.002× on the 208-SM
GPU and 0.997–1.002× on the 216-SM GPU. All are within noise. Only one
owner shape is a changed row: NVFP4 deterministic T = 2048 on 208 SMs.

### [6c86a3d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6c86a3daec9be3659cc5e21d91decda3924f764b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T03:02:02Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_attn_res): token-queue and register-carry programs for more B200, B300 and GB300 shapes (#8428)

This PR changes routes of the Cake AttnRes operator,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kimi_k3_attn_res`, which is exposed as
`flashinfer.kimi_k3_attn_res.prepare_kimi_k3_attn_res` and
`kimi_k3_attn_res`. One launch does residual add, an optional snapshot
write, K+1 candidate scoring, softmax, mix and output RMSNorm. It takes
BF16 inputs with hidden size 7168 and K in [0, 8]. It has one data type,
one layout and two fused forms: dense and snapshot write. This PR
changes routes on GB300, B300 and B200 at both PDL modes. Among the
measured shapes, 5 change on GB300, 3 on B300 and 3 on B200.

- **Token-queue snapshot-write programs (GB300, B300, B200):**
write_m4096_k4_write4 (M 4096 K 4) and write_m4096_k7_write7 (M 4096 K
7) move from the static snapshot-write programs
`persistent:k4_nc3_d2_f111000000000000_write` and
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_write` to their new token-queue
builds, `persistent:k4_nc3_d2_f111000000000000_write_clc` and
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_write_clc`. On GB300,
write_m4096_k1_write1 (M 4096 K 1) moves from
`persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f010000000000010_fm_crheld_write` (PDL off) and
`persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f010000000100000_fm_crheld_write` (PDL on) to
`persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f110000000000010_write_clc` and
`persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f110000000100000_write_clc`. A token-queue
(`_clc`) build launches one CTA per token (grid M) and uses cluster
launch control. Each running CTA processes its own token and then the
tokens of the CTAs it cancels. This spreads tokens over the SMs
dynamically instead of by a static stride.
- **Token-queue dense programs (B300, B200):** On B300, serving_m3072_k7
(M 3072 K 7) moves from `persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f111000000000000_fm` to
the already shipped `persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_clc`. On
B200, serving_m2048_k7 (M 2048 K 7) moves from
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_fm` to its new token-queue build
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_fm_clc`.
- **Small M (GB300):** serving_m384_k5 (M 384 K 5) moves from
`persistent:k5_nc4_d2_f111000000000000`, and serving_m512_k5 (M 512 K 5)
moves from `persistent:k5_nc3_d3_f111000000000000_fm`. Both move to
`persistent:k5_nc4_d3_f001000000000000_fm_crheld_rcp`. A
packed-register-carry (`_rcp`) build keeps the running carry in
registers instead of tensor memory.

The program set stays at 207 programs and 239 libraries. sm_100a goes
from 113 to 116 libraries and sm_103a goes from 126 to 123. This PR adds
5 libraries: sm_100a `persistent:k4_nc3_d2_f111000000000000_write_clc`,
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_write_clc` and
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_fm_clc`, and sm_103a
`persistent:k4_nc3_d2_f111000000000000_write_clc` and
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_write_clc`. It removes 5 sm_103a
libraries that no route uses anymore:
`persistent:k5_nc3_d3_f111000000000000_fm`,
`persistent:k5_nc4_d2_f111000000000000`,
`persistent:k4_nc3_d2_f111000000000000_write`,
`persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f010000000000010_fm_crheld_write` and
`persistent:k1_nc4_d2_f010000000100000_fm_crheld_write`. All other
libraries have SASS identical to the previous version.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of this operator on current
main, last changed by PR #8351. All changed shapes are faster at both

to 1.030) and 3 on B200 (ratios 1.019 to 1.035). For shapes not in the
