### [ce28c2f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ce28c2fac0f37c1c3018c1b165e509775806361e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T02:31:45Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_fmha): give the FP8/FP16 context JITs' final row statistics their own barrier (#8424)

## Problem

Three cake_fmha paged-context JIT kernels can hang a CTA:

- FP8 hd128 (`context_fp8/default.cu`)
- FP8 hd256 (`context_fp8_hd256/is_causal1_output_bf161.cu`)
- FP16 hd256 (`context_fp16_hd256/is_causal0.cu`)

The softmax hands each tile's final row sum/max to the correction warps
with one more `corr_sig` arrive. It does not wait on `corr_done` before
the next tile's first `corr_sig` arrive. Both phases can complete before
the correction's parity wait. When that happens, the correction misses
both and the CTA hangs. Normal timing hides this.

The BF16 hd128 JIT already waits on `corr_done` after its final arrive.
This PR does not change it. The delay test passes for it on main.

A legal schedule reproduces the hang. It adds a 200 µs globaltimer spin
in the correction warps on their first tile, before the final-statistics
wait. With this delay, main hangs for all three kernels on B200 and
GB300. A 60 s watchdog in synchronize catches the hang. The affected
rows are hd128 f_b4/l_b4/s_b256 and hd256 B4 q512 and B1 q4096 (FP8
causal / FP16 non-causal). compute-sanitizer racecheck on main also
hangs (hd128).

## Fix

The final statistics now use their own mbarrier, `stats_full` (count
128). It sits in free shared memory after the TMEM address slot:

- hd128: bytes 304-319, one per softmax stage
- FP8 hd256: bytes 248-255
- FP16 hd256: bytes 216-223

The correction waits on it with parity `tile_iter_1 & 1`. It needs no
phase registers. Dynamic shared memory size does not change. Arithmetic
does not change.

There is one commit per kernel. These three files are maintained by
hand. No generator renders them.

With each fix and the same delay, the call completes. The output is
bitwise equal to undelayed main.

## Tests

- New output is bitwise equal to main. The check also includes an
identical-code control build, A/A and run-to-run. It covers:
- 17 hd128 rows on B200: 14 FP8 (incl. LSE, sink, non-causal,
page-boundary, pack-mismatch) and 3 BF16.
  - 4 hd128 rows on GB300.
  - All 4 hd256 rows (B4 q512 and B1 q4096, FP8 and FP16) on both GPUs.
- FP32 max_abs is unchanged vs main. 0 elements are out of tolerance.
  - hd128: FP8 0.00101-0.0285, BF16 4e-5-8e-5, LSE 2.9e-6 (log2).
  - hd256 FP8: 6.9e-4 / 7.8e-3 on B200, 7.2e-4 / 8.2e-3 on GB300.
  - hd256 FP16: 9.1e-6 / 5.6e-6 on B200, 9.3e-6 / 5.5e-6 on GB300.
- Sanitizers ran on both GPUs.
- hd256 fixes, all 4 rows: racecheck 0 hazards, synccheck 0 errors,
memcheck 0 device errors. The 14 memcheck errors are host-API only.
  - hd128 fix: racecheck 0 hazards, synccheck 0 errors.
- pytest `tests/attention/test_cake_fmha_context_programs.py` +
`tests/attention/test_cake_fmha.py` ran at the PR head with main merged
in. The results match main.
  - B200: 464 + 214 passed.
  - GB300: 458 passed + 6 skipped (sm100a-only programs) + 214 passed.

## Timing

Timing used CUPTI with a cold L2. Each memory layout got the median of 6
alternating rounds. There were 5 seeded layouts. µs is the median over
layouts. The ratio is main/PR per layout, so >1 means the PR is faster.
"control" is main's source compiled as its own module. It separates
code-placement effects. CUDA 13.4. B200 = sm_100a, GB300 = sm_103a.

| GPU | Row | main (µs) | this PR (µs) | control (µs) | main/PR per

### [9f914db](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9f914dbf5c24635cdcb87dfd0f11952a682729ce)

- **作者**: Zihao Ye
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T02:21:14Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_deepgemm_dense_mqa): raw-store programs for clean_logits=False on the 32-head FP8 routes (#8329)

The 32-head FP8 dense MQA logits routes (`fp8_mqa_logits`,
`DenseMqaPlan`) wrote `-inf` to every cell outside each row's window
even with `clean_logits=False`. Each 32-head FP8 route now carries a
`"raw"` variant (catalog `dense_mqa.v14`, route-record key `variants`)
whose logits stage is a raw-store build of its schedule: it skips the
cleanup and writes each row's window cells with the same bits as the
cleaned program. `clean_logits=False` (DeepGEMM's default) launches it;
`clean_logits=True` keeps the cleaned programs. The baseline is the
previous Cake version, which ran the cleaned programs for
`clean_logits=False`.

### [252965d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/252965dc2e3664c2f7267dbf9b5498317dc11fe2)

- **作者**: DwenGu
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T02:13:01Z
- **提交信息**: feat(comm): add SageAttention2 low-precision QKV exchange to UlyssesCommunicator (#4924)

## 📌 Description

Extend `flashinfer.comm.UlyssesCommunicator` with `prepare_qkv()` and
`scatter_qkv()` for low-precision input communication. They accept
FP16/BF16 Q/K/V sequence shards, quantize and pack them before
all-to-all, and return the received SageAttention2 operands plus scales
and metadata. Internally, Q/K are encoded as INT8 and V as FP8 E4M3.
Quantization groups remain on the global sequence grid across rank
boundaries.

The caller supplies the process group and attention invocation. The
communicator prepares reusable storage and owns one statistics AllGather
and one combined payload AllToAll on that group's NCCL backend. Existing
`scatter_heads()` / `gather_heads()` behavior and backend selection are
preserved. Lowp numeric helpers live in the private `_ulysses_lowp.py`
module; the former public module and duplicate `flashinfer.comm` exports
are removed.

[Design and numerical
contracts](https://github.com/DwenGu/flashinfer/blob/44e3c6b1a9fa1e2a1f2dd1b6c43da8e654ceb860/docs/design_docs/ulysses_lowp.md)
· [Distributed acceptance
example](https://github.com/DwenGu/flashinfer/blob/44e3c6b1a9fa1e2a1f2dd1b6c43da8e654ceb860/benchmarks/comm/validate_ulysses_lowp.py)
· [Communicator
benchmark](https://github.com/DwenGu/flashinfer/blob/44e3c6b1a9fa1e2a1f2dd1b6c43da8e654ceb860/benchmarks/comm/bench_ulysses_qkv.py).

### Execution and API

```python
from flashinfer.comm import UlyssesCommunicator

with UlyssesCommunicator(group, max_bytes=3 * q.nbytes, dtype=q.dtype,
                         device=q.device, backend="nccl") as comm:
    workspace = comm.prepare_qkv(q.shape, quantization="sage2", used_sequence=used)
    encoded = comm.scatter_qkv(q, k, v, workspace=workspace)
    # Call the framework's Sage2 adapter with encoded operands and scales.
    # For subsequent serialized calls, reuse output storage with out=encoded.
```

Preparation is collective and validates configuration, layout/JIT
availability and allocation outcomes across ranks. Each execution checks
actual input/output metadata and storage overlap, then invokes shared
private stage implementations without repeating the standalone wrappers'
checks. QKV projection views are accepted without three full contiguous
copies. `UlyssesQKV` contains six tensors plus layout, logical/live
sequence lengths and input dtype; `out=None` owns independent storage
and `out=encoded` reuses it. The `max_bytes` budget must cover the
complete packed input or output operand: `P * chunk_bytes`, including
Q/K/V, transmitted scales and alignment. `3 * q.nbytes` is a
conservative budget for the supported layouts; `q.nbytes` alone is
insufficient. Preparation checks the exact requirement collectively and
allocates the actual payload size. Statistics and final attention inputs
have separate allocations, so this is not a total memory budget.

The shared transport API is integrated with upstream main at
`9643349fca9162cb292dbb0fbab50b8e73b4712b`, including its PCIe/RDMA and
Cake NVLink support:

| Entry point | Contract |
|---|---|
| `UlyssesCommunicator(group, *, max_bytes=None, dtype, backend="auto",
nvlink_kernel="auto", device=None, max_elems=None)` | Capacity is in
bytes per complete operand. Legacy `max_elems=N` remains supported as `N
* dtype.itemsize`; specify exactly one capacity form. Lowp must cover
its combined payload |
| `create_workspace(*, max_elems=None)` | Ordinary staging capacity
remains in elements; the default is `max_bytes // dtype.itemsize` |
| `allocate_output(x, op, *, dtype=None)` | Allocate receive storage
with upstream backend-specific registration and lifetime rules; PCIe
requires registered outputs, and Cake NVLink can register scatter/gather
outputs |
| `exchange_chunks(x, *, out=None, dtype=None)` | Exchange contiguous
`[1, 1, P, C]` chunks: destination-major send, source-major receive.
Explicit output must not overlap input, including single-rank calls |
| `scatter_heads(x, *, out=None, dtype=None, workspace=None)` /
`gather_heads(...)` | Preserve upstream transforms and PCIe per-call
dtype support; NCCL/NVLink head transforms keep the construction dtype |

Lowp uses zero-copy views of its packed payload and calls
`allocate_output(..., "exchange_chunks", dtype=torch.uint8)` during
preparation and `exchange_chunks(..., dtype=torch.uint8)` during
execution. The override selects the dtype of already encoded storage; it
does not convert or requantize values. NCCL and NVLink chunk exchange
supports FP16/BF16/FP32/UINT8 and uses NCCL. The prepared QKV API
accepts `nccl` and `nvlink` communicators and rejects `pcie`
collectively before JIT or allocation. Upstream PCIe/RDMA and Cake paths
remain available for ordinary transforms. The Lowp numerical
implementation, scales, payload bytes, Sage2 operands and CUDA kernels
are unchanged by this integration.

One `BOUNDARY_MERGE` computation path handles aligned and nonaligned
shards. Boundary statistics are merged for every rank contributing to a
global quantization group, including groups spanning more than two
ranks. The single FP32 statistics AllGather carries K sums, V channel
maxima, Q boundary maxima and K boundary extrema. Quantize-and-pack
consumes the finalized scales; the receiver applies Sage's V permutation
and reconstructs global Q/K scale arrays.

Both architecture modules compile head dimensions 64 and 128.
`prepare_qkv()` selects the device layout and dimension from the
supplied shape; callers do not construct layout objects. Host bindings
and kernel templates are shared across architecture specializations.

### Supported configurations and contracts

| Property | Contract |
|---|---|
| Input | Q/K/V with identical `[B, L, H, D]` shape, CUDA device and
FP16/BF16 dtype; positive B/L/H; D=64 or 128 |
| Distribution | Equal L on all ranks; H divisible by P; the prepared
Lowp API accepts P=2/4/8 and rejects P=1/6. Ordinary communicator
behavior is unchanged |
| Sequence | Arbitrary positive local L; global live prefix `0 < U <=
P*L`; caller zero-fills the global tail before sharding |
| SM90 | Q groups of 16 tokens; K groups of 128; V storage padded to 128
rows |
| SM120 | Q groups of 32 tokens; K groups of 64; V storage padded to 64
rows |
| Memory layout | Dense D axis with 16-byte-aligned row addresses,
including interleaved projection views; exact contiguous output buffers
|
| Numeric behavior | FP32 K sums, mean divided by U and rounded to input
dtype before centering; Q/K grouped-amax floor `1e-7`; V channel scale
`amax / 2.25`, with zero-amax channels encoded as positive zero |
| Consumer buffers | Initialize the entire required scale allocation,
unused payload slots and storage tails. Extra Q scales for invalid rows
may be finite nonzero values |

SM89 compilation is retained but is outside the current hardware
acceptance matrix. GQA/MQA with different Q/KV head counts, unequal rank
shard lengths, per-example ragged lengths, training, multi-node
execution, and CUDA graph/`torch.compile` integration are outside this
submission's validated scope.

### Performance evidence

#### SM90: latest transport API alignment (`59e4fbe8` → `44e3c6b1`)

8× NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0; P=8, B=1,
H=56, D=128, BF16, U=P×L, seed `2101 + rank`. The old implementation A
is frozen at `59e4fbe8`; B is the source now committed as `44e3c6b1`.
Runs used the same container, CUDA numerical code and NCCL transport, in
serial order **A1 → B1 → A2 → B2**. Each run used 5 warmups and 5 rounds
× 30 calls; each result is the median of the per-round slowest-rank
synchronized wall times per call.

| Local sequence L | Old A1 / A2 (ms) | New B1 / B2 (ms) | Old two-run
mean (ms) | New two-run mean (ms) | Mean change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4736 | 0.9625 / 0.9580 | 0.9953 / 0.9665 | 0.9603 | 0.9809 |
**+2.15%**, approximately +20.6 us |
| 4737 | 1.0373 / 1.0153 | 1.0097 / 1.0549 | 1.0263 | 1.0323 |
**+0.59%**, approximately +6.1 us |

Times are rounded; changes use the original measurements. These compare
`communicator_reused_out`, including statistics, quantization,
AllGather, AllToAll, unpacking and V-scale output. They exclude
preparation/JIT, attention, output gather and diffusion. The two-run
mean averages two measured medians; it is not a confidence interval. The
direction reverses between runs for L=4737, while both new L=4736
measurements are slower than their corresponding old runs. **These
results do not demonstrate zero overhead or a new
communication-algorithm speedup.** The new public entry point performs
validation and creates views; these measurements do not isolate each
check's cost.

All four runs passed byte-for-byte checks for six outputs and
send/receive payloads. Per-rank workspace sizes remain 205,217,280 bytes
(L=4736) and 205,260,288 bytes (L=4737); there is no additional payload
GPU copy, communication round or wire traffic. The measurement used
`ulysses.py` SHA-256
`e5ba4c96fde553df609614c5881912875b7852ca721a7907474755e843c0ec64` (A)
and `717b4bda1dea73c645540cc19fe1de847979c881a9bd4493377e929744957957`
(B). `_ulysses_lowp.py` is unchanged at
`277a11aa1f359b6198ac3d99a45f5820df499d1e561bf9c8c71ffed7c55e8dec`.

Use the linked communicator benchmark on each revision with `--lengths
4736 4737 --warmup 5 --rounds 5 --iterations 30`; the old benchmark uses
the old constructor and the current one uses `max_bytes`, with the same
measurement logic. No new SM120 run, video generation or diffusion
timeline was collected for this API alignment.

#### Historical SM90: prepared communicator versus the previous
standalone API

The following measurements predate both `59e4fbe8` and the transport API
alignment above; they describe the earlier removal of redundant
validation, not the latest interface overhead.

8× NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0; P=8, B=1,
H=56, D=128, BF16, U=P×L. Both paths use preallocated
output/payload/statistics-gather buffers and copy V scales into
independently owned output storage. Each run uses 5 warmups, 5 rounds ×
30 calls, alternating the compared paths; the reported synchronized wall
time is the median of the per-round slowest-rank means. The frozen old
implementation was run before (A1) and after (A2) the new implementation
(B).

| Local sequence L | Previous standalone A1 (ms) | Previous standalone
A2 (ms) | Prepared communicator B (ms) | Reduction versus previous
standalone |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4736 | 0.9788 | 0.9867 | 0.9652 | 1.39%–2.18% |
| 4737 | 1.0891 | 1.0808 | 1.0255 | 5.12%–5.84% |

The timed interval includes local/final statistics,
quantization/packing, statistics AllGather, payload AllToAll, unpacking
and the V-scale copy. It excludes preparation/JIT, attention, output
gather and full diffusion. Redundant Python validation between stages
was removed while retaining input/output checks at each communicator
call. CUDA kernels and communication volume are unchanged. These figures
do not establish an attention-kernel or full-video speedup.

These September 17 measurements preceded the final Python module rename
and public-export cleanup. That cleanup preserves executable numerical
code, but its timings were not remeasured. No new SM120 timing or
video/timeline collection is claimed.

<details>

The integration measurements below cover **historical D=128 runs on SM90
and SM120, before the D=64 extension**. Each architecture has its own
measured revision and environment; neither integration table is a
measurement of the current PR head or D=64.

#### SM90: 2026-09-11 working-tree snapshot

Environment: 8×H20-3e, UP8/TP1, FSDP off, AdaLN offload on, compile off;
MiniMax-H3, 1248×704, 124 output frames at 24 fps, seed 2101. Baseline:
BF16 input AllToAll followed by **CUDA per-warp Sage2** quantization and
attention. Lowp: statistics AllGather plus low-precision input AllToAll
and prequantized Sage2 attention.

| Measurement | CUDA Sage2 baseline | Lowp-Sage2 | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GPU0 attention-input preparation, cumulative over 100 modules |
167.017 ms | 94.942 ms | 43.15% |
| 50-timestep pipeline, hummingbird case | 97.73 s | 96.28 s | 1.48% |
| 50-timestep pipeline, musician case | 97.75 s | 96.26 s | 1.52% |
| 50-timestep pipeline, waves case | 97.70 s | 96.39 s | 1.34% |

The preparation window starts at the first input preparation GPU
operation and ends at the attention kernel, excluding QKV projection,
attention itself and output AllToAll. The trace requested 3 timesteps
and captured 2 updates × 50 layers; the video runs requested 50
timesteps and performed 49 updates. Each video case has one measured
run, without repeat-run confidence intervals.

The measured benefit combines communication and layout handling; it does
**not** establish that each quantization kernel is faster. For example,
in the inspected single module, Q amax plus quantization took 38.368 µs
in Sage2 and 68.544 µs in Lowp. Lowp uses V scale_max=2.25 while the
measured Sage2 baseline uses 448, so this is not an isolated
transport-only comparison.

The three historical Lowp videos were byte-identical after decoding to
the preceding Lowp implementation. Similarity against BF16 varied by
prompt; this does not establish universal quality parity with BF16 or
stock Sage2.

[Integration environment, reproduction scripts and historical
tables](https://github.com/DwenGu/sglang-minimax/blob/545c135c788e88365b05274484cb10f2538d705f/ULYSSES_LOWP_SM120_HANDOFF.md).
That handoff pins an earlier FlashInfer revision; explicitly use this

and [stock SageAttention
`d1a57a54`](https://github.com/thu-ml/SageAttention/tree/d1a57a546c3d395b1ffcbeecc66d81db76f3b4b5).
This FlashInfer revision predates D=64 support and the current rebase.
The later D=64/128 validation matrix in the Tests section is a separate
run.

| Setting | Measured configuration |
|---|---|
| GPU / interconnect | 8× NVIDIA Graphics Device, CC 12.0, 73,415 MiB
per GPU; PCIe/NUMA, no NVLink; no commercial model inferred |
| Software | PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.95.05; Nsight
Systems 2026.4.1 |

`lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:9e148f5ac788e856a06166bd6347a831831eb9fcfab4d1770874823a7c29a1a1`
|
| Workload | MiniMax-H3 / FL2VA / speed / t2va; D=128; UP8 / TP1 /
ring=1 |

torch.compile OFF |
| Generation | 1248×704, 124 frames at 24 fps, seed 2101; flow_shift=12,
audio_flow_shift=3 |
| Sampling | Warmup per backend, one formal run per prompt; 50 diffusion
timesteps / 49 denoise updates |
| Profiling | Separate case1 run per backend; CUDA/NVTX, 3 timesteps / 2
updates / 100 DiT attention calls per GPU |

The BF16 reference actually used **Torch SDPA**, despite the requested
`fa` setting: the fixed SGLang revision routes SM12.x to this backend.
Sage2 used **CUDA per-warp Q32/K64**; Lowp used the same SM120 Sage
attention core and V `scale_max=2.25`. Thus the main comparison is Lowp
versus CUDA Sage2. BF16 comparisons also change the attention
implementation and precision.

**50-timestep video runs.** Reductions below mean `(baseline - Lowp) /
baseline`; they are elapsed-time reductions, not throughput multipliers.
Pipeline and denoise are separate timers and must not be added.

| Prompt | BF16 SDPA pipeline (s) | CUDA Sage2 pipeline (s) | Lowp-Sage2
pipeline (s) | Reduction vs Sage2 | Reduction vs BF16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| case1: hummingbird / hibiscus | 170.17 | 151.80 | 119.31 | 21.40% |
29.89% |
| case2: rainy sidewalk / musician | 170.28 | 152.24 | 119.91 | 21.24% |
29.58% |
| case3: waves / volcanic rocks | 170.33 | 152.48 | 120.05 | 21.27% |
29.52% |

| Prompt | BF16 SDPA denoise (s) | CUDA Sage2 denoise (s) | Lowp-Sage2
denoise (s) | Reduction vs Sage2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| case1 | 167.0945 | 148.7115 | 116.2086 | 21.86% |
| case2 | 167.1682 | 149.1258 | 116.7757 | 21.69% |
| case3 | 167.2079 | 149.3525 | 116.8975 | 21.73% |

**Separate 3-timestep CUDA/NVTX traces: complete input-preparation
windows.** Each window starts at the first input-pack operation
(BF16/Sage2) or local-stats operation (Lowp), and ends when the actual
attention core starts. It includes communication, layout handling,
statistics, and launch/wait gaps; it excludes QKV projection, QK
norm/RoPE, attention computation, and output AllToAll.

| Backend | GPU0 sum of 100 windows (ms) | Per-call mean (us) | Range of
per-GPU sums across 8 GPUs (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 Torch SDPA | 2659.113 | 26591.126 | 2659.113–2782.819 |
| CUDA Sage2 | 2749.947 | 27499.469 | 2729.988–2787.158 |
| Lowp-Sage2 | 1474.711 | 14747.106 | 1474.711–1505.731 |

GPU0 preparation time decreased **46.37%** versus Sage2. This is a
preparation-window reduction, not a full-pipeline reduction. The eight
GPU totals must not be summed into an end-to-end latency.

**One attention module: GPU0, `denoising_step_1`,
`transformer.blocks.25.attn`.** Stage rows are CUDA kernel-duration
sums; zero means no independent kernel for that stage. Shared statistics
and fused packing are charged to their actual rows. The final
preparation window also includes gaps and may differ from the sum of
kernel durations.

| Stage | CUDA Sage2 (us) | Lowp-Sage2 (us) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Q: amax + INT8 quantization | 53.984 | 94.079 |
| K: separate statistics + INT8 quantization | 139.520 | 135.999 |
| V: separate FP8 quantization | 27.680 | 56.768 |
| Shared K/V statistics | 0.000 | 93.088 |
| Statistics helpers / finalization | 0.000 | 67.264 |
| Statistics AllGather | 0.000 | 564.384 |
| Input AllToAll | 27905.831 | 13312.528 |
| Separate sending QKV pack | 301.088 | 0.000 |
| Receiver BF16 contiguous copies | 328.928 | 0.000 |
| V: separate padding / transpose | 153.088 | 0.000 |
| Receiver Lowp unpack / tail clearing | 0.000 | 147.392 |
| **Complete preparation window** | **28934.247** | **14541.806** |
| Attention core, excluded above | 9439.255 | 9437.141 |

The benefit comes mainly from less input communication and fewer
separate BF16 layout copies. Q quantization and the V quantization stage
are slower in this inspected Lowp module; the Sage core time is
essentially unchanged. NCCL kernel durations include peer
synchronization/waiting and do not measure pure link bandwidth. These
PCIe/NUMA results should not be extrapolated to NVLink systems or SM90.

Quality scope: all nine videos decoded successfully. Full-frame SSIM
versus this batch's local BF16 reference was 0.879573 / 0.822718 /
0.960857 for Lowp and 0.905763 / 0.802927 / 0.971350 for Sage2. The
report records visible pose/composition differences and incomplete human
full-playback acceptance; these similarity scores do not establish
perceptual quality parity. Each prompt has one formal run, without
repeated-batch statistics or confidence intervals.

Reproduce the fixed workload using the [pinned SGLang harness and
environment
instructions](https://github.com/DwenGu/sglang-minimax/blob/545c135c788e88365b05274484cb10f2538d705f/ULYSSES_LOWP_SM120_HANDOFF.md),
with the measured revisions above. From the project root, after
environment setup, choose fresh output and scratch directories:

```bash
H3_BENCH=./sglang-lowp-fi/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/benchmarks/ulysses_lowp
python "$H3_BENCH/run.py" --model-path ./models/MiniMax-H3 --up 8 --port 30041 \
  --mode videos --output ./results-sm120-up8-new --scratch ./work-sm120-up8-new
python "$H3_BENCH/run.py" --model-path ./models/MiniMax-H3 --up 8 --port 30041 \
  --mode timelines --output ./results-sm120-up8-new --scratch ./work-sm120-up8-new
```

* Added prepared Ulysses QKV exchange for SageAttention with reusable
workspaces and output buffers.
* Added low-precision INT8 Q/K and FP8 V quantization with
Sage-compatible packing and unpacking for supported GPUs and head
dimensions 64 and 128.
  * Added packed chunk exchange and generic output allocation utilities.
  * Communicator capacity configuration now uses byte-based `max_bytes`.

* **Documentation**
* Updated API and design documentation for prepared exchange, layouts,
capacity requirements, and constraints.

* **Tests**
* Added extensive correctness, boundary, tracing, benchmarking, and
architecture-specific validation coverage.

### [ff726b4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ff726b4318d69680111839c5be1c72423ee004d0)

- **作者**: Zihao Ye
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T02:12:09Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): swapped small-token forward programs with per-call PDL (#8372)

The Cake deterministic dense projection GEMM
(`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm`) runs a batched
BF16 forward of few tokens against many weight rows (a grouped
projection such as the attention output projection, `out[l] = A[l] @
B[l]` on token-major strided views) on its 256 x 256 CTA-pair tile with
a 2-way stream-K split. This PR adds two programs that put the weight
rows in the MMA's M and the tokens in its N (64 or 128 weight rows per
CTA over a 12- or 8-stage TMA ring, single CTA, no split, the strided
views read and written in place), routes the batched forward rows of at
most 256 tokens whose tiles fit two waves of the device to them, and
adds a per-call `enable_pdl` whose launch loads the weights ahead of the
dependency wait. Against cuBLAS (`torch.bmm` on the same views) and the
previous Cake program:

| shape (8 groups, K 4096, N 1024) | cuBLAS (us) | previous Cake (us) |
this PR (us) | vs cuBLAS | vs previous Cake |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 tokens | 15.90 | 27.74 | 14.85 | 1.07x | 1.87x |
| 32 tokens | 17.18 | 28.58 | 15.49 | 1.11x | 1.85x |
| 64 tokens | 17.86 | 29.02 | 15.52 | 1.15x | 1.87x |
| 96 tokens | 18.24 | 30.11 | 17.73 | 1.03x | 1.70x |
| 128 tokens | 18.85 | 30.11 | 17.60 | 1.07x | 1.71x |
| 192 tokens | 20.45 | 30.82 | 27.42 | 0.75x | 1.12x |
| 256 tokens | 23.10 | 32.74 | 28.22 | 0.82x | 1.16x |

*Median kernel time, back to back, cold L2; GB300 (sm_103a), CUDA 13.4.*

| four dependent projections (distinct weights) in one CUDA graph, per
projection | cuBLAS (us) | this PR, `enable_pdl=True` (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 tokens | 15.26 | 13.31 | 1.15x |
| 64 tokens | 16.92 | 14.18 | 1.19x |
| 128 tokens | 17.46 | 16.78 | 1.04x |
| 256 tokens | 20.02 | 27.51 | 0.73x |

The package's other Cake variant is the non-deterministic
`dense_projection_gemm`, which runs these programs for the forward and
passes `enable_pdl` through; both ship for sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [d933260](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d933260d23c7fcef4b5f28859b8a4ef07b6ab05e)

- **作者**: Zihao Ye
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T01:49:52Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): programmatic dependent launch for the FP8 persistent and M64 sparse-MLA programs (stacked on #8311) (#8314)

`trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4(backend="cake")` ships BF16 and FP8
programs for 8-128 query heads (several bodies per head count, picked
per shape by the host route) and an NVFP4-KV family. This PR makes the
FP8 persistent body and the FP8 single-CTA M64 body programmatic
dependent launches: `enable_pdl` (default: the device's support) is
accepted on SM100/SM103 instead of raising, and these programs wait for
the previous grid after their setup and trigger their dependents right
after. Stacked on #8311.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode, 64 heads per rank, FP8 Q and KV, q_len 4
(rows = batch x 4), 8K context, GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4:
eight calls back to back in one CUDA graph, time per call, cold L2
before each graph launch. Baseline: the previous Cake programs (no PDL);
trtllm-gen in the same harness.

`enable_pdl=True` (us) | speedup | trtllm-gen, PDL on (us) |

* Added an option to enable programmatic dependent launches for
supported Cake FP8 persistent and M64 prefill programs on SM100/SM103
GPUs.

count, improving routing across device configurations.

rejects the option when enabled; the TRTLLM-GEN RopeQuant epilogue
remains unsupported.

### [e919d83](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e919d835b2e0076594ba76b649e5660082366b63)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T01:44:28Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_tinygemm2_wgmma): sm_90a small-batch shapes routed to the paced cluster programs (#8417)

`tinygemm_bf16` is a small-M bf16 GEMM (out = x @ W^T [+ bias]) with
four variants: with or without bias, each with or without programmatic
dependent launch (PDL). On sm_90a, host routing windows pick a generated
wgmma program (`cake_tinygemm2_wgmma`) for each shape. Other shapes use
the mma.sync reference `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. This PR changes only the
sm_90a host routing, for all four variants. The programs are unchanged.
#8377 made the four CLUSTER_S8U8_C4 programs faster by pacing the ring
fill. Several small-batch regions next to the cluster windows were still
routed as if those programs were slower. In those regions,
CLUSTER_S8U8_C4 now beats both the packed tiles and the reference. This
PR adds 33 windows that route these regions to CLUSTER_S8U8_C4, which
takes the total from 390 to 423 windows. Routing uses the first matching
window, and the new windows are placed so that only these regions
change. The scope check covered batch 1-16, output features 16 to 512 in
steps of 16 and input features 1024 to 14336 in steps of 64. Across that
grid, 38490 shapes change routing. Of these, 36423 move from
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`, mostly shapes with output features 129-384 and
input features above 4096. The other 2067 move from packed tiles. A
region moves only if CLUSTER_S8U8_C4 meets three conditions at every
shape re-measured inside it, on every H100 measured. It is bit-identical
to `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. It is at least 3% faster than
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. It is faster than the previous tile in every round,
with a median gain of at least the larger of 0.5% and 40 ns. Cells that
failed on any GPU keep their previous tile. Among the representative
shapes, only 7x128x4096 with bias changes, from PACKED_U4_IL_BOX3D to
CLUSTER_S8U8_C4. It goes from 3.648 us to 3.471 us with PDL off and from
3.648 us to 3.456 us with PDL on. It is faster in all 7 rounds in both
modes, and `csrc/tinygemm2.cu` takes 4.192 us on this shape. The other
representative rows keep their program. Their speedup vs the previous
Cake routing (#8376) ranges from 0.994x to 1.016x, which is noise
between identical code. All 64 representative rows are 1.027x to 4.258x
faster than `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. Each PDL mode has 34 changed rows: that
representative row and 33 samples from the changed regions. Every
changed row is faster than #8376 in all 7 rounds, at 1.021x to 1.305x
with PDL off and 1.031x to 1.299x with PDL on. Against
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`, the changed rows are 1.118x to 1.316x faster.

*NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (SXM, 132 SMs), sm_90a, CUDA 13.4 toolkit (nvcc
13.4.92, torch 2.14.1+cu130). Median CUPTI kernel time, cold L2, 7
interleaved rounds x 200 iterations. All three arms
(`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`, #8376, this PR) were measured in the same process
on the same GPU, and every row is bit-identical to `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`.
The "#8376" column is FlashInfer main after #8376 and #8377. The
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu` column is current main, after #8334. The tables come
from one H100. A second H100 was measured the same way. On it, all 68
changed rows were faster than #8376 in all 7 rounds, at 1.027x to
1.313x. The representative rows were 1.026x to 4.252x faster than
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`, and 7x128x4096 with bias went from 3.648 us to
3.456 us in both PDL modes, faster in 7 of 7 rounds. In the "Program"
column, "(unchanged)" means the same program as #8376. "X ->
CLUSTER_S8U8_C4" gives the #8376 program and then this PR's program.*

### [0a0ee73](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0a0ee73d55c6c45ada4034dec6d9e9e1fc5b33a7)

- **作者**: Zihao Ye
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T01:42:26Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_fp4_allreduce): canonical wire words for pre-quantised NVFP4 input, call-index wrap, async-proxy fence after the PDL wait (#8325)

Cake ships the NVFP4-transport tensor-parallel all-reduce in 3 forms:
TP2 one-shot, TP4 two-shot, and TP2 one-shot fused with residual + Gemma
RMSNorm. Each takes bfloat16 or pre-quantised NVFP4 input; the fused
form writes bfloat16, NVFP4 or MXFP8 output.

This PR updates all three forms with the same fixes:
- A pre-quantised NVFP4 record with an E2M1 `-0` value is now
canonicalised before the push. A standard quantiser emits `-0` for small
negative values, and the receiver polled such a record forever.
- E4M3 block scales are published unsigned, so a NaN scale can never
read as the `0xFF` sentinel.
- The device-side call index now wraps inside the three-buffer rotation,
so the 32-bit wrap no longer reuses an un-rearmed buffer.
- Every thread issues `fence.proxy.async.global` after
`griddepcontrol.wait`.

Speed is unchanged against the previous Cake version (FlashInfer
`main`). The table gives µs, back to back / cooled; each rank's launch
is aligned, the time is the slowest rank's median and the mean of two
interleaved runs. Measured on GB300 (sm_103a), CUDA 13.4, 152-SM grid,
hidden size 6144.

| form, input (schedule) | world, rows | previous Cake (µs) | this PR
(µs) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 two-shot, bf16 (bv0) | 4, 8192 | 84.3 / 84.3 | 84.2 / 84.2 |
1.001x / 1.002x |
| TP4 two-shot, bf16 (bv1) | 4, 4096 | 46.8 / 46.8 | 46.9 / 46.9 |
0.999x / 0.999x |
| TP4 two-shot, bf16 (bv2) | 4, 16384 | 162.2 / 162.2 | 162.6 / 161.8 |
0.998x / 1.002x |
| TP4 two-shot, nvfp4 (bv0) | 4, 8192 | 81.9 / 81.9 | 82.1 / 82.2 |
0.997x / 0.996x |
| TP4 two-shot, nvfp4 (bv1) | 4, 4096 | 43.5 / 43.5 | 43.4 / 43.5 |
1.001x / 0.999x |
| TP4 two-shot, nvfp4 (bv2) | 4, 16384 | 152.2 / 152.3 | 152.6 / 152.6 |
0.998x / 0.998x |
| TP2 one-shot, bf16 | 2, 16384 | 103.2 / 103.1 | 103.0 / 103.0 | 1.002x
/ 1.002x |
| TP2 one-shot, nvfp4 | 2, 16384 | 98.3 / 98.5 | 98.4 / 98.4 | 0.999x /
1.001x |
| TP2 + RMSNorm, bf16 in, bf16 out | 2, 16384 | 159.2 / 159.0 | 159.0 /
159.6 | 1.001x / 0.996x |
| TP2 + RMSNorm, nvfp4 in, bf16 out | 2, 16384 | 141.7 / 141.6 | 141.0 /
140.8 | 1.005x / 1.005x |

The family ships for SM100 (B200), SM103 (B300 / GB300) and SM107. The
other output formats of the fused form (NVFP4, MXFP8) carry the same
changes.

### [25e1329](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/25e13297b43d9e000bd159ba823b038af9e17d98)

- **作者**: Zihao Ye
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T01:37:23Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): route FP8 64-head sparse-MLA decode rows to the M64 body once two CTAs per token exceed the SMs (#8311)

`trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4(backend="cake")` ships BF16 and FP8
programs for 8-128 query heads (several bodies per head count, picked
per shape by the host route) and an NVFP4-KV family. This PR changes the
route of the FP8 64-head decode rows: once two CTAs per token exceed the
SM count, they run the single-CTA M64 body, and the rows that ran the
H64 cluster body run the M64 body at every token count.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode, 64 heads per rank, FP8 Q and KV, q_len 4
(rows = batch x 4), 8K context, GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4,
cold L2, median kernel time. Previous Cake and this PR timed in one
process; trtllm-gen with PDL for reference.

### [626cf46](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/626cf464b29e341dd2d36a9b2bb18a66f519e17d)

- **作者**: Zihao Ye
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T01:37:17Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake): allocate pair tensor memory after the cluster barrier in four more families (#8384)

Four Cake kernel families allocated the CTA pair's tensor memory
(`tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2`) before the cluster barrier that follows
the mbarrier initialization: the batch DeepGEMM FP8 programs (8 kernel
units), the mega MoE v3 grouped L1 and grouped fused programs, the BF16
rank-major MoE-EP layer's FC1 and FC2 kernels, and the CUDA backend of
the MXFP8 MegaMoE EP16 fused kernel. The PTX ISA requires the allocating
warp to make sure the peer CTA has launched first, and compute-sanitizer
racecheck reported the hazard on every one of these programs it could
run on one GPU. This PR moves the cluster barrier ahead of the
allocation; racecheck and synccheck are clean on the fixed programs, and
they time the same as before:

| shape | previous Cake (us) | this PR (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| batch DeepGEMM FP8, 32 x [128 x 2048] x [2048 x 7168], expected M 2 |
77.41 | 77.34 | 1.00x |
| batch DeepGEMM FP8, 64 x [128 x 7168] x [7168 x 4096], expected M 3 |
291.68 | 291.39 | 1.00x |

*Median kernel time, back to back, cold L2; GB300 (sm_103a), CUDA 13.4.*

The other Cake variants of these families (the barrier-first programs
and the EP16 CuTe DSL backend) already allocate after the cluster
barrier; the families ship for sm_100a and sm_103a (MoE-EP also
sm_107a).

### [a18e2f7](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a18e2f7dca4e6185dad542441266c9369aecf9b9)

- **作者**: Alex Yang
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T01:22:07Z
- **提交信息**: fix(msa_ops): serve SM90 sparse-decode coordinates whose planned route was never delivered (#7222) (#8014)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`flashinfer/msa_ops/cake_hopper_sm90.py::plan_sparse_decode` ports the
Cake latency model for the SM90 sparse-decode programs and emits one
logical route per geometry. It checked the delivered program set
(`ROUTES` in `flashinfer/jit/cake_hopper_msa.py`) only for its HALF /
persistent replacements, never for the model's own 128-key coordinate.
On 132-SM parts (H100 SXM, H200) the model picks three ring stages for
nc16 item bands (GQA group > 8) that the export delivered at two stages
only, so `_decode_template` reached `route_program`, which raised
`KeyError`, and `msa_sparse_decode_attention` crashed instead of
computing. `_sm90_dispatch.sparse_decode_sm90` has a CuTe fallback, but
it triggers on dtype / shape admission, not on a planner route without a
program, so nothing caught this.

**Enumeration (CPU, this tree's `ROUTES`).** `plan_sparse_decode` over
`num_sms` {132, 114, 78} x GQA group {1, 4, 8, 9, 16, 17, 32, 33, 48,
49, 64} x KV heads {1, 2, 4, 8} x `seqlen_q` {1, 2, 4, 8} x batch 1..512
x `max_pages` on both sides of the three L2-policy thresholds of
`seqlen_q * 16 / max_pages` plus {1, 1024}: 3,784,704 points. Before the
fix: 25 distinct routes emitted, 3 of them absent from `ROUTES`, all at
132 SMs (none at 114 or 78), 64,374 points in all. After: 22 distinct
routes, all delivered, and every one of the 22 delivered decode programs
is emitted by some point (no unreachable program).

| Undelivered route (before) | Where the model picks it (132 SMs; items
= batch x seqlen_q x KV heads x chunks) | Points | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decode_v5:nc16:s2:st3:evict_first:main` | `seqlen_q` 1 (also 2 / 4 /
8), `max_pages` >= 11, items 265-330, 397-462, 530-594, 794-858 | 24,630
| batch 67, 64 Q / 4 KV heads, 16 pages (the hand case of #7222) |
| `decode_v5:nc16:s1:st3:none:main` | `seqlen_q` 1, `max_pages` <= 10,
items 331-396, 596-660, 860-924, then every other item from 1059 |
13,878 | batch 83, 64 Q / 4 KV heads, 8 pages |
| `decode_v5:nc16:s1:st3:evict_first:main` | `seqlen_q` 2 / 4 / 8,
`max_pages` >= 65 at q-len 2, items 332-396, 596-660, 860-924, then
every other item from 1060 | 25,866 | batch 42, `seqlen_q` 2, 64 Q / 4
KV heads, 65 pages |

**Fix (host planner only; no kernel, binding or program change).** After
the existing HALF / persistent fallback to the model's pick, the planner
now checks the model's own route: if it is not delivered, it serves the
two-stage ring of the same head fold, split count and L2 policy, which
the export delivers for every split count of both folds
(`nc{8,16}:s{1,2,4,8}:st2:{evict_first,none}:main`). The two-stage form
keeps the grid, the split scratch and the kernel scalars (st2 admits
every split count st3 does, `_max_splits(nc, 2) == 16` for both folds,
and it needs less shared memory). If neither route is delivered the
planner raises a `ValueError` naming both, from the planner rather than
`KeyError` from inside the launch template. The three crashing
coordinates now serve `nc16:s2:st2:evict_first`, `nc16:s1:st2:none` and
`nc16:s1:st2:evict_first`.

Regenerating the three st3 programs instead is the other option; this PR
takes the planner-side fallback because it needs no new program and is
what the v0.7.3 window allows. If the export later delivers the st3
routes, the planner serves them automatically and the pin in the CPU
test retires itself (it applies only while the model's route is absent).

## 🔍 Related Issues

Closes #7222. The deslop PR #7332 closed the issue while listing this
item under "Not in this PR" ("Decode routes without a program"); the
issue was reopened on 2026-10-30 for this item only. Feature owner:
yyihuang (#6252, #6140).

## Reviewer Notes

The change is the block at the end of `plan_sparse_decode`, its
docstring and one module comment. Which delivered route to serve is a
judgment call the planner's own cost model can inform. For the three
coordinates it rates the served two-stage ring of the model's split
count at 1.13x (hand case) and 1.29x (the two one-split bands) of its
undelivered st3 pick, while the cheapest *delivered* coordinate of the
same head fold and L2 policy (`s4:st2` for the hand case, `s2:st2` for
the one-split bands) rates at 1.01x and 1.02x. This PR keeps the
same-split two-stage ring: it keeps the model's grid and split scratch,
it is the smallest change, and the model is unmeasured on these bands
(#6252 measured group 16 at 4 / 128 / 512 items only). Re-minimizing the
model over the delivered coordinates instead is an equally small change
if reviewers prefer it; either is a stopgap until the export delivers
the three st3 programs, which the planner would then pick on its own. No
measurement is claimed for the three bands; before this change they did
not run.

Release context: the SM90 Cake MSA ops ship for the first time in
v0.7.3, so this is a crash fix in a new feature rather than a regression
against v0.7.2.post1.

### [f5c654f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f5c654f49313c404e252a94bc4ea6bfb7ff64e88)

- **作者**: Zihao Ye
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T01:15:14Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_deepgemm_dense_mqa): split 32-head FP8 MQA logits past 2^32 elements into row ranges (#8308)

The 32-head FP8 dense MQA logits programs address the output with 32-bit
element offsets, so a `fp8_mqa_logits` call whose `[Q,
logits_stride(K)]` logits pass 2^32 elements (a long prefill chunk, e.g.
Q = K = 65536) wrote its last rows over the first ones. `fp8_mqa_logits`
now runs such a call as one launch per range of whole query blocks on a
row view of the output, and `DenseMqaPlan` refuses a plan over that many
logits. The kernels and every call below 2^32 logits are unchanged.

Correctness on GB300 (sm_103a, CUDA 13.4), causal windows of at most
1000 keys, K = 65536, all cells checked against a torch reference (atol
= rtol = 0.1; -inf outside the windows):

| Q | logits elements | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 65536 (full blocks) | 4,311,744,512 | 254,594 wrong in-window cells,
227,985 out-of-window cells not -inf | 0 / 0 |
| 65533 (partial block) | 4,311,547,136 | 251,632 / 224,898 | 0 / 0 |
| 65283 (short last range) | 4,295,098,336 | n/a | 0 / 0 |
| 4096 | 269,484,032 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

-->

### [23cd5a9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/23cd5a9938e7961defa46cf5d8ed90c038604014)

- **作者**: Zihao Ye
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T01:11:58Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_deepgemm_mega_gate): token mask, image bias, per-call PDL, decode templates and SM107a as a vendorable package (#8320)

Cake ships one fused routing-gate kernel (BF16 routing GEMM,
sqrtsoftplus scoring, expert-group top-k, normalized unbiased weights,
logical-to-physical expert mapping) as 23 schedule templates, K=5120 and
E=384. This PR delivers all of them as a vendorable package and adds
DeepGEMM MegaGate's token mask and image bias, a per-call `enable_pdl`,
six decode templates for 193-960 rows (blocks 48/64/80 on one CTA,
112/128/160 on a CTA pair) and SM107a builds. Speedup against DeepGEMM
MegaGate (`deep_gemm.bf16_mega_gate`), both with PDL, in a chain of a
producer kernel, the gate writing rows [:M] of a 2048-row routing buffer
with the token mask and a static EPLB map, and a consumer that waits and
reads both; latency of the chain in µs, back to back / cooled.

**NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a (compute capability 10.3, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4**

| Rows | Image tokens | Cake (µs) | MegaGate (µs) | Speedup (MegaGate /
Cake) |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 72 | no | 12.16 / 12.13 | 12.83 / 12.70 | 1.055 / 1.047 |
| 72 | yes | 12.58 / 12.54 | 12.96 / 12.93 | 1.030 / 1.031 |
| 128 | no | 14.56 / 14.53 | 15.46 / 15.42 | 1.062 / 1.061 |
| 128 | yes | 14.82 / 14.82 | 15.46 / 15.46 | 1.043 / 1.043 |
| 256 | no | 19.84 / 19.84 | 19.68 / 19.65 | 0.992 / 0.990 |
| 256 | yes | 19.81 / 19.84 | 20.51 / 20.51 | 1.035 / 1.034 |

### [f33e466](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f33e46637962a9fbc4e8a37b06177bab69aa77b5)

- **作者**: rmhaskar
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T01:10:35Z
- **提交信息**: perf(msa_ops sm90): bound the indexer's work by the real sequence length under CUDA graphs (#8056)

## 📌 Description

Under vLLM's full CUDA graphs the MSA indexer is captured at
`max_model_len` (an 8192-page score buffer), and the real lengths only
reach the kernels as device tensors. The SM90 CuTe DSL indexer kernels
sized their work from the captured width rather than from those lengths,
so every decode step paid for the full context window. This PR bounds
the work by the real lengths:

- **Proxy-score decode:** each sequence's tiles are split across CTAs
and only tiles inside its length are scored; the rest of the buffer gets
a cheap `-inf` fill. Also fixes a causal-mask bug: with several query
tokens (MTP) straddling a page boundary, only the last tile was masked.
- **Top-k select:** reads are bounded by each row's valid page count
instead of the full width. The host-side plan is cached, so the call no
longer re-plans every step.
- **Mixed decode + prefill batches:** a batch whose sequences are padded
to the longest query (decodes next to a prefill chunk) now goes to the
CuTe proxy-score prefill kernel, which skips the padded tiles, instead
of Cake, which computes them. Uniform batches stay on Cake.

H100, proxy score + top-k at an 8192-page score buffer:

| Workload | Before (µs) | After (µs) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Decode, 1 request, 8k context | 10.8 | 7.1 | 1.5x |
| Decode, 8 requests, 8k context | 48.7 | 9.1 | 5.4x |
| Decode, 32 requests, 8k context | 170 | 17.2 | 9.9x |
| Decode, 48 requests, 8k context | 250 | 27.5 | 9.1x |
| Mixed: 8 decodes + 2048-token chunk | 472 | 122 | 3.9x |
| Mixed: 16 decodes + 2048-token chunk | 941 | 192 | 4.9x |
| Mixed: 32 decodes + 2048-token chunk | 1766 | 281 | 6.3x |
| Decode, 48 requests, 1M context | 2097 | 2129 | 0.98x |
| Top-k host (CPU) time per call | 65–229 | ~19 | 3.4–12x |

### [0ab2327](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0ab232771fc845a9537799c6040642dcfabacec7)

- **作者**: Alex Yang
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T01:07:51Z
- **提交信息**: ci(release): pass release notes by file and cap them at the GitHub body limit (#7972)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

The v0.7.3rc1 Release run
([41001519355](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/41001519355))
built and validated every artifact and then failed in `create-release`:
`gh release create` received the generated notes as a single `--notes`
argument, and the 205 KB body for the `v0.7.2rc7...v0.7.3rc1` delta
(1,282 entries) exceeds Linux's 128 KiB per-argument limit, so bash
reported `/usr/bin/gh: Argument list too long` (exit 126). Earlier rcs
stayed under the limit (v0.7.2rc1's notes were 45 KB).
`publish-to-pypi`, `update-wheel-index` and `deploy-docs` were skipped
behind it, so nothing was published.

Two changes in `.github/workflows/release.yml`:

- `Create GitHub Release` passes the notes with `--notes-file` (the file
already existed; it was read back into a variable only to be re-expanded
on the command line).
- `Generate release notes` caps the body at 120,000 bytes on a line
boundary and appends a link to the full compare view, because the GitHub
API also rejects release bodies above 125,000 characters, so
`--notes-file` alone would have moved the failure to the API call.

Not changed here: the previous-tag selection (`git tag
--sort=-version:refname`) picked `v0.7.2rc7` rather than `v0.7.2.post1`
as the baseline for the rc1 notes; that is a separate, cosmetic issue.
`nightly-release.yml` passes its (per-day, small) notes the same way and
can follow if its notes ever grow.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Release run
https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/41001519355
(v0.7.3rc1).

### [0ff77be](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0ff77be8f5fce783418d26ea144d9fac826bfaa4)

- **作者**: Zihao Ye
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T01:00:04Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_deepgemm_dense_mqa): split paged FP8 MQA logits past 2^31 elements into request ranges (#8315)

The paged FP8 MQA logits programs (`fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, SM100a /
SM103a) address the output with signed 32-bit element offsets, so a call
whose `[B * next_n, logits_stride(max_context_len)]` logits pass 2^31
elements (a large decode batch at a long `max_context_len`) stored its
last rows at negative offsets and faulted with an illegal memory access.
`fp8_paged_mqa_logits` now runs such a call as one launch per range of
requests on a row view of the output, and `PagedMqaPlan` refuses a plan
over that many logits. The kernels and every call at or below 2^31
logits are unchanged.

Correctness on GB300 (sm_103a, CUDA 13.3): H = 64, page 64, next_n 1,
batch 64, requests of 300-1000 keys, every cell of each request's
written range checked against a torch reference (atol = rtol = 1e-2 of
the row max; -inf past each token's length):

| max_context_len | logits elements | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 34,087,168 | 2,181,578,752 | illegal memory access | 0 wrong cells |
| 33,554,432 | 2,147,483,648 | 0 wrong cells | 0 wrong cells |

### [61da801](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/61da801996ab37d1e8bea6019b36f388e4dcf817)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T00:35:45Z
- **提交信息**: docs(cake_gdn_kcp): plain split views of packed Q/K/V cost a concatenation in the non-deterministic KCP backward (#8393)

Non-deterministic counterpart of #8385 for #8367.

When `q` / `k` / `v` are head views of one packed `[T, (2 H_qk + HV) *
128]` row, the non-deterministic context-parallel GDN backward reaches
full speed only through `packed_qkv_views_kcp`. Plain `split` views give
the same results within the accuracy budgets (bitwise in every run
measured below). They keep torch's own autograd path, so hooks and
`retain_grad` on them fire. But torch's split backward then concatenates
`dq` / `dk` / `dv` into a new row. This PR documents this in the
`packed_qkv_views_kcp` and `chunk_gdn_kcp` docstrings of
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp` and in the README (the
input bullet and the **Packed Q/K/V** section, which it extends). It
also updates the docstring of the facade
`flashinfer.cake_gdn_train_kcp.chunk_gdn_kcp` for `deterministic=False`.
That docstring names both helpers, `packed_qkv_views_kcp` and
`packed_qkv_views_det_kcp`; either one's views get the packed gradient
layout. The docs give the helper's conditions (a dense packed row, token
stride exactly `(2 H_qk + HV) * 128`, and the default `layout="tma"`),
what its autograd node implies, and the measured cost below. The
autograd path is unchanged, and plain views are not rerouted
automatically. The PR also adds tests:
- plain split, packed and contiguous inputs give the same results. The
package is non-deterministic, so bitwise equality is asserted only on
the CPU fake backend. On GPUs the arms are compared within the accuracy
budgets of the test files (on one GPU: relative RMS <= 1e-2, max-abs <=
2e-2 x max |ref|). With the in-kernel L2 norm on, out / dv / dg / dbeta
are compared against an FP64 reference, and dq / dk between the arms;
- hooks and `retain_grad` on the views and on the split outputs fire
with the gradient, and the gradient layout and the packed/split
statistics are checked exactly;
- packed views refuse in-place changes while the packed row requires
grad;
- the in-kernel Q/K L2 norm is covered off and on, and both direct and
checkpointed calls are covered;
- coverage includes the CPU fake backend, one GPU and the multi-GPU
context-parallel rows.

Cost of plain split views (issue repro with `deterministic=False`:
`(H_qk, HV) = (16, 48)`, 32,768 tokens in five documents, one-rank
context; checkpointed step = two forwards and one backward; CUDA-event

### [e4f5a75](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e4f5a75fcc4cc60dace8c9faf1810c2fad22a31c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T00:23:57Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_fmha): BF16 decode page tables, retained-KV sink grid, the exact B128 retained-KV member and a correction-warp race (#8406)

## Problem

This PR fixes four separate problems in the BF16 decode path:

- **Page tables.** DEC_SINK, DEC_B128 and the JIT members read 8 page
ids per evened 128-token block using 16-byte loads. Narrow tables went
to the compat path, which takes about 38 ms per call. If the table width
was not divisible by 4, or the table base was misaligned, the kernel
faulted with `misaligned address` (b128, width 97).
- **Retained-KV grid.** The binding launched the retained-KV B256 sink
member with a 3-D grid. The kernel strides tiles over `gridDim.x = 1`,
so every CTA ran all 1024 tiles (about 50 ms per call).
- **Exact B128 retained-KV member (host scale).** This member gives
wrong results and is nondeterministic. On GB300, kv300 has 6504 bad
elements (rel_l2 0.19) and 0/10 runs agree. A b128 short-KV clean case
has 112-125 bad elements and a different output hash on each run. On
B200, racecheck reports 34530 errors.
- **Correction-warp race in `decode_native_bf16/default.cu`.** The
correction warps read `smem_exch` / `smem_corr`. Then only one elected
thread per warp arrived on `stats_empty`, so the softmax warps' writes
for the next tile raced those reads. racecheck reports 23041-56065 WAR
errors on main's generic member.

## Fix

- **Page tables:** the kernels read a padded copy of the table at the
end of the workspace, and the binding pads it for the JIT members.
Short-KV launches now use DEC_B128 / DEC_SINK when the table fits.
- **Retained-KV grid:** the B256 sink member gets its persistent 1-D
grid.
- **Exact B128 retained-KV member:** removed. The generic member and
DEC_B128 now handle its launches. The short-KV case above now runs
DEC_B128 with 0 bad elements and the same hash on 3 runs.
- **Race:** `stats_empty` is initialized with 128, and all 128
correction threads arrive. Outputs are bitwise unchanged. This file is
maintained by hand (no generator produces it). The generated programs
already use this pattern.

## Tests

- New host and GPU tests cover padded tables, odd widths 97/98/99,
short-KV programs and member grids.
- pytest on B200 and GB300: the selected set gives 211 passed / 0 failed
(main: 188 / 0). The full
`tests/attention/test_cake_fmha_decode_programs.py` gives 292 / 0 (main:
269 / 0).
- compute-sanitizer: racecheck reports 0 on the 3 changed rows on both
GPUs. memcheck reports 0 and synccheck reports 0.
- pre-commit passes.

## Timing

Times are in µs. B200 (sm_100a), GB300 (sm_103a), CUDA 13.4.

**Changed rows**

| row | GPU | main | this PR | trtllm-gen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| narrow table (width 82), host scale | GB300 | 37734 | 173.5 | 116.2 |
| kv3585, table width 232 | GB300 | 103968 | 353.9 | 279.5 |
| retained-KV sink, kv1152 | GB300 | 48936 | 115.4 | 103.5 |
| retained-KV sink, kv300 | GB300 | 20913 | 49.6 | 38.9 |
| b128 short-KV, kv1024 | GB300 | 64.67 | 48.38 | 55.46 |
| narrow table (width 82), host scale | B200 | 38220 | 144.1 | 118.2 |
| retained-KV sink, kv1152 | B200 | 50910 | 113.0 | 105.3 |
| b128 short-KV, kv1024 | B200 | 61.18 | 49.02 | 56.51 |

**Unchanged rows (main and this PR are bitwise identical)**

| row | GPU | main | this PR | trtllm-gen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| b128 4096 | GB300 | 168.90 | 168.93 | 171.33 |
| sink 4096 | GB300 | 316.93 | 316.77 | 314.37 |
| b4 1024 | GB300 | 7.33 | 7.33 | 8.06 |
| b128 4096 | B200 | 169.86 | 169.89 | 172.90 |
| sink 4096 | B200 | 319.33 | 319.23 | 316.99 |
| b4 1024 | B200 | 7.62 | 7.62 | 8.51 |

**Cost of using the generic member for the removed member's launches**
(same process, 5 memory layouts):

- B200: +0-0.8 % (kv640), +0.9-1.4 % (kv1152), +1.9-2.7 % (kv300).
- GB300: +0.8-2.6 %. On these launches the removed member's output was
wrong.

**Remaining gap (follow-up work):** the padded and device-scale routes
replace the compat path, cutting milliseconds to microseconds, but they
are still slower than trtllm-gen. Examples on GB300: narrow table (width
82), host scale 173.5 vs 116.2; retained-KV sink device scale kv1152
290.7 vs 141.0; b128 short-KV device scale kv1152 239.0 vs 97.8.

### [eabf03f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/eabf03fe55e77e3305c503b5cbfa1e60450c4227)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T00:14:20Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_fmha): BF16 decode programs read no V page past a request's length (#8407)

## Problem

The six BF16 decode programs (DEC_B128/_DS, DEC_B4C4/_DS, DEC_SINK/_DS)
load page-table slots up to `max_local_seq_len` for every request. A
slot past a request's length points to whatever the table or pool holds
there:

- A NaN pool page reaches P·V as 0·NaN, and the output becomes NaN (for
example, 128/128 requests on b128).
- A request with `kv_len = 0` still sees key 0 and writes a non-zero O.

## Fix

- A V slot at or past the tile's visible keys now points to page 2**30,
which TMA zero-fills. visible = min(q_pos + 1, kv_len), so a request
with no keys writes O = 0.
- K slots are unchanged, because the softmax already masks every score
past the length.
- In the stream-K B128 programs, one load-warp thread warms the length
lines in L2 during the prologue.
- Clean outputs are bitwise identical to main. The programs are
regenerated.

## Tests

- New `test_cake_decode_bf16_programs_read_no_page_past_the_length` (3
rows x host/device scale x NaN pages / garbage ids): main 12 failed,
this PR 12 passed, on B200 and GB300.
- Full `tests/attention/test_cake_fmha_decode_programs.py`: 281 passed
(main: 269) on both GPUs at the PR head.
- NaN screen of 24 cases x 6 inputs: every clean, garbage and kv0 output
of the changed programs is bitwise equal to main. The 9 NaN-page cases
go from non-finite to finite (FP32 reference check: 0 bad).
- compute-sanitizer memcheck, racecheck and synccheck are clean on both
GPUs.
- pre-commit passes.

## Timing

Method: CUPTI, cold L2, 6 rotating rounds, 5 seeded memory layouts;
values are medians in µs. "control" is main's source compiled as its own
module, which separates out code-placement effects. Ratio = control /
PR, so a value > 1 means the PR is faster. B200 (sm_100a), GB300
(sm_103a), CUDA 13.4.

| row | GPU | main | PR | control | trtllm-gen | control/PR median
[min,max] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| b128 s4096 | B200 | 169.89 | 169.82 | 169.92 | 171.42 | 1.0003
[0.9997,1.0008] |
| b128 s4096 | GB300 | 166.02 | 166.00 | 166.08 | 168.99 | 0.9996
[0.9985,1.0004] |
| b128 s4096 log2 | B200 | 170.05 | 170.14 | 170.05 | 172.16 | 0.9991
[0.9982,0.9995] |
| b128 s4096 log2 | GB300 | 165.63 | 165.79 | 165.60 | 168.80 | 0.9991
[0.9980,1.0000] |
| b128 s4096 device scale | B200 | 226.14 | 226.77 | 226.65 | 186.46 |
0.9981 |
| b128 s4096 device scale | GB300 | 270.88 | 274.18 | 272.16 | 208.72 |
0.9981 |
| b256 s4096 sink | B200 | 320.52 | 321.34 | 320.30 | 318.97 | 0.9994
[0.9966,1.0007] |
| b256 s4096 sink | GB300 | 308.70 | 308.43 | 308.50 | 309.50 | 0.9996
[0.9978,1.0003] |
| b256 s4096 sink device scale | B200 | 375.85 | 376.64 | 376.00 |
332.73 | 0.9988 |
| b256 s4096 sink device scale | GB300 | 411.89 | 412.83 | 416.08 |
350.01 | 0.9979 |
| b4 s1024 | B200 | 7.44 | 7.46 | 7.46 | 8.35 | 0.9959 (32 ns timer
steps) |
| b4 s1024 | GB300 | 7.46 | 7.46 | 7.46 | 8.35 | 1.0000 |
| b4 s1024 device scale | B200 | 63.85 | 64.30 | 64.35 | 25.14 | 1.0025
|
| b4 s1024 device scale | GB300 | 113.09 | 110.86 | 111.99 | 51.36 |
1.0196 (GB300 run-to-run noise ±25 %) |

**Cost:**

- b128 log2 is about 0.09 % slower on both GPUs (0.09 µs on B200, 0.16
µs on GB300).
- sink b256 is 0.25-0.34 % below the control in 2 of 5 B200 layouts
(median 0.06 %).
- All other rows are within noise.

### [95500c6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/95500c681f72fb3c6ba5d1c16cf09030d197da76)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T00:09:49Z
- **提交信息**: test(cake_fused_moe): Kimi-K3 NVFP4 SiTU 64-token fused quant+route bitwise case for hot experts (#8409)

Follow-up to #8383. It adds a bitwise case to the 64-token
fused-versus-separate comparison in
`tests/moe/test_cake_kimi_k3_situ.py`. In this case, all tokens route to
a small set of hot experts.

At 64 tokens, the existing cases spread the 1024 routed pairs over many
experts, with 1–2 rows per expert. The new `"hot"` routing sends every
token to experts 0..15. Each of those experts gets 64 rows (4 full tiles
at tile-N16), and the other 880 experts get none. The case `m64_hot`
checks that the fused quant+route launch (`m64_claim8_qr`) gives a
bitwise-identical result to the five-launch route. It also checks that
the route produces 64 tiles. Like the other `m64_claim8_qr` cases, it
runs on SM100 and skips on SM103. Only the test file changes.

### [a72f407](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a72f407d20d2488a380fbab11acc9dd3d5405245)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T00:06:33Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_fmha): sync the warp after the NVFP4 context JIT member's page_empty wait (#8408)

## Problem

The NVFP4 context JIT member
`csrc/cake_fmha/cuda/context_nvfp4/enable_sink0_is_causal1_return_lse0_static_one_tile1.cu`
reads shared memory after an mbarrier wait on `page_empty`, with no
`__syncwarp()` after the wait. Some threads of a warp can therefore move
past the wait out of sync with threads that are still waiting.

## Fix

Add `__syncwarp()` after that wait. The generated NVFP4 context programs
already do this.

## Tests

- `tests/attention/test_cake_fmha_context_programs.py -k nvfp4`: 28
passed (main: 28) on B200 and GB300.
- `tests/attention/test_cake_fmha.py -k nvfp4`: 8 passed (main: 8) on
B200.
- compute-sanitizer on GB300, on the two NVFP4 shapes, for both main and
this PR: racecheck 0 hazards, synccheck 0 errors.

## Timing

GB300 (sm_103a), CUDA 13.4. Outputs are bitwise identical to main on all
5 cases. The main/PR median ratios are 1.0025, 0.9968, 0.9994, 1.0023
and 0.9888 (nv_small: 26.88 vs 27.17 µs). All are within main's own
run-to-run spread.

## AI分析总结

## hao-ai-lab/FastVideo 昨日提交分析

### 1. 主要更新类型

- **功能新增**（3项）：NVFP4 QAD 量化训练链路、FP4 注意力机制、共享配方
- **性能优化**（1项）：Q/K 前置处理与量化的融合内核
- **文档更新**（2项）：cookbook 与组件选择文档
- **Bug 修复**（1项）：CI 套件修复

以功能新增和性能优化为主，属于一次围绕 **NVFP4 量化推理/训练** 的密集迭代。

### 2. 关键变更点与项目方向的关系

- **Pika H3 Flex NVFP4 QAD 全链路打通**：从校准（calibration）、量化感知训练（QAD）、FP4 attention 到模型导出，形成完整的低比特视频模型训练与部署流程，这与 FastVideo 追求高效视频生成的定位高度一致。
- **共享 QAD 配方**：将 FastH3 NVFP4 FP4-attention 配方抽象为 OmniRef + V2 T2AV 共享，减少重复配置，体现项目在多模型间复用量化方案的工程化思路。
- **融合算子优化**：把 Q/K preconditioning 与 NVFP4 quantize 融合进 FA4 NVFP4 attention，并强调 **bit-identical**（位级一致），在提速的同时保证结果可复现。
- **配套文档与 CI 修复**：cookbook 补充 `--weights` 参数（针对 NVFP4 QAD 发布与 FP4 attention），修复内存报告与组件选择文档，并让主干 CI 全绿（pytest 9 兼容、Qwen golden 环境）。

### 3. 对项目的影响和潜在意义

- **推理/训练成本显著下降**：NVFP4（4-bit）量化 + FP4 attention 可大幅降低显存与算力需求，使更大规模的视频模型在消费级/推理卡上可用。
- **发布就绪度提升**：QAD 发布、导出路径、cookbook 参数与 CI 绿灯齐备，说明 NVFP4 版本正走向正式可用状态。
- **可维护性改善**：共享配方与文档修复降低了新用户上手和多模型维护的成本。

### 4. 值得关注的技术点

- **bit-identical 融合优化**：验证量化融合不改变数值结果，是高性能内核落地的关键质量门槛。
- **FA4（FlashAttention-4）与 NVFP4 的结合**：低比特注意力对数值精度极敏感，其校准与实现值得关注。
- **QAD（量化感知训练）与导出的端到端衔接**：训练态量化到推理态导出的一致性是常见坑点，本次一次性打通。
- **pytest 9 与 Qwen golden 环境修复**：反映项目在跟进依赖升级时对回归测试的重视。

### 5. 对项目发展的整体影响

结合 README，FastVideo 是面向高效视频生成的框架，配有文档、Cookbook、Quick Start 和每周开发会议。本次提交集中强化了 **低比特（NVFP4）高效推理/训练** 这一核心卖点，使性能优化从单点算子扩展到完整的校准—训练—导出—文档—CI 闭环，既提升了模型的部署效率与可用性，也通过共享配方和文档修复降低了社区贡献与用户使用门槛，为后续正式发布 NVFP4 版模型奠定了基础。

## huggingface/diffusers 昨日提交分析（第 1/1 批）

### 1. 主要更新类型
- **功能新增**：两个新的模型管线接入（P-H3-Image 图像生成/编辑、Kandinsky S2V 1.0 语音转视频）
- **Bug 修复**：修复注意力后端跨模型泄漏问题
- **文档更新**：文档构建改为仅保留英文，其他语言机器翻译

### 2. 关键变更点与项目方向的关系
- **模块化管线（Modular Pipeline）架构的持续扩展**：两个新模型均以 modular pipeline 形式接入（P-H3-Image 使用 `PH3ImageModularPipeline`/`PH3ImageBlocks`，Kandinsky S2V 复用 `PiflowScheduler`），延续了 diffusers 近期将新模型统一到模块化抽象层的战略方向，减少管线间代码重复。
- **多模态能力拓宽**：P-H3-Image 引入 prompt 上采样器（基于 Qwen3.5-9B）和 MiniMax-H3 VAE，支持最多八张图的图像编辑；Kandinsky S2V 则将支持范围扩展到语音到视频（speech-to-video），并接受波形音频输入而非仅文件路径。
- **注意力后端修复**（#14335）：解决全局状态跨模型污染的隐蔽问题，提升多模型共存场景的可靠性。
- **文档国际化策略调整**（#15149）：降低非英文文档的维护成本，反映项目在国际化与维护开销之间的权衡。

### 3. 对项目的影响和潜在意义
- 新增两个 SOTA 模型接入，增强 diffusers 作为统一扩散模型库的覆盖面，尤其在语音驱动视频生成这一新兴领域取得布局。
- 注意力后端修复消除潜在的静默错误（如不同模型间推理结果互扰），对生产环境稳定性有实质意义。
- 模块化管线的复用模式（如 PiflowScheduler 跨 K6/S2V 复用）为后续新模型接入建立了更清晰的模板。

### 4. 值得关注的技术点
- **量化安全的 modulation 设计**：`KandinskyS2VModulation` 通过调用层而非读取权重实现，并用 `_keep_in_fp32_modules` 保持调制层 fp32，与 Kandinsky 6（K6）保持一致——这是数值精度与量化兼容性的重要模式。
- **RoPE 表 fp32 保持**：S2V 的 RoPE 表以普通属性存放，确保 `.to(torch.bfloat16)` 时仍为 fp32，防止位置编码精度退化。
- **PiflowScheduler 的采样器对齐**：最终步的策略传递与 eps 夹紧逻辑对齐原生 K6/S2V 采样器行为，保证与官方实现的数值等价性。
- **可选依赖的延迟导入**（librosa、soundfile、torchvision 经 `is_*_available()` 门控），保持核心包轻量。
- **离线 offload 策略**：文档更新 Pro 卸载峰值（约 50 GiB），并引入 `memory_reserve_margin="40GiB"` 的按余量卸载机制，反映大模型推理的显存管理实践。

### 5. 基于项目背景的影响
diffusers 作为 HuggingFace 生态的核心扩散模型库，其目标是提供统一、高效、可扩展的模型接入框架。本批提交通过模块化管线新增两个前沿多模态模型，强化了"新模型即插即用"的架构承诺；注意力后端修复和依赖门控则体现了对库级稳定性和轻量性的持续投入。文档策略调整暗示项目在社区规模增长后开始优化维护效率。总体上，这批提交在功能扩展、架构统一性和工程健壮性三个维度同步推进，与项目作为扩散模型基础设施的长期定位一致。

* add kandinsky-s2v

* Address review: reuse PiflowScheduler, keep RoPE tables fp32, validate inputs

- Drop KandinskyS2VPiflowScheduler; the distilled blocks use PiflowScheduler.
- PiflowScheduler: on the final step, pass the nominal segment to the policy
  and clamp only the rollout end to eps, as the native K6 and S2V samplers do.

  them in fp32.

  is passed, and when the Euler path gets num_inference_steps < 2.

* Address review: quantization-safe modulation, drop duration, guard optional deps

- KandinskyS2VModulation calls its layer instead of reading the weight, and
  keeps the modulation layers in fp32 via _keep_in_fp32_modules (as in K6).
- Remove the transformer's `duration` argument; it can only be the frame count.
- Import librosa, soundfile and torchvision behind is_*_available().
- PiflowScheduler: walk raw time one segment at a time and give the policy the
  nominal segment on every step, as the native samplers do.

- Fold the one-line helpers into their callers, inline the memory embedding,
  name the projection layers explicitly and spell out the block arguments.

- Run the fp16 test with the pipeline loaded in fp16; drop the variant test.
- Docs: offload Pro with memory_reserve_margin="40GiB" and show a full run.

* Address review: no file inputs, standalone top-level blocks

- Take `image` as a PIL image and `audio` as a 16 kHz waveform; the docs load them.
- Pass components to the encode helpers explicitly.
- Drop the guider from the text encoder: standalone it encodes a negative
  prompt only when passed; in the pipeline it follows the guider.
- Remove the input step: the text encoder plans the chunks, the VAE encoder
  picks the resolution.
- Group prepare and the chunk loop into one `denoise` step.
- Distilled blocks: no guider and no negative prompt.

* Docs: save the video with the original speech track

* Address review: validation-only checks, no latent output, video_processor

- Inline the grouped attention into the processor.
- `prompt` defaults to DEFAULT_PROMPT in its signature; check_inputs only validates.
- Add auto docstrings to the distilled text encoder and prepare steps.
- Drop `output_type="latent"`; the latents are in the state as `latent_chunks`.
- Preprocess the reference frame with the video processor.
- Remove three tests the review asked to drop.

* Address review: explicit arguments for the helpers

- encode_prompt_and_speech and shared_transformer_kwargs take their components
  and values explicitly and return their results.
- The negative prompt gets its own prepare block in the base pipeline; the
  distilled pipeline uses the shared prepare step.
- check_inputs of the prepare steps take explicit values.

main checks that the denoise group leaves latents in one canonical form
(test_latents_output_in_canonical_form). Point it at latent_chunks: one
chunk per entry, channels last.

- Speech cross-attention keeps static shapes: the per-frame audio groups
  are computed from shapes as Python ints and gathered into a padded,

- Remove dead code: unread attributes, the batched visual-embedding
  branch, unused helper parameters.

* Encode speech with get_audio_features instead of a hook

The speech features now come from the Thinker's public
get_audio_features rather than a forward hook on its audio tower. The
tower runs twice per call, once inside the Thinker forward for the text
hidden states and once for the features: +20 ms on a 12 s track (bf16,

# DiffSynth-Studio 昨日提交分析（第 1/1 批）

## 1. 主要更新类型
本次提交以**功能新增与 Bug 修复为主**，辅以少量性能调优和仓库清理。其中功能新增 1 项（warm-up 预热支持），Bug 修复约 4 项（SDXL clip skip、DeepSpeed ZeRO3 预设 LoRA 加载、OPD 训练问题、krea2 注意力路由），另含默认关闭 sage attention 的行为调整与无用文件移除。

## 2. 关键变更点及其与项目整体方向的关系
- **多 GPU 预热与调度器同步**（#1804）：为大规模分布式训练提供启动优化，契合项目作为一站式扩散模型训练/推理框架的定位。
- **SDXL 双文本编码器的 clip skip 修正**（#1754）：提升文本条件编码的正确性，直接影响生成质量与复现性。
- **krea2 注意力统一走共享 `attention_forward`**（#1793）：由于 cuDNN SDPA 在 ROCm 上无内核，此举增强 AMD GPU 兼容性，扩大硬件覆盖面。
- **DeepSpeed ZeRO3 预设 LoRA 加载修复**（#1803）：保障参数高效微调在分片并行下的可靠性。
- **OPD 训练修复**（#1801）：调整 teacher target 计算顺序与 sigma 匹配策略，并新增 `--disable_strict_interval_matching` 开关，提升知识蒸馏训练的数值正确性。
- **默认禁用 sage attention**（#1802）：以兼容性优先换取稳定性，减少用户默认路径上的潜在崩溃。

## 3. 对项目的影响和潜在意义
这些改动整体提升了框架在**多 GPU 分布式、多硬件平台（含 AMD）、多微调方案（LoRA/ZeRO3）** 下的稳定性与正确性，降低用户在训练与推理环节的踩坑概率，增强项目作为生产可用工具的成熟度。

## 4. 值得关注的技术点
- warm-up 阶段需跨 GPU **同步调度器**状态，涉及分布式一致性设计。
- OPD 修复中 teacher target 须在**梯度追踪的学生前向之前**计算，以确保 checkpoint 重算能感知学生 LoRA 缩放，体现对重计算（recomputation）语义的深入处理。
- krea2 的 attention 统一路由展示了对**后端内核可用性差异**的抽象封装思路。
- clip skip 同时作用于两个文本编码器，提示 SDXL 条件链路的对称性问题。

## 5. 对项目发展的整体影响
结合 README 可知 DiffSynth-Studio 旨在提供统一的扩散模型生成、训练与微调能力。本批提交从分布式训练效率、跨平台兼容、微调正确性三个维度补齐短板，使框架更贴近**工业级多卡训练场景**，并为后续支持更大规模模型与更复杂蒸馏流程（如 OPD）打下稳定基础。这些夯实基础的改动有助于巩固其作为社区主流扩散模型工作室的地位。

# SGLang 仓库昨日提交总结（共 62 条提交）

## 一、主要更新类型
本次更新以性能优化为主导（约 20 条），其次是调度器与导入体系重构（约 10 条）、Bug 修复（约 15 条），功能新增、CI、文档与测试各占少量。多硬件平台覆盖持续扩展：AMD（MI355X CI、AITER、KDA）、NPU（MLA FP8 KVCache、DCP）、NVIDIA（DeepGEMM、QK-norm 复用）均有进展；新模型接入包括 MiniMax-M3/M3.1、Kimi-K3 及 DeepSeek 配方等，体现多后端、多模型生态战略。

## 二、关键变更点
调度器请求队列系列重构（#43905–#43910）是本批最大的系统性改动，将等待队列、chunked slot 与中止逻辑统一到请求列表接口；其中 #43904 进一步把请求所有权校验收敛为 step 启动时的一次性检查，减少每步调度的重复开销，为跨 batch 复用、抢占式调度等后续演进奠定语义基础。DeepSeek-V4 MoE 性能簇（#48245、#48229、#47976、#48099、#47641）覆盖 mega MoE 预分发、indexer 页表 Triton 核、权重局部化与单 warp 路由，直接服务"快速推理"核心目标。导入与模块边界清理（#47990、#47992、#48087、#48119）消除 re-export shim、拆分 tokenizer/detokenizer 依赖并以 lint 强制约束。缓存体系方面，HiCache 主机池装配、写回由逐受害者等待改为逐轮等待、分页专家自动定容，形成统一的分层缓存能力。

## 三、修复与回滚
关键修复包括采样 top-k/top-p 一致性（#41916）、语法超时缓存（#45466）、调度器指标及各平台兼容性问题，明显提升输出正确性。回滚方面，#47994 撤销了 `moe_finalize_fuse_shared` 的 JIT 重写（回退 #47784），#48054、#48055 则撤销 FlashInfer prefill MoE tactic 与 BRIA Fibo，反映项目"稳定性优先于激进优化"的取舍，提示 JIT 融合类优化需更完善的正确性验证流程。

## 四、项目影响
调度器重构降低后续开发风险但属高风险改动，需回归验证；MoE 优化直接提升 prefill/decode 吞吐，强化大 MoE 模型推理竞争力；采样与语法修复对生产用户价值显著；CI 加固（AMD nightly、lint 规则、VRAM 基线刷新）提升多硬件仓库的可持续性。整体上，项目正从"快速堆叠功能"转向"性能纵深 + 架构治理"并重的发展阶段。

## 五、值得关注的技术点
大量提交由 Claude 系列模型共同署名，AI 辅助开发已深度融入其工作流；Triton/CUDA 手写核持续投入（单 warp MoE 路由、indexer 页表单核展开、深度可分离卷积融合）表明算子层优化仍处核心地位。后续需跟踪两点：所有权检查在 step 启动时统一校验是否覆盖全部状态迁移路径及配套测试；JIT 重写失败的具体原因（数值精度、编译时长或架构兼容）将决定 JIT 优化的回归方式。调度器重构与 MoE 回滚分别触及 CPU 侧调度与 GPU 侧算子，展现了 SGLang 优化工作的双线并行特征，也为其在与 vLLM 等框架竞争中保持性能与稳定性口碑提供了安全的迭代基线。

## AI分析总结

## 1. 主要更新类型

- **功能新增**：逐层量化精度观测器（可选启用）
- **重构**：CUDA 扩展构建开关统一、观测器 API 类化
- **文档更新**：待接入模型 RFC 持续维护、生态交叉核查、安装指引统一为 pip
- **构建系统改进**：CUDA 构建逻辑简化

## 2. 关键变更点及其与项目整体方向的关系

- **逐层量化精度观测器**是本次最重要的功能，直接服务于项目核心目标之一——量化（Quantization）。`QuantizeObserverConfig` 默认关闭，启用后会在量化前快照 bf16 权重，对每个量化线性层输出 rel_err、余弦相似度、激活异常值比率等指标，帮助开发者定位哪种量化类型真正损害了哪些层。同时支持 TorchAO float8 和 SVDQuant W4A4 两种运行时层。API 从三个模块级函数收敛为一个 `QuantizeObserver` 类，简化了调用方。
- **CUDA 构建开关统一**（`CACHE_DIT_BUILD_CUDA` 替代三个独立开关）与项目的可维护性方向一致，消除了隐式包含链，统一 SM 目标解析，并对"全部扩展被跳过"给出明确错误，避免产出无扩展的空轮子。
- **待接入模型 RFC 维护**（Pika-H3-Flex 记录、2026-11-03 生态快照）体现了项目对第三方 DiT 生态的持续追踪，包括 PEFT LoRA 包装、diffusers 补丁、前缀误分发审计等实际接入障碍的结构化记录。

## 3. 对项目的影响和潜在意义

- 观测器使量化调参从"黑盒试错"变为"逐层可诊断"，文档中明确标注了启用成本（观测层约 1.5-2 倍 transformer 前向开销），默认零开销保证生产路径不受影响——这种"可选诊断、默认无损"的设计对量化推理引擎非常关键。
- 构建系统统一降低了贡献者上手门槛和 CI 配置复杂度；pip-only 安装指引和环境安静提示减少了用户安装失败的误诊率。
- 生态 RFC 的持续更新（新增 R.9 前缀误分发审计、8.2 生态核查配方）为后续快速接入新模型建立了可复用的流程资产。

## 4. 值得关注的技术点

- **SVDQuant 的精度观测**：利用 SVDQuant 平滑变换的精确性，从 bf16 快照重建参考输出，而权重保持打包状态使 weight-only error 报告为 null——这是一个精巧的数学性质利用。
- **`layer_name_patterns` 的 re.search 过滤**在快照前生效，可将观测范围收窄到 FFN 或 adaLN 投影，进一步降低开销。
- **构建跳过用 warning 类别而非 print**：因为 pip 转发后端 warning 但丢弃 stdout，且专用类别确保 `-W error` 不会把跳过变成构建失败——细节考虑周到。
- **编辑轮子在扩展编译后才组装**导致的 vcs-versioning 导入失败问题被文档化，避免用户将环境问题误判为编译器故障。

## 5. 对项目发展的整体影响

这些提交共同推进了 cache-dit 作为"生产级 DiT 推理引擎"的成熟度：量化诊断工具的加入使其量化功能从"能用"走向"可调优、可解释"；构建系统和文档的清理降低了维护成本；生态 RFC 的系统性更新则为项目在 DiT 多样化模型生态中的持续适配能力打下了基础。整体上，项目正从功能堆叠期进入工程化和可诊断性提升的阶段。

### [9a3a07e](https://github.com/vipshop/cache-dit/commit/9a3a07ebc68fca214b0ba9d3c9779d99534b9369)

- **作者**: DefTruth
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T10:43:00Z
- **提交信息**: feat: opt-in per-layer quantization accuracy observers (#1216)

* feat(quantize): add opt-in per-layer accuracy observers

Add QuantizationObserverConfig, exposed as QuantizeConfig.observer and
disabled by default, to analyze which layers a quantization type actually
hurts. When enabled, cache-dit snapshots the pre-quantization bf16 weights,
recomputes a bf16 reference for every quantized linear on each forward and
dumps per-layer rel_err, cosine similarity, activation outlier ratio and
weight-only error as JSON.

The feature is strictly opt-in: with observer unset (the default) the
quantize path skips it entirely -- no module walk, no bf16 snapshot, no
hooks -- so latency and numerics are unchanged. layer_name_patterns
(re.search on the fully qualified layer name) narrows the observation set
before the snapshot, e.g. to only the FFN or adaLN projections.

Documented in docs/user_guide/QUANTIZATION.md with the enabled cost
(~1.5-2x transformer forward on the observed layers) and covered by
tests/quantization/test_quantize_observers.py.

* docs: describe the observer cost without internal model names

* feat(quantize): support SVDQuant in the accuracy observers, fold the API into a class

The per-layer observers now cover cache-dit's SVDQuant W4A4 runtime layer in
addition to TorchAO float8: the packed SVDQW4A4Linear is detected through its
qweight attribute, and the reference output is recomputed from the bf16
weight snapshot, which stays valid because the SVDQuant smoothing transform is
exact. The weight-only error is reported as null for SVDQuant because the
weights stay packed.

The three module-level helpers (capture_references / attach_observers /
is_enabled) are replaced by a single QuantizeObserver class that owns the
whole lifecycle of one observation session: capture before quantization,
attach after quantization, dump the statistics. The quantization call sites now
import one name instead of three.

Behavior is unchanged when the observer is disabled: the quantize path skips
the feature entirely.

pipeline (PEFT LoRA r128, six-step re-noising sampler). No new BlockAdapter
is needed - the transformer is MiniMaxH3Transformer3DModel - so the row
records the real obstacles instead: PEFT-wrapped Linear names vs the shipped
TP/quantization keys, the diffusers patches the package applies, the
block-level group offload it already occupies, and the ~0-hit DCE budget of
a six-evaluation ladder that re-noises with fresh noise every step.

### [2611425](https://github.com/vipshop/cache-dit/commit/261142505455e2788cd3f83b9912aecfde67750c)

- **作者**: DefTruth
- **时间**: 2026-11-03T04:38:52Z
- **提交信息**: build(cuda): unify the CUDA extension switches into CACHE_DIT_BUILD_CUDA (#1210)

* build(cuda): unify the CUDA extension switches into CACHE_DIT_BUILD_CUDA

Replace CACHE_DIT_BUILD_SVDQUANT, CACHE_DIT_BUILD_COMM and CACHE_DIT_BUILD_ATTN -- which formed an implicit inclusion chain -- with a single CACHE_DIT_BUILD_CUDA that requests every optional extension at once, and rename CACHE_DIT_SVDQUANT_BUILD_MODE to CACHE_DIT_CUDA_BUILD_MODE since it drives the arch resolution of all three.

setup.py resolves the SM targets once through _resolve_sm_targets(scope, is_supported), which applies the per-extension predicate on all three branches (explicit arch list, FAST detection, default set), keeps an explicit list authoritative instead of falling back to the default set, and deduplicates. An extension whose targets all fail the predicate is skipped with a warning in a base build and still fails a cu13 release build, and a build where all three are skipped exits with an error instead of producing an extension-less wheel. The skip notice is a warning rather than a print because pip forwards backend warnings and drops stdout, and it uses a dedicated category so -W error cannot turn a skip into a build failure. SVDQuant initializes its spdlog submodule only after the skip check, so a Hopper build no longer needs it.

Docs, the release scripts and the repo skills follow the new names.

* docs: tell users to keep the environment quiet during a CUDA build

The editable wheel is assembled after the extensions compile, and that step imports setuptools-scm / vcs-versioning. Replacing those packages in the same environment mid-build fails the wheel at the very end with an ImportError raised from vcs_versioning, which reads like a compiler failure but happens minutes after the last object file.

* docs: install with pip everywhere, drop the uv instructions

Every install snippet now uses pip. The notes that compared the two installers are reduced to the pip behaviour they described -- pip merges the extra index with PyPI and takes the highest version -- because naming a second installer in a one-command installation only invites the reader to pick the wrong one. The generated index page (tools/make_index.py) carries the same text, so it stops advertising an installer the docs no longer use.

* docs: spell the installer as pip everywhere

The install instructions mixed pip and pip3, and so did the ImportError messages that tell a user how to install a missing dependency. pip is the spelling that works in every environment these docs target, so use it alone.

* docs: update docs

## AI分析总结

# vLLM 昨日提交分析总结

## 一、主要更新类型

昨日共 124 个提交，以 **Bug 修复为主**（约 50 余条），其次是**性能优化**（约 30 条）、**功能新增**（约 15 条），其余为重构、测试/CI 与文档维护。修复集中在 KV Offload、LoRA、Spec Decode、多模态、内核与硬件平台适配等核心链路；性能优化则围绕内核融合、量化调优与 Prefill/Decode 加速展开。

## 二、关键变更点与项目方向

- **KV 缓存与卸载（低成本主线）**：围绕可扩展 KV 缓存的内存估算、异步加载、卸载重构与状态机并发修复（如批次已满时的有上限异步预取、SWA 空页偏移、P2P 缓冲处理、嵌套连接器角色检测等）展开密集改动，夯实长上下文与 PD 分离场景下的内存成本优势。
- **Speculative Decoding 提速（快速主线）**：AR 推测器重构并启用 CUDA Graph、DFlash 候选打分融合进 Triton 内核、Mamba ReplaySSM 上 GPU、后缀解码 speculator、XPress 接受度估计器等，延续吞吐提升路线。
- **量化与模型适配**：NVFP4/FP8 权重缓存重启、统一 Hadamard/在线旋转替代旧路径、Qwen3.5 AR+norm+quant 融合、ModelOpt 支持 CSF 压缩 NVFP4 块 scale，降低量化部署门槛；新增 DeepSeek V4.1 语言模型 LoRA 适配器，修复多处嵌入层与多硬件 LoRA 正确性问题。
- **功能扩展**：Anthropic `min_tokens`、Granite 工具调用解析、Rust 前端无状态 Responses API、EPD 支持 DeepSeek-V4.1 仅图像元数据输入、Mooncake 选择性前缀租约、EngineCore 层水印配置强制覆盖等。
- **硬件生态**：约 20 条为多平台适配，涵盖 ROCm/Aiter（gfx1151 GDN 后端、MI355X 特化解码）、NVIDIA SM110（CUTLASS FP4 MoE 门控、协作式 top-k 调度）、Intel XPU（triton shim、MoE 收缩/展开）等。
- **CI 与供应链**：依赖哈希固定、ROCm CI 简化、非可信构建复用镜像，增强供应链安全。

## 三、影响与潜在意义

密集修复提升了多硬件、多模型下的正确性与稳定性，降低 OOM、碎片与边缘场景故障风险；内核融合与 Spec Decode 带来可量化的吞吐提升，巩固性能竞争力；工具解析与 Anthropic API 兼容改善 Agent/RAG 生态接入体验；强制水位配置与流式 API 修复则增强了多租户部署的运维管控与评测可信度。

## 四、值得关注的技术点

- CUDA Graph 与推测解码草稿模型的协同（f352490）；
- FlashInfer all-reduce 的 16 字节对齐门控（#63123）与稠密 GEMM 分发短路（#64417），体现算子契约管理与精准调优；
- 系统级配置覆盖请求级选择的优先级仲裁（#62966）；
- 嵌套 KV 连接器的角色推断（#65060）；
- 大量提交含 Claude/Codex 等 AI 辅助共同署名，反映 AI 辅助开发已成常态。

## 五、对项目发展的意义

结合"Easy, fast, and cheap LLM serving for everyone"的愿景，昨日提交呈现三条主线：以 KV 缓存卸载重构降低成本、以内核融合与 Spec Decode 推高性能、以 API 兼容与 CI 加固扩大生态与可靠性。项目已进入成熟期的精细化打磨阶段，在性能微调、边缘场景正确性与生产治理三维度同步推进，为吸引企业级用户、迈向"生产可靠"奠定了坚实基础。

## AI分析总结

## vllm-omni 昨日提交分析（22条）

### 1. 主要更新类型
- **CI/构建优化**：占比最大（约10条），涉及ROCm、CPU、Ascend多平台测试管线加固
- **新模型/功能**：新增Stable Audio 3、Video Depth Anything深度估计、SheetSage2 HTTP服务
- **硬件适配**：Ascend NPU多项修复与IPC权重共享、ROCm测试矩阵扩展
- **Bug修复**：MiniCPM-o 4.5 duplex KV、MammothModa2 AR网格、Diffusion MoE LoRA等
- **文档与工具**：迁移废弃API、路由Ascend优化文档、移除冗余测试

### 2. 关键变更点与项目方向的关系
- **多模态广度扩展**：Stable Audio 3（文本到音频扩散）、Video Depth Anything深度估计，直接呼应"omni-modality"全模态定位，从语言/视觉向音频、3D/深度任务延伸。
- **全平台推理覆盖**：ROCm持续增加Qwen-Image、MiniCPM、Drama 3等模型在READY/MERGE各级别的测试；Ascend修复AR embedding、KV重锚定、NPU codec权重共享——体现"cheap serving"目标下对AMD GPU与华为NPU一线硬件的深度支持。
- **CI稳定性与可观测性**：CPU多worker覆盖率收集修复、TIME-01套件计时、deflake接收测试、L4 KV资源调优、冗余测试清理，表明项目正从"能跑"转向"跑得稳、跑得快、可度量"。

### 3. 影响与潜在意义
- **对用户**：更多模型（音频扩散、深度估计）开箱可用；Ascend/ROCm用户获得更可靠的推理路径。
- **对维护者**：CI分层（READY→MERGE）与计时基线将降低回归排查成本，提升合并信心。
- **对生态**：cherry-pick流程与跨厂商协作者（AMD、华为、DaoCloud、Red Hat）高频参与，说明社区治理与多硬件共建趋于成熟。

### 4. 值得关注的技术点
- **NPU codec持久化IPC权重共享**：跨进程权重复用，是Ascend上降低加载开销的关键优化。
- **MiniCPM-o duplex KV reanchor修复**：双工对话场景KV缓存锚定，影响实时语音交互延迟与正确性。
- **稳定音频扩散管线（Stable Audio 3）**：引入新的diffusion模态，需关注其与现有调度器的集成方式。
- **recv drain burst测试deflake**：以每chunk轮询次数为度量消除时序抖动，是CI工程化的良好实践。
- **pkg_resources→importlib.metadata**：为Python 3.12+兼容性铺路。

### 5. 对项目发展的影响
结合README"Easy, fast, and cheap omni-modality model serving for everyone"的愿景，这批提交呈现清晰的三条发展线：**广度上**补齐音频与深度模态，兑现omni承诺；**硬件上**在Ascend与ROCm两个非NVIDIA生态建立可验证的支持矩阵，扩大"everyone"的覆盖人群；**质量上**通过CI分层、计时基线、deflake与冗余清理夯实工程底座，为后续大规模模型接入提供可持续的迭代节奏。整体上，项目正从多模态框架的早期构建期，迈向生产级可靠性与多硬件普惠的新阶段。
